11.meaning: It passed, went before, or is now bygone — belonging to the past and already gone by. The root denotes what precedes or is sent ahead in time.
11.grammar: A past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('it passed / went before'); the final -a marks a completed action. The same root also yields a noun meaning 'predecessors / those who went before.'
11.root: س-ل-ف (s-l-f) — to precede, go before, be past

12.meaning: An emphasis particle fused with a pronoun, meaning 'indeed He' or 'truly He'. The particle inna strongly affirms and certifies the statement that follows ('it is certainly the case that…'), with 'He' as its subject.
12.grammar: The emphasising particle inna ('indeed/truly') with the attached pronoun -hu ('He'). inna affirms and strengthens the whole statement and grammatically takes a following noun or pronoun as its subject. The lengthened -hū is how this pronoun is pronounced after an -u vowel.

13.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

13.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

14.meaning: A gross indecency or shameful, immoral act — conduct that is flagrantly obscene and exceeds the bounds of decency. The word names something whose ugliness is extreme and obvious.
14.grammar: A feminine noun in the indefinite. The '-tan' ending combines the feminine '-t-' with '-an', the accusative-indefinite marker ('an indecency'), which typically signals the direct object of a verb or a non-specific 'a/an'.
14.root: ف-ح-ش (f-ḥ-sh) — to be excessive, foul, indecent; gross immorality

15.meaning: And something intensely hated and detestable — an object of loathing and disgust. The word denotes the strongest kind of hatred, contempt for something vile.
15.grammar: A connecting 'and' (wa) joined to a verbal noun. The final -an (tanwīn) marks the noun as indefinite ('a detestable thing / an object of hatred') and accusative — the case used for a noun functioning as an object or in a similar governed position.

16.meaning: And it was bad or evil — an expression of strong disapproval. The verb is one of dispraise, meaning 'how wretched or evil a thing it is,' declaring something to be miserable, foul, or grievous.
16.grammar: A connecting 'and' (wa) joined to a past-tense (perfect) verb, third-person masculine singular: 'it was evil.' It commonly works as a verb of blame ('how wicked a thing…'), the opposite of a verb of praise. The final -a closes the completed-action verb with a single masculine subject.
16.root: س-و-ء (s-w-ʾ) — evil, badness; to be bad, harm

17.meaning: A way, path, or road; figuratively a course of conduct, a means, or a manner of acting that one follows.
17.grammar: A singular noun (usable as masculine or feminine). The final -an (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('a way') and accusative — the case used, among other things, for a noun that specifies or clarifies a preceding statement ('… an evil path').

1.meaning: She/it was made forbidden, prohibited, declared unlawful and off-limits — set apart as sacred or sanctioned against. The opposite of being made permissible.
1.grammar: A past-tense passive verb (Form II, its doubled middle root letter giving intensity): 'she/it was made forbidden' — passive because no doer is named, only that the thing was prohibited. The ending -at marks a third-person feminine singular subject. The internal u–i vowel pattern of the stem is the mark of the passive ('was forbidden' rather than 'forbade').
1.root: ح-ر-م (ḥ-r-m) — to forbid; declare sacred or inviolable

2.meaning: 'Upon you (all)' — the preposition 'upon/on/over' joined to the plural 'you,' indicating something resting on or directed at a group.
2.grammar: The preposition 'ʿalā' ('upon/on/over') in its joined form 'ʿalay-' plus the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you all,' masculine plural). It marks the group as the recipients or target of whatever is laid 'upon' them.
2.root: — (preposition; no triliteral root)

3.meaning: Your mothers — those who gave you birth, extended to include those reckoned as mothers (such as grandmothers). The 'your' addresses a group of males or a mixed group.
3.grammar: A sound feminine plural noun ('mothers') with the attached pronoun -kum ('your,' addressing a group of males or mixed company). The -u ending is nominative — the case a noun takes when it is the subject of a sentence or what the sentence is about.

4.meaning: And your daughters — your female children, and by extension female descendants. The 'your' addresses a group of males or a mixed group.
4.grammar: A connecting 'and' (wa) plus the sound feminine plural noun 'daughters' with the attached pronoun -kum ('your'). The -u ending is nominative, marking the noun as a subject or topic.
4.root: ب-ن-و / ب-ن-ي (b-n-w / b-n-y) — son/child, offspring; to build

5.meaning: And your sisters — female siblings sharing one or both parents. The 'your' addresses a group of males or a mixed group.
5.grammar: A connecting 'and' (wa) plus the sound feminine plural noun 'sisters' with the attached pronoun -kum ('your'). The -u ending is nominative — the case used for a subject or topic.

6.meaning: And your paternal aunts — the sisters of one's father. The 'your' addresses a group of males or a mixed group.
6.grammar: A connecting 'and' (wa) plus the sound feminine plural noun 'paternal aunts' (the feminine of ʿamm, a father's brother) with the attached pronoun -kum ('your'). The -u ending is nominative, marking a subject or topic.
6.root: ع-م-م (ʿ-m-m) — paternal uncle/aunt; to be general or comprehensive

7.meaning: And your maternal aunts — the sisters of one's mother. The 'your' addresses a group of males or a mixed group.
7.grammar: A connecting 'and' (wa) plus the sound feminine plural noun 'maternal aunts' (the feminine of khāl, a mother's brother) with the attached pronoun -kum ('your'). The -u ending is nominative — the subject/topic case.

8.meaning: And daughters of — female children of someone, the female offspring belonging to a named relation. This form leads into a following noun that specifies whose daughters.
8.grammar: A connecting 'and' (wa) plus the sound feminine plural 'daughters.' The noun carries the -u nominative ending (marking it as a subject or topic) and stands in the construct state — bound to a following noun to mean 'daughters OF…,' so it appears without a definite article or final tanwīn while awaiting its possessor.
8.root: ب-ن-و / ب-ن-ي (b-n-w / b-n-y) — son/child, offspring; to build

9.meaning: The brother — a male sibling sharing one or both parents.
9.grammar: The definite article al- ('the') with the singular noun 'brother.' The -i ending is genitive — the case a noun takes after a preposition, or when it is the possessor in an 'X OF Y' chain (here completing 'daughters OF the brother').

10.meaning: And daughters of — female children of someone, the female offspring belonging to a named relation. This form leads into a following noun that specifies whose daughters.
10.grammar: A connecting 'and' (wa) plus the sound feminine plural 'daughters.' The noun carries the -u nominative ending (marking it as a subject or topic) and stands in the construct state — bound to a following noun to mean 'daughters OF…,' so it appears without a definite article or final tanwīn while awaiting its possessor.
10.root: ب-ن-و / ب-ن-ي (b-n-w / b-n-y) — son/child, offspring; to build

11.meaning: The sister — a female sibling sharing one or both parents.
11.grammar: The definite article al- ('the') with the singular noun 'sister' (the feminine counterpart of 'brother,' formed with the feminine -t). The -i ending is genitive — the case after a preposition or as the possessor in an 'X OF Y' chain (here 'daughters OF the sister').

12.meaning: And your mothers — those who gave you birth, and by extension those counted as mothers. The 'your' addresses a group of males or a mixed group.
12.grammar: A connecting 'and' (wa) plus the sound feminine plural 'mothers' with the attached pronoun -kum ('your'); its vowel appears as -kumu, the u added to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a connecting hamza. The -u on the noun is nominative — the subject/topic case.

13.meaning: Those (women) who — a relative pronoun introducing a description, referring to a group of females and meaning 'the ones who…' or 'those females that…'.
13.grammar: A relative pronoun, feminine plural: 'those (women) who.' It is indeclinable — its form does not change for case — and it links a following clause back to a feminine-plural group, much like English 'who/which/that' applied to women.

14.meaning: They (women) suckled or nursed you — gave you milk at the breast. The 'you' object addresses a group of males or a mixed group.
14.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb on the Form IV (causative) pattern — 'to give suck.' The ending -na marks a third-person feminine plural subject ('they, the women, nursed'), and the attached -kum is the object pronoun 'you' (a group of males or mixed company).
14.root: ر-ض-ع (r-ḍ-ʿ) — to suckle, nurse at the breast

15.meaning: And your sisters — female siblings sharing one or both parents. The 'your' addresses a group of males or a mixed group.
15.grammar: A connecting 'and' (wa) plus the sound feminine plural noun 'sisters' with the attached pronoun -kum ('your'). The -u ending is nominative — the case used for a subject or topic.

16.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
16.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

17.meaning: The suckling — the act or relationship of breastfeeding, the nursing through which milk-kinship is established.
17.grammar: The definite article al- ('the,' its l assimilated into the following r so it is heard as ar-raḍāʿa) with a verbal noun naming the act of breastfeeding. The -i ending is genitive — the case taken after a preposition or as the possessor in an 'X OF Y' chain.
17.root: ر-ض-ع (r-ḍ-ʿ) — to suckle, nurse at the breast

18.meaning: And mothers of — those who are mothers to someone, leading into a following noun that specifies whose mothers. Used here in the sense of mothers-in-law.
18.grammar: A connecting 'and' (wa) plus the sound feminine plural 'mothers.' The -u ending is nominative (the subject/topic case), and the noun stands in the construct state — bound to a following noun to mean 'mothers OF…,' so it appears without article or tanwīn while awaiting its possessor.

19.meaning: 'Your wives / your women.' The plural noun for women or wives, joined to 'your' (addressing a group) — denoting the women belonging to or married to the people addressed.
19.grammar: An irregular plural noun ('women, wives') with the attached pronoun -kum ('your,' addressing a group). The -i before the pronoun is the genitive ending, which appears because the noun is possessed ('the women OF you'); the pronoun -kum marks plural ownership ('your').
19.root: ن-س-و (n-s-w) — woman, womankind

20.meaning: And your stepdaughters — the daughters a wife brings from a previous marriage, the foster-daughters under one's care. The 'your' addresses a group of males or a mixed group.
20.grammar: A connecting 'and' (wa) plus a broken (irregular) plural noun meaning 'stepdaughters' — literally those reared in one's house — with the attached pronoun -kum ('your'), its vowel given as -kumu to ease pronunciation before a following connecting hamza. The -u on the noun is nominative — the subject/topic case.
20.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, rear, foster; lordship over

21.meaning: Those (women) who — a relative pronoun introducing a description, referring to a group of females and meaning 'the ones who…' or 'those females that…'.
21.grammar: A relative pronoun, feminine plural: 'those (women) who.' It is indeclinable — its form does not change for case — and it links a following clause back to a feminine-plural group, much like English 'who/which/that' applied to women.

22.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
22.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

23.meaning: Your laps, bosoms, or care — the protective keeping of a household. The word literally means the laps or embraces in which children are reared, and stands for being raised under someone's guardianship and protection. The 'your' addresses a group of males or a mixed group.
23.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural noun ('laps/bosoms,' hence protective care) with the attached possessive pronoun -kum ('your'). The -i ending is genitive — the case a noun takes after a preposition or as the possessor in an 'X OF Y' construction.
23.root: ح-ج-ر (ḥ-j-r) — lap/bosom, enclosure; to restrain or protect

24.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
24.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

25.meaning: A word meaning 'your women' or 'your wives' — the plural of woman/wife joined to a 'your' (plural, masculine) possessor. The base noun denotes adult females, and in many contexts specifically wives.
25.grammar: A plural noun (an irregular 'broken' plural) ending in hamza, which is part of the noun itself. It carries the genitive case-vowel -i, the ending a possessed noun takes before an attached possessive pronoun (the iḍāfa construction). The suffix -kum means 'your' for a group of males or a mixed group; its vowel is lengthened to -kumu when a vowel follows.

26.meaning: Those (women) who — a relative pronoun introducing a description, referring to a group of females and meaning 'the ones who…' or 'those females that…'.
26.grammar: A relative pronoun, feminine plural: 'those (women) who.' It is indeclinable — its form does not change for case — and it links a following clause back to a feminine-plural group, much like English 'who/which/that' applied to women.

27.meaning: A verb meaning 'you (plural) entered' or 'you went in.' The core sense is entering or going into something; idiomatically the root can imply intimacy or consummation when paired with a person.
27.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb. The ending -tum marks the subject as 'you' for a group of males or a mixed group, indicating a completed action they performed. The suffix both names the doer and signals that the event is finished.

28.meaning: A small phrase meaning 'with them' or 'in/at them,' referring to a group of females. It combines the preposition bi- (with, in, by) and an attached 'them' for a feminine group.
28.grammar: A preposition plus an attached pronoun. Bi- links to what follows and adds senses such as 'with,' 'in,' 'by means of,' or attachment to a verb. The pronoun -hinna means 'them' for a group of females; its -i- form (hinna rather than hunna) is the regular shape taken after the vowel of bi-.
28.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun)

29.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'fa-' ('then', 'so', 'but') drawing a consequence, joined to the conditional particle 'in' ('if'). Together: 'then if …', 'but if …'.
29.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that signals a result or transition ('then/so'). 'in' is the conditional particle 'if', introducing a supposed condition. Both are indeclinable particles with no case ending.

30.meaning: The particle 'lam', a negating word used to push a verb into the past: it means 'did not' / 'has not'. Though it sits before a present-tense verb form, it negates the action as something that did not happen.
30.grammar: 'lam' is a negating particle that governs a following present-tense verb but gives it past meaning ('did not …'). It also puts that verb into the shortened (jussive) form. 'lam' itself carries no ending.

31.meaning: You (plural) are / you happen to be. A form of the 'hollow' verb kāna ('to be'), which links a subject to a state or description, or expresses simply being or existing.
31.grammar: Present/imperfect verb, 2nd person masculine plural ('you all'). The ta- prefix marks 2nd person; the -ū ending marks masculine plural. The dropping of the usual final -na (so takūnū rather than takūnūna) shows the verb is in the subjunctive or jussive mood — the form expected after conditional or subordinating particles.
31.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

32.meaning: A verb meaning 'you (plural) entered' or 'you went in.' The core sense is entering or going into something; idiomatically the root can imply intimacy or consummation when paired with a person.
32.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb. The ending -tum marks the subject as 'you' for a group of males or a mixed group, indicating a completed action they performed. The suffix both names the doer and signals that the event is finished.

33.meaning: A small phrase meaning 'with them' or 'in/at them,' referring to a group of females. It combines the preposition bi- (with, in, by) and an attached 'them' for a feminine group.
33.grammar: A preposition plus an attached pronoun. Bi- links to what follows and adds senses such as 'with,' 'in,' 'by means of,' or attachment to a verb. The pronoun -hinna means 'them' for a group of females; its -i- form (hinna rather than hunna) is the regular shape taken after the vowel of bi-.

34.meaning: A two-part word: the connective particle 'fa-' meaning 'so', 'then', or 'therefore' (drawing a consequence from what precedes), joined to 'lā', the particle of negation/prohibition. Together they convey 'so do not …' or 'so there is no …'.
34.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that links a clause to what came before and often signals a result or consequence. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a present-tense verb it commonly forms a prohibition ('do not …') or a simple negation ('not'). It carries no ending of its own.

35.meaning: Blame, sin, or fault — moral liability incurred by a wrong action; the sense of wrongdoing that counts against a person, or any leaning toward error.
35.grammar: A masculine noun. The final -a is the accusative case ending; this ending appears, among other uses, on the noun governed by a negating particle (as in the common construction 'there is no blame …').
35.root: ج-ن-ح (j-n-ḥ) — to incline, lean, tilt (toward wrong); hence fault/sin

36.meaning: A small phrase meaning 'upon you' or 'on you' (a group). It combines the preposition ʿalā (on, upon, against) with an attached 'you.' It often conveys an obligation or burden resting on someone.
36.grammar: A preposition plus an attached pronoun. ʿAlā shifts to the form ʿalay- when a pronoun is attached. The suffix -kum means 'you' for a group of males or a mixed group. The phrase commonly signals something incumbent on, or directed at, the people referred to.

37.meaning: A word meaning 'and the lawful wives (of…)' — literally 'and the women made lawful (in marriage).' The base noun is the plural of a term for a wedded woman who is permitted to her husband, prefixed with 'and.'
37.grammar: The prefix wa- means 'and,' joining this to what precedes. The noun is a 'broken' plural and carries the nominative case-vowel -u, the ending typically used when a word is the subject or topic. The term itself denotes women who are lawfully married (and so forbidden to others).

38.meaning: A word meaning 'your sons' (and by extension male descendants), joined to a 'your' (plural, masculine) possessor. The base is the plural of 'son.'
38.grammar: A plural noun ('broken' plural of ibn, 'son') ending in hamza, which is part of the noun itself. It carries the genitive case-vowel -i, the ending a possessed noun takes before an attached possessor (the iḍāfa construction). The suffix -kum means 'your' for a group of males or a mixed group; it lengthens to -kumu when a vowel follows.
38.root: ب-ن-و / ب-ن-ي (b-n-w / b-n-y) — son, offspring, building up

39.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
39.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

40.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
40.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

41.meaning: A word meaning 'your loins' or 'your backbones,' joined to a 'your' (plural, masculine) possessor. The base noun is the plural of the lower back / spine, used to denote one's own lineage and natural offspring.
41.grammar: A plural noun ('broken' plural of ṣulb, 'backbone/loin') carrying the genitive case-vowel -i, the ending used before an attached possessor or after a preposition. The suffix -kum means 'your' for a group of males or a mixed group.

42.meaning: A two-part connector: 'and that.' The 'wa' joins what precedes, and 'an' is the subordinating particle 'that,' which introduces a following verb-clause (often steering it into the subjunctive) — used to report or quote a command, statement, or purpose.
42.grammar: The conjunction wa- ('and') plus the particle an, a subordinator meaning 'that' which heads a clause and commonly puts a following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood (often expressing purpose, intention, or reported speech). It is a particle and does not itself take a case ending.

43.meaning: A verb meaning 'you (plural) join together' or 'you combine/gather.' The core sense is bringing two or more things together into one whole.
43.grammar: A present/future-tense verb. The ta- prefix marks a 'you' subject, and the -ū ending makes that subject plural masculine, so together they mean 'you all.' This verb form, with its final long -ū written with a silent alif, is the shape used in non-past tense after certain particles (e.g., when negated or in a 'that…' clause).

44.meaning: Between; in the midst of two things. An adverb of place marking the space separating or lying among parties or points.
44.grammar: An adverb of place ('between'). It always ends in -a and grammatically governs what follows it, putting the following noun(s) into the genitive 'of' relationship. It does not change to show 'the' or a case of its own; the fixed -a is simply how this word is formed.
44.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction, what lies between

45.meaning: A word meaning 'the two sisters' — the dual (exactly two) of 'sister,' with the definite article 'the.'
45.grammar: A dual noun: the ending -ayni specifically means 'two' of the thing and is the form used in the object position or after a preposition (as opposed to -āni for the subject position). The prefix al- ('the') makes it definite. So the word denotes a specific pair of sisters.

46.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
46.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

47.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
47.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

48.meaning: A short particle placed before a verb to emphasize or affirm it. Before a past-tense verb it means 'indeed / certainly / has already (happened)'; before a present-tense verb it can mean 'sometimes / may'. It sharpens and confirms the verb that follows.
48.grammar: An indeclinable particle (its form never changes). It does not take case or tense endings; its job is to color the following verb — affirming and intensifying a past action ('has indeed done') or signaling occasional possibility with a present verb.

49.meaning: It passed, went before, or is now bygone — belonging to the past and already gone by. The root denotes what precedes or is sent ahead in time.
49.grammar: A past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('it passed / went before'); the final -a marks a completed action. The same root also yields a noun meaning 'predecessors / those who went before.'
49.root: س-ل-ف (s-l-f) — to precede, go before, be past

50.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
50.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

51.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
51.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

52.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

52.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

53.meaning: A word meaning 'much-forgiving' or 'ever-forgiving' — an intensive form describing one whose forgiveness is abundant and constant. It is one of the qualities of Allah.
53.grammar: An intensive adjective on the pattern faʿūl, conveying that the quality is great in degree and repeated. The ending -an is the accusative case with tanwīn (the indefinite 'n' sound), written with a supporting alif; it is the form an indefinite word takes when it is, for example, a predicate of certain verbs/particles or otherwise placed in the object position.

54.meaning: 'Most Merciful / deeply compassionate' — an intensive form of raḥima, denoting one full of mercy and tender compassion; a frequent description of Allah.
54.grammar: An intensive adjective on the fa'īl pattern, expressing a deep, abiding quality — abounding in mercy. The -an ending is the accusative case with indefinite (tanwīn) 'n,' often marking it as a predicate or as describing someone as 'most merciful.'

1.meaning: A word meaning 'and the chaste/married women' — those who are protected or fortified, hence wedded women (or, in other contexts, free or chaste women). It is prefixed with 'and' and 'the.'
1.grammar: The prefix wa- means 'and'; al- means 'the.' The noun is a sound feminine plural (the -āt ending marks a plural of females) built from a passive participle ('ones who have been made secure/protected'). It carries the nominative case-vowel -u, the ending typically used for a subject or topic. The doubled w of wa- here reflects assimilation with a preceding word.

2.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
2.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

3.meaning: 'The women' — the plural used for women/females collectively. (It serves as the plural of mar'a, 'woman.')
3.grammar: A plural noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending is genitive: it marks the word as following a preposition or standing in a possessive ('of …') relationship. The l of al- assimilates into the following n in pronunciation (a 'sun letter').

4.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
4.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

5.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
5.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

6.meaning: It/she possessed, owned, or held in ownership — a completed act of having something under one's control or right.
6.grammar: A past-tense verb with the feminine ending -at: 'she/it possessed'. The -at marks completed action by a feminine singular subject. In the idiom 'what your right hands have possessed', the feminine subject is the (grammatically feminine) 'right hands'.
6.root: م-ل-ك (m-l-k) — to own, possess, hold sway

7.meaning: Your (plural) right hands — literally the right hands, used idiomatically for solemn oaths and for lawful possession or authority. With the suffix: 'your right hands'.
7.grammar: A plural noun carrying the nominative -u ending, which typically marks it as the subject (the doer) of a verb. The suffix -kum is the attached possessive pronoun 'your' (plural masculine). The plural can mean 'right hands' or 'oaths', and the phrase 'what your right hands possess' is an idiom for those under one's lawful charge.
7.root: ي-م-ن (y-m-n) — right hand/side; oath; good fortune

8.meaning: A word meaning 'a decree' or 'a prescription' — literally 'a writing.' It denotes something written down and so binding, an ordinance or prescribed duty.
8.grammar: A noun on the pattern fiʿāl carrying the accusative case-vowel -a. The accusative is the ending used for the object of a verb and also for an emphatic verbal noun placed as a kind of stamp on a statement (e.g., '… as an ordained prescription'). Without the article and without tanwīn here, it stands in a possessive ('… of') link with a following word.

9.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
9.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

10.meaning: 'Upon you (all)' — the preposition 'upon/on/over' joined to the plural 'you,' indicating something resting on or directed at a group.
10.grammar: The preposition 'ʿalā' ('upon/on/over') in its joined form 'ʿalay-' plus the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you all,' masculine plural). It marks the group as the recipients or target of whatever is laid 'upon' them.

11.meaning: A phrase meaning 'and it has been made lawful' or 'and it is permitted.' It joins 'and' to a passive verb declaring something allowed.
11.grammar: The prefix wa- means 'and.' The verb is in the passive past tense ('was/has been made lawful'), recognizable from the u-…-i- vowel pattern (uḥilla). The final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject — 'he/it' — for a completed action, here an impersonal 'it is permitted.'

12.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
12.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

13.meaning: A short, highly versatile particle 'mā.' It can mean 'what' or 'that which,' can negate ('not'), and can serve as an intensifier attached to another word. Its precise force depends on what it accompanies, but its core is to point to a thing or to add emphasis.
13.grammar: A multifunctional particle. It does not take case endings. Depending on usage it can be a relative ('that which'), an interrogative ('what?'), a negator ('not'), or — when joined to another particle — an emphasizer. It is uninflected and indeclinable.

14.meaning: Behind / beyond — an adverb of place meaning what lies behind or past something; it can also denote what is beyond or in addition to a thing.
14.grammar: An adverb of place (functioning like a preposition). The '-a' ending is the accusative, the standard form for such place-words; it links to a following noun to mean 'behind ___ / beyond ___'.
14.root: و-ر-ي (w-r-y) — that which is behind or hidden from view

15.meaning: A demonstrative meaning 'that' addressed to a group of people (plural 'you'). It points to something at a distance — whether physical, or to a previously mentioned matter — and is directed at multiple listeners.
15.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun for something distant. The base 'dhā' carries the sense 'that', the 'li' is an element of distance, and the ending '-kum' tells you the speaker is addressing a plural 'you' — it specifies the audience, not the thing pointed at. It does not change for case.

16.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
16.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'
16.root: — (particle; no root)

17.meaning: To seek after, strive for, or desire something; to pursue a goal or aim. It carries the sense of actively wanting and going after what one hopes to gain.

parts.en: seek / pursue (Form VIII stem with plural wāw)
silent spelling alif (alif al-fāriqa), written after a plural verb wāw; not pronounced

17.grammar: A present/future tense verb, Form VIII (the -t- infix). The ta- prefix together with the plural wāw (-ū) means 'you (plural masculine) seek'. The final alif is a purely orthographic 'separating alif' that is conventionally written after the wāw of plural verbs and is entirely silent — the plural sense is carried by the wāw alone, not by this alif. The dropped final nūn (tabtaghū rather than tabtaghūna) indicates a subjunctive or jussive mood, typical after particles meaning 'that', 'so that', or in negative/conditional constructions.
17.root: ب-غ-ي (b-gh-y) — to seek, desire, or strive after

18.meaning: A phrase meaning 'with your wealth/property.' It combines 'with/by means of,' the plural noun for goods and possessions, and a 'your' (plural) possessor.
18.grammar: The preposition bi- ('with, by means of') governs the noun, which therefore takes the genitive case-vowel -i (the ending always required after a preposition). The noun is a 'broken' plural of māl ('wealth'). The suffix -kum means 'your' for a group of males or a mixed group.

19.meaning: A word meaning 'men seeking to be chaste,' i.e., taking women in honourable marriage and guarding their chastity (literally 'ones fortifying/protecting'). It describes men acting within lawful, modest bounds.

parts.en: one seeking chastity / guarding (himself or another)

19.grammar: An active participle (one who does the action of 'fortifying / keeping chaste') in the sound masculine plural. The ending -īna marks 'more than two' males and is the form used in the object position or after a preposition (as opposed to -ūna for the subject position). Participles like this describe a state or ongoing manner of acting.
19.root: ح-ص-ن (ḥ-ṣ-n) — being fortified, protected, chaste

20.meaning: 'Other than / different from / not'. A noun used to express difference or negation — 'something other than X', and so 'not-X'. It functions to exclude or contrast with what follows.
20.grammar: A noun of difference/exception. The -a ending marks the accusative case, the form it takes when it serves as a direct object or as a descriptive substitute standing in an object position; it governs a following noun in the genitive ('other than …'). That it takes case endings and tanwīn confirms it is a true noun, not a particle.
20.root: غ-ي-ر (gh-y-r) — to be other, different; otherness, change

21.meaning: A word meaning 'fornicators' or 'men pouring out (their desire) unlawfully' — those engaging in illicit, promiscuous relations. The root image is of pouring or spilling forth.
21.grammar: An active participle (one who does the action) in the sound masculine plural. The ending -īna marks 'more than two' males and is the form used in the object position or after a preposition (as opposed to subject-form -ūna). The participle pattern here (mu-…-i-) belongs to a verb form that often implies a mutual or repeated act.
21.root: س-ف-ح (s-f-ḥ) — pouring out, spilling (fig. illicit relations)

22.meaning: A two-part expression: 'so/then' joined to a negating word 'not.' The first piece links to what precedes (drawing a result or sequence), and the second negates the statement that follows. Together roughly: 'so… not / and so it did not…'
22.grammar: A connective particle fa- ('so, then,' showing result or sequence) plus the negating particle mā. When mā precedes a past-tense verb, it denies that the action happened ('did not…').

23.meaning: A verb meaning 'you (plural) sought enjoyment / took benefit.' The core sense is deriving pleasure or profit from something; the form adds the idea of seeking or asking for that benefit.
23.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in the 'seeking' pattern (the ist- prefix that often means to seek or ask for the action). The ending -tum marks the subject as 'you' for a group of males or a mixed group and signals a completed action.

24.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
24.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

25.meaning: A small phrase meaning 'from them' or 'of them,' referring to a group of females. It combines the preposition min (from, of, some of) with an attached 'them' (feminine).
25.grammar: A preposition plus an attached pronoun. Min means 'from,' 'out of,' or 'some of.' The pronoun -hunna means 'them' for a group of females; after the n of min it keeps its base vowel -u (hunna). The combination commonly expresses source, origin, or a part taken from a whole.

26.meaning: A phrase meaning 'so give them' — a command to hand over or render something to a group of females. It combines 'so/then,' the command 'give,' and 'them.'
26.grammar: The prefix fa- means 'so' or 'then,' linking this as a result or sequel. The verb is a command (imperative) addressed to a group of males/mixed group — the long -ū is the plural 'you all' ending of the order. The attached -hunna ('them,' feminine) is the recipient. 'Give' here means to hand over or pay what is due.
26.root: ا-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — coming; (form used here) bringing / giving

27.meaning: A word meaning 'their wages / dues / rewards,' referring to a group of females. The base noun is the plural of 'wage, recompense, due reward,' joined to a 'their' (feminine) possessor.
27.grammar: A 'broken' plural noun (of ajr, 'wage/reward') carrying the accusative case-vowel -a, the ending used for the object of a verb. The suffix -hunna means 'their' for a group of females. The word denotes compensation or a rightful due owed in return for something.

28.meaning: A noun meaning 'an ordained obligation, a fixed and binding portion,' and specifically a stipulated bridal gift (dower) that is set and due as a duty.
28.grammar: A singular feminine noun. The -an ending is the accusative indefinite (tanwīn): it commonly marks the noun as a direct object of a verb, or expresses 'as a(n) …' / a specified amount, and lacks the definite article ('the').
28.root: ف-ر-ض (f-r-ḍ) — to appoint, ordain, make obligatory, fix a portion

29.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
29.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

30.meaning: Blame, sin, or fault — moral liability incurred by a wrong action; the sense of wrongdoing that counts against a person, or any leaning toward error.
30.grammar: A masculine noun. The final -a is the accusative case ending; this ending appears, among other uses, on the noun governed by a negating particle (as in the common construction 'there is no blame …').
30.root: ج-ن-ح (j-n-ḥ) — to incline, lean, tilt (toward wrong); hence fault/sin

31.meaning: 'Upon you (all)' — the preposition 'upon/on/over' joined to the plural 'you,' indicating something resting on or directed at a group.
31.grammar: The preposition 'ʿalā' ('upon/on/over') in its joined form 'ʿalay-' plus the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you all,' masculine plural). It marks the group as the recipients or target of whatever is laid 'upon' them.
31.root: — (preposition; no triliteral root)

32.meaning: A compound particle joining the preposition 'in/about' with the relative pronoun 'what', yielding 'in that which' or 'concerning what' — pointing to the matter or subject about which something is said or done.
32.grammar: A fixed combination of the preposition 'fī' and the indeclinable relative 'mā'. Being particles, neither takes a case ending; the phrase functions as 'in/about what…'.

33.meaning: A verb meaning 'you (plural) mutually agreed / were pleased with one another.' The core sense is reaching mutual consent and contentment between parties.
33.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in the reciprocal pattern (the ta-…-ā- shape that means doing something to or with one another). The ending -tum marks the subject as 'you' for a group of males or a mixed group and signals a completed action. The reciprocal sense makes it 'agreed mutually / each pleased the other.'
33.root: ر-ض-و / ر-ض-ي (r-ḍ-w / r-ḍ-y) — being pleased, content, consenting

34.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
34.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

35.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
35.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

36.meaning: A noun/adverb meaning 'after' — the time or position following something; 'afterward', 'following'.
36.grammar: An adverb of time functioning as a noun, here in the genitive case marked by the final -i. The genitive ending typically appears after a preposition or as the second term of a construct ('after THE …'), linking 'after' to a following noun to specify what it comes after.
36.root: ب-ع-د (b-ʿ-d) — to be after, to follow, distance in place or time

37.meaning: A word meaning 'the obligation' or 'the fixed/prescribed portion' — a duty or share that has been clearly appointed and made binding. With the definite article 'the.'
37.grammar: A noun on the pattern faʿīla (here with a passive sense, 'that which is made obligatory'), prefixed with al- ('the'). It carries the genitive case-vowel -i, the ending used after a preposition or in a possessive ('… of') link. The word denotes something appointed as a firm, set duty or allotted share.

38.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
38.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

39.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
39.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

40.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

40.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

41.meaning: All-Knowing; one possessing complete, perfect knowledge. As an intensive form it conveys knowledge that is total and unfailing, encompassing all things.
41.grammar: An intensive adjective ('all-knowing') on the faʿīl pattern, which stresses the quality to its fullest degree. The -an (tanwīn) joins the -a accusative ending — typical of a predicate or object — with the -n marking it indefinite.

42.meaning: All-Wise; one possessing perfect wisdom, who places everything in its right place and decides with flawless judgement. As an intensive form it conveys wisdom that is complete and sound.
42.grammar: An intensive adjective ('all-wise') on the faʿīl pattern, stressing the quality to its fullest degree. The -an (tanwīn) combines the -a accusative ending — typical of a predicate or object — with the -n marking it indefinite.

1.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
1.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

2.meaning: The particle 'lam', a negating word used to push a verb into the past: it means 'did not' / 'has not'. Though it sits before a present-tense verb form, it negates the action as something that did not happen.
2.grammar: 'lam' is a negating particle that governs a following present-tense verb but gives it past meaning ('did not …'). It also puts that verb into the shortened (jussive) form. 'lam' itself carries no ending.

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'he is (not) able' or 'he can(not)' — the core sense is having the power, capacity, or means to do something. The 'seeking' form softens it to 'manage to' or 'be capable of.'
3.grammar: A present/future-tense verb. The ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it'). The clipped ending (a bare -iʿ with no final vowel, the 'jussive' form) is the shortened shape the verb takes after certain particles such as 'not' (lam) or in conditional 'if' clauses; it typically signals negation of a completed possibility or a conditional. The ist- pattern conveys seeking or being able to do the action.
3.root: ط-و-ع (ṭ-w-ʿ) — obeying, being capable, having power to do

4.meaning: A combination meaning 'from among you' or 'of you' — singling out a part or some individuals out of a larger group being addressed.
4.grammar: The preposition min ('from, among, some of') with the attached pronoun -kum, which means 'you' for a group of two or more (grammatically masculine plural). Because the pronoun follows a preposition, it is in the object form; the whole expression partitions or draws out individuals from the addressed group.
4.root: — (min is a particle/preposition; -kum is a pronoun)

5.meaning: Means-and-capacity: ampleness, abundance, the wherewithal to do something. Most often refers to the financial means or affluence by which a person can afford a course of action.
5.grammar: A masculine singular noun. The -an ending marks the accusative case (and adds tanwīn, the 'n' sound that signals indefinite 'a/some'); the accusative typically marks a word as the direct object of a verb or as what a verb's action falls upon.
5.root: ط-و-ل (ṭ-w-l) — length, extent; by extension abundance, reach, capacity

6.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
6.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'
6.root: — (particle; no root)

7.meaning: To marry, to take in lawful wedlock; the act of contracting marriage with a woman.

parts.en: he / it (3rd-person masculine prefix, with assimilated gemination)

7.grammar: A present-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular ('he marries'). The ya- prefix signals 'he/it' as the doer; it carries a shadda (doubling) because a preceding particle's final consonant has assimilated into the yā'. The final -a (instead of -u) is the subjunctive mood, which appears after certain particles meaning 'to/that/so that' and gives the sense of an intended, hoped-for, or hypothetical action rather than a plain statement of fact.

8.meaning: Women who are protected and guarded — chaste, honourably married or kept free from unlawful relations. The term carries the sense of being fortified within a fortress of virtue or wedlock.

parts.en: feminine plural ending in the genitive/accusative (-āt → -i)

8.grammar: A feminine plural passive participle ('women who have been guarded/made chaste') with the definite article 'the'. The sound feminine plural ending -āt takes -i here rather than -u, which marks it as genitive or accusative — i.e. linked to a preceding preposition, or standing as the object of an action, rather than as the subject doing something.
8.root: ح-ص-ن (ḥ-ṣ-n) — to fortify, guard, make inaccessible; a fortress

9.meaning: Believing women — females who have faith, who trust and affirm Allah and His message and live in security of belief.

parts.en: feminine plural ending in the genitive/accusative (-āt → -i)

9.grammar: A feminine plural active participle ('women who believe') with 'the'. The sound feminine plural ending -āt takes -i rather than -u, marking the genitive or accusative — i.e. tied to a preceding preposition or noun, or serving as the object of an action, not as the active subject.
9.root: أ-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — safety, security; faith, to believe and trust

10.meaning: A connector meaning 'then/so... from (among)'. It joins a result or consequence ('then') to a partitive sense ('from, out of, some of').
10.grammar: Two particles joined. The prefix fa- links what follows to what came before, signalling sequence or result ('then, so, and then'). 'min' is a preposition meaning 'from, out of, among'; words it governs take the genitive case. Particles like these do not themselves change form.

11.meaning: A short, highly versatile particle 'mā.' It can mean 'what' or 'that which,' can negate ('not'), and can serve as an intensifier attached to another word. Its precise force depends on what it accompanies, but its core is to point to a thing or to add emphasis.
11.grammar: A multifunctional particle. It does not take case endings. Depending on usage it can be a relative ('that which'), an interrogative ('what?'), a negator ('not'), or — when joined to another particle — an emphasizer. It is uninflected and indeclinable.

12.meaning: It/she possessed, owned, or held in ownership — a completed act of having something under one's control or right.
12.grammar: A past-tense verb with the feminine ending -at: 'she/it possessed'. The -at marks completed action by a feminine singular subject. In the idiom 'what your right hands have possessed', the feminine subject is the (grammatically feminine) 'right hands'.
12.root: م-ل-ك (m-l-k) — to own, possess, hold sway

13.meaning: Your (plural) right hands — literally the right hands, used idiomatically for solemn oaths and for lawful possession or authority. With the suffix: 'your right hands'.
13.grammar: A plural noun carrying the nominative -u ending, which typically marks it as the subject (the doer) of a verb. The suffix -kum is the attached possessive pronoun 'your' (plural masculine). The plural can mean 'right hands' or 'oaths', and the phrase 'what your right hands possess' is an idiom for those under one's lawful charge.
13.root: ي-م-ن (y-m-n) — right hand/side; oath; good fortune

14.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
14.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

15.meaning: Young women in one's charge — specifically maidservants or bondwomen ('your slave-girls'); the feminine of a word for youths/young people.
15.grammar: A feminine plural noun with an attached possessive 'your' (addressed to a group of males). The plural ending -āt shows -i (genitive), which here arises because the noun is owned by the following pronoun — the genitive is the regular case for the first noun in a possessive 'X of Y' pairing. The pronoun -kum gains an extra -u (-kumu) simply to ease pronunciation before the next word.
15.root: ف-ت-ي (f-t-y) — youth, young person; vigour of youth

16.meaning: Believing women — females who have faith, who trust and affirm Allah and His message and live in security of belief.

parts.en: feminine plural ending in the genitive/accusative (-āt → -i)

16.grammar: A feminine plural active participle ('women who believe') with 'the'. The sound feminine plural ending -āt takes -i rather than -u, marking the genitive or accusative — i.e. tied to a preceding preposition or noun, or serving as the object of an action, not as the active subject.
16.root: أ-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — safety, security; faith, to believe and trust

17.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
17.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
17.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

18.meaning: 'I know' — a present-tense verb of knowing: to have certain knowledge or awareness of something.
18.grammar: A present/future (Form I) verb, first-person singular ('I'), marked by the prefix a-. This a- is the first-person agreement marker built into the conjugation, not a free-standing pronoun. The final -u marks the indicative — a plain statement of ongoing or habitual knowing.

19.meaning: 'By/through your faith' — the prepositional phrase ties the means or measure of something to faith, the inner conviction and trust in Allah.
19.grammar: Preposition bi- ('with, by, through') + the noun 'faith' + 'your' (group of males). The preposition forces the genitive case, shown by the -i on 'īmāni'. The phrase expresses the means, instrument, or basis — 'by means of / in respect of your faith'.
19.root: أ-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — safety, security; faith, to believe and trust

20.meaning: A phrase meaning 'some of you' or 'one part of you'. It singles out a portion of an addressed group, often paired with 'to/for another' to express a reciprocal relationship within that group.
20.grammar: A noun meaning 'a part/some' carrying the -u ending, which typically marks the word as the subject or doer in its clause. The attached -kum means 'of you all' (plural), so the whole means 'some part of you'.

21.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
21.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

22.meaning: 'Some (others)' / 'a part' — the same noun for 'a portion or some,' here left indefinite, often functioning as the counterpart in the 'one another' construction.
22.grammar: A noun 'part/some' in the genitive case with indefinite marking (the -in ending, called tanwīn). The genitive typically follows a preposition or links it to a preceding noun ('… of …'); the doubled -n sound marks it as indefinite ('a part / some').
22.root: ب-ع-ض (b-ʿ-ḍ) — a part, portion, or some of a whole

23.meaning: 'So marry them' — a command to a group to take certain women in lawful marriage.

parts.en: marry! (command to a group of males)

23.grammar: Prefix fa- ('so, then') + an imperative (command) verb addressed to a group of males + the object 'them (women)'. The -ū ending on the verb marks the masculine-plural command ('you all, do this!'). The suffix -hunna means 'them' for a group of females and serves as the direct object of the marrying.

24.meaning: 'By the leave of / with the permission of' — formed from 'with/by' plus 'permission, leave, sanction'. It conveys that something happens by someone's authorization or enabling will.
24.grammar: The prefix bi- is a preposition 'with/by'. The noun 'idhn' means 'permission, leave, sanction'. After the preposition it takes the genitive -i ending, the form used following a preposition and typically linking on to a following noun ('the permission OF …').
24.root: أ-ذ-ن (ʾ-dh-n) — to permit, give leave; also listening/ear

25.meaning: 'Their family / their people' — the household, kinsfolk, or folk to whom a group of females belongs.
25.grammar: The noun 'family/people' with an attached possessive 'their' (a group of females). The -i ending on 'ahli' is genitive — caused here by the following possessor pronoun, since the owned noun in an 'X of Y' pairing regularly takes the genitive. The suffix -hinna means 'of them (females)'.
25.root: أ-ه-ل (ʾ-h-l) — family, kinsfolk, the people belonging to a place or person

26.meaning: 'And give them' — a command to a group to hand over or grant something to certain females.

parts.en: give! / grant! (command to a group of males)

26.grammar: Connector wa ('and') + an imperative verb 'give!' addressed to a group of males + the object 'them (females)'. The -ū ending marks the masculine-plural command. The suffix -hunna ('them', females) is the recipient/object. This verb comes from a form meaning 'to bring/give to', so the action is one of granting or handing over.
26.root: أ-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; in this form, to bring, to give, to grant

27.meaning: A word meaning 'their wages / dues / rewards,' referring to a group of females. The base noun is the plural of 'wage, recompense, due reward,' joined to a 'their' (feminine) possessor.
27.grammar: A 'broken' plural noun (of ajr, 'wage/reward') carrying the accusative case-vowel -a, the ending used for the object of a verb. The suffix -hunna means 'their' for a group of females. The word denotes compensation or a rightful due owed in return for something.

28.meaning: 'In a fitting / honourable / customary way' — bi- ('with/in') joined to al-ma'rūf, literally 'that which is known and recognised', i.e. what is right, decent, and approved by sound custom and morality.

parts.en: what is right / recognised as good

28.grammar: The bi- prefix is a preposition 'with / in'. The l- is 'the'. The stem is a passive participle meaning 'that which is known/recognised (as good)'. The final -i is the genitive case, the form taken after a preposition like bi-.
28.root: ع-ر-ف (ʿ-r-f) — to know, recognise; hence what is recognised as good

29.meaning: Chaste, guarded women — females kept honourably within virtue or wedlock; indefinite, 'some women who are chaste'.
29.grammar: A feminine plural passive participle ('women who are guarded/made chaste'), indefinite (no 'the'). The ending shows -in: the sound feminine plural takes -i for genitive/accusative, and the extra -n (tanwīn) signals indefiniteness ('some/any'). So it marks an indefinite noun in the genitive or accusative — linked to a preposition or standing as object/description, not as an active subject.
29.root: ح-ص-ن (ḥ-ṣ-n) — to fortify, guard, make inaccessible; a fortress

30.meaning: 'Other than / different from / not'. A noun used to express difference or negation — 'something other than X', and so 'not-X'. It functions to exclude or contrast with what follows.
30.grammar: A noun of difference/exception. The -a ending marks the accusative case, the form it takes when it serves as a direct object or as a descriptive substitute standing in an object position; it governs a following noun in the genitive ('other than …'). That it takes case endings and tanwīn confirms it is a true noun, not a particle.
30.root: غ-ي-ر (gh-y-r) — to be other, different; otherness, change

31.meaning: Women given to open fornication — those who commit unlawful sexual relations flagrantly. The root image is of 'pouring out', i.e. squandering oneself in promiscuity.

parts.en: openly fornicating women (active participle, feminine plural)

31.grammar: A feminine plural active participle ('women who fornicate openly'), indefinite. The ending -in combines the genitive/accusative marker -i of the sound feminine plural with tanwīn -n for indefiniteness. So it marks an indefinite noun in the genitive or accusative — typically the object of an action, a description, or governed by a preposition.
31.root: س-ف-ح (s-f-ḥ) — to pour out, spill; figuratively, illicit sexual outpouring, fornication

32.meaning: 'And not' — a connector 'and' joined to the negative particle 'not,' negating a following statement.
32.grammar: Two particles: the joining 'and' (wa) plus the negator lā ('not'). Lā commonly negates a present-tense verb or a noun. Neither particle takes case endings.

33.meaning: Women who take or adopt (something) for themselves — those who acquire or take on a thing as their own.

parts.en: women who take/adopt for themselves (active participle, feminine plural)
feminine plural ending in the genitive/accusative (-āt → -i)

33.grammar: A feminine plural active participle of a reflexive form meaning 'to take for oneself, adopt'. The sound feminine plural ending takes -i (genitive or accusative) rather than -u, marking it as linked to a following noun, governed by a preposition, or standing as the object of an action — not as the active subject.
33.root: أ-خ-ذ (ʾ-kh-dh) — to take, seize, grasp; this form, to take for oneself

34.meaning: Secret lovers, intimate companions taken in concealment — a partner in a hidden, illicit liaison; plural of a word for a clandestine paramour.

parts.en: secret lovers / hidden paramours (broken plural, indefinite genitive)

34.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural noun, indefinite. Its final diacritic -in is the genitive case plus tanwīn (the -n that marks 'some/any'), so it marks an indefinite noun in the genitive — usually because it follows a preposition or is the object owned/taken in an 'X of Y' relationship.
34.root: خ-د-ن (kh-d-n) — companionship, intimate association; a confidant or secret lover

35.meaning: A connecting phrase meaning 'then when / and when', introducing a circumstance whose occurrence triggers a following response. 'Fa-' links it to what precedes; 'idhā' sets up a 'when … (then) …' condition for something expected to happen.
35.grammar: A particle cluster, not a noun or verb, so it has no case ending. 'Idhā' is a conditional/temporal particle ('when') used for events regarded as bound to occur, and it normally introduces a clause followed by a main response. The prefixed fa- ('then/so') ties the whole condition to the preceding statement.

36.meaning: 'They (women) have been guarded / brought into the protection of marriage' — made chaste, taken into wedlock. The passive sense is that the protection is conferred upon them.

parts.en: were guarded / made chaste (past-tense passive stem)

36.grammar: A past-tense passive verb, 3rd-person feminine plural. The opening u- vowel marks the passive ('were made/done to' rather than 'did'). The ending -na attached to a past-tense verb means 'they (females)' as the subject. So: 'they (women) were guarded / brought into chaste protection'.
36.root: ح-ص-ن (ḥ-ṣ-n) — to fortify, guard, make inaccessible; a fortress

37.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'fa-' ('then', 'so', 'but') drawing a consequence, joined to the conditional particle 'in' ('if'). Together: 'then if …', 'but if …'.
37.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that signals a result or transition ('then/so'). 'in' is the conditional particle 'if', introducing a supposed condition. Both are indeclinable particles with no case ending.

38.meaning: 'They (women) committed / brought about' — they did or perpetrated an act; literally 'they came with / brought' a deed, used for committing something.

parts.en: committed / brought about / came with (past-tense stem)

38.grammar: A past-tense verb, 3rd-person feminine plural. The ending -na on a past-tense verb marks the subject as 'they (females)'. The verb's root sense is 'to come', but with an object it means to bring about or commit a deed — hence 'they (women) committed/perpetrated'.
38.root: أ-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; with an object, to bring or commit (a deed)

39.meaning: A noun preceded by 'with,' built on the word for a gross indecency — an outrageous, shameful, morally excessive act; sexual immorality or any flagrant transgression.
39.grammar: A noun governed by the preposition bi- ('with/by'). The tāʾ marbūṭa (-at) marks it as a feminine singular noun denoting the act itself. The final -in (tanwīn kasra) is the indefinite genitive ending ('a …'), the case regularly required after a preposition.

40.meaning: 'Then upon them (is)' — a connector introducing what is laid as a duty or penalty resting upon a group of females ('then against/upon them').
40.grammar: Prefix fa- ('then, so', marking a result) + the preposition 'upon/against' + 'them (females)'. The preposition 'ʿalā' appears as 'ʿalay-' before a pronoun. Combined with a following obligation, 'upon them' conveys what is due from or charged against them — duty, liability, or penalty.

41.meaning: A half; one of two equal portions of a whole.
41.grammar: A singular noun. The final -u is the nominative case-ending, which typically marks the word as the subject of a sentence or as a predicate ('… is a half'). The absence of a final -n (no tanwīn) shows it is grammatically definite, often because it is linked to a following noun ('the half of …').

42.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
42.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

43.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
43.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
43.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

44.meaning: Women who are protected and guarded — chaste, honourably married or kept free from unlawful relations. The term carries the sense of being fortified within a fortress of virtue or wedlock.

parts.en: feminine plural ending in the genitive/accusative (-āt → -i)

44.grammar: A feminine plural passive participle ('women who have been guarded/made chaste') with the definite article 'the'. The sound feminine plural ending -āt takes -i here rather than -u, which marks it as genitive or accusative — i.e. linked to a preceding preposition, or standing as the object of an action, rather than as the subject doing something.
44.root: ح-ص-ن (ḥ-ṣ-n) — to fortify, guard, make inaccessible; a fortress

45.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
45.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

46.meaning: The punishment, torment, or chastisement — severe penalty or suffering inflicted as retribution.
46.grammar: A singular masculine noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending is the genitive, which typically links it to a preceding noun ('… of the punishment') or follows a preposition.

47.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
47.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

48.meaning: 'for whoever / to the one who' — the preposition 'for/to' joined with the relative word 'who', introducing the person(s) about whom something is said.
48.grammar: A preposition ('for/to') combined with the relative/interrogative word 'man' ('who, whoever'). Together they single out a person or group as the focus ('for the one(s) who...').

49.meaning: 'He feared / was in awe' — felt a reverent dread or apprehension; a fear mingled with awe and wariness of a possible harm or of someone great.

parts.en: he feared / dreaded with awe (past-tense verb)

49.grammar: A past-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular ('he feared'). With no added subject ending, the bare form already means 'he' did the action. The middle -i- vowel pattern (khashiya) is typical of verbs describing inner states and emotions. The fear it names is reverent and wary, not mere fright.
49.root: خ-ش-ي (kh-sh-y) — to fear with reverence and awe; dread of something mighty

50.meaning: Hardship and distress, especially the strain or ruin that leads one into sin or moral collapse; the difficulty by which one may fall into wrongdoing.

parts.en: hardship / distress / falling into sin (noun, accusative)

50.grammar: A masculine noun with 'the'. Its final vowel -a marks the accusative case, which typically identifies the word as the direct object of a verb — the thing affected, feared, or undergone.
50.root: ع-ن-ت (ʿ-n-t) — hardship, distress; difficulty leading to sin or harm

51.meaning: A combination meaning 'from among you' or 'of you' — singling out a part or some individuals out of a larger group being addressed.
51.grammar: The preposition min ('from, among, some of') with the attached pronoun -kum, which means 'you' for a group of two or more (grammatically masculine plural). Because the pronoun follows a preposition, it is in the object form; the whole expression partitions or draws out individuals from the addressed group.
51.root: — (min is a particle/preposition; -kum is a pronoun)

52.meaning: A two-part connector: 'and that.' The 'wa' joins what precedes, and 'an' is the subordinating particle 'that,' which introduces a following verb-clause (often steering it into the subjunctive) — used to report or quote a command, statement, or purpose.
52.grammar: The conjunction wa- ('and') plus the particle an, a subordinator meaning 'that' which heads a clause and commonly puts a following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood (often expressing purpose, intention, or reported speech). It is a particle and does not itself take a case ending.

53.meaning: "You are patient / you endure steadfastly" — the act of a group exercising patience: self-restraint, perseverance, and steadfast endurance in the face of hardship.
53.grammar: A present/jussive verb. The ta-…-ū pattern marks a masculine plural addressee, 'you all'. The dropped final -na (taṣbirū rather than taṣbirūna) signals the jussive or subjunctive mood, typical after conditional particles ('if you are patient …').

54.meaning: 'Better / best; good' — an adjective of comparison meaning more good, preferable, or superior. It also serves broadly for 'goodness' and that which is good and beneficial.
54.grammar: A noun/adjective bearing the ending -un (nunation): the doubled-u 'n' sound marks the word as both indefinite ('a/an', no 'the') and nominative — the case used for the subject of a sentence or the predicate that describes it.
54.root: خ-ي-ر (kh-y-r) — good, goodness, that which is choice and beneficial

55.meaning: 'for you,' 'to you,' 'for your benefit' — the preposition 'for/to' joined to 'you (plural).' It marks the party for whose sake, benefit, or possession something exists or is given.
55.grammar: A preposition ('for/to') with the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you, plural'). It assigns a benefit, purpose, or recipient — 'for you (all).' The suffix '-kum' is the plural 'you,' showing the recipients are a group.

56.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
56.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
56.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

57.meaning: An intensive adjective/name meaning 'much-forgiving, ever-ready to forgive, one who veils and pardons faults again and again'. The form stresses abundance, so it conveys forgiveness as a constant, far-reaching quality.
57.grammar: An intensive adjective (the ghafūr 'doer-in-abundance' pattern), used as a divine attribute of Allah. The -un ending is nunation in the nominative case: it marks the word as indefinite and in the nominative, the case typically used for the subject or for a predicate that describes the subject.

58.meaning: Most Merciful / ever-compassionate — one whose mercy is deep, constant, and abundantly bestowed; an intensive form stressing enduring tenderness and care. The '-un' nunation marks it as indefinite nominative.
58.grammar: An intensive adjective (faʿīl pattern) conveying a lasting, abundant quality. The '-un' (nunation on the ḍamma) marks it as indefinite and in the nominative case, typically used for a subject or predicate ("is most merciful").

1.meaning: He/it wills, wants, intends, desires — to seek or aim at something purposefully.
1.grammar: A present-tense (form IV) verb, third-person masculine singular ('he wills/wants'). The ya- prefix marks 'he', and the final -u is the indicative ending, signalling an ongoing or habitual action ('does / is doing').
1.root: ر-و-د (r-w-d) — to seek, to want; (form IV) to will/intend

2.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
2.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence.
