So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.
2.root: — (proper divine name)

3.meaning: 'So that He may make clear / explain plainly' — to clarify, distinguish, and set forth distinctly so that nothing remains obscure.

parts.en: so that / in order to (purpose particle)

3.grammar: Purpose particle li- ('so that, in order that') + a present-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular ('He makes clear'). The doubled middle letter (bayyana) is an intensive/causative form: 'to make plain, clarify'. Because of the li- particle, the verb takes the subjunctive -a ending, giving the sense 'so that He may make clear' rather than a flat 'He makes clear'.
3.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinctness; to be clear, to make evident

4.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
4.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

5.meaning: 'And to guide you' — and that He may lead you on the right way, directing a group along the path of right guidance.

parts.en: guides / leads on the right way (present-tense stem)

5.grammar: Connector wa ('and') + a present-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular 'He guides', + the object 'you' (a group of males). The ya- prefix signals 'he'. The -a ending on the verb (-hdiya) is the subjunctive, carried over from a preceding 'so that' purpose; it gives the sense 'and that He may guide'. The suffix -kum is the one guided.
5.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — guidance, to lead rightly, to show the way

6.meaning: Well-trodden ways, customary paths, established practices; the recognised courses or precedents that others followed before. Plural of 'sunna' (a way or practice).

parts.en: ways / customary practices / precedents (broken plural, accusative)

6.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural noun. Its final vowel -a marks the accusative case, typically identifying the word as the direct object of a verb or as the first term in a possessive 'ways of …' construction. The singular 'sunna' denotes an established way or practice that becomes a pattern to follow.
6.root: س-ن-ن (s-n-n) — to set a course or pattern; a way, custom, or established practice

7.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
7.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

8.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
8.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

9.meaning: 'before you,' 'prior to you' — an expression of precedence in time or place, here relating that precedence to 'you (plural).' The core word denotes the 'before' side, what comes earlier or in front.
9.grammar: An adverb of time/place ('before') joined to the pronoun '-kum' ('you, plural'). The '-i' ending is genitive: such words of place/time regularly take this case, especially after a preposition, and the attached pronoun completes the sense as 'before you.'

10.meaning: 'And that He may turn in mercy / accept repentance' — and that He may relent toward and accept the return of one who repents. Said of Allah, it means He grants pardon and welcomes the penitent back.
10.grammar: Connector wa ('and') + a present-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular. The ya- prefix marks 'he'. The -a ending (-tūba) is the subjunctive, carried over from a preceding 'so that' purpose, giving 'and that He may turn (in mercy)'. The root means 'to turn/return': of a servant it is repenting; of Allah it is relenting and accepting that repentance.
10.root: ت-و-ب (t-w-b) — to turn back, return; repentance, and Allah's acceptance of it

11.meaning: 'Upon you (all)' — the preposition 'upon/on/over' joined to the plural 'you,' indicating something resting on or directed at a group.
11.grammar: The preposition 'ʿalā' ('upon/on/over') in its joined form 'ʿalay-' plus the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you all,' masculine plural). It marks the group as the recipients or target of whatever is laid 'upon' them.

12.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
12.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
12.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

13.meaning: An intensive adjective/name meaning 'All-Knowing / fully aware' — one whose knowledge is complete, deep, and all-encompassing; as a divine attribute it denotes Allah's perfect knowledge.
13.grammar: An intensive adjective (the pattern faʿīl conveys 'thoroughly, abundantly'). The ending -un is the indefinite nominative — the nominative case marks it as the subject or the quality being affirmed, and the -n (nunation) signals 'a / an', i.e. indefinite. So it reads '(is) all-knowing'.

14.meaning: All-Wise: possessing perfect wisdom — placing everything in its right place with flawless knowledge, judgment, and purpose. As a divine attribute it denotes Allah's consummate wisdom.
14.grammar: A masculine singular adjective/intensive noun on the faʿīl pattern, expressing a deep, settled quality of wisdom. The final -un (nunation) marks it as indefinite and nominative — the case used for a subject or, very often, a predicate describing the doer ('[He is] All-Wise').
14.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — to judge, to be wise

1.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
1.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
1.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

2.meaning: He/it wills, wants, intends, desires — to seek or aim at something purposefully.
2.grammar: A present-tense (form IV) verb, third-person masculine singular ('he wills/wants'). The ya- prefix marks 'he', and the final -u is the indicative ending, signalling an ongoing or habitual action ('does / is doing').
2.root: ر-و-د (r-w-d) — to seek, to want; (form IV) to will/intend

3.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
3.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

4.meaning: 'He turns / repents' or, of Allah, 'He relents and accepts repentance' — the act of turning back: a servant turning from sin, or Allah turning toward the servant in pardon.

parts.en: he / it (3rd-person masculine prefix, with assimilated gemination)

4.grammar: A present-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular. The ya- prefix signals 'he/it' as the doer; it carries a shadda (doubling) because a preceding particle's final consonant has assimilated into the yā'. The final -a (rather than -u) is the subjunctive mood, which follows particles meaning 'to/that/so that' and conveys an intended or hoped-for action. The root 'to turn back' yields 'to repent' (of a servant) and 'to relent / accept repentance' (of Allah).
4.root: ت-و-ب (t-w-b) — to turn back, return; repentance, and Allah's acceptance of it

5.meaning: A combination meaning roughly 'upon/over you (plural)' or 'against you (plural)'. The preposition denotes resting on, being incumbent upon, or being directed against, while the attached pronoun refers to a group of people being addressed.
5.grammar: A preposition with a fused object pronoun. The base form ʿalā shortens to ʿalay- before an attached pronoun. The ending -kum marks a masculine plural addressee ('you all'); whatever the preposition governs is in the genitive by virtue of following it.

6.meaning: 'And he/it wills, wants, intends, or desires.' It conveys deliberate volition and purpose aimed at bringing something about, not mere fleeting wish.
6.grammar: A connector wa- ('and/but') joined to a present-tense (imperfect) verb in derived Form IV. The yu- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it') acting now or habitually. The final -u is the indicative ending, the default mood for a simple statement of fact.
6.root: ر-و-د (r-w-d) — to seek, want, intend

7.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
7.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

8.meaning: 'They follow, pursue, or go after,' in the sense of taking something as a path, conforming to it, or chasing after it.
8.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) verb in derived Form VIII (which adds an internal -t-). The ya-…-ūna frame marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'). The full -ūna ending (rather than bare -ū) is the indicative, signalling a plain statement of ongoing or habitual action.

9.meaning: 'the desires / desired things / lusts' — the plural of the word for a craving or appetite; the objects of worldly desire, or the cravings themselves.
9.grammar: A sound feminine plural of shahwa ('desire, craving'), with the definite article (whose 'l' assimilates into the 'sh,' shown by the doubling). The -āti ending is the feminine-plural form in its genitive/accusative (oblique) state; the -i shows it is linked to a preceding noun ('… OF the desires') or governed by a preposition.

10.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
10.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

11.meaning: 'You (plural) incline, lean, swerve, or deviate' — to tilt away from a straight course toward one side.
11.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) verb addressed to a masculine plural 'you.' The dropped final -n (giving -ū rather than -ūna) shows the verb is in a dependent mood (subjunctive/jussive), the form used after certain particles such as those expressing purpose ('so that…'), negation, or condition.

12.meaning: 'An inclining, a leaning, a swerving away' — the act or instance of tilting off a straight course; figuratively, a deviation.
12.grammar: A verbal noun (the action made into a noun). The -an ending is the indefinite accusative ('a …'), typically marking the object of a verb or, as often with such nouns, an emphasising cognate object that reinforces the verb's own meaning (e.g. 'incline a great inclining').

13.meaning: 'Great, immense, mighty, momentous.' It describes something vast in size, weight, or seriousness, and is often used of grave or awe-inspiring matters.
13.grammar: An adjective on the intensive faʿīl pattern. The -an ending is the indefinite accusative ('a great …'), commonly marking an adjective that agrees with an indefinite accusative noun it describes, or the object of a verb.

1.meaning: He/it wills, wants, intends, desires — to seek or aim at something purposefully.
1.grammar: A present-tense (form IV) verb, third-person masculine singular ('he wills/wants'). The ya- prefix marks 'he', and the final -u is the indicative ending, signalling an ongoing or habitual action ('does / is doing').
1.root: ر-و-د (r-w-d) — to seek, to want; (form IV) to will/intend

2.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
2.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.
2.root: — (proper divine name)

3.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
3.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

4.meaning: 'That he/it should lighten, ease, or reduce a burden' — to make something less heavy, less demanding, or more bearable.
4.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) verb in derived Form II, whose doubled middle consonant gives an intensive or causative sense ('to make light'). The yu- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject. The final -a is the subjunctive ending, the mood used after particles meaning 'to / so that,' expressing intent or a desired outcome.
4.root: خ-ف-ف (kh-f-f) — to be light, to lighten

5.meaning: 'From you / off you' (addressing a group). The preposition 'ʿan' (denoting moving away from, or 'concerning') fused with a plural 'you'.
5.grammar: A preposition 'ʿan' with an attached pronoun object. 'ʿan' conveys moving away or off from something (and so pairs naturally with pardoning — lifting a fault away); the suffix '-kum' means a plural 'you'.

6.meaning: 'And he/it was created, brought into being, fashioned.' The verb is passive, so the focus is on the thing made rather than the Maker.
6.grammar: A connector wa- ('and') joined to a past-tense (perfect) verb in the passive voice. The internal vowel pattern khu-i-a marks the passive ('was …'). The final -a is the standard ending for a third-person masculine singular subject in the past, indicating a completed action.
6.root: خ-ل-ق (kh-l-q) — to create, originate, fashion

7.meaning: 'Mankind, the human being, humanity' — the human as a species or as the representative human creature.
7.grammar: A definite noun: the prefix al- ('the') here generalises to the whole class ('humankind as such'). The final -u is the nominative ending, the case that typically marks the subject (the doer or the thing spoken about) of a sentence.
7.root: ا-ن-س (ʾ-n-s) — to be sociable, familiar; humankind

8.meaning: A noun/adjective meaning 'weak', 'frail', or 'feeble' — lacking strength, whether in body, capacity, or means.
8.grammar: A descriptive noun on the intensive pattern faʿīl, singular indefinite. The -an ending (accusative with tanwīn) marks it as 'a weak one' standing as an object, or as a predicate describing someone.
8.root: ض-ع-ف (ḍ-ʿ-f) — weakness, feebleness, lack of strength

1.meaning: 'O…!' — a compound vocative expression used to call out and summon an audience before addressing them. It fuses the call-particle 'yā' ('O') with a noun that means 'the one(s) addressed,' yielding an emphatic 'O you…!' that introduces direct address.
1.grammar: A vocative (calling) construction. 'Yā' is the particle for calling out; 'ayyu' carries a nominative '-u' as the one being summoned; 'hā' is an attention-drawing particle. Together they function as 'O you…!,' setting up the noun of address that follows.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
3.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

4.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
4.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

5.meaning: '(that) you eat / consume' — to take in food, and by extension to devour or consume wealth or property. Addressed to a group ('you all').
5.grammar: A present-tense verb, second-person masculine plural ('you all'). The plural '-ū' ending (without the usual final '-na') shows the verb is in the subjunctive or jussive — typically after a particle of purpose, negation, or prohibition ('that you (not) eat').

6.meaning: Your possessions / your wealth; the properties and goods belonging to you (a group).
6.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural noun with an attached possessive pronoun. The -a marks the accusative case, signaling it is the direct object (the thing acted upon); the ending -kum means 'your' for a group being addressed.
6.root: م-و-ل (m-w-l) — wealth, property, possessions

7.meaning: Between you / among you; the space or relation linking the members of a group.
7.grammar: An adverb of place ('between/among') with an attached pronoun. The fixed -a ending is characteristic of such place-words; the ending -kum means 'you' for a group, so the whole means 'among you all'.
7.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation/interval; the space between two things

8.meaning: With / by falsehood — 'the false, the vain, the baseless' joined to a preposition and 'the'.
8.grammar: The preposition bi- joined to the definite noun 'the falsehood' (an active participle meaning 'that which is null/vain'). The -i ending is the genitive, required because the noun follows the preposition.
8.root: ب-ط-ل (b-ṭ-l) — to be void, false, vain, of no effect

9.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
9.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

10.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
10.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

11.meaning: A verb meaning 'it is / it comes to be / it exists.' From kāna, the core verb of being, here in its present form expressing being or coming into a state.
11.grammar: A present/imperfect verb of being. The ta- prefix marks a third-person feminine singular subject ('it/she'). The final -a is the subjunctive ending, which typically appears after particles meaning 'that,' 'so that,' or 'until,' giving a sense of 'that it be' or 'so that it may be.'
11.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

12.meaning: Trade, commerce, or a commercial transaction — the noun for buying and selling and the dealings of merchants; also the profit-seeking enterprise itself. The -an ending leaves it indefinite ('a transaction / some trade').
12.grammar: An indefinite feminine noun. The -ah/-at ending is the feminine marker (tāʾ marbūṭah). The -an (tanwīn) is the indefinite accusative: it commonly marks the object of a verb or the noun in certain constructions, and signals the word is indefinite ('a trade').

13.meaning: A preposition meaning 'on behalf of,' 'for,' 'about,' or 'away from.' It often conveys removing a burden from someone or acting in their place.

parts.en: on behalf of / for / away from

13.grammar: A preposition (a linking particle). It governs the noun that follows it, putting that noun into the genitive case. It does not change form.

14.meaning: A noun meaning 'mutual consent' or 'mutual agreement' — both sides being pleased and willing together. From the root for contentment, in a form that signals reciprocity between parties.
14.grammar: A verbal noun with the indefinite genitive ending -in (the tanwīn on a word ending in a weak letter). The genitive is the case used after a preposition or in a possessive link ('… of …'). The ta-...-ā- shape conveys mutuality — being pleased with one another.
14.root: ر-ض-و (r-ḍ-w) — to be content, pleased, satisfied

15.meaning: A combination meaning 'from you (plural)' or 'of/among you (plural).' The preposition denotes origin, source, separation, or partition ('part of'), and the pronoun refers to a group being addressed.
15.grammar: A preposition with a fused object pronoun. min governs the genitive case, and the attached -kum marks a masculine plural reference ('you all'). The pairing commonly expresses 'from among you' or 'part of you.'

16.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
16.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

17.meaning: 'You (plural) kill, slay, put to death.'
17.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) verb addressed to a masculine plural 'you.' The dropped final -n (giving -ū not -ūna) shows a dependent mood (subjunctive/jussive), the form used after particles of prohibition ('do not…'), negation, purpose, or condition.

18.meaning: 'Yourselves' — your own selves, persons, or souls. The base noun 'nafs' means the self, soul, or inner person.
18.grammar: A plural noun, 'selves,' with the attached pronoun '-kum' ('your,' addressed to a group). The '-a' before the pronoun is the accusative case, marking the word as the direct object — the thing being acted upon.

19.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
19.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

20.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
20.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

21.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

21.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

22.meaning: A preposition 'bi' ('with / by / in / for') joined to the attached pronoun 'you all', yielding 'with you' or 'for you (plural)'. The exact shade — attachment, instrument, or benefit — depends on the verb it accompanies.
22.grammar: A preposition plus an attached pronoun. 'bi' is a versatile preposition (with, by, in, for), and -kum is the genitive/object pronoun 'you all' (masculine plural). Pronouns following a preposition always take this attached (genitive) form.

23.meaning: 'Most Merciful, ever-compassionate' — one who continually and abundantly shows mercy. On the faʿīl pattern it conveys a deep, settled, characteristic quality of mercy.
23.grammar: An adjective/intensive noun on the faʿīl pattern denoting a permanent trait. The -an ending is the indefinite accusative ('a most merciful …'), commonly marking the object/complement of a verb or an adjective agreeing with an indefinite accusative noun.

1.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
1.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

2.meaning: He does, makes, or carries out; the doing or performing of an act. A general verb for engaging in or committing some deed.
2.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he'). The ya- prefix marks the singular male subject. The final consonant carries no vowel (the jussive/conditional form), which is the shortened form a present verb takes after conditional or certain other particles, typically giving the sense 'if/whoever does…'.
2.root: ف-ع-ل (f-ʿ-l) — doing, making, performing an act

3.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
3.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

4.meaning: 'Aggression, transgression, hostility, overstepping' — wrongfully going beyond proper limits against another.
4.grammar: A verbal noun naming the action of transgressing. The -an ending is the indefinite accusative ('… aggression'), here typically functioning adverbially to state the manner or motive of an act (i.e. doing something 'out of aggression') or as a verb's object.
4.root: ع-د-و (ʿ-d-w) — to transgress, exceed limits, be hostile

5.meaning: 'And injustice, wrongdoing, oppression' — placing something where it does not belong; acting unjustly against what is right.
5.grammar: A connector wa- ('and') joined to a verbal noun. The -an ending is the indefinite accusative ('… injustice'), often used adverbially to express the manner or motive ('out of injustice') or as the object of a verb.
5.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — to wrong, oppress, do injustice

6.meaning: A two-part marker meaning 'then/so' plus 'shall/will.' It announces something forthcoming as a consequence: the particle sawfa points to the future, generally a more remote or emphatic future than the shorter prefix sa-.
6.grammar: A linking particle fa- ('then/so,' signalling result or sequence) joined to the future particle sawfa, which is placed before a present-tense verb to throw its action into the future ('will/shall …').

7.meaning: 'We will make him enter / roast / be exposed to (a fire).' The verb means to bring someone into a fire to be scorched by it; with the attached pronoun, 'him/it.'
7.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) verb in derived Form IV (causative) with a fused object pronoun. The nu- prefix marks a first-person plural subject ('we'). The attached -hi means 'him/it' as the object. The pronoun takes the -i vowel (hi) after a preceding -ī sound.
7.root: ص-ل-ي (ṣ-l-y) — to roast, burn, be exposed to fire

8.meaning: Fire — blazing flame; by extension heat, burning, or (in many contexts) the Fire of punishment. The core image is leaping, consuming flame.
8.grammar: A feminine noun in the indefinite accusative, marked by the -an ending (the 'nunation' tanwīn). This ending commonly signals 'a fire' as the direct object of a verb, i.e. the thing acted upon.
8.root: ن-و-ر (n-w-r) — to give light, shine, illuminate (نَار 'fire' is a derived noun from this root)

9.meaning: And he was / he became — a verb of being that places a subject in a past state or links it to a description in the past.
9.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'kāna' is a past-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular, meaning 'he was/became'; it commonly introduces a past condition and is typically followed by a noun describing the subject's state. The final -a marks completed past action by a single male.

10.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
10.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

11.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
11.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
11.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

12.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
12.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

13.meaning: 'Easy, effortless, slight, manageable.' It describes something simple to do or small in amount.
13.grammar: An adjective on the faʿīl pattern. The -an ending is the indefinite accusative ('an easy …'), commonly marking an adjective agreeing with an indefinite accusative noun it describes, or a verb's object/complement.
13.root: ي-س-ر (y-s-r) — to be easy, light, manageable

1.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
1.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

2.meaning: 'You (plural) avoid, shun, keep away from, steer clear of' something.
2.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) verb in derived Form VIII (internal -t-), addressed to a masculine plural 'you.' The dropped final -n (-ū not -ūna) marks a dependent mood (subjunctive/jussive), the form used after particles of condition ('if…'), purpose, or negation.
2.root: ج-ن-ب (j-n-b) — side; to keep to one side of, avoid

3.meaning: 'Major / grave instances of (something)' — the great ones, the most serious of a category. As a plural of the 'greatest/gravest,' it denotes the most weighty members of a class (e.g. grave sins).
3.grammar: A noun in the broken (internal) plural on the kabāʾir pattern, meaning 'great/grave ones.' Because of its plural pattern it is 'diptote' — it takes a bare -a for the accusative (and genitive) and does not add the usual nunation. The -a here typically marks it as the object of a verb.
3.root: ك-ب-ر (k-b-r) — to be great, large, grave

4.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
4.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

5.meaning: 'You (plural) are forbidden, prohibited, restrained from' something. The verb is passive, so the focus is on those being told to stop.
5.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) verb in the passive voice ('you are …ed'), addressed to a masculine plural 'you.' The tu- prefix with the internal vowel pattern signals the passive. The full -na on the ending (-awna) is the indicative, marking a plain statement of fact.

6.meaning: A combination meaning 'from him / from it / about him.' The preposition denotes moving away from, departing from, or concerning a thing, and the pronoun refers to a single masculine entity.
6.grammar: A preposition with a fused object pronoun. ʿan governs the genitive and conveys separation or 'concerning.' The attached -hu marks a third-person masculine singular object ('him/it').

7.meaning: 'We blot out, cover over, expiate, wipe away.' On the Form II pattern it means to cause sins to be covered and effaced so they no longer count against a person.
7.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) verb in derived Form II, whose doubled middle consonant gives an intensive/causative sense ('to cover up thoroughly'). The nu- prefix marks a first-person plural subject ('we'). The vowelless ending (-r, no final vowel) is the jussive/conditional mood, the clipped form used in 'if … then …' constructions and after certain particles.
7.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; (Form II) to efface, expiate

8.meaning: 'From you / off you' (addressing a group). The preposition 'ʿan' (denoting moving away from, or 'concerning') fused with a plural 'you'.
8.grammar: A preposition 'ʿan' with an attached pronoun object. 'ʿan' conveys moving away or off from something (and so pairs naturally with pardoning — lifting a fault away); the suffix '-kum' means a plural 'you'.

9.meaning: Your evil deeds, misdeeds, or bad actions — the plural of a word denoting a wrong or offense, something that brings harm or ill, paired with the second-person plural 'your.'
9.grammar: A feminine sound plural noun ('evil deeds') with the attached pronoun -kum ('your,' for a group). The -āt ending is the regular feminine plural. The -i vowel before the pronoun is the genitive case, which here signals possession — the noun is joined to a following possessor ('the misdeeds OF you' = 'your misdeeds').
9.root: س-و-ء (s-w-ʾ) — to be bad, evil, to harm

10.meaning: 'And We will bring you (plural) in / admit you / cause you to enter.' The verb means to cause someone to go into a place; with the suffix, the object is a group being addressed.
10.grammar: A connector wa- joined to a present-tense (imperfect) verb in derived Form IV (causative, 'to make enter'), with a fused object pronoun. The nu- prefix marks a first-person plural subject ('we'); the attached -kum is a masculine plural object ('you all'). The verb's stem ending is vowelless (jussive/conditional), the clipped form used in 'if … then …' constructions.
10.root: د-خ-ل (d-kh-l) — to enter; (Form IV) to cause to enter, admit

11.meaning: 'A place of entry, a point/manner of admission' — the location or way by which one is brought in. As a passive-style noun of place it can mean 'an honoured entering' or 'an entrance into which one is admitted.'
11.grammar: A Form IV noun of place/passive participle ('a place into which one is made to enter'). The -an ending is the indefinite accusative ('an entrance …'), which here typically marks the noun as the object of a verb (the thing one is admitted into).
11.root: د-خ-ل (d-kh-l) — to enter; (Form IV) to cause to enter, admit

12.meaning: Noble, generous, honourable — describing something or someone of high worth, dignity, and openhanded goodness. Used of provision, status, or character that is precious and held in honour.
12.grammar: An adjective in the indefinite accusative. The -an ending (tanwīn) marks the indefinite accusative case, which typically signals the object of a verb or a descriptive/adverbial role, in an unspecified, non-particular sense ('a noble/generous one').

1.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
1.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

2.meaning: To long for, covet, or wish for something — to set one's heart on having what another possesses or on an outcome one desires.
2.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, second person masculine plural ('you all'). It is Form V (tafaʿʿala), whose stem already begins with ta- (tamannā); the imperfect 'you' prefix ta- is added before that stem, so the written form opens with a doubled tā- (ta + tamannā). The -ū ending (written wāw + alif) marks the masculine plural subject; the vowel-less ending reflects the subjunctive/jussive mood (typically after a particle such as a negative or 'so that'). Form V often carries the sense of seeking or bringing about something for oneself — hence 'to wish/covet for oneself'.
2.root: م-ن-ي (m-n-y) — wishing, desiring, hoping

3.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
3.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

4.meaning: To favour, prefer, or grant excellence — to give one party an advantage, bounty, or superiority over another.
4.grammar: A past-tense verb, third person masculine singular ('he'). The doubled middle consonant marks it as Form II (faʿʿala), which intensifies or makes causative the base sense — here 'to cause one to have more, to prefer/favour'. The final -a is the standard past-tense ending for 'he'.

5.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
5.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

6.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
6.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

7.meaning: Some of you, a portion of you — singling out one part of a group in relation to another.
7.grammar: A noun 'a part / some' with the attached plural pronoun -kum ('you all'), forming a possessive link ('some of you'). The -a ending on the noun marks the accusative case, which typically signals that the word is the object of a verb.

8.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
8.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

9.meaning: 'Some (others)' / 'a part' — the same noun for 'a portion or some,' here left indefinite, often functioning as the counterpart in the 'one another' construction.
9.grammar: A noun 'part/some' in the genitive case with indefinite marking (the -in ending, called tanwīn). The genitive typically follows a preposition or links it to a preceding noun ('… of …'); the doubled -n sound marks it as indefinite ('a part / some').
9.root: ب-ع-ض (b-ʿ-ḍ) — a part, portion, or some of a whole

10.meaning: 'For the men / belonging to the men' — denoting that something is due, allotted, or belongs to males (men, as opposed to women).
10.grammar: The preposition li- ('for/to/belonging to') joined to the definite article al- ('the') and the plural noun rijāl ('men'). Because it follows a preposition the noun is in the genitive case, shown by the final -i vowel, giving 'for/to the men.' The doubling of the r occurs because the article's 'l' assimilates into the following 'sun letter' r (so al-rijāl is pronounced ar-rijāl).
10.root: ر-ج-ل (r-j-l) — man, manhood; relating to the male and, by extension, going on foot

11.meaning: A portion, share, or allotted part — what falls to someone as their due lot or stake.
11.grammar: A singular noun. The final -un (tanwīn ḍamma) marks it as indefinite ('a share') and in the nominative case, the form typically used for the subject of a sentence or the thing being stated to exist ('there is a share').
11.root: ن-ص-ب (n-ṣ-b) — to allot, set up; (a share) apportioned

12.meaning: A fused word combining the preposition 'min' ('from', 'of', 'about') with the relative/indefinite 'mā' ('what', 'that which'). Together: 'from what', 'about that which', 'of what'.
12.grammar: The preposition 'min' and the word 'mā' merge in pronunciation (the 'n' assimilating into the 'm'). 'min' governs a genitive, and 'mā' here functions as a relative pronoun introducing a clause ('that which …'). These are indeclinable particles without case endings.

13.meaning: They acquired, earned, or gained — to obtain something through one's own effort or deeds, often with a sense of deliberate striving for personal benefit.
13.grammar: A past-tense verb, third person masculine plural ('they', men). The -ū ending marks a plural masculine subject. It is Form VIII (iftaʿala), whose infixed -t- typically adds a reflexive sense of doing something for or to oneself — hence 'to earn/acquire for one's own account'.

14.meaning: 'And for the women / belonging to the women' — denoting that something is due, allotted, or belongs to females (women, as opposed to men).
14.grammar: The connective wa- ('and') with the preposition li- ('for/to/belonging to'), the definite article al-, and the plural noun nisāʾ ('women' — a plural with no singular from its own root). Because it follows a preposition the noun is in the genitive case, shown by the final -i vowel: 'and for the women.' The doubling of the n is the article's 'l' assimilating into the 'sun letter' n.
14.root: ن-س-و / ن-س-ء (n-s-w / n-s-ʾ) — womankind; the word for women, with no masculine singular of its own

15.meaning: A portion, share, or allotted part — what falls to someone as their due lot or stake.
15.grammar: A singular noun. The final -un (tanwīn ḍamma) marks it as indefinite ('a share') and in the nominative case, the form typically used for the subject of a sentence or the thing being stated to exist ('there is a share').
15.root: ن-ص-ب (n-ṣ-b) — to allot, set up; (a share) apportioned

16.meaning: A fused word combining the preposition 'min' ('from', 'of', 'about') with the relative/indefinite 'mā' ('what', 'that which'). Together: 'from what', 'about that which', 'of what'.
16.grammar: The preposition 'min' and the word 'mā' merge in pronunciation (the 'n' assimilating into the 'm'). 'min' governs a genitive, and 'mā' here functions as a relative pronoun introducing a clause ('that which …'). These are indeclinable particles without case endings.

17.meaning: They acquired, earned, or gained — the same act of obtaining through effort, attributed to a group of females.
17.grammar: A past-tense verb, third person feminine plural ('they', women). The -na ending marks a plural feminine subject. It is Form VIII (iftaʿala), whose infixed -t- typically adds a reflexive sense of acting for oneself — hence 'to earn/acquire for one's own account'.

18.meaning: And ask, request, or inquire — a command to put a question to someone or to ask for something.
18.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to a masculine plural ('you all'), prefixed with 'and'. The -ū ending marks the plural addressees. The base verb means 'to ask/request', and the imperative form directs the listeners to carry out that action.

19.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
19.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.
19.root: — (proper name)

20.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
20.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

21.meaning: 'His bounty / grace / favor' — faḍl is overflowing generosity, an extra goodness given beyond what is owed; with the attached pronoun it means the bounty belonging to Him (Allah).
21.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive pronoun '-hi' ('his/His'). The -i vowel before the pronoun is the genitive case, which typically appears after a preposition or links the noun to what follows in an 'of' relationship; here it carries through to the possessor.
21.root: ف-ض-ل (f-ḍ-l) — excess, surplus; hence bounty, grace, superiority

22.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
22.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

23.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
23.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

24.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

24.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

25.meaning: 'Of every / with all' — the preposition 'bi' ('with / in / by') joined to the word 'every / each / all', expressing comprehensiveness applied to whatever noun follows.
25.grammar: A preposition plus a noun. The prefix bi- ('with / in / by') always places the following noun in the genitive ('of') state. The final -i on 'kull' is that genitive ending, signalling the word is governed by the preposition. 'Kull' denotes totality — 'every (single)' or 'all'.

26.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
26.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
26.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

27.meaning: All-Knowing; one possessing complete, perfect knowledge. As an intensive form it conveys knowledge that is total and unfailing, encompassing all things.
27.grammar: An intensive adjective ('all-knowing') on the faʿīl pattern, which stresses the quality to its fullest degree. The -an (tanwīn) joins the -a accusative ending — typical of a predicate or object — with the -n marking it indefinite.

1.meaning: A combination meaning 'and for each / and to everyone' — joining 'and' with the preposition 'for/to' and the word 'all, each one', indicating that something belongs to or applies to every one.
1.grammar: A cluster: wa- 'and', the preposition li- 'for/to', and the noun kull 'all/each'. The ending -in is genitive (the case required after the preposition li-), and its final -n (tanwīn) marks the word as indefinite ('every one, each'). The doubled l (shadda) is part of kull.

2.meaning: We made, rendered, set up, or appointed. A completed act of making or designating, done by a group or by a majestic 'We.'
2.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb with the attached subject ending -nā, meaning 'we' did the action. 'Jaʿala' carries senses from 'to make/create' to 'to render X into Y' or 'to appoint.'
2.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, render, appoint, place

3.meaning: Heirs, kinsmen, guardians, allies — those bound by ties of kinship, loyalty, or protection. The singular (mawlā) covers a range of close relationships: master, protector, helper, freed slave, or near relative who inherits.
3.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural that is morphologically 'defective' — its final root letter is a weak yāʾ. In the construct state (iḍāfa, the 'of' linkage to a following noun), the plural's normal long final -ī shortens to -iya, written with yāʾ + fatḥa (ـيَ). This -ya is the construct/defective-noun form rather than a plain case ending; in context the word stands in the accusative.

4.meaning: From what / from that which — a fusion of the preposition 'from' with the relative 'what/which', introducing the thing or situation being referred to.
4.grammar: A merger of 'min' ('from') and 'mā' ('what/that which'); the 'n' of 'min' assimilates into the 'm' of 'mā', doubling it. The combination means 'from what ...' and typically introduces a following clause describing the thing referred to. Being particles, neither part takes a case ending.

5.meaning: He left behind / he left, abandoned, or relinquished — a completed act of leaving something or someone, including leaving property behind (as an inheritance).
5.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb. The final '-a' marks third-person masculine singular: "he" did the action, viewed as completed.

6.meaning: 'The two parents / the father and mother' — the pair who beget, i.e. one's two begetters taken together as a unit.
6.grammar: The definite article al- ('the') on the noun wālid ('a parent/begetter'), with the dual ending -āni meaning exactly two. The -āni form is the nominative dual, the case used when the pair is the subject/doer or simply named: 'the two parents.' (Were they an object or after a preposition, the ending would shift to -ayni.)
6.root: و-ل-د (w-l-d) — to beget, give birth; offspring, parentage, lineage

7.meaning: 'And the nearer kin / close relatives' — those who are near in kinship, one's closest relations. Grammatically a plural denoting such near relatives as a group.
7.grammar: The connective wa- ('and') with the definite article al- and the elative aqrab ('nearer, closest' — the afʿal comparative pattern), here used substantively ('the nearer ones, i.e. near kin') and so taking the sound masculine plural ending -ūna. The -ūna ending marks a masculine human plural in the nominative case (used when the word is a subject or is simply being named): 'the nearer kin.'
7.root: ق-ر-ب (q-r-b) — nearness, closeness; to draw near, be close in distance or kinship

8.meaning: 'And those who': a connective phrase introducing a specified group of people (masculine plural) about whom something will be said. It links them to what came before.
8.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'), which is masculine plural. A relative pronoun stands for a group and is normally followed by a clause describing them. Its form does not change for case; it stays alladhīna whatever its grammatical role.

9.meaning: She/it tied, bound, contracted, or made firm — to fasten or knot, and by extension to conclude a binding agreement, pact, or oath.
9.grammar: A past-tense verb, third person feminine singular ('she' or a feminine 'it'). The -at ending marks a feminine singular subject. The core sense is the firm 'tying' of a knot, applied figuratively to sealing covenants and commitments.

10.meaning: Your (plural) right hands — literally the right hands, used idiomatically for solemn oaths and for lawful possession or authority. With the suffix: 'your right hands'.
10.grammar: A plural noun carrying the nominative -u ending, which typically marks it as the subject (the doer) of a verb. The suffix -kum is the attached possessive pronoun 'your' (plural masculine). The plural can mean 'right hands' or 'oaths', and the phrase 'what your right hands possess' is an idiom for those under one's lawful charge.
10.root: ي-م-ن (y-m-n) — right hand/side; oath; good fortune

11.meaning: Then give them — a command to hand over or grant something to a group of people, introduced by 'then/so' marking it as a consequence.
11.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to a masculine plural ('you all'), carrying the attached object pronoun -hum ('them'), introduced by fa- ('then/so'). The -ū ending marks the plural addressees. It is Form IV (afʿala), which gives a causative/transitive sense — 'to cause someone to have something', i.e. 'to give'.
11.root: أ-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — coming; in Form IV, bringing/giving

12.meaning: Their share, portion, or due lot — the part allotted to a group of people.
12.grammar: A noun 'share/portion' with the attached plural pronoun -hum ('their'), forming a possessive link ('their share'). The -a ending on the noun marks the accusative case, which typically signals that the word is the object of a verb.
12.root: ن-ص-ب (n-ṣ-b) — to set up / allot; a fixed, appointed portion

13.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
13.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

14.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
14.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

15.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

15.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

16.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
16.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

17.meaning: 'every,' 'each,' or 'all' — a word expressing totality or completeness. It indicates the entirety of something: when joined to a singular indefinite noun it means 'every (single) one,' and when joined to a definite noun it can mean 'all of' or 'the whole of.'
17.grammar: A noun of totality. The final '-i' ending is genitive (the 'of/possession' case): it marks the word as governed by a preceding preposition or as the first term of a possessive link to a following noun, so it typically reads 'of every…' or 'every…' leading into what follows.

18.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
18.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
18.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

19.meaning: 'A witness' — one who sees and attests, who can give evidence; also carries the sense of one who is present and observant, and at times 'a martyr' (one who bears witness with their life).
19.grammar: An intensive describing-noun (pattern fa‘īl) meaning 'a witness, one who fully attests', indefinite. The -an ending (the accusative with 'tanwīn') marks it as indefinite and in the accusative — the case used for a direct object, or for a word that describes the state or role in which someone stands.
19.root: ش-ه-د (sh-h-d) — witnessing, being present, testifying

1.meaning: The men — adult males, the menfolk, as a defined group.
1.grammar: A definite plural noun ('the men'), marked definite by the prefix al- ('the'). The -u ending marks the nominative case, which typically signals that the word is the subject of a sentence or the topic being described.

2.meaning: Upholders, maintainers, those who stand firmly in charge — people who take full, steadfast responsibility for managing, protecting, and providing. The intensive form stresses constancy and thoroughness in 'standing over' an affair.
2.grammar: An intensive agent-noun (faʿʿāl pattern, conveying one who does something constantly or to a high degree), masculine plural. The -ūna ending marks a masculine plural in the nominative case, which typically signals the subject or the thing being described.
2.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — standing, rising, upholding, maintaining

3.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
3.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
3.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

4.meaning: 'The women' — the plural used for women/females collectively. (It serves as the plural of mar'a, 'woman.')
4.grammar: A plural noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending is genitive: it marks the word as following a preposition or standing in a possessive ('of …') relationship. The l of al- assimilates into the following n in pronunciation (a 'sun letter').

5.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
5.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

6.meaning: To favour, prefer, or grant excellence — to give one party an advantage, bounty, or superiority over another.
6.grammar: A past-tense verb, third person masculine singular ('he'). The doubled middle consonant marks it as Form II (faʿʿala), which intensifies or makes causative the base sense — here 'to cause one to have more, to prefer/favour'. The final -a is the standard past-tense ending for 'he'.
6.root: ف-ض-ل (f-ḍ-l) — bounty, excess, preference, excellence

7.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
7.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

8.meaning: "some of them / a part of them" — the word baʿḍ means 'a portion/some', and with the attached pronoun it means 'some of them', singling out part of a group.
8.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive/partitive pronoun. The -a ending is the accusative case, the form a noun takes as the object of an action or the second term of certain constructions. The suffix -hum means 'them' (third-person masculine plural).

9.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
9.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

10.meaning: 'Some (others)' / 'a part' — the same noun for 'a portion or some,' here left indefinite, often functioning as the counterpart in the 'one another' construction.
10.grammar: A noun 'part/some' in the genitive case with indefinite marking (the -in ending, called tanwīn). The genitive typically follows a preposition or links it to a preceding noun ('… of …'); the doubled -n sound marks it as indefinite ('a part / some').
10.root: ب-ع-ض (b-ʿ-ḍ) — a part, portion, or some of a whole

11.meaning: And because of / and by reason of what — a connective phrase joining a cause: 'and because of that which…'.
11.grammar: A combination of particles: the connector wa- ('and'), the preposition bi- (here giving the sense 'because of / by means of'), and the word mā ('what / that which'). Together they introduce a reason or means. Such particles do not change their endings.

12.meaning: 'They spent / disbursed' — the act of laying out wealth, giving it away, or expending it, done by a group in the past.
12.grammar: A past-tense verb in a pattern meaning to spend or expend (especially wealth). The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'); the silent alif written after it is a spelling convention and is not pronounced.

13.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
13.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

14.meaning: Their wealth, property, possessions — the goods and assets belonging to a group of people.
14.grammar: A plural noun 'wealth/properties' with the attached plural pronoun -him ('their'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically appears when the word follows a preposition or is linked to a preceding noun (the 'of' relationship).

15.meaning: So the righteous women — virtuous, upright women who do what is good and sound; introduced by 'so/therefore'.
15.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun/adjective ('the righteous women'), built on the active-participle pattern (ṣāliḥ, 'one who is righteous/sound'), with feminine plural -āt, made definite by al- and introduced by fa- ('so'). The -u ending marks the nominative case, which typically signals the subject or topic being described.

16.meaning: Devoutly obedient ones, humbly submissive — those who stand in willing, sustained obedience and devotion. Qunūt conveys quiet, constant, reverent compliance.
16.grammar: An active participle (qānit, 'one who is devoutly obedient'), feminine plural (-āt), and indefinite. The -un ending (tanwīn) marks the indefinite nominative case, which typically signals the subject of a sentence or a predicate describing the subject ('are devoutly obedient ones').
16.root: ق-ن-ت (q-n-t) — devout obedience, humble submission, standing in worship

17.meaning: Guardians, ones who carefully keep, preserve, and protect — those who watch over and safeguard a trust.
17.grammar: An active participle (ḥāfiẓ, 'one who guards/preserves'), feminine plural (-āt), and indefinite. The -un ending (tanwīn) marks the indefinite nominative case, which typically signals the subject or a predicate describing it ('are ones who guard').

18.meaning: For/of the unseen — pertaining to what is hidden, absent, or out of sight: that which is not witnessed or is concealed from view.
18.grammar: The noun ghayb ('the unseen/hidden'), made definite by 'the' and preceded by the preposition li- ('for / with regard to'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which is the expected case after a preposition (here giving 'for/in respect of the unseen').

19.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
19.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.
19.root: — (particle + relative pronoun)

20.meaning: He/it guarded, preserved, kept, or protected — to watch over something and keep it safe and intact.
20.grammar: A past-tense verb, third person masculine singular ('he' or a masculine 'it'). The final -a is the standard past-tense ending for 'he'. The core sense is keeping something safe, intact, and under careful watch.

21.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
21.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

22.meaning: 'And those (females) who' — a connective 'and' plus the feminine plural relative pronoun, introducing a clause about a group of women ('those women who …').
22.grammar: Connective 'and' + a relative pronoun, feminine plural ('those who…'). It refers to a group of females and introduces a following descriptive clause. Relative pronouns are fixed in form and do not change for grammatical case.

23.meaning: You fear, dread, or apprehend — to be afraid of something or to anticipate a feared outcome.
23.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, second person masculine plural ('you all'). The ta- prefix marks 'you', and the -ūna ending marks a plural subject in the indicative mood, typically describing an ongoing or general action ('you (all) fear').

24.meaning: Their rebelliousness, defiance, or ill-conduct — a rising up against and turning away from one's due relationship or duty; arrogant disobedience and discord. The base sense is something 'rising/raised up'.
24.grammar: A verbal noun 'rebelliousness/discord' with the attached feminine plural pronoun -hunna ('their'), forming a possessive link. The -a ending on the noun marks the accusative case, which typically signals that the word is the object of a verb.
24.root: ن-ش-ز (n-sh-z) — rising up, elevation; defiance, discord

25.meaning: Then admonish them, counsel them, urge them — a command to give earnest moral exhortation and reminder to a group of females; introduced by 'then/so'.
25.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to a masculine plural ('you all'), carrying the attached object pronoun -hunna ('them', feminine), introduced by fa- ('then/so'). The -ū ending marks the plural addressees. The verb means to counsel earnestly with a reminder of right and consequence.
25.root: و-ع-ظ (w-ʿ-ẓ) — admonition, earnest counsel, moral exhortation

26.meaning: And forsake them, withdraw from them, leave their company — a command to keep apart from a group of females; the verb conveys separating oneself or abandoning closeness. Introduced by 'and'.
26.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to a masculine plural ('you all'), carrying the attached object pronoun -hunna ('them', feminine), prefixed with 'and'. The -ū ending marks the plural addressees. The verb means to part from, withdraw from, or leave aside.
26.root: ه-ج-ر (h-j-r) — departing, forsaking, separating, abandoning

27.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
27.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

28.meaning: The places of lying down — beds or sleeping-places. A plural noun with the definite article, naming the spots where one reclines to rest or sleep.
28.grammar: A plural noun of place (pattern mafāʿil) carrying the definite article 'the.' The final -i is the genitive case ending: it marks the word as the second term of a possessive construction ('… OF …') or as governed by a preceding preposition.
28.root: ض-ج-ع (ḍ-j-ʿ) — to lie down, recline

29.meaning: And strike them (a group of females). A command addressed to a plural (male/mixed) audience, with the object being a group of women.
29.grammar: A Form I plural imperative, 'strike!' The initial alif is hamzat al-waṣl (a connecting alif, dropped in pronunciation after the preceding wa-). The -ū ending marks the command as given to a male/mixed plural addressee. The attached -hunna is the object pronoun 'them,' referring to a feminine-plural group. The wa- prefix means 'and.'
29.root: ض-ر-ب (ḍ-r-b) — to strike, beat; also to set forth (an example), to travel

30.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'fa-' ('then', 'so', 'but') drawing a consequence, joined to the conditional particle 'in' ('if'). Together: 'then if …', 'but if …'.
30.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that signals a result or transition ('then/so'). 'in' is the conditional particle 'if', introducing a supposed condition. Both are indeclinable particles with no case ending.

31.meaning: They (a group of females) obey you. A verb stating that a group of women render obedience to a plural 'you.'
31.grammar: A Form IV verb (base أَطَاعَ, aṭāʿa, 'to obey'). With a feminine-plural subject the long stem-vowel shortens before the suffix, so أَطَاعَ contracts to aṭaʿ- (hence aṭaʿna, not aṭāʿna). The -na suffix is the feminine-plural subject marker ('they, a group of women'); the attached -kum is the object pronoun 'you,' addressed to a plural (male/mixed) group.
31.root: ط-و-ع (ṭ-w-ʿ) — to obey, comply, submit willingly

32.meaning: A two-part word: the connective particle 'fa-' meaning 'so', 'then', or 'therefore' (drawing a consequence from what precedes), joined to 'lā', the particle of negation/prohibition. Together they convey 'so do not …' or 'so there is no …'.
32.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that links a clause to what came before and often signals a result or consequence. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a present-tense verb it commonly forms a prohibition ('do not …') or a simple negation ('not'). It carries no ending of its own.

33.meaning: You (plural) seek, pursue, or desire — to go after something, whether a goal, a way, or a pretext.
33.grammar: A present/imperfect verb addressed to a plural 'you.' The ta- prefix marks second-person and the -ū ending marks a plural (male/mixed) subject: 'you all seek.' The verb is tabghū, not the indicative tabghūna: dropping the final nūn marks the subjunctive/jussive mood (triggered by a preceding subjunctive particle or a jussive/conditional/prohibitive context). The trailing alif is a silent orthographic alif (alif al-fāriqah) written after a plural -ū; it carries no sound.
33.root: ب-غ-ي (b-gh-y) — to seek, desire, pursue; also to transgress, act wrongfully

34.meaning: A compound meaning 'upon them' or 'against them (a group of females).' It places a duty, burden, or claim 'on' a group of women — what is incumbent upon or held against them.
34.grammar: The preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, against') takes the form ʿalay- when an attached pronoun follows, often conveying obligation or something weighing upon someone. The suffix -hinna is the third-person feminine plural pronoun 'them,' for a group of females; the -i- vowel is the form the pronoun takes after this preposition.

35.meaning: A way, path, road, or means — a route to a destination, hence also a way or means of accomplishing something.
35.grammar: A singular noun. The '-an' ending is accusative and indefinite: the accusative case commonly marks the direct object of a verb, and the final 'n' sound marks it indefinite ('a way'). It denotes a path one travels or a means to an end.

36.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
36.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

37.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
37.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

38.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

38.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

39.meaning: High, exalted, lofty — supremely elevated in rank and majesty. As a divine attribute of Allah it conveys 'the Most High.'
39.grammar: An adjective on the pattern faʿīl meaning 'high/exalted.' The root's final radical is a weak wāw (ع-ل-و); in this pattern that wāw turns into yāʾ and merges with the preceding yāʾ to give the doubled -yy- of ʿaliyy (so the doubling is a phonological result of the weak root, not a separate intensifier). The -an ending is the indefinite accusative: here it functions as a predicate complement (e.g. the khabar of a kāna-type clause or a ḥāl), and the doubled nasal -n (tanwīn) signals it is indefinite.
39.root: ع-ل-و (ʿ-l-w) — to be high, to rise; loftiness, elevation
