40.meaning: Large, great, big, or major — an adjective describing something of great size, amount, or importance. It can also mean elder/older in age. The -an ending leaves it indefinite ('a large …').
40.grammar: An indefinite adjective on the faʿīl pattern. The -an ending is the indefinite accusative (tanwīn): it commonly marks the object of a verb, or works adverbially, and signals the word is indefinite ('a large one'). It pairs with ṣaghīr ('small').
40.root: ك-ب-ر (k-b-r) — greatness, largeness, being great or old

1.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
1.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

2.meaning: 'You (all) feared,' 'you became afraid/apprehensive.' It states that a group experienced fear or wary concern in the past.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb. The ending -tum marks the subject as second-person masculine plural, 'you all (did).' The hollow root's middle letter has dropped before the consonant ending, leaving the short stem khif- (compare khāfa, 'he feared').
2.root: خ-و-ف (kh-w-f) — to fear, be afraid, be in awe

3.meaning: A split, schism, or breach — deep discord in which two parties stand on opposing sides, each pulling away from the other.
3.grammar: A verbal noun (maṣdar of Form III) denoting mutual opposition and rupture. The final -a is the accusative case ending: it commonly marks the word as the object of a verb or as the thing feared/expected. Without tanwīn the -a can also signal that the noun is joined to a following genitive in a possessive construction.
3.root: ش-ق-ق (sh-q-q) — to split, cleave, divide; figuratively to be at odds

4.meaning: Between the two of them — the space or relationship lying amid a pair.
4.grammar: An adverb of place, 'between,' here in a possessive ('between … of …') construction. The -i ending is genitive, the case used when a word follows a preposition or is governed by another noun. The attached -himā is the dual pronoun 'the two of them' (exactly two).
4.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction; that which lies between

5.meaning: So/then send forth, dispatch, or raise up — a command to a plural audience to send someone or rouse something into action.
5.grammar: A Form I plural imperative, 'send forth!' The initial alif is hamzat al-waṣl (a connecting alif dropped after the preceding fa-). The -ū ending marks the command as given to a male/mixed plural; the trailing alif is a silent orthographic alif (alif al-fāriqah) written after plural -ū. The fa- prefix means 'so/then,' linking the command to what precedes as a consequence.
5.root: ب-ع-ث (b-ʿ-th) — to send, dispatch, raise up, resurrect

6.meaning: An arbiter or judge — one appointed to decide between disputing parties and pronounce a binding ruling.
6.grammar: A noun denoting one who arbitrates. The -an ending is the indefinite accusative ('an arbiter'): this case typically marks the word as the object of a verb, and the doubled nasal -n (tanwīn) shows it is indefinite.
6.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — to judge, decide, govern; wisdom, sound judgment

7.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
7.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

8.meaning: Its people / its folk — those who belong to it: its inhabitants, household, or rightful members.
8.grammar: The stem 'ahl' means the people who belong to a place or thing. The attached pronoun -hi means 'its/his' and pulls the noun into a possessive link, so the noun carries the genitive -i before it ('the people of it'). The -hi form (with the i-vowel) is the regular shape after a genitive ending.

9.meaning: And an arbiter — a second one appointed to judge between disputing parties, joined by 'and' to a preceding one.
9.grammar: A noun for an arbitrator with the prefix wa- ('and'). The -an ending is the indefinite accusative ('an arbiter'): typically the object of a verb, with the doubled nasal -n (tanwīn) marking it as indefinite.
9.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — to judge, decide, govern; wisdom, sound judgment

10.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
10.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

11.meaning: Her people / her household — those belonging to her: her family, kin, or the folk to whom she pertains.
11.grammar: A noun meaning 'the people belonging to' someone, here in a possessive construction. The -i ending is genitive, the case used when a word follows a preposition or is the second term of a possessive ('… of …'). The attached -hā is the pronoun 'her' (or 'its,' feminine).
11.root: ا-ه-ل (ʾ-h-l) — family, kinfolk, the people proper to a place or thing

12.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
12.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

13.meaning: They two intend / desire / aim at — a verb stating that a pair (exactly two) wills or sets its purpose toward something.
13.grammar: A present/imperfect Form IV verb (base أَرَادَ, 'to want/intend'). The yu- prefix marks a third-person subject; the verb stem is yurīd-, and the long -ā is the dual subject suffix ('the two of them want'). The form is yurīdā, not the indicative yurīdāni: the missing final nūn marks the subjunctive/jussive mood (after a subjunctive particle or in a conditional/jussive context).
13.root: ر-و-د (r-w-d) — to seek, will, intend; to go to and fro after a thing

14.meaning: 'Setting right, reconciliation, putting matters back in order, making peace and improvement' — the verbal noun for bringing about reform and amends.
14.grammar: A verbal noun (the 'name of the action') from a fourth-form verb meaning 'to set right, reform, reconcile'. The -an ending is accusative with tanwīn, marking it indefinite and signalling the role of a direct object (the thing wanted/done) or a stated purpose.
14.root: ص-ل-ح (ṣ-l-ḥ) — to be sound/good; to set right, reconcile

15.meaning: He brings into accord / grants success in reconciling — to make two things fit together harmoniously, especially to bring agreement between people. Often conveys Allah granting concord and success.
15.grammar: A present/imperfect Form II verb (waffaqa, 'to make things fit together, grant harmony/success'). The yu- prefix marks a third-person singular subject ('he'). The verb is in the jussive mood (as after a conditional particle), which strips its final short vowel and leaves the stem ending in a consonant cluster; the -i (kasra) is then a helping vowel (kasrat al-iltiqāʾ) inserted to break that cluster before the next word — a direct consequence of the jussive truncation, not a general liaison vowel.
15.root: و-ف-ق (w-f-q) — agreement, harmony, fittingness; to be in accord

16.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
16.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.
16.root: — (proper divine name)

17.meaning: Between the two of them — the space or relation lying amid a pair.
17.grammar: An adverb of place, 'between,' fixed in the accusative as adverbs of place commonly are; the -a marks its adverbial function ('in the place that is between'). The attached -humā is the dual pronoun 'the two of them' (exactly two).
17.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction; that which lies between

18.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
18.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

19.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
19.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.
19.root: — (proper name)

20.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

20.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

21.meaning: All-Knowing; one possessing complete, perfect knowledge. As an intensive form it conveys knowledge that is total and unfailing, encompassing all things.
21.grammar: An intensive adjective ('all-knowing') on the faʿīl pattern, which stresses the quality to its fullest degree. The -an (tanwīn) joins the -a accusative ending — typical of a predicate or object — with the -n marking it indefinite.

22.meaning: Deeply aware, well-acquainted, fully informed — one whose knowledge penetrates the inner realities and hidden details of things. As a divine attribute of Allah, the All-Aware.
22.grammar: An adjective on the pattern faʿīl meaning 'thoroughly acquainted with inner realities.' The -an ending is the indefinite accusative: here it functions as a predicate complement ('… is all-aware') in clauses that take an accusative predicate, and the doubled nasal -n (tanwīn) shows it is indefinite.
22.root: خ-ب-ر (kh-b-r) — to know thoroughly, be acquainted with the inner truth of things; inner knowledge

1.meaning: And worship / serve — a command to a plural audience to render worship and humble service, conveying total devotion and obedient servitude to a deity.
1.grammar: A Form I plural imperative, 'worship!' It begins with hamzat al-waṣl (a connecting alif): pronounced uʿbudū in isolation, but the initial vowel drops after the preceding wa- (so wa-uʿbudū elides in connected speech). The -ū ending marks the command as given to a male/mixed plural; the trailing alif is a silent orthographic alif (alif al-fāriqah) written after plural -ū. The wa- prefix means 'and.'
1.root: ع-ب-د (ʿ-b-d) — to worship, serve, submit as a devoted servant

2.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
2.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.
2.root: — (proper name)

3.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
3.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

4.meaning: You (plural) associate / set up a partner — to ascribe partners or equals to a deity, treating another as sharing in what belongs to Allah alone.
4.grammar: A present/imperfect Form IV verb (base أَشْرَكَ, imperfect stem -shrik-, 'to make a partner/associate'). The tu- prefix marks second-person address and the -ū ending marks a plural (male/mixed) subject: 'you all associate.' The verb is tushrikū, not the indicative tushrikūna: the missing final nūn marks a non-indicative mood (here typically after the prohibitive lā or in a jussive context). The trailing alif is a silent orthographic alif (alif al-fāriqah) written after plural -ū.
4.root: ش-ر-ك (sh-r-k) — partnership, sharing; to associate partners (with Allah)

5.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
5.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

6.meaning: A thing; something or anything. With a negation it commonly amounts to 'nothing at all.'
6.grammar: A singular masculine noun, indefinite ('a thing'). The -an ending (tanwīn fatḥa) is the indefinite accusative, often used here as an object or an adverbial 'in any respect / at all.'
6.root: ش-ي-أ (sh-y-ʾ) — thing, to will

7.meaning: And toward the two parents — directing kindness and good treatment to one's mother and father (the pair of parents).
7.grammar: A dual noun, 'the two parents,' preceded by the preposition bi- ('with/to/toward') and the article 'the,' all joined by wa- ('and'). A dual noun ends in -āni in the nominative but in -ayni in the oblique (the shared genitive/accusative case); after the preposition bi- it is genitive, hence the -ay…ni form here. It denotes exactly two.
7.root: و-ل-د (w-l-d) — to give birth, beget; parent and offspring

8.meaning: Good treatment, excellence, doing what is beautiful and right — acting toward others with kindness, generosity, and the highest moral excellence (iḥsān), going beyond mere duty to genuine goodness.
8.grammar: A verbal noun (the act of doing good). The -an ending (tanwīn fatḥ) marks the indefinite accusative; it often functions adverbially or as an object, conveying 'doing good' or '[show] good treatment' — describing the manner or content of an action.
8.root: ح-س-ن (ḥ-s-n) — to be good, beautiful, excellent

9.meaning: And to the possessor of / the one having — 'and with him who is endowed with' something. A relational word meaning 'owner of / one possessing,' used to attribute a quality or relationship to a person.
9.grammar: A relational noun meaning 'owner/possessor of,' which must be followed by another noun ('possessor OF …'). It declines for case: dhū (nominative), dhī (genitive), dhā (accusative); after the preposition bi- it appears in its genitive form dhī (ending -ī). The wa- prefix means 'and.' This word never stands alone — it always governs a following noun.
9.root: — (a relational noun meaning 'possessor of'; no verbal root)

10.meaning: Nearness, kinship, closeness of relation — the bond of being near in blood, hence 'relatives' or 'near kin'. The word names the quality of family closeness itself.
10.grammar: A noun with the definite article 'al-' (the). It ends in a fixed long -ā (alif maqṣūra) that does not change for case; such words show their grammatical role through context rather than a changing final vowel. The sense is abstract: 'nearness of kin'.
10.root: ق-ر-ب (q-r-b) — to be near, close; nearness, kinship

11.meaning: And the orphans — children who have lost their father (and so lack support). The plural refers to such fatherless children as a group.
11.grammar: 'wa' (and) plus the definite article 'al-' (the). 'yatāmā' is a broken (irregular) plural of 'yatīm' (orphan). It ends in a fixed long -ā that stays the same regardless of grammatical case, so its role is shown by context rather than a final case vowel.

12.meaning: The poor and needy — those in straitened circumstances who lack sufficient means and are humbled by want.
12.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural noun meaning 'the needy', with prefixes wa- 'and' and al- 'the'. The final -i is the genitive ending, which typically links the word to a preceding preposition or to a noun before it ('… of …').
12.root: س-ك-ن (s-k-n) — to be still, to be subdued; one humbled by poverty

13.meaning: And the neighbor — one who dwells nearby, a person living close at hand.
13.grammar: A noun, 'the neighbor,' with the definite article. The -i ending is genitive: the case used when a word follows a preposition or is governed by another noun ('… of …'). The wa- prefix means 'and.'
13.root: ج-و-ر (j-w-r) — to be adjacent, neighbor; nearness of dwelling, also to seek protection

14.meaning: Possessor of / the one having — a relational word meaning 'owner of' or 'endowed with,' used to attach a quality or relationship to the noun it describes.
14.grammar: A relational noun meaning 'owner/possessor of,' which must be followed by another noun ('possessor OF …'). It declines for case: dhū (nominative), dhī (genitive), dhā (accusative). The form dhī (ending -ī) is its genitive, used when it follows a preposition or describes a preceding genitive noun. It never stands alone; it always governs a following noun.
14.root: — (a relational noun meaning 'possessor of'; no verbal root)

15.meaning: Nearness, kinship, closeness of relation — the bond of being near in blood, hence 'relatives' or 'near kin'. The word names the quality of family closeness itself.
15.grammar: A noun with the definite article 'al-' (the). It ends in a fixed long -ā (alif maqṣūra) that does not change for case; such words show their grammatical role through context rather than a changing final vowel. The sense is abstract: 'nearness of kin'.
15.root: ق-ر-ب (q-r-b) — to be near, close; nearness, kinship

16.meaning: And the neighbor — one who dwells nearby, a person living close at hand.
16.grammar: A noun, 'the neighbor,' with the definite article. The -i ending is genitive: the case used when a word follows a preposition or is governed by another noun ('… of …'). The wa- prefix means 'and.'
16.root: ج-و-ر (j-w-r) — to be adjacent, neighbor; nearness of dwelling, also to seek protection

17.meaning: The distant one / the stranger — one who is remote, kept at a distance, or unrelated. On the pattern fuʿul, this is a distinct word from janb ('side/flank'), though both share the root meaning of 'side' (hence 'one set aside, far off').
17.grammar: A noun on the pattern fuʿul with the definite article, meaning 'the one who is distant / a stranger.' The -i ending is genitive: the case used after a preposition, when the second term of a possessive, or when describing a preceding genitive noun. (Distinct from janb, 'side/flank,' which shares the same root.)
17.root: ج-ن-ب (j-n-b) — side, flank; to be aside, to keep at a distance; hence remoteness, being a stranger

18.meaning: And the companion — one who keeps company, an associate or fellow who accompanies another.
18.grammar: An active participle used as a noun, 'the one who accompanies / the companion,' with the definite article (the l- assimilates into the following ṣ, written ṣ-ṣ). The -i ending is genitive: the case used after a preposition or when governed by another noun. The wa- prefix means 'and.'

19.meaning: At the side / alongside — 'by one's side,' indicating close physical or relational proximity, being adjacent or near at hand.
19.grammar: A noun, 'the side,' governed by the preposition bi- ('at/by') with the definite article. The -i ending is genitive, the case a noun takes after a preposition; the whole phrase functions adverbially to mean 'alongside / at the side.'
19.root: ج-ن-ب (j-n-b) — side, flank; nearness, adjacency

20.meaning: Son of — used in the construction 'son of the road' (ibn al-sabīl), an idiom for the traveller or wayfarer.
20.grammar: A masculine noun, 'son', with the prefix wa- 'and'. The initial alif carries a connecting hamza (hamzat al-waṣl): its helping vowel is not pronounced here because the preceding wa- runs straight into the word, so it reads 'wab-' in connected speech. The final -i is the genitive ending, which typically links the word to a preceding preposition or to the following noun in a possessive chain ('son OF …').
20.root: ب-ن-و / ب-ن-ي (b-n-w / b-n-y) — to build; son, offspring

21.meaning: The way, road, or path — a route one travels; very often used figuratively for a course of life, conduct, or the path of religion. The attached article makes it definite: 'the way'.
21.grammar: al- is the definite article 'the' (its 'l' assimilates to the following 's', heard as 'as-sabīl'). The final -i is the genitive ending, marking the word as joined to a preceding noun ('… OF the way') or governed by a preposition.

22.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
22.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

23.meaning: It/she possessed, owned, or held in ownership — a completed act of having something under one's control or right.
23.grammar: A past-tense verb with the feminine ending -at: 'she/it possessed'. The -at marks completed action by a feminine singular subject. In the idiom 'what your right hands have possessed', the feminine subject is the (grammatically feminine) 'right hands'.
23.root: م-ل-ك (m-l-k) — to own, possess, hold sway

24.meaning: Your (plural) right hands — literally the right hands, used idiomatically for solemn oaths and for lawful possession or authority. With the suffix: 'your right hands'.
24.grammar: A plural noun carrying the nominative -u ending, which typically marks it as the subject (the doer) of a verb. The suffix -kum is the attached possessive pronoun 'your' (plural masculine). The plural can mean 'right hands' or 'oaths', and the phrase 'what your right hands possess' is an idiom for those under one's lawful charge.
24.root: ي-م-ن (y-m-n) — right hand/side; oath; good fortune

25.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
25.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

26.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
26.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.
26.root: — (proper name)

27.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
27.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

28.meaning: He loves / likes / holds dear. To have affection for and approval of something or someone.
28.grammar: A present-tense verb in the fourth pattern, third-person masculine singular ('he…'). The yu- prefix signals a single masculine subject, and the final -u ending marks the indicative mood, presenting the action as an established fact or ongoing reality.
28.root: ح-ب-ب (ḥ-b-b) — love, affection; to hold dear

29.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
29.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

30.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

30.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.
30.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existence; to be

31.meaning: One who is self-admiring and strutting with conceit; a person puffed up with arrogance who carries himself proudly and looks down on others. It is an intensive form denoting a settled, swaggering vanity.
31.grammar: An active participle (form VIII) naming the doer of the action: 'one who behaves with conceit.' The final '-an' (tanwīn fatḥa) marks the indefinite accusative case, typically used for the object of a verb or the predicate after certain particles, and lending the sense 'a … (one).'
31.root: خ-ي-ل (kh-y-l) — imagining, fancying; vain self-display and conceit

32.meaning: One given to boasting and bragging; a person who loudly vaunts his own merits and possessions. The form is intensive, denoting someone habitually and excessively boastful.
32.grammar: An intensive adjective (the faʿūl pattern) signifying one who does something to a high degree: 'a constant boaster.' The final '-an' marks the indefinite accusative, used for an object or predicate and giving the sense 'a … (one).'
32.root: ف-خ-ر (f-kh-r) — pride, glorying, boasting of one's own excellence

1.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
1.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

2.meaning: They are stingy, they hold back and refuse to give — to be tight-fisted and withhold what one has, especially from others in need.
2.grammar: A present-tense verb, third person masculine plural ('they withhold'). The -ūna ending does double duty: the -ū marks 'they' (a group of males) and the final -na marks the indicative mood, the plain form used for stating an ongoing or habitual fact.
2.root: ب-خ-ل (b-kh-l) — stinginess, withholding, miserliness

3.meaning: And they command, order, or bid — expressing the act of instructing others to do something, often with the sense of urging good conduct.
3.grammar: A present-tense verb. The wa- prefix means 'and'. The base ya- prefix marks third person ('he/they'), and the -ūna ending marks a masculine plural subject ('they') in the present/ongoing tense: 'they command'. This ending signals an unfinished or habitual action by a group of males.

4.meaning: Mankind, humanity, people in general — the collective of human beings.
4.grammar: A definite noun ('the people') with the attached 'al-' ('the'). The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 'n' (a sun letter), which is why the 'n' is doubled — this is a pronunciation effect, not a separate piece. The final '-a' ending is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb (the one being acted upon) or the subject of certain particles.
4.root: ن-و-س (n-w-s) — to move/sway; by extension, people

5.meaning: Miserliness and tight-fistedness — the withholding of wealth or good where it is due. The phrase carries the sense 'with/by stinginess.'
5.grammar: A preposition 'bi' (with/by) joined to the definite noun 'al-bukhl' (the stinginess). After the preposition the noun takes the genitive case, shown by the final '-i'; the genitive is the case regularly required after a preposition.

6.meaning: They conceal or keep hidden — to suppress something and not disclose it, hiding it deliberately from view or knowledge.
6.grammar: A present-tense verb prefixed with 'wa' (and). The 'ya-…-ūna' frame marks a third-person masculine plural acting now or habitually: 'they conceal.' The retained 'na' (the '-ūna' ending) signals the indicative mood, i.e. a plain statement of fact rather than a command or a negated/subjunctive form.
6.root: ك-ت-م (k-t-m) — concealing, suppressing, keeping secret

7.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
7.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

8.meaning: He gave / granted / bestowed upon them — to bring, hand over, or confer (a gift or favour) to someone.
8.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in Form IV ('to give/bestow'). With no subject suffix, it is third-person masculine singular ('he did'). The attached object pronoun 'them' (here voweled '-humu' to connect to the next word) gives 'he bestowed upon them.'
8.root: ا-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (Form IV) to bring, give, bestow

9.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
9.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

10.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
10.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

11.meaning: 'His bounty / grace / favor' — faḍl is overflowing generosity, an extra goodness given beyond what is owed; with the attached pronoun it means the bounty belonging to Him (Allah).
11.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive pronoun '-hi' ('his/His'). The -i vowel before the pronoun is the genitive case, which typically appears after a preposition or links the noun to what follows in an 'of' relationship; here it carries through to the possessor.
11.root: ف-ض-ل (f-ḍ-l) — excess, surplus; hence bounty, grace, superiority

12.meaning: And We have made ready — to prepare, arrange, and set something in store beforehand so it stands waiting.
12.grammar: A past-tense verb (form VIII) prefixed with 'wa' (and). The 't' in the stem is the form VIII infix, not a root letter. The suffix '-nā' is the subject ending meaning 'we (did it),' marking a completed action performed by a first-person plural — an act already accomplished.
12.root: ع-د-د (ʿ-d-d) — counting, reckoning; readying and setting in store (form VIII اعتدّ, with the doubled dāl, from this root)

13.meaning: A three-part word: 'for' + 'the' + 'those who cover up the truth / reject faith.' The base noun denotes the kāfir — one who disbelieves, denies, and ungratefully conceals the truth and Allah's favor. With 'for,' it marks them as the ones for whom something is intended.
13.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('for/to') joined to a definite plural noun, masculine. The '-īna' ending is the sound masculine plural in its genitive/accusative (oblique) form, here required because it follows the preposition 'li-'. The whole denotes 'for the disbelievers.'
13.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal, disbelieve, be ungrateful

14.meaning: 'A punishment / torment.' A noun naming chastisement or painful suffering inflicted as a penalty.
14.grammar: A masculine noun. The -an ending marks it as indefinite ('a punishment') and in the accusative case — the form a noun takes as the object of a verb or as the thing being described/quantified.

15.meaning: Disgracing and degrading — that which humiliates and brings abasement, stripping away honor and dignity.
15.grammar: An active participle (form IV) naming what causes the action: 'something that humiliates.' The final '-an' (tanwīn fatḥa) marks the indefinite accusative case, used for an object or as a describing word in that case, giving 'a humiliating (one).'
15.root: ه-و-ن (h-w-n) — lowliness, disgrace; to abase or render contemptible

1.meaning: 'And those who': a connective phrase introducing a specified group of people (masculine plural) about whom something will be said. It links them to what came before.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'), which is masculine plural. A relative pronoun stands for a group and is normally followed by a clause describing them. Its form does not change for case; it stays alladhīna whatever its grammatical role.

2.meaning: 'They spend/give out': to expend wealth or provision, especially by giving it away in charity and in good causes. The word centers on disbursing what one has rather than hoarding it.
2.grammar: A present/future-tense verb in Form IV (anfaqa, 'to spend, expend'). The imperfect prefix is only yu-; the nūn that follows is the first root letter (of ن-ف-ق), not part of the prefix. The yu- prefix together with the -ūna ending marks the subject as 'they' (masculine plural) doing the action now or habitually. The -ūna ending also signals the indicative mood, the default 'plain' form used for ongoing or repeated action.
2.root: ن-ف-ق (n-f-q) — to spend, expend, give out

3.meaning: 'Their wealth / their possessions' — property, riches, and goods belonging to a group of males or a mixed group.
3.grammar: A plural noun (the plural of 'māl', wealth) carrying the -a accusative ending, which marks it as the object of a verb or otherwise governed into the accusative. The attached -hum means 'their', referring to a masculine or mixed group.

4.meaning: Showing off, ostentation, or doing something to be seen by people — performing an act for the sake of others' eyes and praise rather than sincerely.
4.grammar: A verbal noun of Form III, conveying mutual seeing — acting so as to be observed by others. The '-a' ending is accusative; in this pattern it often expresses purpose or motive ('out of / for the sake of showing off').
4.root: ر-ا-ي (r-ʾ-y) — to see, to be seen

5.meaning: Humankind, people, mankind — the collective of human beings.
5.grammar: A collective noun ('people, mankind') carrying the definite article al- ('the'); the 'l' of the article assimilates into the following 'n', doubling it (al-nās → an-nās). The genitive ending -i marks the word as governed by a preposition or as the second term of a possessive.
5.root: ء-ن-س (ʾ-n-s) — humankind, sociability, familiarity; the word for 'people' is most commonly traced to this root (related to insān, 'human being')

6.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
6.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

7.meaning: 'They believe / they have faith' — to affirm something as true with trusting inner conviction and to feel secure in it. The verb carries both believing and being at peace through that belief; in religious use it is to commit oneself in faith.
7.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb, masculine plural. The yu-…-una frame means 'they (men, or a mixed group) do' the action now or habitually. The retained final -na marks the indicative (a plain, unqualified statement) — 'they believe' — as opposed to forms where that -na drops. The verb is Form IV (amana), used intransitively here meaning simply 'to believe / to have faith'.

8.meaning: A phrase 'in Allah / by Allah', combining the preposition 'with/in/by' and the divine name Allah, the proper name of the One God.
8.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with, by means of') prefixed to the divine name Allah. A preposition always forces the following noun into the genitive case, which is why Allah here ends in -i. With verbs of believing, bi- conveys the object of faith — to believe IN.
8.root: — (Allah is the proper name of God and is not derived from a triliteral root in the usual sense)

9.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
9.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

10.meaning: The Day — a span of time; in religious usage it commonly points to the appointed Day (the Last Day, the Day of Resurrection and Judgment). The phrase reads 'in/by the Day.'
10.grammar: A preposition 'bi' (in/by) joined to the definite noun 'al-yawm' (the day). The noun is in the genitive case — shown by the final '-i' — because a noun following a preposition is regularly put in the genitive.
10.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day; a defined period of time

11.meaning: An adjective meaning 'the last,' 'the latter,' or 'the final' — that which comes at the end of a sequence. It is the common counterpart to 'the first,' and is often used as a name for the world or life to come (the Hereafter, the Last Day), i.e. the ultimate end of all things.
11.grammar: An active-participle-type adjective on the pattern fāʿil. It carries the definite article 'al-' ('the'). The final -i is the genitive case, signaling that the word is governed by a preceding preposition or particle, or stands as the second term of a possessive link ('… of …'). It is masculine singular.
11.root: ء-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — to be last, to come after, to defer / postpone

12.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
12.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

13.meaning: He/it is or comes to be — a verb of being expressing existence or a state. This is a shortened (jussive) form of the verb 'to be.'
13.grammar: A present-tense verb of being in the shortened (jussive) mood, which drops the final vowel — typically after a particle of negation or condition — to give 'is/was (not),' or 'should be.' The closing '-i' here is not a case ending but a helper vowel added to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a cluster.
13.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

14.meaning: Shayṭān / Satan — a rebellious, malevolent being who incites to evil; the term denotes one that is remote from goodness and given to misleading. With 'al-', it points to the well-known devil.
14.grammar: 'al-' is 'the' (its 'l' assimilates into the 'sh', doubling it). 'shayṭān' is a noun for a devil or inciter of evil. The final -u is nominative, the form a word takes as the subject or doer of an action.

15.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
15.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

16.meaning: A close associate or constant companion — one who keeps another's company and is paired with him, whether a comrade or an attached fellow.
16.grammar: A noun on the faʿīl pattern denoting one joined to another: 'a companion.' The final '-an' (tanwīn fatḥa) marks the indefinite accusative case, used for the object of a verb or the predicate after certain verbs of being, giving 'a companion.'
16.root: ق-ر-ن (q-r-n) — joining, coupling, linking two things together

17.meaning: Then how evil/wretched it is! — a fixed expression of blame and condemnation declaring something to be exceedingly bad.
17.grammar: A past-tense verb used to express dispraise, meaning 'how evil it is!' Prefixed with 'fa' (then/so), which links it as a consequence. As a verb of blame it functions as a frozen exclamation rather than an ordinary statement of a past event.
17.root: س-و-ء (s-w-ʾ) — evil, badness, harm; that which is wretched

18.meaning: A close associate or constant companion — one who keeps another's company and is paired with him, whether a comrade or an attached fellow.
18.grammar: A noun on the faʿīl pattern denoting one joined to another: 'a companion.' The final '-an' (tanwīn fatḥa) marks the indefinite accusative case, used for the object of a verb or the predicate after certain verbs of being, giving 'a companion.'
18.root: ق-ر-ن (q-r-n) — joining, coupling, linking two things together

1.meaning: And what? — a combination meaning 'and what thing?', used to ask about or point to a matter. It can open a question ('what is it that…?') or introduce an emphatic 'what.'
1.grammar: An interrogative compound: the question-word 'mā' (what) joined with 'dhā' (this/that which), together asking 'and what is it that…?' Being particles/pronouns, the words carry no case endings; the form is invariable.

2.meaning: A compound meaning 'upon them' or 'against them': the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over, against') joined to the plural pronoun 'them'. It conveys something resting on, being incumbent upon, or weighing against a group.
2.grammar: ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay- before a pronoun. The suffix -him is the attached pronominal suffix for a masculine plural group ('them'); after a preposition it carries genitive/prepositional force, and the -i- vowel reflects its position after this preposition. Together they signal a relationship of something being over, upon, or burdensome to that group.
2.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

3.meaning: A conditional particle introducing a hypothetical or contrary-to-fact supposition: 'if (it were the case that…)'. It typically presents a condition that is unfulfilled or merely imagined, often implying the result did not or would not happen.
3.grammar: An indeclinable particle (no case ending). It signals a hypothetical 'if': it sets up a supposed condition whose consequence is then stated, frequently with the sense 'if X were so, then Y would be so' — often where X is contrary to fact.

4.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
4.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

5.meaning: A phrase 'in Allah / by Allah', combining the preposition 'with/in/by' and the divine name Allah, the proper name of the One God.
5.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with, by means of') prefixed to the divine name Allah. A preposition always forces the following noun into the genitive case, which is why Allah here ends in -i. With verbs of believing, bi- conveys the object of faith — to believe IN.
5.root: — (Allah is the proper name of God and is not derived from a triliteral root in the usual sense)

6.meaning: "And the Day" — a stretch of time, a day; also used for the appointed Day of Judgement and Resurrection. The opening element is the conjunction 'and'.
6.grammar: A masculine singular noun with the definite article 'the' and the conjunction 'and'. The final -i is the genitive case ending: it typically signals that the word is linked to a preceding noun ('… of …') or governed by a preposition or oath particle.
6.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day / period of time

7.meaning: An adjective meaning 'the last,' 'the latter,' or 'the final' — that which comes at the end of a sequence. It is the common counterpart to 'the first,' and is often used as a name for the world or life to come (the Hereafter, the Last Day), i.e. the ultimate end of all things.
7.grammar: An active-participle-type adjective on the pattern fāʿil. It carries the definite article 'al-' ('the'). The final -i is the genitive case, signaling that the word is governed by a preceding preposition or particle, or stands as the second term of a possessive link ('… of …'). It is masculine singular.
7.root: ء-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — to be last, to come after, to defer / postpone

8.meaning: And they spent or laid out — to disburse wealth, expending it (especially in giving and charitable outlay).
8.grammar: A past-tense verb (form IV) prefixed with 'wa' (and). The suffix '-ū' is the subject ending for a third-person masculine plural — 'they (did it)' — marking a completed action carried out by a group.

9.meaning: From what / from that which — a fusion of the preposition 'from' with the relative 'what/which', introducing the thing or situation being referred to.
9.grammar: A merger of 'min' ('from') and 'mā' ('what/that which'); the 'n' of 'min' assimilates into the 'm' of 'mā', doubling it. The combination means 'from what ...' and typically introduces a following clause describing the thing referred to. Being particles, neither part takes a case ending.

10.meaning: He provided/granted them sustenance — to bestow provision and the means of life upon someone, the giving coming from the Provider.
10.grammar: A past-tense verb. The '-a' on the stem marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he provided'), and the attached '-hum(u)' is the object pronoun 'them.' The base vowel of that pronoun is shifted to '-humu' to smooth the join with a following word.
10.root: ر-ز-ق (r-z-q) — provision, sustenance, the bestowing of livelihood

11.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
11.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

12.meaning: And he was / he became — a verb of being that places a subject in a past state or links it to a description in the past.
12.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'kāna' is a past-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular, meaning 'he was/became'; it commonly introduces a past condition and is typically followed by a noun describing the subject's state. The final -a marks completed past action by a single male.

13.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
13.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

14.meaning: An expression meaning 'at them' or 'with them' — the preposition 'bi' (with, by, at) joined to the pronoun 'them' (a group). The exact shade ('at/by/with them') depends on the verb it accompanies.
14.grammar: A preposition (bi-, 'with/by/at') with the attached pronoun -him ('them,' for a group of males). The pronoun is in the genitive, the case always required after a preposition.

15.meaning: All-Knowing; one possessing complete, perfect knowledge. As an intensive form it conveys knowledge that is total and unfailing, encompassing all things.
15.grammar: An intensive adjective ('all-knowing') on the faʿīl pattern, which stresses the quality to its fullest degree. The -an (tanwīn) joins the -a accusative ending — typical of a predicate or object — with the -n marking it indefinite.

1.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
1.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

2.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
2.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.
2.root: — (proper name)

3.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
3.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

4.meaning: He wrongs or deals unjustly — to commit injustice, to put something out of its right place, or to deprive another of what is due.
4.grammar: A present-tense verb. The 'ya-' prefix marks a third-person masculine singular doing something now or habitually ('he wrongs'), and the final '-u' marks the indicative mood — a plain statement of fact rather than a command or a subjunctive/jussive form.
4.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — wrongdoing, injustice, oppression; misplacing a thing

5.meaning: The weight or measure of something — the amount that balances against it on a scale; figuratively even the tiniest equivalent quantity.
5.grammar: A noun denoting a unit of weight: 'the weight of.' The final '-a' marks the accusative case, here typical of a noun functioning as the object of a verb. It also stands as the first term of a possessive pairing ('weight OF …'), in which a following noun is read in the genitive.
5.root: ث-ق-ل (th-q-l) — weight, heaviness; that which weighs in a balance

6.meaning: A tiny particle — a mote, a speck of dust, the smallest ant; proverbially the least conceivable amount of matter.
6.grammar: A singular noun (the unit-noun of 'specks'). The final '-in' (tanwīn kasra) marks the indefinite genitive — 'of a speck' — the form a noun takes when it follows another noun in a possessive pairing or comes after a preposition.
6.root: ذ-ر-ر (dh-r-r) — minute particles; motes of dust scattered in the air

7.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
7.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

8.meaning: It/she is or comes to be — a verb of being expressing existence or a state, in a shortened form of the verb 'to be.'
8.grammar: A present-tense verb of being in the shortened (jussive) mood. The 'ta-' prefix marks a third-person feminine singular (or 'it') subject. The jussive drops the final vowel — and here even the final 'n' of 'takun' falls away — giving the clipped sense 'is/was (not),' a form occurring after particles of negation or condition.
8.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

9.meaning: Something good, fine, or beautiful; a good deed, a benefit, or a blessing. As a noun it denotes a good thing or good fortune.
9.grammar: A feminine singular noun/adjective (the -a marks feminine gender). The final -tan (tanwīn fatḥa) marks it as indefinite ('a good thing') and in the accusative case, typically used for the direct object of a verb or as the thing requested/described.
9.root: ح-س-ن (ḥ-s-n) — to be good, beautiful, fine

10.meaning: He multiplies or increases it manifold — to compound a thing several times over, giving back far more than the original.
10.grammar: A present-tense verb (form III) with the 'yu-' prefix marking a third-person masculine singular subject ('he multiplies'). The stem is in the shortened (jussive) mood, its final consonant left vowelless ('-if') as occurs after a conditional particle. The attached '-hā' is the object pronoun 'it' (referring to a feminine noun).
10.root: ض-ع-ف (ḍ-ʿ-f) — doubling, multiplying; increase by like amounts

11.meaning: And He gives or grants — to bestow and hand over something to someone.
11.grammar: A present-tense verb (form IV) prefixed with 'wa' (and); the 'yu-' marks a third-person masculine singular ('he gives'). It stands in the shortened (jussive) mood: for this weak-ending verb the jussive is shown by dropping the final long vowel, leaving the bare '-ti' instead of 'yuʾtī.'
11.root: ا-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — coming; in this form, bringing or giving

12.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
12.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

13.meaning: From with Him / from His presence — an expression denoting immediate nearness and direct source, 'from right beside Him' or 'out of His own bestowal.'
13.grammar: An invariable adverb of place meaning 'in the presence of / right by,' here joined to the pronoun '-hu' (him) to give 'from His side/presence.' As a fixed adverb it takes no case ending; the suffix '-hu' is a possessive/attached pronoun referring to a masculine singular.
13.root: — (invariable adverb of place; no triliteral root)

14.meaning: A reward, wage, or recompense — the return earned for work or conduct, whether worldly pay or otherworldly recompense.
14.grammar: A noun meaning 'a reward.' The final '-an' (tanwīn fatḥa) marks the indefinite accusative case, the case used for the object of a verb (e.g. of 'to give'), giving the sense 'a reward.'
14.root: ا-ج-ر (ʾ-j-r) — reward, wage, recompense for what one does

15.meaning: 'Great, immense, mighty, momentous.' It describes something vast in size, weight, or seriousness, and is often used of grave or awe-inspiring matters.
15.grammar: An adjective on the intensive faʿīl pattern. The -an ending is the indefinite accusative ('a great …'), commonly marking an adjective that agrees with an indefinite accusative noun it describes, or the object of a verb.

1.meaning: So how? / Then in what manner or state? — kayfa is the interrogative 'how', asking after the manner, condition or circumstance of something. With the prefixed 'so/then' it introduces a question following from what precedes, often expressing wonder or warning.
1.grammar: An interrogative particle ('how') carrying the connective prefix fa- ('so / then'), which links it to a preceding statement as a consequence or follow-up. As a particle, kayfa is indeclinable: its fixed final -a is not a case ending and does not change.

2.meaning: 'When' — a particle introducing a time or circumstance, generally pointing to something expected or definite to come ('when/whenever it happens'). It sets up a condition or moment whose outcome then follows.
2.grammar: An indeclinable adverb/particle of time; it has no case ending and never changes form. It typically introduces a clause about a future or recurring event ('when …'), and is normally followed by a verb describing what takes place.
2.root: — (a time particle; no triliteral root)

3.meaning: We came / We brought — to arrive, or to bring something forward and present it.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb. The suffix '-nā' is the subject ending meaning 'we (did it),' marking a completed action performed by a first-person plural — something already brought about.

4.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
4.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

5.meaning: 'every,' 'each,' or 'all' — a word expressing totality or completeness. It indicates the entirety of something: when joined to a singular indefinite noun it means 'every (single) one,' and when joined to a definite noun it can mean 'all of' or 'the whole of.'
5.grammar: A noun of totality. The final '-i' ending is genitive (the 'of/possession' case): it marks the word as governed by a preceding preposition or as the first term of a possessive link to a following noun, so it typically reads 'of every…' or 'every…' leading into what follows.

6.meaning: A community, nation, or people — a body of people bound together by shared faith, way of life, or origin; one collective group.
6.grammar: A feminine noun. The final -in (genitive with 'nunation') marks it as indefinite ('a community') and links it to a preceding noun or preposition ('… of a community'). The feminine -t sound surfaces before the ending.
6.root: ء-م-م (ʾ-m-m) — community, way, intent

7.meaning: A witness — one who testifies to what he has seen or knows; also one present and observing. The faʿīl form can carry an intensive sense ('ever-witnessing').
7.grammar: A preposition 'bi' (with) joined to the noun 'shahīd' (a witness); the construction 'come with (someone)' yields 'bring (a witness).' The final '-in' (tanwīn kasra) marks the indefinite genitive, the case a noun takes after a preposition.
7.root: ش-ه-د (sh-h-d) — witnessing, being present, bearing testimony

8.meaning: And We came / and We brought — to arrive, or to bring something forward and present it.
8.grammar: A past-tense verb prefixed with 'wa' (and). The suffix '-nā' is the subject ending meaning 'we (did it),' marking a completed action performed by a first-person plural.

9.meaning: With You / in You — the preposition 'with/by/in' joined to the pronoun 'You' (addressing a single person), expressing reliance upon or recourse to that person.
9.grammar: The preposition bi- ('with/in/by') with the attached pronoun -ka ('you', addressing one male). Pronouns following a preposition take this object form.

10.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
10.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

11.meaning: These / those — a plural demonstrative pointing to a group of people or things. Its core sense is the near demonstrative 'these', but it is very commonly rendered 'those' in translation when the group it points to has already been described or named rather than being physically present.
11.grammar: A plural demonstrative pronoun, used for a group of either gender. Its base value is near-deixis ('these'), built from an attention-drawing prefix 'hā-' ('lo!, here') plus the base 'ulāʾi'. In practice it is often translated 'those' when the referent is already mentioned or understood rather than literally nearby. Its form is fixed and does not change for grammatical case; it points to a group rather than naming it.

12.meaning: 'A witness' — one who sees and attests, who can give evidence; also carries the sense of one who is present and observant, and at times 'a martyr' (one who bears witness with their life).
12.grammar: An intensive describing-noun (pattern fa‘īl) meaning 'a witness, one who fully attests', indefinite. The -an ending (the accusative with 'tanwīn') marks it as indefinite and in the accusative — the case used for a direct object, or for a word that describes the state or role in which someone stands.

1.meaning: On that day / that day — pointing back to a particular past day already in view; 'a day, at that time.'
1.grammar: A time-word ('day') joined to 'idhin' ('at that time'), together meaning 'on that day.' The '-in' ('tanwīn') compensates for an understood clause ('the day when…'). The form functions adverbially, locating an event at a specific past moment.

2.meaning: He/it wishes, longs for, or would dearly love something — an inward yearning, often tinged with what one would prefer if given the choice.
2.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it'). On its own the form is ya-wadd-u: the ya- prefix marks the 'he/it' subject and the final -u is the indicative mood, signalling a plain ongoing or repeated action ('wishes / keeps wishing') as opposed to a command or a clipped/subjunctive form. The ya- here carries a shadda (doubled: yy) because a preceding word's final n-sound assimilates into it (idgham), fusing into the ya rather than adding a separate letter; the underlying verb itself begins with a single ya. The stem doubles its own final consonant (wadd) as a feature of this root.
2.root: و-د-د (w-d-d) — affection, love, fond wishing

3.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
3.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

4.meaning: 'They disbelieved / rejected faith' — from a root meaning to cover over or conceal. To disbelieve in this sense is to cover up and refuse the truth, and also to be ungrateful, hiding or denying favours received.
4.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third person masculine plural: 'they disbelieved'. The completed action is built into the stem kafara ('he disbelieved'), and the -ū suffix (written وا) marks the doer as 'they' (masculine plural). The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention with no sound.
4.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to reject faith, be ungrateful

5.meaning: And they rebelled, defied, or disobeyed — they refused to comply with a command or authority.
5.grammar: A past-tense verb with the wa- prefix meaning 'and'. The plural ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they did' the action); because the root ends in a weak letter, the usual -ū surfaces as -aw before the silent spelling alif. Past tense presents the act as completed.

6.meaning: The messenger, envoy, or emissary: one who is sent with a message; in the Qur'an typically a prophet sent by Allah bearing revelation to a people.
6.grammar: A noun on the form faʿūl (an intensive/agent pattern, 'one sent'), prefixed with al- ('the'). The final -a ending is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb ('… the messenger') or the subject of certain particles. The 'l' of al- assimilates into the following 'r' (a 'sun letter'), pronounced ar-rasūl.
6.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — sending, dispatching a message

7.meaning: A conditional particle introducing a hypothetical or contrary-to-fact supposition: 'if (it were the case that…)'. It typically presents a condition that is unfulfilled or merely imagined, often implying the result did not or would not happen.
7.grammar: An indeclinable particle (no case ending). It signals a hypothetical 'if': it sets up a supposed condition whose consequence is then stated, frequently with the sense 'if X were so, then Y would be so' — often where X is contrary to fact.

8.meaning: It is made level, smoothed flat, or evened out — brought to an even surface, as ground levelled to the earth.
8.grammar: A present-tense passive verb (the subject undergoes the action rather than doing it). The tu- prefix with the inner vowel pattern marks the passive ('is being made…'), and the third-person feminine singular agrees with an 'it/she' subject. The final -ā reflects the weak final root letter in this passive form.

9.meaning: 'By/with them' or 'for them' — the preposition bi ('with, by, through, for') joined to the attached pronoun 'them' (a masculine group).
9.grammar: The preposition bi- ('with, by, for') attached to the pronoun -him ('them', masculine plural). The final -u is a connecting vowel added so the word joins smoothly to whatever follows. The preposition naturally puts its pronoun in the genitive.

10.meaning: A noun meaning 'the earth', 'the ground', or 'the land' — the terrestrial world, the soil and land surface as opposed to the sky.
10.grammar: A noun with the definite article 'al-' ('the'). The -u ending is nominative, which typically marks the word as the subject of a sentence (the one doing the action). This noun is grammatically feminine.

11.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
11.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

12.meaning: They conceal, hide, or keep something hidden — deliberately suppressing knowledge or truth and withholding it from others.
12.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine plural ('they …'). The ya-…-ūna frame marks an ongoing or habitual present action; the final -ūna (with the retained final nūn) is the indicative mood, the form used for a plain statement of fact.
12.root: ك-ت-م (k-t-m) — to conceal, hide, keep secret

13.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
13.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

14.meaning: A piece of speech, an account, a report, or a narrated statement — something said or related; the word also carries the sense of something new or newly arising.
14.grammar: A singular indefinite noun. The -an ending (tanwīn with an 'a' vowel) marks the accusative case while signalling 'a/some' (indefinite). The accusative is the case of a direct object or of a noun governed by certain particles, so it commonly reads as the receiver of an action.
14.root: ح-د-ث (ḥ-d-th) — to happen anew, to relate/narrate speech

1.meaning: 'O…!' — a compound vocative expression used to call out and summon an audience before addressing them. It fuses the call-particle 'yā' ('O') with a noun that means 'the one(s) addressed,' yielding an emphatic 'O you…!' that introduces direct address.
1.grammar: A vocative (calling) construction. 'Yā' is the particle for calling out; 'ayyu' carries a nominative '-u' as the one being summoned; 'hā' is an attention-drawing particle. Together they function as 'O you…!,' setting up the noun of address that follows.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
3.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

4.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
4.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

5.meaning: You (plural) approach, draw near to, or come close to something — physically nearing it or, by extension, engaging in or attempting it.
5.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ta- prefix marks a second-person subject ('you'), and the -ū ending makes it masculine plural ('you all'). With the short, vowelless ending (rather than -ūna), this jussive/subjunctive form is the shape used after particles of prohibition or command — i.e. the form for 'do not approach' or 'so that you approach'.

6.meaning: The ritual prayer (ṣalāh): the prescribed formal worship of standing, bowing, and prostrating before Allah at appointed times. As a verbal noun it also carries the underlying sense of calling upon, supplicating, and blessing.
6.grammar: A definite feminine noun. The -a ending is accusative: it generally marks the word as the direct object of a verb (the thing being acted upon, e.g. that which is established or performed), or the object of certain particles.
6.root: ص-ل-و (ṣ-l-w) — prayer, worship, supplication

7.meaning: And you / while you (all) — the conjunction 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'you' (masculine plural), often introducing an accompanying circumstance ('while you …').
7.grammar: The conjunction wa- joined to the detached subject pronoun 'you all' (masculine). This standalone pronoun stands as a subject or for emphasis; it has a fixed form and does not change for case. With wa- it can mark a simultaneous state ('and you / while you').

8.meaning: Intoxicated ones, those who are drunk — people overcome by drink so that their senses are clouded.
8.grammar: A plural adjective/noun describing a group as 'drunk'. It follows the broken-plural pattern fuʿālā, used for adjectives of state or affliction (like 'sick' or 'dead'). The -ā ending belongs to this fixed plural pattern; the word does not take ordinary case endings.

9.meaning: 'Until / up to the point that; so that' — a particle marking a limit or goal. It expresses the end-point reached ('until') or the purpose aimed at ('so that, in order that').
9.grammar: A particle indicating a goal or limit. When followed by a present-tense verb it places that verb in the subjunctive mood (clipping its ending to -a), conveying 'until / so that' something comes about. Ḥattā itself is invariable.

10.meaning: You (plural) know, understand, or have knowledge of something — grasping a fact with certainty.
10.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ta- prefix marks a second-person subject ('you'), and the -ū ending makes it masculine plural ('you all'). The short, vowelless -ū (not -ūna) is the jussive/subjunctive shape, used after particles of command, negation, or purpose ('until you know' / 'so that you know').

11.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
11.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

12.meaning: You say / do you say — to utter or declare in speech, addressed to a group ('you all'), presented as ongoing or habitual.
12.grammar: Present-tense verb. The 'ta-' prefix with the '-ūna' ending marks 'you' (masculine plural) speaking now or habitually. The full '-ūna' ending signals the indicative mood — a plain statement or question, not a command.

13.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
13.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

14.meaning: In a state of major ritual impurity — the condition requiring a full ritual washing before prayer; describing someone as 'sexually impure' in the technical religious sense.
14.grammar: A noun/adjective of state. The -an ending (tanwīn 'a') marks the accusative case and indefiniteness. The accusative is commonly used for a circumstantial state — describing the condition someone is in while something else happens ('being in a state of impurity').

15.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
15.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

16.meaning: Ones who pass through or cross over — passers-by, those merely traversing a place rather than stopping in it.
16.grammar: An active participle in the masculine plural, naming the doer of the act ('those who cross'). The -ī ending is the plural marker in its 'construct' shape — the form a sound masculine plural takes when it is joined to a following noun, where the final -na is dropped, leaving -ī. It thus links to a following noun meaning '… of …'.
16.root: ع-ب-ر (ʿ-b-r) — to cross over, pass through, traverse

17.meaning: A way, road, or path — a route one travels; by extension a course, means, or manner of proceeding.
17.grammar: A singular indefinite noun. The -in ending (tanwīn 'i') marks the genitive case together with indefiniteness ('a way'). The genitive typically appears after a preposition or as the second noun in a possessive link ('… of a way'/'a way of …').

18.meaning: 'Until / up to the point that; so that' — a particle marking a limit or goal. It expresses the end-point reached ('until') or the purpose aimed at ('so that, in order that').
18.grammar: A particle indicating a goal or limit. When followed by a present-tense verb it places that verb in the subjunctive mood (clipping its ending to -a), conveying 'until / so that' something comes about. Ḥattā itself is invariable.

19.meaning: You (plural) wash yourselves fully, perform a complete bath — cleansing the whole body with water.
19.grammar: A present-tense verb in a reflexive pattern (Form VIII), meaning the subject washes their own self. The ta- prefix marks a second-person subject ('you') and -ū makes it masculine plural. The short, vowelless -ū (not -ūna) is the jussive/subjunctive shape, used after particles of negation or purpose ('until you wash' / 'so that you wash').
19.root: غ-س-ل (gh-s-l) — washing, bathing, cleansing

20.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
20.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

21.meaning: A past-tense verb of 'being' addressed to a group: 'you (all) were', 'you (all) used to be'. From kāna, the core verb 'to be'. With a following predicate it often means 'you were (in a state of) …' or 'you used to …'.
21.grammar: This is a past-tense verb. The '-tum' suffix is the attached subject marker for a masculine plural 'you all'. Since the doer is built into the suffix, the verb stands in its base past form ('you all were').
21.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

22.meaning: Sick or ill ones — those suffering bodily ailment or disease.
