22.grammar: A plural adjective/noun meaning 'the sick'. It follows the broken-plural pattern faʿlā used for states of affliction. The -ā ending belongs to this fixed plural pattern and does not change for ordinary case.

23.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
23.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

24.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
24.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

25.meaning: A journey, travel, a trip away from home — the act or state of traveling.
25.grammar: A verbal noun (masdar). The ending -in (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('a journey') and in the genitive case, the form taken after a preposition such as 'on/upon.'
25.root: س-ف-ر (s-f-r) — to travel, journey; to uncover

26.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
26.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

27.meaning: He/it came, arrived, or came about — the act of coming into presence or of something occurring.
27.grammar: A past-tense verb with no prefix and no personal suffix, naming a completed act by a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it came'). All three letters here are root letters: jā spells the first radical plus the lengthened weak middle radical, and the final hamza (ء) is the third root consonant — not an ending. The fatḥa (-a) on that hamza is simply the past-tense vocalization for a 'he' subject sitting on the last root letter; there is no separable suffix.

28.meaning: One, a single one, anyone — denotes an individual unit; in negative or questioning contexts it often means 'anyone at all'.
28.grammar: An indefinite noun. The '-un' ending (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('one'/'anyone') and in the nominative case, the form typically used for the subject of a sentence.
28.root: ء-ح-د (ʾ-ḥ-d) — oneness, a single one

29.meaning: 'From you / among you (plural)' — indicating a part taken out of, or belonging to, a group of people being addressed.
29.grammar: The preposition min ('from, of, among') joined to the attached pronoun -kum ('you all,' masculine plural). Together they express partition or origin: a part drawn 'from / among' the addressed group.

30.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
30.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

31.meaning: Low or sunken ground; by polite usage a euphemism for the place one relieves oneself (the privy), since such places were sought in low-lying spots.
31.grammar: A definite singular noun ('the…'). The al- prefix is the definite article 'the'. The final -i ending marks the genitive case, the case used after a preposition or in a possessive link ('… of the …').
31.root: غ-و-ط (gh-w-ṭ) — low-lying ground, a depression in the land

32.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
32.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

33.meaning: You (plural) touched, had contact with, or (as a delicate idiom) were intimate with — mutual touching between parties.
33.grammar: A past-tense verb in the mutual/reciprocal pattern (Form III), which adds the sense of doing something with or to another party. The suffix -tum marks a second-person masculine plural subject ('you all did'); its final vowel appears here as -tumu to ease pronunciation before the next word.
33.root: ل-م-س (l-m-s) — touching, feeling by hand, contact

34.meaning: 'The women' — the plural of 'woman' (a suppletive plural drawn from a different stem); women collectively.
34.grammar: A definite plural noun ('the women'). It is a suppletive plural — its singular comes from a different stem (imraʾa, 'woman'). This word is a diptote (mamnūʿ min al-ṣarf): it never takes tanwīn and uses -a for BOTH the accusative and the genitive, so it ends in -a even after a preposition (where an ordinary noun would take -i). The final -a here is therefore the diptote ending, marking the accusative as a direct object — but note it would remain -a, not -i, in the genitive too. (The 'l-' is the assimilated 'the', merging with the following n-.)

35.meaning: A two-part device meaning 'did not …' — it combines 'and/then so' with a negating word that turns a present-tense verb into a flat statement that something did NOT happen in the past.
35.grammar: A connecting particle fa- ('and so / then') joined to the negative particle lam. Lam negates the past: it precedes a present-tense verb but flips its meaning to 'did not do', and it puts that following verb into the jussive (clipped) form.

36.meaning: You (all) find, come upon, or obtain something. The verb covers both locating something searched for and finding oneself in a state or circumstance.
36.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ta- prefix marks a second-person subject ('you'), and the -ū ending makes it plural ('you all'). The shortened spelling (dropping the final nūn) shows it is in the jussive/subjunctive mood, the form used after particles like 'lam' (did not) or 'not'.
36.root: و-ج-د (w-j-d) — to find, to obtain, to find oneself in a state

37.meaning: 'water' — water in general, the fluid essential to life; also used for liquid such as rain. A basic noun for the substance of water.
37.grammar: An indefinite noun. The '-an' ending (tanwīn al-fatḥ) marks the accusative case together with indefiniteness — commonly the role of a direct object, the thing acted upon (e.g. what is sent down or brought).

38.meaning: Then betake yourselves to clean earth (for purification) — perform tayammum, the dry cleansing with pure earth or dust that substitutes for washing with water; literally 'aim for / seek out' something.
38.grammar: A command (imperative) verb prefixed with fa- ('then/so'). It uses the Form V pattern (doing something to/for oneself, hence 'direct yourselves toward'). The -ū ending addresses a masculine plural 'you all', instructing the group to perform the action.
38.root: ي-م-م (y-m-m) — to aim for, head toward, intend a destination

39.meaning: The surface of the earth; clean ground, dust, or fine soil — the upper face of the land.
39.grammar: A singular indefinite noun. The -an ending (tanwīn 'a') marks the accusative case with indefiniteness ('some ground'). The accusative is the case of a direct object or of a noun governed by certain verbs and particles.
39.root: ص-ع-د (ṣ-ʿ-d) — to rise / ascend; the surface that rises uppermost

40.meaning: Good, wholesome, pure, and pleasant — fine in quality and free of impurity; agreeable to the senses.
40.grammar: A singular indefinite adjective. The -an ending (tanwīn 'a') marks the accusative case with indefiniteness. As an adjective it agrees with and describes a noun in the same case; the accusative shows that the noun it describes is itself accusative.

41.meaning: So wipe over / pass the hand across (a surface) — to stroke or rub something lightly, as in wiping a body part during purification.
41.grammar: A command (imperative) verb prefixed with fa- ('so/then'). The -ū ending addresses a masculine plural 'you all', instructing the group to perform the wiping. The opening vowel of the stem is written with a connecting alif that drops in pronunciation after the prefix.
41.root: م-س-ح (m-s-ḥ) — to wipe, stroke, pass the hand over

42.meaning: With/over your (plural) faces — the face being the front of the head; combined here with the sense 'with' or 'upon'.
42.grammar: A noun phrase: the preposition bi- ('with/over') + a plural noun ('faces') + the attached pronoun -kum ('your', masculine plural). The -i vowel before -kum is the genitive case forced by the preposition bi-, and the pronoun shows possession by a group ('your').
42.root: و-ج-ه (w-j-h) — face, front, direction one faces

43.meaning: And your (plural) hands — the hand/forearm; joined with 'and'.
43.grammar: A noun phrase: the connector wa- ('and') + the plural noun 'hands' (a broken plural of 'hand') + the attached pronoun -kum ('your', masculine plural). The pronoun -kum shows possession by a group; the noun's form reflects the genitive/accusative shape of this irregular plural.

44.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
44.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

45.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
45.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

46.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

46.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

47.meaning: One who pardons abundantly — who effaces and lets go of faults, blotting out wrongs as if they never were; an intensive describing a constant, generous pardoner.
47.grammar: An intensive adjective on the faʿūl pattern, which conveys that the quality is possessed to a high or constant degree ('ever-pardoning'). The -an ending (tanwīn 'a') marks the accusative case with indefiniteness, the case used for a direct object or as the predicate after certain particles.
47.root: ع-ف-و (ʿ-f-w) — to pardon, efface, forgive and overlook

48.meaning: A word meaning 'much-forgiving' or 'ever-forgiving' — an intensive form describing one whose forgiveness is abundant and constant. It is one of the qualities of Allah.
48.grammar: An intensive adjective on the pattern faʿūl, conveying that the quality is great in degree and repeated. The ending -an is the accusative case with tanwīn (the indefinite 'n' sound), written with a supporting alif; it is the form an indefinite word takes when it is, for example, a predicate of certain verbs/particles or otherwise placed in the object position.

1.meaning: 'Did not…?' — a particle combining a question with negation, used to ask 'Have I/has he not…?', often expecting agreement or serving as a gentle reminder.
1.grammar: An interrogative prefix 'a-' ('?') joined to the negation 'lam'. 'lam' negates a verb and places it firmly in the past ('did not'), and grammatically puts the following present-tense verb into the jussive (clipped) form. Together they form a rhetorical or confirming question.

2.meaning: You see, perceive, or take notice; to observe with the eye, or by extension to come to know or consider. Often used to draw attention, as in 'have you considered…?'
2.grammar: A present-tense verb addressed to a single male 'you,' marked by the 'ta-' prefix. The root's weak final letter has dropped, leaving the short final -a; this shortened form is the jussive/apocopated form, which appears after certain particles (such as 'did not' or in questions like 'have you not seen?').
2.root: ر-أ-ي (r-ʾ-y) — to see, perceive, consider, form an opinion

3.meaning: 'To / toward / up to' — a preposition marking the endpoint, goal, or limit of an action or motion: the direction something moves toward or the boundary at which it stops.
3.grammar: An invariable preposition. It has no case ending of its own but puts the noun that follows it into the genitive ('of / to' state). It indicates direction toward, or the terminal limit of, something.

4.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
4.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

5.meaning: They were given / granted — the passive past tense of the verb 'to give/bring' (form IV of ʾ-t-y), where a plural group receives something without the giver being named.
5.grammar: Passive past tense. The internal vowelling (u-...-u) marks it as passive — the subject receives the action rather than doing it. The '-ū' ending means 'they', giving 'they were given' (the giver left unmentioned).
5.root: ا-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (form IV) to bring or give

6.meaning: A portion / a share / an allotted part: a fixed amount or lot assigned to someone — what falls to them as their due share. Indefinite ('a portion').
6.grammar: An indefinite noun. The ending -an does two things at once: the final -n (nunation) marks it indefinite ('a portion'), and the -a vowel is the accusative case, which commonly marks the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon) or specifies amount/respect.
6.root: ن-ص-ب (n-ṣ-b) — to set up/allot; a fixed share/portion

7.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
7.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

8.meaning: 'The Book / the Scripture' — a written record or revealed scripture; literally that which is written.
8.grammar: The definite article al- with the noun kitāb ('book, scripture'), itself a verbal noun from 'to write.' The -i ending is genitive, typically marking the word as following a preposition or standing in an 'of' relationship to a preceding noun.

9.meaning: A verb meaning 'they buy / they trade / they exchange' — to acquire something by giving up something else in return. It often carries the sense of a bad bargain when one trades away something precious.
9.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) form-VIII verb, 3rd-person masculine plural ('they'). The ya-…-ūna frame marks 'they', and the inseparable -ūna suffix shows the base (indicative) form, expressing an ongoing or habitual act of buying/exchanging.
9.root: ش-ر-ي (sh-r-y) — to buy, sell, trade, exchange (a transaction)

10.meaning: Error, straying, being lost — the state of having wandered off the right path or away from truth and guidance. The opposite of being rightly guided.
10.grammar: A feminine noun carrying 'the' (al-). The final -a ending is accusative, the case that typically marks the object of a verb (the thing acted upon) — e.g., the thing bought, sought, or received.
10.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to go astray, lose the way, err

11.meaning: And they want, intend, will, or desire — a purposeful wanting that aims at and seeks to bring something about.
11.grammar: A present-tense verb (Form IV, conveying purposeful willing) with wa- ('and'). The yu- prefix marks a third-person subject and the -ūna ending makes it masculine plural ('they'). The full -ūna ending is the indicative mood, signalling a plain ongoing or repeated action ('they want / keep wanting'), not a command or a clipped form.
11.root: ر-و-د (r-w-d) — to seek, will, intend, desire

12.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
12.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

13.meaning: A verb meaning 'you go astray, you stray, you lose the right path or wander off course' — addressed to a group. It conveys deviating from correct guidance, whether literally or in belief and conduct.
13.grammar: An imperfect (present/future) verb. The ta- prefix marks a second-person subject ('you'), and the -ū ending makes it plural ('you all'). The form lacks the final nūn (taḍillūna), which signals a subjunctive or jussive mood — the verb is governed by a preceding particle such as 'so that not' or 'lest', expressing purpose or warning rather than a plain statement.
13.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to go astray, lose the way, err

14.meaning: 'The way, the path, the road' — used both for a physical route and, very commonly, for the figurative 'path' of right conduct, religion, or a course of action.
14.grammar: A definite noun: the al- prefix means 'the'. The final -a is the accusative ending, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon) or signals an adverbial sense.

1.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
1.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
1.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

2.meaning: 'I know' — a present-tense verb of knowing: to have certain knowledge or awareness of something.
2.grammar: A present/future (Form I) verb, first-person singular ('I'), marked by the prefix a-. This a- is the first-person agreement marker built into the conjugation, not a free-standing pronoun. The final -u marks the indicative — a plain statement of ongoing or habitual knowing.
2.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — knowing, knowledge

3.meaning: 'About / concerning your enemies' — built on a noun meaning 'enemies, adversaries, those hostile to you', joined to a preposition and a 'your (plural)' possessive.
3.grammar: A noun phrase introduced by the preposition bi- ('with/about'). 'Aʿdāʾ' is a plural noun ('enemies'). The -i ending is genitive, which is the case required after a preposition. The attached -kum is a possessive pronoun meaning 'your' for a group.

4.meaning: 'And He suffices / is enough' — to be sufficient, adequate, and fully enough so that nothing more is needed. It conveys complete adequacy, often used to affirm that Allah alone is enough.
4.grammar: The connective wa- ('and') prefixed to a 3rd-person masculine singular perfect (past-tense) verb (Form I) whose final weak root letter (the yāʾ) appears as a long -ā. It states a completed yet timeless fact — 'and He is sufficient' — the kind of perfect form used for an enduring truth.
4.root: ك-ف-ي (k-f-y) — to suffice, be enough, be adequate; to spare someone need of anything else

5.meaning: A phrase 'in Allah / by Allah', combining the preposition 'with/in/by' and the divine name Allah, the proper name of the One God.
5.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with, by means of') prefixed to the divine name Allah. A preposition always forces the following noun into the genitive case, which is why Allah here ends in -i. With verbs of believing, bi- conveys the object of faith — to believe IN.
5.root: — (Allah is the proper name of God and is not derived from a triliteral root in the usual sense)

6.meaning: 'A protector, ally, guardian, patron' — one who is close to another and takes charge of their care, support, and protection; the bond it implies is loyalty and guardianship.
6.grammar: An indefinite noun. The -an ending (tanwīn) marks the accusative case and indefiniteness ('a protector'), often functioning as a direct object or, with verbs of being/sufficing, as a predicate or specifier describing in what capacity something stands.
6.root: و-ل-ي (w-l-y) — to be near, to be an ally, to take charge of

7.meaning: 'And He/it suffices, is enough, is sufficient' — a verb expressing that someone or something is fully adequate and needs nothing added.
7.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third-person masculine singular ('he/it sufficed'), preceded by the connector wa- ('and'). The final long -ā is the root's weak final letter, characteristic of this verb's base form; it carries no separate case ending. Such verbs often introduce a following noun in the accusative naming the capacity in which the subject suffices.
7.root: ك-ف-ي (k-f-y) — to suffice, to be enough

8.meaning: A phrase 'in Allah / by Allah', combining the preposition 'with/in/by' and the divine name Allah, the proper name of the One God.
8.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with, by means of') prefixed to the divine name Allah. A preposition always forces the following noun into the genitive case, which is why Allah here ends in -i. With verbs of believing, bi- conveys the object of faith — to believe IN.
8.root: — (Allah is the proper name of God and is not derived from a triliteral root in the usual sense)

9.meaning: 'A helper, supporter, one who gives aid and victory' — an intensive form stressing reliable, effective help.
9.grammar: An indefinite noun on an intensive pattern (faʿīl) that conveys a strong or constant doer — 'a true helper'. The -an ending marks the accusative and indefiniteness, commonly used here as a specifier naming the capacity ('as a helper').
9.root: ن-ص-ر (n-ṣ-r) — to help, to aid, to give victory

1.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
1.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: 'They became Jews / adopted Judaism', or in the verb's wider sense 'they turned (back) in repentance'. A completed act by a group of taking on the way of the Jewish community.

parts.en: became Jews / turned back (past, masc. plural)

3.grammar: A past-tense verb from a hollow root. The whole form hādū is already 3rd-person masculine plural ('they turned/became Jews'): the long ū plus the final silent alif are the plural marker, so no separate ending is split off. The action is presented as completed; the root carries the idea of turning toward or returning, from which the sense 'to follow Judaism' derives.
3.root: ه-و-د (h-w-d) — turning back, returning; hence following Judaism

4.meaning: 'They alter, distort, twist, tamper with' — an intensive verb describing deliberately shifting words or meanings away from their correct sense. It is said of a group (third person, 'they') acting repeatedly.

parts.en: he / they — third-person present-tense subject marker

4.grammar: An imperfect (present/future) verb in an intensive (form II) pattern that adds force or deliberateness to 'distort'. The yu- prefix plus the -ūna ending mark a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'). The retained final nūn (-ūna) marks the indicative mood — a plain ongoing statement of fact.
4.root: ح-ر-ف (ḥ-r-f) — edge, to turn aside, to distort

5.meaning: 'The word(s), speech, utterance' — a collective noun for words or statements taken as speech, especially weighty or revealed words.
5.grammar: A definite collective noun ('the words/speech'); the al- prefix means 'the'. The final -a is the accusative ending, typically marking the word as the direct object of a verb (the thing being acted upon).

6.meaning: A preposition meaning 'on behalf of,' 'for,' 'about,' or 'away from.' It often conveys removing a burden from someone or acting in their place.

parts.en: on behalf of / for / away from

6.grammar: A preposition (a linking particle). It governs the noun that follows it, putting that noun into the genitive case. It does not change form.

7.meaning: 'Its proper places, its positions, the spots where it belongs' — a plural noun for locations or settings, joined to an 'its/his' possessive.
7.grammar: A plural noun of place (pattern mafāʿil) meaning 'places/positions'. The -i ending is genitive, the case used when a noun is possessed by a following pronoun or governed by a preposition. The attached -hi is a possessive pronoun, 'its/his'.
7.root: و-ض-ع (w-ḍ-ʿ) — to put, to place, to set down

8.meaning: A verb meaning 'and they say / and they keep saying' — to utter or assert in speech. The structure presents an ongoing or repeated act of speaking by a group.
8.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) verb joined by wa- ('and'). The ya-…-ūna frame marks the 3rd-person masculine plural ('they'); the full -ūna ending is the inseparable indicative-plural suffix, showing the verb is in its base (indicative) form and expressing an ongoing or habitual action.

9.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'we heard / we listened' — the act of perceiving sound or a message, often carrying the further nuance of heeding or taking in what was said.
9.grammar: A completed (past-tense) verb. The attached ending -nā marks the subject as 'we', so the action is something a group did and finished: 'we heard'.

10.meaning: 'And we disobeyed, we rebelled, we defied (a command)' — a past-tense verb of refusing to obey, with 'we' as the actor.
10.grammar: A past-tense verb preceded by the connector wa- ('and'). The suffix -nā marks a first-person plural subject ('we'). The base verb has a weak final letter (seen as -ay- before the ending), characteristic of this root.
10.root: ع-ص-ي (ʿ-ṣ-y) — to disobey, to rebel, to defy

11.meaning: 'And hear! / and listen!' — a command to a single person to hear or pay attention.
11.grammar: An imperative (command) verb addressed to one person, preceded by the connector wa- ('and'). The helping initial vowel (the 'i' of is-) is added because the root's first letter carries no vowel of its own, and the bare, vowelless ending (-ʿ) is the standard form for a command given to a single male addressee.

12.meaning: 'Other than / different from / not'. A noun used to express difference or negation — 'something other than X', and so 'not-X'. It functions to exclude or contrast with what follows.
12.grammar: A noun of difference/exception. The -a ending marks the accusative case, the form it takes when it serves as a direct object or as a descriptive substitute standing in an object position; it governs a following noun in the genitive ('other than …'). That it takes case endings and tanwīn confirms it is a true noun, not a particle.
12.root: غ-ي-ر (gh-y-r) — to be other, different; otherness, change

13.meaning: A passive participle that can mean 'one who is made to hear' or 'something heard'. It also occurs in a pointed idiom of speech meaning roughly 'may you not be made to hear' — i.e. words framed as a blessing but twistable into an insult.
13.grammar: An indefinite passive participle (from a causative form: 'made to hear'). The -in ending (tanwīn) marks the genitive case together with indefiniteness — the genitive is the case used after a preposition or in a possessive link.

14.meaning: 'And tend us / regard us / give us heed' — a command meaning 'attend to us, watch over us, mind us'. The same sounds can be twisted into a mocking insult, which is why its use is significant.
14.grammar: An imperative (command) verb addressed to a single person, preceded by the connector wa- ('and'). The attached -nā is an object pronoun meaning 'us'. The base 'rāʿi' is a command from a verb of caring/heeding; the final -i reflects its weak final letter once the object pronoun is attached.
14.root: ر-ع-ي (r-ʿ-y) — to tend, to pasture, to look after, to heed

15.meaning: 'A twisting, a bending, a distortion' — a verbal noun for the act of warping something, especially twisting the tongue/words to bend a meaning.
15.grammar: An indefinite verbal noun ('twisting'). The -an ending marks the accusative and indefiniteness, a case commonly used to express manner or the reason/circumstance of an action ('by way of twisting').
15.root: ل-و-ي (l-w-y) — to twist, to bend, to turn

16.meaning: 'With/by their tongues' — the noun 'tongues' (the organs of speech, hence speech itself), joined to a preposition and a 'their' possessive.
16.grammar: A noun phrase opened by the preposition bi- ('with/by'). 'Alsina' is a plural noun ('tongues'). The -i ending is genitive, the case required after a preposition and before a possessive pronoun. The attached -him means 'their' for a group.
16.root: ل-س-ن (l-s-n) — tongue, language

17.meaning: 'And a stabbing / a defaming / an attack' — a verbal noun whose literal sense is 'piercing, thrusting' and which extends to verbally attacking, slandering, or maligning.
17.grammar: An indefinite verbal noun preceded by the connector wa- ('and'). The -an ending marks the accusative and indefiniteness, here functioning to name an action set alongside another ('and a defaming…').
17.root: ط-ع-ن (ṭ-ʿ-n) — to pierce, to stab, to defame, to attack

18.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
18.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

19.meaning: A term for 'the religion, the faith, the way of life and obedience owed to Allah'. It covers belief, worship, law, and the system of accountability and recompense — broader than the English word 'religion'.
19.grammar: A definite noun ('the religion'); the al- prefix means 'the'. The -i ending is genitive, the case used after a preposition or in a possessive link ('… of …').
19.root: د-ي-ن (d-y-n) — religion, judgment, requital, obedience, debt

20.meaning: 'and if' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the particle 'if'. This particular 'if' (law) introduces a hypothetical or contrary-to-fact condition: 'if (such-and-such had been the case)…', often implying it was not.
20.grammar: A conjunction plus a conditional particle. wa- means 'and'. law is a non-changing particle (no case ending) that sets up a supposition, typically answered by a clause beginning with la- ('… then certainly …').

21.meaning: 'That they…' — an emphatic connector 'anna' ('that, indeed') fused with the pronoun 'they,' used to introduce an affirmed clause as the content of a thought or statement.
21.grammar: Built on the particle 'anna' ('that…, indeed'), which introduces and affirms a following clause (often after verbs of knowing, thinking, or saying) and puts its noun into the accusative. The attached '-hum' is the pronoun 'they/them' for a male-inclusive group.

22.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
22.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.

23.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'we heard / we listened' — the act of perceiving sound or a message, often carrying the further nuance of heeding or taking in what was said.
23.grammar: A completed (past-tense) verb. The attached ending -nā marks the subject as 'we', so the action is something a group did and finished: 'we heard'.

24.meaning: "and we obeyed / and we have complied" — wa- joins it on; the verb means to obey, submit to, and willingly comply with a command.
24.grammar: A past-tense verb with the subject suffix -nā meaning 'we.' Past tense presents the action as already completed ('we obeyed'); the -nā ending shows 'we' are the ones who did it.

25.meaning: 'And hear! / and listen!' — a command to a single person to hear or pay attention.
25.grammar: An imperative (command) verb addressed to one person, preceded by the connector wa- ('and'). The helping initial vowel (the 'i' of is-) is added because the root's first letter carries no vowel of its own, and the bare, vowelless ending (-ʿ) is the standard form for a command given to a single male addressee.

26.meaning: 'And look at us / wait for us / regard us' — a command to a single person to direct attention to, or wait for, 'us'.
26.grammar: An imperative (command) verb addressed to one person, preceded by the connector wa- ('and'), with the object pronoun -nā ('us') attached. The helping initial vowel (the 'u' of un-) appears because the root's first letter is vowelless; the verb's bare jussive form (without final vowel) is the standard shape of a singular command.
26.root: ن-ظ-ر (n-ẓ-r) — to look, to see, to wait, to regard

27.meaning: 'Surely it would have been / it certainly was' — the verb 'to be' (past tense) carrying an emphatic 'surely', often introducing the result of a hypothetical condition.

parts.en: it was / it would have been

27.grammar: The past-tense verb kāna ('was/were'), third-person masculine singular, with the emphatic prefix la- ('surely'). In conditional sentences this combination commonly heads the consequence clause ('then it surely would have been…'). The verb kāna typically takes a following predicate in the accusative describing the subject's state.
27.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to become

28.meaning: Good — that which is beneficial, virtuous, and excellent; goodness as a thing one can do or possess, and what is better or preferable.
28.grammar: A noun (also serving as the 'better/best' form). The final -an (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite and in the accusative case — the case used for the direct object of a verb ('to do good') and for similar governed roles.
28.root: خ-ي-ر (kh-y-r) — good, beneficial, choice, excellence

29.meaning: 'For them / to them / theirs' — a preposition 'for / to / belonging to' joined to the pronoun 'them,' expressing that something pertains, belongs, or is owed to that group.
29.grammar: The preposition li- ('for / to / belonging to'), whose vowel becomes -a before an attached pronoun, joined to -hum ('them'). It commonly expresses possession or benefit — 'theirs / for them.' Particles like this carry no case or tense of their own.

30.meaning: 'And more upright / more proper / more sound / more fitting' — a comparative form from a root meaning straightness and correctness, so 'straighter, more rightly set'.
30.grammar: A comparative/superlative adjective (pattern afʿal: 'more/most upright'), preceded by the connector wa- ('and'). The final -a is the accusative ending. Adjectives on this afʿal pattern do not take tanwīn (the 'n' sound), so the accusative shows as a plain -a; it commonly serves as a predicate or describes a stated thing.
30.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, to be upright, straightness, to set right

31.meaning: 'But / however / yet' — a particle of correction and contrast that sets aside what came before and affirms something different instead.
31.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') attached to lākin ('but / however'). Lākin is a particle of rectification: it draws a contrast with, or corrects, the preceding idea and introduces an opposing or qualifying statement ('... but rather...').

32.meaning: To curse, to cast away from mercy — for Allah, to expel from His grace and blessing; for others, to invoke such removal. It signifies banishment from divine compassion.
32.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third-person masculine singular ('he cursed') — the bare stem with an -a ending marks a completed act by a single masculine subject. The attached -hum is the object 'them'; its vowel appears as -humu before a following word.
32.root: ل-ع-ن (l-ʿ-n) — to curse, banish from mercy

33.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
33.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

34.meaning: On account of disbelief or ingratitude — the act of covering over and rejecting truth, refusing faith. Kufr is both the denial of belief and ingratitude toward what is given.
34.grammar: A noun ('disbelief') preceded by the preposition bi- ('with/because of') and ending in -i, the genitive case that regularly follows a preposition. The attached -him means 'their,' linking the disbelief to a group.
34.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; disbelief, ingratitude

35.meaning: A two-part word: the connective particle 'fa-' meaning 'so', 'then', or 'therefore' (drawing a consequence from what precedes), joined to 'lā', the particle of negation/prohibition. Together they convey 'so do not …' or 'so there is no …'.
35.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that links a clause to what came before and often signals a result or consequence. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a present-tense verb it commonly forms a prohibition ('do not …') or a simple negation ('not'). It carries no ending of its own.

36.meaning: 'They believe / they have faith' — to affirm something as true with trusting inner conviction and to feel secure in it. The verb carries both believing and being at peace through that belief; in religious use it is to commit oneself in faith.
36.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb, masculine plural. The yu-…-una frame means 'they (men, or a mixed group) do' the action now or habitually. The retained final -na marks the indicative (a plain, unqualified statement) — 'they believe' — as opposed to forms where that -na drops. The verb is Form IV (amana), used intransitively here meaning simply 'to believe / to have faith'.

37.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
37.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

38.meaning: 'A little / a small amount' — an adjective/noun meaning small in quantity, few, scant, or trifling.
38.grammar: A noun/adjective 'little' in the accusative case with indefinite marking (the -an ending, tanwīn). The accusative commonly marks an object or specifies amount/manner; the doubled -n sound marks it as indefinite, 'a little.'
38.root: ق-ل-ل (q-l-l) — fewness; being little, scant, or small in amount

1.meaning: 'O…!' — a compound vocative expression used to call out and summon an audience before addressing them. It fuses the call-particle 'yā' ('O') with a noun that means 'the one(s) addressed,' yielding an emphatic 'O you…!' that introduces direct address.
1.grammar: A vocative (calling) construction. 'Yā' is the particle for calling out; 'ayyu' carries a nominative '-u' as the one being summoned; 'hā' is an attention-drawing particle. Together they function as 'O you…!,' setting up the noun of address that follows.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: They were given / granted — the passive past tense of the verb 'to give/bring' (form IV of ʾ-t-y), where a plural group receives something without the giver being named.
3.grammar: Passive past tense. The internal vowelling (u-...-u) marks it as passive — the subject receives the action rather than doing it. The '-ū' ending means 'they', giving 'they were given' (the giver left unmentioned).
3.root: ا-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (form IV) to bring or give

4.meaning: The Book, the Scripture — a written revelation; the term for a divinely revealed text.
4.grammar: A definite noun ('the Book') with attached 'al-' ('the'). The final '-a' ending is the accusative case, typically marking the word as the direct object of a verb.
4.root: ك-ت-ب (k-t-b) — to write; a writing, book

5.meaning: 'Believe!' — a command to a group: have faith, trust, and affirm. Built on the verb meaning to attain security and to believe, it calls people to embrace faith.
5.grammar: A command (imperative) verb on the causative (Form IV) pattern, from the verb meaning 'to believe / to have faith'. The -ū ending directs the command to a second-person masculine plural audience, 'you all — believe!'.

6.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
6.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.
6.root: — (particle + relative pronoun)

7.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'We sent down', 'We revealed', 'We caused to descend' — the form (with doubled middle letter) suggests a sending-down done gradually or emphatically, fittingly used of revelation.
7.grammar: This is a past-tense verb in an intensive pattern (the doubled middle consonant of nazzala). The '-nā' suffix is the attached subject marker meaning 'we', so the whole word reads 'We sent down'.
7.root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — to descend, to come/send down

8.meaning: Confirming, verifying, attesting to the truth of something — declaring that a thing is true and corroborating it.
8.grammar: An active participle of the intensive (fa''ala) pattern, naming the doer of the action ('one confirming'). The -an ending is the indefinite accusative, often marking a noun as an object or describing the manner/state in which something occurs ('as a confirmer').

9.meaning: To / for that which — a preposition 'to, for' joined to a relative word meaning 'what' or 'that which'.
9.grammar: A combination of the preposition li- ('to, for') with the relative pronoun mā ('that which'). Together they introduce something toward or for which an action is directed; mā itself does not change for case.

10.meaning: An expression meaning 'with you' — combining the word for accompaniment, togetherness, or presence-alongside with the attached pronoun 'you' (a group). It signals being in the company of, or on the side of, the addressed people.
10.grammar: An adverb of accompaniment (maʿa, 'with/in the company of') carrying the attached pronoun -kum ('you,' for a group of males). It expresses togetherness or being alongside the people addressed.

11.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
11.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

12.meaning: A noun/adverb meaning 'before' — denoting that which precedes in time or order.
12.grammar: An adverb/noun of time. The -i ending is genitive, which here arises because it follows a preposition (commonly 'min', 'from'); it characteristically links to a following noun ('before … OF …').
12.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to precede, come before; the front or prior side

13.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
13.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

14.meaning: '(That) we efface, blot out, wipe away, obliterate the features of' — a verb of erasing or smoothing away marks and distinctions, with 'we' as the actor.
14.grammar: An imperfect (present/future) verb whose na- prefix marks a first-person plural subject ('we'). The final -a is the subjunctive ending, which appears after particles meaning 'that / before / so that' and gives the sense of a contemplated or purposed action rather than a flat statement.
14.root: ط-م-س (ṭ-m-s) — to efface, to blot out, to obliterate

15.meaning: 'Faces' — the plural of 'face'. Beyond the literal face, it can stand for a person's self, presence, direction, or favour.
15.grammar: An indefinite plural noun ('faces'). The -an ending (tanwīn) marks the accusative case with indefiniteness, a case that typically identifies the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon).
15.root: و-ج-ه (w-j-h) — face, direction, to face/turn toward

16.meaning: '(That) we turn them back / return them / send them back' — a verb of turning or driving something back to a prior point or direction, with 'we' acting and 'them' (feminine) as the object.
16.grammar: An imperfect verb joined by fa- ('and so/then'), with the na- prefix marking a 'we' subject and the attached -hā meaning 'them' (a feminine plural or singular object). The -a vowel before the pronoun is the subjunctive ending, signalling an action linked in purpose or sequence to a preceding verb rather than a standalone statement.
16.root: ر-د-د (r-d-d) — to turn back, to return, to repel

17.meaning: A preposition meaning 'on, upon, over,' and by extension 'against' or 'incumbent upon.' It can mark something resting on top of, an obligation laid on someone, or being set over/above something.
17.grammar: An indeclinable preposition (its form never changes). It governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case, and conveys location 'on/upon,' or figuratively duty or opposition ('against').

18.meaning: 'Their backs / their rears / what is behind them' — the plural of 'back', joined to a 'their' possessive; used for the hinder parts or the direction behind.
18.grammar: A plural noun ('backs'). The -i ending is genitive, the case used after a preposition or when a noun is possessed by a following pronoun. The attached -hā is a possessive pronoun, 'their/its' (feminine).
18.root: د-ب-ر (d-b-r) — back, rear, to turn the back, what comes behind

19.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
19.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

20.meaning: A first-person plural verb meaning 'we curse / we banish from divine mercy.' To curse, in this sense, is to expel someone far from the favor and good of Allah. The form belongs to Allah's speech in the 'majestic We', with an attached object 'them'.
20.grammar: The na- prefix marks a first-person plural subject ('we'). The final -a vowel on the verb stem is the subjunctive/jussive shape that typically appears when the verb follows a governing particle (such as one meaning 'before' or 'lest'). The suffix -hum is an object pronoun meaning 'them'.
20.root: ل-ع-ن (l-ʿ-n) — to curse, to banish from mercy

21.meaning: 'Just as / in the same way that' — a phrase of comparison joining 'like / as' to 'what', meaning 'like that which...' or 'in the manner that...'.
21.grammar: The comparison particle ka- ('like / as') joined to mā ('what / that which'). Together they introduce a likeness or manner — 'just as...', 'in the same way that...' — comparing one thing or action to another.

22.meaning: A first-person plural past-tense verb: 'we cursed,' i.e. 'we cast out from mercy.' It states a completed act of cursing attributed to the divine 'We'.
22.grammar: This is a past-tense (perfect) verb. The ending -nā attached to the stem marks the subject as 'we' and the action as already completed; the doubled n reflects the verb's final root letter meeting the 'we' ending.
22.root: ل-ع-ن (l-ʿ-n) — to curse, to banish from mercy

23.meaning: Plural of ṣāḥib: 'companions, associates, people belonging to / dwellers of.' It denotes those who keep company with something or are bound to it, hence 'the people of …' or 'the folk of …'.
23.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural noun. The final -a ending is the accusative case; in a possessive chain it also signals that a following noun completes the phrase ('companions OF …'). The accusative typically marks the object of a verb or follows certain particles.

24.meaning: The Sabbath — the sacred day of rest and worship, on which ordinary labour was set aside. Here in an 'of/after a preposition' relationship.

parts.en: Sabbath / day of rest (with the article's 'l' assimilated, plus the genitive vowel -i)

24.grammar: A definite noun: 'al-' is 'the', and because the next letter is a 'sun letter' (س), the article's 'l' sound merges into it, giving 'as-sabt'. The final -i is the genitive case vowel sitting on the noun's own last root letter (ت), not a separate suffix; this vowel appears when the noun follows a preposition or is linked to a preceding noun in an 'of' relationship.
24.root: س-ب-ت (s-b-t) — to rest, cease (from work); the Sabbath

25.meaning: And he was / he became — a verb of being that places a subject in a past state or links it to a description in the past.
25.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'kāna' is a past-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular, meaning 'he was/became'; it commonly introduces a past condition and is typically followed by a noun describing the subject's state. The final -a marks completed past action by a single male.

26.meaning: 'Command, order, affair, matter.' This noun covers both a directive that is commanded and a situation or affair that comes to pass — what is decreed or what is the case.
26.grammar: A singular noun. The final -u ending is the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the thing being described.
26.root: ا-م-ر (ʾ-m-r) — to command; an affair/matter

27.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
27.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

28.meaning: Passive participle of 'to do/make': 'done, carried out, accomplished.' It describes something that has been or will be brought into effect — an act fulfilled rather than left pending.
28.grammar: A passive participle on the pattern mafʿūl ('that which is done'). The ending -an is the indefinite accusative (the final 'tanwīn' n-sound), which commonly marks a predicate, an object, or a descriptive complement.
28.root: ف-ع-ل (f-ʿ-l) — to do, to make, to act

1.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
1.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

2.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
2.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.
2.root: — (proper name)

3.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
3.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

4.meaning: 'He forgives / pardons' — to cover over and wipe away sins, granting protective pardon. The root carries the image of covering a fault so it is no longer held against a person.
4.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he'). The separate final -u is the indicative ending, marking a plain, ongoing statement of fact ('he forgives').

5.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
5.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

6.meaning: A passive verb meaning 'that partners be associated (with Him),' i.e. that anything be set up as an equal or partner alongside Allah. It is the verb at the heart of shirk — ascribing partners to Allah.
6.grammar: A present-tense passive verb. The yu- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it'), and the internal vowelling (u…a) makes it passive ('be associated'). The final -a vowel is the subjunctive, the shape used after governing particles (e.g. 'that …').
6.root: ش-ر-ك (sh-r-k) — to share, to associate as a partner

7.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
7.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

8.meaning: 'And He forgives / and He pardons.' The verb denotes covering over and wiping away sins; ghafr is forgiveness that both conceals the fault and remits its punishment. Prefixed with 'and'.
8.grammar: The wa- prefix means 'and' (sometimes 'but'). The ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'). The final -u vowel marks the indicative, the ordinary present-tense form expressing an ongoing or habitual action ('He forgives').
8.root: غ-ف-ر (gh-f-r) — to forgive, to cover over (sin)

9.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
9.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

10.meaning: An adverb/preposition meaning 'apart from, other than, short of, below.' It points to something falling outside or beneath a named thing — 'aside from X' or 'lesser than X'.
10.grammar: An invariable adverbial noun used like a preposition. It carries a fixed -a ending and governs a following noun in the genitive, yielding the sense 'other than …' or 'short of …'.
10.root: د-و-ن (d-w-n) — to be below, lesser, or beneath

11.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
11.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

12.meaning: 'for whoever / to the one who' — the preposition 'for/to' joined with the relative word 'who', introducing the person(s) about whom something is said.
12.grammar: A preposition ('for/to') combined with the relative/interrogative word 'man' ('who, whoever'). Together they single out a person or group as the focus ('for the one(s) who...').

13.meaning: A present-tense verb meaning 'he wills, he wishes, he chooses' — to want or intend something by one's own decision.
13.grammar: A present/ongoing action by a single masculine subject ('he'); the ya- prefix marks third-person masculine singular, and the final -u marks the indicative mood — a plain statement of fact ('he wills'), as opposed to a command or a verb governed by 'that.'
13.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʾ) — willing, wishing; the root behind 'thing' (shayʾ)

14.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
14.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

15.meaning: An active verb: 'he associates a partner (with Allah),' i.e. he commits shirk by setting up someone or something as an equal or rival to Allah. The doer here is the one ascribing the partner.
15.grammar: A present-tense active verb. The yu- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'). The final consonant carries a silent/sukūn ending (-ik with no vowel), the jussive form that appears after conditional or negating particles (e.g. 'if he …', 'let him not …').
15.root: ش-ر-ك (sh-r-k) — to share, to associate as a partner

16.meaning: A phrase 'in Allah / by Allah', combining the preposition 'with/in/by' and the divine name Allah, the proper name of the One God.
16.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with, by means of') prefixed to the divine name Allah. A preposition always forces the following noun into the genitive case, which is why Allah here ends in -i. With verbs of believing, bi- conveys the object of faith — to believe IN.
16.root: — (Allah is the proper name of God and is not derived from a triliteral root in the usual sense)

17.meaning: 'Then/so, indeed …' — the connector 'then/so' joined to the particle 'qad', which before a past-tense verb stresses that the action has certainly and already happened.
17.grammar: A connecting particle 'fa-' ('then/so', often signalling a result) plus 'qad'. With a following perfect verb, 'qad' emphasises that the act is real and completed ('have indeed …'). The final -i on 'qad' is a helping vowel added to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a cluster; it carries no grammatical meaning of its own.

18.meaning: 'He fabricated, invented, forged (a lie); he concocted falsely' — made something up and falsely attributed it, especially a lie. A verb of deliberate fabrication.

parts.en: connecting (helping) vowel for the verb pattern
past-tense 3rd person masculine singular ending '-ā' (from a weak final root letter)

18.grammar: A past-tense verb, 3rd person masculine singular ('he fabricated'). It is a Form VIII (ifta'ala) verb. The final '-ā' (written as alif maqṣūra) is how the past-tense '-a' ending appears when the root ends in a weak letter (w/y). The initial 'i-' is a helping vowel that lets the consonant cluster of this pattern be pronounced.
18.root: ف-ر-ي (f-r-y) — to fabricate, forge, invent (a falsehood)

19.meaning: Sin — a blameworthy, morally culpable act; deliberate wrongdoing or guilt. The '-an' nunation marks it as indefinite and accusative.
19.grammar: A noun in the indefinite accusative. The '-an' (nunation on the fatḥa, with following alif) marks it as indefinite and accusative — the case typically used for the object of a verb.
19.root: ا-ث-م (ʾ-th-m) — to sin; sin, guilt

20.meaning: 'Great, immense, mighty, momentous.' It describes something vast in size, weight, or seriousness, and is often used of grave or awe-inspiring matters.
20.grammar: An adjective on the intensive faʿīl pattern. The -an ending is the indefinite accusative ('a great …'), commonly marking an adjective that agrees with an indefinite accusative noun it describes, or the object of a verb.

1.meaning: 'Did not…?' — a particle combining a question with negation, used to ask 'Have I/has he not…?', often expecting agreement or serving as a gentle reminder.
1.grammar: An interrogative prefix 'a-' ('?') joined to the negation 'lam'. 'lam' negates a verb and places it firmly in the past ('did not'), and grammatically puts the following present-tense verb into the jussive (clipped) form. Together they form a rhetorical or confirming question.

2.meaning: You see, perceive, or take notice; to observe with the eye, or by extension to come to know or consider. Often used to draw attention, as in 'have you considered…?'
2.grammar: A present-tense verb addressed to a single male 'you,' marked by the 'ta-' prefix. The root's weak final letter has dropped, leaving the short final -a; this shortened form is the jussive/apocopated form, which appears after certain particles (such as 'did not' or in questions like 'have you not seen?').
2.root: ر-أ-ي (r-ʾ-y) — to see, perceive, consider, form an opinion

3.meaning: 'To / toward / up to' — a preposition marking the endpoint, goal, or limit of an action or motion: the direction something moves toward or the boundary at which it stops.
3.grammar: An invariable preposition. It has no case ending of its own but puts the noun that follows it into the genitive ('of / to' state). It indicates direction toward, or the terminal limit of, something.

4.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
4.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

5.meaning: A plural present verb: 'they declare (themselves) pure, they claim purity / praise themselves as righteous.' From the sense of purifying and clearing of fault, it conveys ascribing innocence or sanctity to oneself.
5.grammar: A present-tense verb of the intensive (form II) pattern, meaning to make pure or claim purity. The yu-…-ūna framing marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'); the final -na is the indicative ending, signalling an ordinary, ongoing statement.

6.meaning: A noun meaning 'their own selves' or 'themselves' — the plural of 'nafs' (self, soul, person, inner self), joined to the pronoun 'their.' It commonly conveys the reflexive idea of acting upon one's own self.
6.grammar: A noun (a broken/irregular plural of 'nafs') with the attached possessive pronoun '-hum' ('their/them,' masculine plural). The -a case ending before the pronoun is accusative, typically marking the word as the direct object of a verb — i.e. the self upon which the action falls.
6.root: ن-ف-س (n-f-s) — self, soul, person; breath

7.meaning: Rather / nay, but — a particle that cancels or corrects what came before and introduces a contrasting truth: 'no — instead …'. It sets aside a prior idea and replaces it.
7.grammar: A particle of retraction and correction; it does not change endings on other words. Its base form is 'bal'; the final -i here is a connecting vowel added to ease pronunciation before a following word that begins with a cluster.

8.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
8.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

9.meaning: A singular present verb: 'He purifies, He cleanses, He sanctifies.' It expresses making someone pure of sin and causing them to grow in goodness — a purification granted by Allah.
9.grammar: A present-tense verb of the intensive (form II) pattern. The yu- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'). The final long -ī is the indicative form of this 'weak-ending' verb, expressing an ongoing or habitual action ('He purifies').

10.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
10.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

11.meaning: A present-tense verb meaning 'he wills, he wishes, he chooses' — to want or intend something by one's own decision.
11.grammar: A present/ongoing action by a single masculine subject ('he'); the ya- prefix marks third-person masculine singular, and the final -u marks the indicative mood — a plain statement of fact ('he wills'), as opposed to a command or a verb governed by 'that.'
11.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʾ) — willing, wishing; the root behind 'thing' (shayʾ)

12.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
12.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

13.meaning: They are wronged / treated unjustly — to suffer ẓulm, the placing of something out of its right place: injustice, oppression, being deprived of one's due. The passive form names being on the receiving end of wrongdoing.
13.grammar: Present-tense passive verb, third-person masculine plural. The yu- prefix (with the internal vowelling) marks the third person and the passive 'are being …', and the -ūna ending makes it 'they' (masculine plural) as the ones undergoing the action: 'they are wronged'. The -na is the indicative marker.

14.meaning: 'A fatīl' — the tiny thread or fibre running along the cleft of a date-stone. It is proverbial for something utterly negligible, the smallest conceivable amount.
14.grammar: A singular noun. The ending -an is the indefinite accusative (the 'tanwīn' n-sound), here typically functioning to specify an amount ('by so much as a fatīl'); the accusative commonly marks an object or a quantifying complement.
14.root: ف-ت-ل (f-t-l) — to twist, to spin (a thread)

1.meaning: A command 'look! / consider! / observe!' It directs the listener to turn their gaze or attention toward something, whether with the eye or with the mind.
1.grammar: A singular masculine imperative (command) addressed to 'you'. The helping 'u' at the start lets the cluster be pronounced, and the vowelless final consonant (-ur with sukūn) is the standard imperative ending, issuing a direct order.
1.root: ن-ظ-ر (n-ẓ-r) — to look, to see, to consider

2.meaning: An interrogative meaning 'how?' — asking about the manner, condition, or state of something ('how?', 'in what way?'). It can also express astonishment.
2.grammar: An interrogative particle (kayfa) ending in an invariable -a; it does not change for case. It asks about the manner or state of an action ('how…?') and is sometimes used rhetorically to express wonder or rebuke rather than a genuine question.
2.root: — (interrogative particle; no triliteral root)

3.meaning: They fabricate or invent falsely — to forge a lie, concoct something untrue and attribute it where it does not belong. The verb specifically names inventing falsehood and slander out of nothing.
3.grammar: Present-tense verb in the (form VIII) pattern, third-person masculine plural. The ya- prefix marks the third person and, together with the -ūna ending, yields 'they' (masculine plural) acting in ongoing/present time. The retained -na is the mark of the indicative ('they are fabricating / they fabricate').

4.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
4.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
4.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

5.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
5.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

6.meaning: A noun meaning 'the lie / falsehood' — a deliberate untruth, a fabricated statement that contradicts reality.
6.grammar: A definite masculine noun with the prefix al- ('the'). The final -a marks the accusative case, which most commonly identifies the noun as the direct object — the thing upon which an action (such as saying or inventing) falls.
6.root: ك-ذ-ب (k-dh-b) — to lie, to be false, to deny the truth

7.meaning: 'And He suffices / is enough' — to be sufficient, adequate, and fully enough so that nothing more is needed. It conveys complete adequacy, often used to affirm that Allah alone is enough.
7.grammar: The connective wa- ('and') prefixed to a 3rd-person masculine singular perfect (past-tense) verb (Form I) whose final weak root letter (the yāʾ) appears as a long -ā. It states a completed yet timeless fact — 'and He is sufficient' — the kind of perfect form used for an enduring truth.
7.root: ك-ف-ي (k-f-y) — to suffice, be enough, be adequate; to spare someone need of anything else

8.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
8.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

9.meaning: Sin — a blameworthy, morally culpable act; deliberate wrongdoing or guilt. The '-an' nunation marks it as indefinite and accusative.
9.grammar: A noun in the indefinite accusative. The '-an' (nunation on the fatḥa, with following alif) marks it as indefinite and accusative — the case typically used for the object of a verb.

10.meaning: Active participle: 'clear, plain, manifest, making evident.' It describes something that is itself obvious and that also makes the truth plain to others — both 'evident' and 'evidencing'.
10.grammar: An active participle of the form-IV pattern (mufʿil), meaning 'one that makes clear.' The ending -an is the indefinite accusative (the 'tanwīn' n-sound), which commonly marks a descriptive complement or an object.

1.meaning: 'Did not…?' — a particle combining a question with negation, used to ask 'Have I/has he not…?', often expecting agreement or serving as a gentle reminder.
1.grammar: An interrogative prefix 'a-' ('?') joined to the negation 'lam'. 'lam' negates a verb and places it firmly in the past ('did not'), and grammatically puts the following present-tense verb into the jussive (clipped) form. Together they form a rhetorical or confirming question.

2.meaning: You see, perceive, or take notice; to observe with the eye, or by extension to come to know or consider. Often used to draw attention, as in 'have you considered…?'
2.grammar: A present-tense verb addressed to a single male 'you,' marked by the 'ta-' prefix. The root's weak final letter has dropped, leaving the short final -a; this shortened form is the jussive/apocopated form, which appears after certain particles (such as 'did not' or in questions like 'have you not seen?').
2.root: ر-أ-ي (r-ʾ-y) — to see, perceive, consider, form an opinion

3.meaning: 'To / toward / up to' — a preposition marking the endpoint, goal, or limit of an action or motion: the direction something moves toward or the boundary at which it stops.
3.grammar: An invariable preposition. It has no case ending of its own but puts the noun that follows it into the genitive ('of / to' state). It indicates direction toward, or the terminal limit of, something.

4.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
4.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

5.meaning: They were given / granted — the passive past tense of the verb 'to give/bring' (form IV of ʾ-t-y), where a plural group receives something without the giver being named.
5.grammar: Passive past tense. The internal vowelling (u-...-u) marks it as passive — the subject receives the action rather than doing it. The '-ū' ending means 'they', giving 'they were given' (the giver left unmentioned).
5.root: ا-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (form IV) to bring or give

6.meaning: A portion / a share / an allotted part: a fixed amount or lot assigned to someone — what falls to them as their due share. Indefinite ('a portion').
6.grammar: An indefinite noun. The ending -an does two things at once: the final -n (nunation) marks it indefinite ('a portion'), and the -a vowel is the accusative case, which commonly marks the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon) or specifies amount/respect.
6.root: ن-ص-ب (n-ṣ-b) — to set up/allot; a fixed share/portion

7.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
7.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

8.meaning: 'The Book / the Scripture' — a written record or revealed scripture; literally that which is written.
8.grammar: The definite article al- with the noun kitāb ('book, scripture'), itself a verbal noun from 'to write.' The -i ending is genitive, typically marking the word as following a preposition or standing in an 'of' relationship to a preceding noun.

9.meaning: 'They believe / they have faith' — to affirm something as true with trusting inner conviction and to feel secure in it. The verb carries both believing and being at peace through that belief; in religious use it is to commit oneself in faith.
9.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb, masculine plural. The yu-…-una frame means 'they (men, or a mixed group) do' the action now or habitually. The retained final -na marks the indicative (a plain, unqualified statement) — 'they believe' — as opposed to forms where that -na drops. The verb is Form IV (amana), used intransitively here meaning simply 'to believe / to have faith'.

10.meaning: 'The jibt' — a term for a false object of worship: an idol, a soothsayer, sorcery, or any vain superstition set up in place of the truth. Prefixed with 'in/by'.
10.grammar: The bi- prefix is a preposition ('in/by'), and al- is the definite article 'the'. The final -i ending is the genitive case, used because the noun follows a preposition (the genitive typically follows prepositions or links one noun to another, 'of …').
