11.meaning: 'The ṭāghūt' — anything worshipped or obeyed in defiance of Allah: a false god, tyrant, idol, or any agent of transgression. Built from the sense of overstepping all bounds. Prefixed with 'and'.
11.grammar: The wa- prefix means 'and', and al- is the definite article 'the' (its 'l' assimilates into the following ṭ). The final -i ending is the genitive case, typically used after a preposition or to link the noun to a preceding one.
11.root: ط-غ-ي (ṭ-gh-y) — to exceed all bounds, to tyrannize

12.meaning: A verb meaning 'and they say / and they keep saying' — to utter or assert in speech. The structure presents an ongoing or repeated act of speaking by a group.
12.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) verb joined by wa- ('and'). The ya-…-ūna frame marks the 3rd-person masculine plural ('they'); the full -ūna ending is the inseparable indicative-plural suffix, showing the verb is in its base (indicative) form and expressing an ongoing or habitual action.

13.meaning: A compound meaning 'for those who' or 'belonging to those who'. It joins the preposition 'for/to' with a masculine plural relative pronoun ('those who'), introducing a clause that describes a group of people by something they do or possess.
13.grammar: The prefix 'li-' is a preposition meaning 'for', 'to', or expressing ownership/benefit ('belonging to'). The relative pronoun is 'alladhīna' ('those who'), but when 'li-' attaches to it the connecting hamza of 'al-' drops out and the two lām sounds merge into one doubled lām, so the form is written and read 'lilladhīna' rather than 'li-alladhīna'. 'alladhīna' has a fixed shape and does not change for case.

14.meaning: 'They disbelieved / rejected faith' — from a root meaning to cover over or conceal. To disbelieve in this sense is to cover up and refuse the truth, and also to be ungrateful, hiding or denying favours received.
14.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third person masculine plural: 'they disbelieved'. The completed action is built into the stem kafara ('he disbelieved'), and the -ū suffix (written وا) marks the doer as 'they' (masculine plural). The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention with no sound.
14.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to reject faith, be ungrateful

15.meaning: These / those — a plural demonstrative pointing to a group of people or things. Its core sense is the near demonstrative 'these', but it is very commonly rendered 'those' in translation when the group it points to has already been described or named rather than being physically present.
15.grammar: A plural demonstrative pronoun, used for a group of either gender. Its base value is near-deixis ('these'), built from an attention-drawing prefix 'hā-' ('lo!, here') plus the base 'ulāʾi'. In practice it is often translated 'those' when the referent is already mentioned or understood rather than literally nearby. Its form is fixed and does not change for grammatical case; it points to a group rather than naming it.

16.meaning: Comparative/elative adjective from guidance: 'more rightly guided, better guided, more on the straight path.' It weighs one party against another in nearness to true guidance.
16.grammar: An elative (comparative/superlative) adjective on the pattern afʿal, formed from a 'weak' root, hence the long final -ā. As an elative it conveys 'more …' or 'most …' and does not change for case in this fixed shape.
16.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — guidance, right direction

17.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
17.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

18.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
18.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

19.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
19.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.
19.root: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — safety, security, trust, faith

20.meaning: A way, path, road, or means — a route to a destination, hence also a way or means of accomplishing something.
20.grammar: A singular noun. The '-an' ending is accusative and indefinite: the accusative case commonly marks the direct object of a verb, and the final 'n' sound marks it indefinite ('a way'). It denotes a path one travels or a means to an end.

1.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'those' — pointing to people or things that are distant or already known. It singles out a group ('those ones', 'it is those who').
1.grammar: A plural demonstrative pronoun, 'those'. It is fixed in form (no case endings). The -ka element signals distance/remoteness, pointing to something far off or notable. It can refer to people of either gender.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: A past-tense verb with an attached object: 'He cursed them / has cursed them,' i.e. cast them out from His mercy. A completed act of cursing with the doer 'he' and object 'them'.
3.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb with a built-in third-person masculine singular subject ('he'). The suffix -hum(u) is an object pronoun meaning 'them'; its vowel is lengthened to -humu to ease pronunciation before a following word.
3.root: ل-ع-ن (l-ʿ-n) — to curse, to banish from mercy

4.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
4.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

5.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
5.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

6.meaning: A present-tense verb: 'curses / banishes from mercy.' It states the act of cursing, with a third-person masculine singular doer.
6.grammar: The ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'). The verb is in the jussive (the shape after conditional or negating particles); its normally vowelless final consonant takes an -i here only to avoid an awkward consonant cluster before the next word.
6.root: ل-ع-ن (l-ʿ-n) — to curse, to banish from mercy

7.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
7.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

8.meaning: So never / then never — a connector 'so/then' joined to an emphatic particle of negation that denies a future action absolutely: 'will never (at all)'.
8.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector meaning 'so/then', linking to what precedes. 'lan' negates a following present-tense verb and casts it into the future with emphatic force ('will never'); it also puts that verb into the subjunctive, which shows up as a final '-a' on the verb.

9.meaning: A second-person present verb: 'you find / you come upon.' It denotes discovering or encountering something, whether by searching or by chance.
9.grammar: The ta- prefix marks a second-person masculine singular subject ('you'). The final -a vowel is the subjunctive, the shape used after governing particles (such as 'never' or 'that'), often projecting the action into the future.
9.root: و-ج-د (w-j-d) — to find, to come upon

10.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
10.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

11.meaning: 'A helper, supporter, one who gives aid and victory' — an intensive form stressing reliable, effective help.
11.grammar: An indefinite noun on an intensive pattern (faʿīl) that conveys a strong or constant doer — 'a true helper'. The -an ending marks the accusative and indefiniteness, commonly used here as a specifier naming the capacity ('as a helper').
11.root: ن-ص-ر (n-ṣ-r) — to help, to aid, to give victory

1.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'or', specifically the 'or' that pairs with a preceding question to offer an alternative ('…or…?'). It links two possibilities being weighed against each other, often after an opening interrogative.

parts.en: or (in alternatives, esp. after a question)

1.grammar: An indeclinable particle (no case or tense ending). It typically introduces the second branch of a two-part question or a balanced alternative, presenting the two as equally consequential.

2.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
2.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

3.meaning: A portion, share, or allotted part — what falls to someone as their due lot or stake.
3.grammar: A singular noun. The final -un (tanwīn ḍamma) marks it as indefinite ('a share') and in the nominative case, the form typically used for the subject of a sentence or the thing being stated to exist ('there is a share').
3.root: ن-ص-ب (n-ṣ-b) — to allot, set up; (a share) apportioned

4.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
4.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

5.meaning: The dominion, kingship, sovereign power — al-mulk is rule and possession on the grandest scale: the authority of a king, the realm ruled, and the very power to command and dispose. It denotes sovereignty itself.
5.grammar: A masculine noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The final -i is the genitive case, typically marking it as the second term of a possessive phrase ('… OF the dominion') or as governed by a preceding preposition.

6.meaning: A compound: 'in that case, then, therefore.' It draws a consequence from what was just said — 'if so, then …' — and prefixed with 'and/so' it links that consequence to the foregoing.
6.grammar: The fa- prefix is a connective meaning 'so/then', drawing a result. 'Idhan' is a response particle expressing consequence ('in that case'); its -an ending belongs to the fixed shape of the word, not a case marker.
6.root: — (particles; no triliteral root)

7.meaning: 'Not' — a particle of negation. Depending on context it denies a present fact, forbids an action, or rules something out ('do not / there is no').
7.grammar: A negating particle, 'not / no'. It is used to deny or prohibit — negating present-tense statements, expressing 'there is no...', or, with a command form, forbidding an action ('do not...').

8.meaning: A plural present verb: 'they give, they bestow, they hand over.' It denotes the act of granting or delivering something to others.
8.grammar: A present-tense verb of the form-IV pattern ('to give'). The yu-…-ūna framing marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'); the final -na is the indicative ending, marking an ordinary, ongoing statement.
8.root: ا-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (form IV) to give, to bring

9.meaning: Mankind, humanity, people in general — the collective of human beings.
9.grammar: A definite noun ('the people') with the attached 'al-' ('the'). The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 'n' (a sun letter), which is why the 'n' is doubled — this is a pronunciation effect, not a separate piece. The final '-a' ending is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb (the one being acted upon) or the subject of certain particles.
9.root: ن-و-س (n-w-s) — to move/sway; by extension, people

10.meaning: A 'naqīr' — the tiny pit or speck on the back of a date-stone. Like the date-stone's thread, it is proverbial for the most trifling amount, 'not even a jot.'
10.grammar: A singular noun. The ending -an is the indefinite accusative (the 'tanwīn' n-sound), here typically quantifying an amount ('by so much as a naqīr'); the accusative commonly marks an object or such a complement.
10.root: ن-ق-ر (n-q-r) — to peck, to hollow out, a small notch

1.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'or', specifically the 'or' that pairs with a preceding question to offer an alternative ('…or…?'). It links two possibilities being weighed against each other, often after an opening interrogative.

parts.en: or (in alternatives, esp. after a question)

1.grammar: An indeclinable particle (no case or tense ending). It typically introduces the second branch of a two-part question or a balanced alternative, presenting the two as equally consequential.

2.meaning: A plural present verb: 'they envy, they are jealous.' Ḥasad is the envy that begrudges another the blessings Allah has given and may wish them removed.
2.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ya-…-ūna framing marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'); the final -na is the indicative ending, signalling an ordinary, ongoing statement ('they envy').
2.root: ح-س-د (ḥ-s-d) — envy, begrudging another's blessing

3.meaning: Mankind, humanity, people in general — the collective of human beings.
3.grammar: A definite noun ('the people') with the attached 'al-' ('the'). The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 'n' (a sun letter), which is why the 'n' is doubled — this is a pronunciation effect, not a separate piece. The final '-a' ending is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb (the one being acted upon) or the subject of certain particles.
3.root: ن-و-س (n-w-s) — to move/sway; by extension, people

4.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
4.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

5.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
5.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

6.meaning: He gave / granted / bestowed upon them — to bring, hand over, or confer (a gift or favour) to someone.
6.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in Form IV ('to give/bestow'). With no subject suffix, it is third-person masculine singular ('he did'). The attached object pronoun 'them' (here voweled '-humu' to connect to the next word) gives 'he bestowed upon them.'
6.root: ا-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (Form IV) to bring, give, bestow

7.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
7.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

8.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
8.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

9.meaning: 'His bounty / grace / favor' — faḍl is overflowing generosity, an extra goodness given beyond what is owed; with the attached pronoun it means the bounty belonging to Him (Allah).
9.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive pronoun '-hi' ('his/His'). The -i vowel before the pronoun is the genitive case, which typically appears after a preposition or links the noun to what follows in an 'of' relationship; here it carries through to the possessor.
9.root: ف-ض-ل (f-ḍ-l) — excess, surplus; hence bounty, grace, superiority

10.meaning: A two-part connector: fa- means 'so', 'then', or 'and so', linking what follows as a result or consequence; qad before a past-tense verb intensifies it, conveying 'certainly', 'indeed', or 'already' — stressing that the action has truly and definitely occurred.
10.grammar: fa- is a connecting particle meaning 'so' or 'then', often marking a result. qad is a particle of emphasis; placed before a completed (past-tense) verb it affirms that the action has definitely or already happened. Neither part takes a case ending.

11.meaning: 'We gave / granted / brought'. To hand over or bestow something upon someone; to come to someone with a gift or grant.
11.grammar: A past-tense verb in the causative (form IV) sense 'to bring/grant to someone'. The '-nā' suffix is the doer 'we' in completed past time. It often takes two objects — the recipient and the thing given.
11.root: أ-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (form IV) to give, bring

12.meaning: The 'house', family, kinsfolk, or followers of someone — those belonging to a person's household or close circle, including dependents and adherents.
12.grammar: A noun meaning the people/household belonging to someone. The '-a' ending is the accusative case (marking it as a direct object); as the first term of a possessive pairing it is typically followed by the name of the one whose folk they are ('the folk OF …').
12.root: Uncertain/contested: most classical grammarians (e.g. Sibawayh) treat it as a contraction of أَهْل (ʾ-h-l, 'folk, household'); others trace it to ء-و-ل (ʾ-w-l, 'to return to, belong to')

13.meaning: The proper name Ibrāhīm (the Prophet Abraham).
13.grammar: A proper name of non-Arabic origin. The -a ending here serves for both accusative and genitive because the name is a diptote — a class of nouns that refuses tanwīn (no -an/-in) and uses a single -a for these two cases. So this one -a covers 'Ibrāhīm' whether as an object or as 'of Ibrāhīm'.

14.meaning: The Book, the Scripture — a written revelation; the term for a divinely revealed text.
14.grammar: A definite noun ('the Book') with attached 'al-' ('the'). The final '-a' ending is the accusative case, typically marking the word as the direct object of a verb.
14.root: ك-ت-ب (k-t-b) — to write; a writing, book

15.meaning: "and the wisdom" — sound judgement and deep understanding that puts things in their right place; 'ḥikma' is wisdom: knowledge joined to right action, insight into the true nature and proper order of things.
15.grammar: A definite feminine noun ('the wisdom'); 'wa-' is 'and' and 'al-' is 'the.' The final '-a' is the accusative case ending, the form a noun takes as the direct object of a verb or when joined to another accusative noun.
15.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — to judge, govern wisely; wisdom, sound judgement

16.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'and we gave/granted them' — the action of bestowing or conferring something upon a group, with the doer being a plural 'we' and the recipients a plural 'them'. The verb carries the sense of granting or handing over a possession.
16.grammar: The stem is a completed (past) action of giving. The -nā ending attached to the verb marks the doer as 'we' (a plural subject). The final -hum is an attached object pronoun meaning 'them' (third-person masculine plural). The opening wa- is a connective particle meaning 'and'.
16.root: ا-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come / to bring; in this derived (Form IV) shape, to bring to someone, i.e. to give or grant

17.meaning: Kingdom, sovereignty, dominion — the authority and right to rule, possession of power over a realm. It denotes both the territory ruled and the ruling power itself.
17.grammar: A singular noun. The final -an (tanwīn fatḥ) marks it as indefinite ('a kingdom') and in the accusative case, which commonly signals that the noun is the direct object of a verb or otherwise governed into the accusative.
17.root: م-ل-ك (m-l-k) — to own, to possess, to hold sovereign power

18.meaning: 'Great, immense, mighty, momentous.' It describes something vast in size, weight, or seriousness, and is often used of grave or awe-inspiring matters.
18.grammar: An adjective on the intensive faʿīl pattern. The -an ending is the indefinite accusative ('a great …'), commonly marking an adjective that agrees with an indefinite accusative noun it describes, or the object of a verb.

1.meaning: "so / and among them / of them (there are)" — the preposition min ('from, among, of') with the pronoun 'them', expressing 'among them' or 'some of them', introduced by 'so/and'.
1.grammar: A connective particle plus a preposition with an attached pronoun. Fa- means 'so/and then', linking to what precedes. Min ('from/among') takes no case ending; the suffix -hum is 'them' (third-person masculine plural). The phrase often introduces a partition ('among them are…').

2.meaning: A versatile word meaning 'who / whoever / the one who.' It can ask a question ('who?') or introduce a clause ('whoever does…'), referring to persons.
2.grammar: An indeclinable particle/pronoun with a fixed form (it does not change for case). Used for rational beings ('who'), functioning either as an interrogative ('who?') or as a conditional/relative ('whoever, the one who').

3.meaning: 'He believed' — he had faith, trusted, and affirmed. The basic past-tense form of the verb meaning to believe and to find security in faith.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb on the causative (Form IV) pattern, from the root for security and faith. The -a ending marks a third-person masculine singular subject, 'he (believed)', stating a completed act of coming to faith.

4.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
4.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

5.meaning: 'And among them / and some of them' — a connective 'and' plus a preposition meaning 'from / among / part of,' joined to the pronoun 'them'; often introduces a subgroup ('among them are …').
5.grammar: A connective wa- ('and') with the preposition min ('from / among'), which always governs a following word in the genitive. Here that word is the attached pronoun -hum ('them'), giving 'and among them / and from them.' Particles like these do not themselves carry case or tense.

6.meaning: A versatile word meaning 'who / whoever / the one who.' It can ask a question ('who?') or introduce a clause ('whoever does…'), referring to persons.
6.grammar: An indeclinable particle/pronoun with a fixed form (it does not change for case). Used for rational beings ('who'), functioning either as an interrogative ('who?') or as a conditional/relative ('whoever, the one who').

7.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'he turned away / he hindered' — either turning oneself aside from something, or obstructing and barring others from a path. It conveys aversion as well as the act of blocking access.
7.grammar: A completed (past) action with a third-person masculine singular subject, 'he'. The doubled final consonant (shadda on the dāl) reflects that the root's second and third letters are identical, merged in pronunciation. The final -a is the standard past-tense ending for 'he did'.
7.root: ص-د-د (ṣ-d-d) — to turn away, to avert, to hinder or bar from

8.meaning: A combination meaning 'from him / from it / about him.' The preposition denotes moving away from, departing from, or concerning a thing, and the pronoun refers to a single masculine entity.
8.grammar: A preposition with a fused object pronoun. ʿan governs the genitive and conveys separation or 'concerning.' The attached -hu marks a third-person masculine singular object ('him/it').

9.meaning: 'And He suffices / is enough' — to be sufficient, adequate, and fully enough so that nothing more is needed. It conveys complete adequacy, often used to affirm that Allah alone is enough.
9.grammar: The connective wa- ('and') prefixed to a 3rd-person masculine singular perfect (past-tense) verb (Form I) whose final weak root letter (the yāʾ) appears as a long -ā. It states a completed yet timeless fact — 'and He is sufficient' — the kind of perfect form used for an enduring truth.
9.root: ك-ف-ي (k-f-y) — to suffice, be enough, be adequate; to spare someone need of anything else

10.meaning: A proper name with a prefixed particle: Jahannam, the Hellfire — the abode of punishment in the Hereafter. As a name it is largely treated as fixed and is generally not declined for case.
10.grammar: The prefix bi- here is an augmentative (extra, pleonastic) particle that carries no independent meaning of its own and is not translated; it formally puts the following noun into the genitive form while that noun still functions as the logical subject. The name Jahannam ends in -a here; being a proper name that does not take tanwīn (a diptote), it shows a single -a in the genitive position rather than the usual -i.

11.meaning: A blazing, fiercely kindled fire — flame that has been set ablaze and roars with intensity. The form conveys a fire that is made to burn violently.
11.grammar: A noun/intensive adjective. The final -an (tanwīn fatḥ) marks it as indefinite and in the accusative case, which typically signals a direct object or a descriptive complement governed into the accusative.
11.root: س-ع-ر (s-ʿ-r) — to kindle, to set ablaze, to make a fire flare up

1.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
1.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: 'They disbelieved / rejected faith' — from a root meaning to cover over or conceal. To disbelieve in this sense is to cover up and refuse the truth, and also to be ungrateful, hiding or denying favours received.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third person masculine plural: 'they disbelieved'. The completed action is built into the stem kafara ('he disbelieved'), and the -ū suffix (written وا) marks the doer as 'they' (masculine plural). The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention with no sound.
3.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to reject faith, be ungrateful

4.meaning: By/in Our signs. Āyāt is the plural of āya — a sign, token, or evidence. Signs are pointers that indicate a greater reality. With the prefixed particle and pronoun it means 'with/in Our signs'.
4.grammar: A plural noun preceded by the preposition bi- ('with, in, by'), which requires the following noun to take the -i (genitive) ending. The attached -nā means 'our' when joined to a noun. The genitive here is governed by the preposition.

5.meaning: A future-marking particle meaning 'shall / will (eventually)'. Placed before a present-tense verb, it pushes the action into the future, often with a sense of a more distant or assured 'in time, it shall come to pass'.
5.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it has no case ending and never changes form). Its sole function is to mark futurity on the present-tense verb that follows it.

6.meaning: A present/future verb meaning 'we cause them to roast / we make them enter the fire and burn'. It denotes scorching someone in fire, making them undergo burning.

parts.en: cause to roast / burn in fire

6.grammar: An ongoing/future action. The nu- prefix marks the doer as 'we' and, in this causative (Form IV) pattern, gives the sense 'we make (them) burn'. The attached -him is the object pronoun 'them' (third-person masculine plural). The verb is in the indicative mood (a plain statement of fact).
6.root: ص-ل-ي (ṣ-l-y) — to roast, to burn, to be scorched by fire

7.meaning: Fire — blazing flame; by extension heat, burning, or (in many contexts) the Fire of punishment. The core image is leaping, consuming flame.
7.grammar: A feminine noun in the indefinite accusative, marked by the -an ending (the 'nunation' tanwīn). This ending commonly signals 'a fire' as the direct object of a verb, i.e. the thing acted upon.
7.root: ن-و-ر (n-w-r) — to give light, shine, illuminate (نَار 'fire' is a derived noun from this root)

8.meaning: 'whenever / every time' — a compound expressing that something recurs each and every time a condition is met.
8.grammar: A compound of kull ('every', in the accusative -a used adverbially) and mā ('what / the time that'). Together it works as a conditional time-word, 'each time that …', linking a repeated condition to its repeated result.

9.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'it became fully cooked / roasted / ripe'. Of flesh, it means thoroughly burned or cooked through; the root broadly covers reaching full ripeness or doneness.
9.grammar: A completed (past) action. The final -at (here written -t) is the feminine ending, marking the subject as third-person feminine singular, 'she / it'.
9.root: ن-ض-ج (n-ḍ-j) — to be or become fully cooked, roasted, or ripe

10.meaning: Their skins — the outer coverings of the body, belonging to a group of males. It is the plural of 'skin' joined to a possessor 'them'.
10.grammar: A plural noun in the possessed (construct) state. The -u ending marks the nominative case, typically the case of the subject of a sentence. The attached -hum means 'their' (third-person masculine plural), making the whole 'their skins'.
10.root: ج-ل-د (j-l-d) — skin, hide; (also the act of flogging the skin)

11.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'we exchanged / replaced for them' — to substitute one thing for another, putting a new thing in place of the old. The intensive form stresses a thorough swapping or transformation.
11.grammar: A completed (past) action in the intensive (Form II) pattern, which here conveys thorough substitution. The -nā ending marks the doer as 'we'. The attached -hum is the object pronoun 'them' (third-person masculine plural).
11.root: ب-د-ل (b-d-l) — to change, exchange, substitute one thing for another

12.meaning: Skins — the plural of 'skin', the body's outer covering, here standing on its own without a possessor.
12.grammar: A plural noun. The final -an (tanwīn fatḥ) marks it as indefinite and in the accusative case, which typically signals that it is a direct object of a verb.

13.meaning: Other than it / different from it — a word meaning 'something else', marking difference or otherness, joined to a feminine 'it/that' to mean 'other than that thing'.
13.grammar: The word ghayr signals difference ('other than'). Its -a ending is accusative, here functioning as a descriptive qualifier ('[ones] other than'). The attached -hā is the possessive/object pronoun 'it / that', referring to a feminine singular thing.
13.root: غ-ي-ر (gh-y-r) — otherness, difference, being other than

14.meaning: A verb phrase meaning 'so that they may taste' — to taste or experience something directly. The opening particle gives it the sense of purpose: 'in order that they taste'. Tasting here implies undergoing and feeling an experience first-hand.
14.grammar: The prefix li- is the particle of purpose ('so that, in order to'), which puts the verb into the subjunctive mood (used for intended or hoped-for actions). The ya- prefix with the -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'; in the subjunctive the final nūn of the indicative is dropped, leaving -ū plus a silent spelling alif.
14.root: ذ-و-ق (dh-w-q) — to taste, to experience or feel directly

15.meaning: The punishment, chastisement, or torment — a penalty inflicted as retribution, especially the painful suffering of divine reckoning.
15.grammar: A definite masculine noun ('the punishment'). The final -a is the accusative ending, which generally marks the word as the direct object of a verb or the subject/predicate after certain particles.
15.root: ع-ذ-ب (ʿ-dh-b) — to punish, torment; the inflicting of pain

16.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
16.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

17.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
17.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

18.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

18.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

19.meaning: Mighty, all-powerful, invincible — one who is dominant and cannot be overcome; also carrying the sense of precious and held in high honor. Of a person it means strong and unassailable.
19.grammar: An intensive adjective (of the faʿīl pattern, conveying a deep, settled quality). The final -an (tanwīn fatḥ) marks it as indefinite and in the accusative case, which typically signals a direct object or a descriptive complement governed into the accusative.
19.root: ع-ز-ز (ʿ-z-z) — might, strength, dominance; also honor and preciousness

20.meaning: All-Wise; one possessing perfect wisdom, who places everything in its right place and decides with flawless judgement. As an intensive form it conveys wisdom that is complete and sound.
20.grammar: An intensive adjective ('all-wise') on the faʿīl pattern, stressing the quality to its fullest degree. The -an (tanwīn) combines the -a accusative ending — typical of a predicate or object — with the -n marking it indefinite.

1.meaning: 'And those who': a connective phrase introducing a specified group of people (masculine plural) about whom something will be said. It links them to what came before.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'), which is masculine plural. A relative pronoun stands for a group and is normally followed by a clause describing them. Its form does not change for case; it stays alladhīna whatever its grammatical role.

2.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
2.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.
2.root: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — safety, security, trust, faith

3.meaning: A two-part word: 'and' + 'they did / worked / performed.' The verb denotes doing deeds, working, putting effort into action — practical doing as opposed to mere speaking or believing.
3.grammar: A conjunction 'wa' + a past-tense verb, 3rd person masculine plural. The -ū ending marks the subject as 'they' (a group of males or a mixed group): 'and they did / worked.'

4.meaning: 'The righteous deeds / good works' — the definite plural of a word meaning that which is sound, wholesome, upright, and beneficial. As a noun it refers to good, virtuous actions that set things right.
4.grammar: A definite sound feminine plural noun ('the good deeds'). The -i ending is the oblique case used by feminine plurals to mark either the genitive ('… of …' / after a preposition) or the accusative (direct object); for this plural pattern the accusative and genitive share the same -i ending.
4.root: ص-ل-ح (ṣ-l-ḥ) — to be sound, good, upright, set right

5.meaning: A future verb meaning 'we shall admit them / cause them to enter'. It denotes bringing someone into a place, with the prefixed letter marking certainty about the future.
5.grammar: The prefix sa- marks the near future ('shall, will'). The nu- prefix marks the doer as 'we', and the causative (Form IV) pattern gives the meaning 'we make (them) enter'. The attached -hum is the object pronoun 'them' (third-person masculine plural).
5.root: د-خ-ل (d-kh-l) — to enter, to go in; (causative) to bring in, admit

6.meaning: 'Gardens' — the plural of a lush, walled garden thick with trees whose foliage covers the ground. The root sense is concealment by dense greenery; it is the standard word for the gardens of Paradise.
6.grammar: An indefinite sound feminine plural noun ('gardens'). The '-in' (tanwīn) ending marks it as indefinite ('some gardens'), and for this plural form it stands in the oblique case (genitive or accusative), used after prepositions/possessives or as a direct object.
6.root: ج-ن-ن (j-n-n) — to cover, conceal, hide (hence a dense garden)

7.meaning: A verb 'it flows, runs, streams' — used of water and rivers moving along, and of things that run or course freely. It describes continuous, ongoing motion.
7.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, 3rd person feminine singular. The ta- prefix here marks a feminine 'it/she' subject. The verb describes an ongoing or habitual action: 'it flows / keeps flowing.'

8.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
8.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

9.meaning: 'Beneath it / underneath it' — the noun for the underside or lower region of something, with an attached pronoun 'its' (referring to a feminine thing). It points to the space below or underneath a thing.
9.grammar: A location noun ('underneath') with the attached pronoun '-hā' ('its/her'), referring to a feminine noun. The -i ending is the genitive case, normally triggered here because words of place like 'under' commonly follow a preposition such as 'from' (min taḥti = 'from beneath').

10.meaning: 'The rivers / the streams' — the definite plural of a word for a flowing river or watercourse. It denotes large, running channels of water.
10.grammar: A definite plural noun ('the rivers'). The -u ending is the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence — the doer of the verb or the thing being described.

11.meaning: Ones who abide / remain forever — those who dwell perpetually and permanently in a state or place, without end. The word denotes lasting, undying permanence.
11.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer' word: 'ones abiding'). The -īna ending is the sound masculine plural in its accusative/genitive form, used when the word is an object or governed by a preceding element. It describes people characterized by perpetual abiding.

12.meaning: 'In it / therein.' A preposition with an attached pronoun: 'in' plus a feminine singular 'it,' meaning 'inside it / within it,' referring back to some feminine or grammatically feminine thing (such as a place).
12.grammar: A prepositional phrase: fī ('in, within') with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine singular). The pronoun is the object of the preposition and points back to a previously mentioned feminine noun.

13.meaning: An adverb meaning 'ever / forever / at any time' — used to stress that something will never (or always) be the case throughout all time, especially with a negative to mean 'never, not ever'.
13.grammar: A noun used adverbially. The ending -an is the indefinite accusative, the form regularly used to turn a word into an adverb of time ('… ever / forever'); the -n (nunation) marks it as indefinite. Paired with a negation it strengthens it to 'never, not ever'.

14.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
14.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

15.meaning: 'In it / therein.' A preposition with an attached pronoun: 'in' plus a feminine singular 'it,' meaning 'inside it / within it,' referring back to some feminine or grammatically feminine thing (such as a place).
15.grammar: A prepositional phrase: fī ('in, within') with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine singular). The pronoun is the object of the preposition and points back to a previously mentioned feminine noun.

16.meaning: 'Spouses / mates / pairs.' The plural of a noun denoting a partner of a pair — a husband or wife, or more broadly one of two things that go together as a matched set.
16.grammar: A plural noun. The -un ending is the indefinite nominative, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or a thing being identified as existing; the doubled 'n' sound (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('spouses / some mates').
16.root: ز-و-ج (z-w-j) — pair, couple, to join two as a pair

17.meaning: Purified, made clean — thoroughly cleansed of impurity or blemish, whether physical or moral. The form indicates something that has been actively purified by another.
17.grammar: A passive participle (something to which purifying was done) of the intensive (Form II) pattern, which stresses thorough cleansing. The tā' marbūṭa marks it feminine (describing a feminine noun). The final -un (tanwīn ḍamm) marks it indefinite and in the nominative case, the case typically used for a subject or a predicate describing one.
17.root: ط-ه-ر (ṭ-h-r) — purity, cleanliness, freedom from defilement

18.meaning: A future verb meaning 'and we shall admit them / cause them to enter' — to bring someone into a place, opened by a connective 'and'.
18.grammar: An ongoing/future action. The opening wa- is the connective particle 'and'. The nu- prefix marks the doer as 'we', and the causative (Form IV) pattern gives 'we make (them) enter'. The attached -hum is the object pronoun 'them' (third-person masculine plural). The verb is in the indicative mood (a plain statement).
18.root: د-خ-ل (d-kh-l) — to enter, to go in; (causative) to bring in, admit

19.meaning: Shade, shadow — the cool, sheltered area shielded from direct sun; figuratively a place of ease, protection, and comfort.
19.grammar: A singular noun. The final -an (tanwīn fatḥ) marks it as indefinite ('a shade') and in the accusative case, which typically signals a direct object or a word otherwise governed into the accusative.
19.root: ظ-ل-ل (ẓ-l-l) — shade, shadow, shelter from the sun

20.meaning: Deeply shading, abundantly shady — describing shade that is dense, extensive, and cool, casting a full and lasting shadow. An intensive form stressing the richness of the shade.
20.grammar: An intensive adjective (of the faʿīl pattern). The final -an (tanwīn fatḥ) marks it indefinite and in the accusative case; as an adjective this case typically matches and describes a preceding accusative noun.
20.root: ظ-ل-ل (ẓ-l-l) — shade, shadow; here in the sense of casting rich shade

1.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
1.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

2.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
2.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.
2.root: — (proper name)

3.meaning: 'He commands you' / 'He orders you' — the act of issuing an order or directive to a group. Conveys an authoritative instruction to do something.
3.grammar: A present-tense verb 'to command'. The ya- prefix marks the subject as 'he'. The base verb ends in -u, the normal indicative ending signalling an ongoing or habitual action (a simple statement, not a command or a negated/subjunctive form). The attached -kum is the object 'you all'.

4.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
4.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

5.meaning: A verb meaning 'that you (all) deliver / hand over faithfully' — to convey something to its rightful owner, to discharge a duty or pay back what is due. The intensive form stresses fully carrying through the delivery.
5.grammar: An ongoing action in the intensive (Form II) pattern (stressing thorough discharge). The tu- prefix plus the -ū ending marks a second-person masculine plural subject, 'you (all)'. The loss of the final nūn (leaving -ū plus a silent spelling alif) shows the verb is in the subjunctive or jussive mood — the form used after particles of purpose, command, or condition.
5.root: ا-د-ي (ʾ-d-y) — to convey, deliver, discharge or pay back a due

6.meaning: Trusts — things entrusted to one's safekeeping; responsibilities, deposits, or obligations that must be faithfully kept and returned. The plural of 'a trust' (amāna).
6.grammar: A sound feminine plural noun made definite by the prefix al- ('the'). The final -i marks the genitive case; for this kind of plural, -i is also the case used when it serves as a direct object, and it likewise follows prepositions and links one noun to another ('… of …').
6.root: ا-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — safety, trust, security; that which is confided for safekeeping

7.meaning: "to / towards" — a preposition marking the end-point, goal, or direction of a movement or extent ("up to," "as far as," "toward").
7.grammar: An indeclinable preposition; it has no case ending of its own and always governs a following noun in the genitive case.

8.meaning: Her people / her household — those belonging to her: her family, kin, or the folk to whom she pertains.
8.grammar: A noun meaning 'the people belonging to' someone, here in a possessive construction. The -i ending is genitive, the case used when a word follows a preposition or is the second term of a possessive ('… of …'). The attached -hā is the pronoun 'her' (or 'its,' feminine).
8.root: ا-ه-ل (ʾ-h-l) — family, kinfolk, the people proper to a place or thing

9.meaning: 'And when...' — a linking phrase joining 'and' to 'when', used to introduce a circumstance or a recurring situation: 'and whenever / and at the time that...'.
9.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') attached to idhā ('when'). Idhā is a particle pointing to a time or condition, generally referring to something expected or recurring in the future ('when / whenever' it happens), and it normally introduces a following clause that states what occurs at that time.

10.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'you (all) judged / decided / ruled' — to pass a judgment, decide a matter, or govern between parties. The action of adjudicating.
10.grammar: A completed (past) action. The -tum ending marks the doer as second-person masculine plural, 'you (all)'.
10.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — to judge, decide, govern; wisdom and authority

11.meaning: Between; in the midst of two things. An adverb of place marking the space separating or lying among parties or points.
11.grammar: An adverb of place ('between'). It always ends in -a and grammatically governs what follows it, putting the following noun(s) into the genitive 'of' relationship. It does not change to show 'the' or a case of its own; the fixed -a is simply how this word is formed.
11.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction, what lies between

12.meaning: Humankind, people, mankind — the collective of human beings.
12.grammar: A collective noun ('people, mankind') carrying the definite article al- ('the'); the 'l' of the article assimilates into the following 'n', doubling it (al-nās → an-nās). The genitive ending -i marks the word as governed by a preposition or as the second term of a possessive.
12.root: ء-ن-س (ʾ-n-s) — humankind, sociability, familiarity; the word for 'people' is most commonly traced to this root (related to insān, 'human being')

13.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
13.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

14.meaning: A verb meaning 'that you (all) judge / decide' — to pass judgment or rule between parties. Refers to the act of adjudicating, here in a form awaiting a governing particle.
14.grammar: An ongoing action. The ta- prefix plus the -ū ending marks a second-person masculine plural subject, 'you (all)'. The dropped final nūn (leaving -ū with a silent spelling alif) shows the subjunctive or jussive mood — used after particles of purpose, condition, or command.
14.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — to judge, decide, govern; wisdom and authority

15.meaning: The noun 'justice / fairness / equity' introduced by the preposition 'with/in', giving the sense 'with justice' or 'in fairness' — acting in a balanced, even-handed manner.
15.grammar: A preposition 'bi-' plus the definite noun 'al-ʿadl'. The -i ending is genitive, which is required after the preposition; the whole phrase functions adverbially ('with/in justice').
15.root: ع-د-ل (ʿ-d-l) — justice, fairness, balance, setting straight

16.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
16.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

17.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
17.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

18.meaning: An expression of strong praise meaning 'how excellent it is! / what a fine thing!'. It is built from the praise-verb niʿma ('how good/excellent') fused with mā ('that which / a thing'), used to commend something highly.
18.grammar: A frozen praise-construction: the verb niʿma ('how excellent / how good') is followed by mā ('that which'), the two merging in pronunciation (the doubled mīm). It does not conjugate for case or tense in the ordinary way; its whole purpose is to voice admiration or commendation.
18.root: ن-ع-م (n-ʿ-m) — goodness, favor, that which is excellent and pleasing

19.meaning: He admonishes / counsels you (plural) — to exhort, warn, and instruct in a way that softens the heart and turns one toward right conduct.
19.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he'), with the ya- prefix marking 'he/it'. The -u before the suffix shows the indicative mood (a plain ongoing or habitual statement). The attached -kum is the object pronoun 'you all'.
19.root: و-ع-ظ (w-ʿ-ẓ) — admonition, exhortation, counsel

20.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
20.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

21.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
21.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

22.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
22.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

23.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

23.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

24.meaning: All-Hearing — one who hears fully and perfectly. This is an intensive adjective (faʿīl pattern) conveying that hearing is a permanent, all-encompassing attribute, not a single act of hearing.
24.grammar: An indefinite noun/adjective on the intensive faʿīl pattern. The final -an (tanwīn fatḥah) marks the accusative case, the form a word typically takes as the object of a verb or as a predicate after certain particles; the -n also signals that it is indefinite ('a hearer / hearing').

25.meaning: All-Seeing — one who sees fully and perfectly. An intensive adjective (faʿīl pattern) expressing sight as a permanent, comprehensive attribute that misses nothing.
25.grammar: An indefinite noun/adjective on the intensive faʿīl pattern. The final -an (tanwīn fatḥah) marks the accusative case — the form used for the object of a verb or a predicate after certain particles — and the -n shows it is indefinite ('a seer / seeing').

1.meaning: 'O…!' — a compound vocative expression used to call out and summon an audience before addressing them. It fuses the call-particle 'yā' ('O') with a noun that means 'the one(s) addressed,' yielding an emphatic 'O you…!' that introduces direct address.
1.grammar: A vocative (calling) construction. 'Yā' is the particle for calling out; 'ayyu' carries a nominative '-u' as the one being summoned; 'hā' is an attention-drawing particle. Together they function as 'O you…!,' setting up the noun of address that follows.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
3.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

4.meaning: Obey! — a plural command to comply, submit, and do as one is told. The verb denotes willing, active obedience and yielding to authority.
4.grammar: A Form IV imperative (command) built on the root for obedience. The -ū ending marks a masculine plural addressee — 'obey, all of you!'. (The written final alif after the wāw is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.)

5.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
5.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

6.meaning: 'and obey!' — a command to a group to comply, submit to, and follow an order or authority. The leading 'wa' joins it ('and …').
6.grammar: An imperative (command) verb addressed to a masculine plural ('you all obey!'), joined by 'wa' ('and'). The '-ū' ending marks the plural addressee in commands.
6.root: ط-و-ع (ṭ-w-ʿ) — to obey, comply, submit willingly

7.meaning: The messenger, envoy, or emissary: one who is sent with a message; in the Qur'an typically a prophet sent by Allah bearing revelation to a people.
7.grammar: A noun on the form faʿūl (an intensive/agent pattern, 'one sent'), prefixed with al- ('the'). The final -a ending is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb ('… the messenger') or the subject of certain particles. The 'l' of al- assimilates into the following 'r' (a 'sun letter'), pronounced ar-rasūl.

8.meaning: and possessors of / and those who have — a compound opening with 'and', then a word meaning the owners or holders of something (e.g. 'those of authority', 'those of knowledge'). 'Ulī' is the plural construct form meaning 'possessors of', always followed by the thing possessed.
8.grammar: The prefix wa- means 'and'. 'Ulī' is an irregular plural noun meaning 'possessors/owners of', appearing in the oblique (genitive/accusative) form ending in -ī; it is a construct word, so it leans on a following noun ('possessors OF …'). It has no singular from its own root and is used only in such possessive constructions.
8.root: — (no triliteral root; suppletive plural meaning 'possessors of')

9.meaning: The matter, affair, command, or decision — either a thing being dealt with or an authoritative order that is issued. The definite article marks it as a specific, known matter.
9.grammar: A definite masculine noun. The final -i is the genitive ending, which generally links it to a preceding noun ('… of the matter') or follows a preposition.
9.root: ا-م-ر (ʾ-m-r) — to command; a matter or affair

10.meaning: A combination meaning 'from among you' or 'of you' — singling out a part or some individuals out of a larger group being addressed.
10.grammar: The preposition min ('from, among, some of') with the attached pronoun -kum, which means 'you' for a group of two or more (grammatically masculine plural). Because the pronoun follows a preposition, it is in the object form; the whole expression partitions or draws out individuals from the addressed group.
10.root: — (min is a particle/preposition; -kum is a pronoun)

11.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'fa-' ('then', 'so', 'but') drawing a consequence, joined to the conditional particle 'in' ('if'). Together: 'then if …', 'but if …'.
11.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that signals a result or transition ('then/so'). 'in' is the conditional particle 'if', introducing a supposed condition. Both are indeclinable particles with no case ending.

12.meaning: you disputed / you quarreled with one another — to contend back and forth, each side pulling against the other in an argument. The form carries the sense of mutual, reciprocal disagreement among a group.
12.grammar: A past-tense verb of the reciprocal pattern (Form VI, tafāʿala), which signals an action done mutually 'with one another'. The suffix -tum is the subject ending meaning 'you all' (masculine plural) and shows the action is completed.

13.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
13.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

14.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
14.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
14.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

15.meaning: so refer it back / then return it — a command to hand something over or take it back to a referee or authority for settlement. The opening 'fa' adds the sense of 'so/then', linking it as a consequence.
15.grammar: The prefix fa- means 'so' or 'then', marking a result or sequence. 'Ruddū' is a plural command (imperative) addressed to a group of males: 'refer/return it!' The attached -hu is an object pronoun meaning 'it' or 'him'. The doubled d reflects the geminate root.
15.root: ر-د-د (r-d-d) — to return, send back, refer

16.meaning: 'To / toward / up to' — a preposition marking the endpoint, goal, or limit of an action or motion: the direction something moves toward or the boundary at which it stops.
16.grammar: An invariable preposition. It has no case ending of its own but puts the noun that follows it into the genitive ('of / to' state). It indicates direction toward, or the terminal limit of, something.

17.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
17.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

18.meaning: Means 'and the Messenger' — the one sent with a message, an envoy commissioned to deliver. It refers to a messenger sent by Allah.
18.grammar: A definite noun ('the messenger'). The -i ending is genitive: it typically marks the word as following a preposition or as joined (by 'and') to another genitive word, or as the second term of a possessive pair. 'al-' means 'the' (its 'l' is assimilated into the following 'r', hence 'ar-rasūl'); the wa- means 'and'.

19.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
19.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

20.meaning: A past-tense verb of 'being' addressed to a group: 'you (all) were', 'you (all) used to be'. From kāna, the core verb 'to be'. With a following predicate it often means 'you were (in a state of) …' or 'you used to …'.
20.grammar: This is a past-tense verb. The '-tum' suffix is the attached subject marker for a masculine plural 'you all'. Since the doer is built into the suffix, the verb stands in its base past form ('you all were').
20.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

21.meaning: you believe / you have faith — to trust and affirm with conviction, especially faith in Allah and what He has revealed. The verb denotes ongoing, present believing.
21.grammar: A present-tense verb of Form IV (āmana), which makes the act of believing/granting security. The tu- prefix marks a 'you' subject, and the ending -ūna marks masculine plural and the indicative mood (a plain, ongoing statement: 'you all believe'). The -na would drop if a governing particle put it in another mood. The hamzah at the start of the stem belongs to the root.

22.meaning: A phrase 'in Allah / by Allah', combining the preposition 'with/in/by' and the divine name Allah, the proper name of the One God.
22.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with, by means of') prefixed to the divine name Allah. A preposition always forces the following noun into the genitive case, which is why Allah here ends in -i. With verbs of believing, bi- conveys the object of faith — to believe IN.
22.root: — (Allah is the proper name of God and is not derived from a triliteral root in the usual sense)

23.meaning: "And the Day" — a stretch of time, a day; also used for the appointed Day of Judgement and Resurrection. The opening element is the conjunction 'and'.
23.grammar: A masculine singular noun with the definite article 'the' and the conjunction 'and'. The final -i is the genitive case ending: it typically signals that the word is linked to a preceding noun ('… of …') or governed by a preposition or oath particle.

24.meaning: An adjective meaning 'the last,' 'the latter,' or 'the final' — that which comes at the end of a sequence. It is the common counterpart to 'the first,' and is often used as a name for the world or life to come (the Hereafter, the Last Day), i.e. the ultimate end of all things.
24.grammar: An active-participle-type adjective on the pattern fāʿil. It carries the definite article 'al-' ('the'). The final -i is the genitive case, signaling that the word is governed by a preceding preposition or particle, or stands as the second term of a possessive link ('… of …'). It is masculine singular.
24.root: ء-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — to be last, to come after, to defer / postpone

25.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
25.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

26.meaning: 'Better / best; good' — an adjective of comparison meaning more good, preferable, or superior. It also serves broadly for 'goodness' and that which is good and beneficial.
26.grammar: A noun/adjective bearing the ending -un (nunation): the doubled-u 'n' sound marks the word as both indefinite ('a/an', no 'the') and nominative — the case used for the subject of a sentence or the predicate that describes it.
26.root: خ-ي-ر (kh-y-r) — good, goodness, that which is choice and beneficial

27.meaning: and better / and more fitting — a compound of 'and' with the comparative/superlative 'aḥsan', meaning 'more excellent, finer, more suitable'. Built on the comparative pattern (afʿal) from the idea of beauty and goodness.
27.grammar: The prefix wa- means 'and'. 'Aḥsanu' is a comparative/superlative adjective on the afʿal pattern ('more/most good'). Its ending -u marks the nominative case, the form typically used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate. As an afʿal comparative it is diptote and normally does not take tanwīn.

28.meaning: interpretation / final outcome — explaining the deeper meaning of something, or the ultimate result and end to which a matter leads. The word combines the senses of 'how a thing is construed' and 'where a thing ends up'.
28.grammar: A verbal noun (maṣdar) of Form II (tafʿīl pattern) denoting the act/result of interpreting or the eventual outcome. The hamzah is the middle root letter. The final -an (tanwīn fatḥah) marks the accusative — used for an object or for a noun specifying respect ('… as to interpretation/outcome') — and the -n shows it is indefinite.
28.root: ء-و-ل (ʾ-w-l) — to return to an origin; to construe, trace back

1.meaning: 'Did not…?' — a particle combining a question with negation, used to ask 'Have I/has he not…?', often expecting agreement or serving as a gentle reminder.
1.grammar: An interrogative prefix 'a-' ('?') joined to the negation 'lam'. 'lam' negates a verb and places it firmly in the past ('did not'), and grammatically puts the following present-tense verb into the jussive (clipped) form. Together they form a rhetorical or confirming question.

2.meaning: You see, perceive, or take notice; to observe with the eye, or by extension to come to know or consider. Often used to draw attention, as in 'have you considered…?'
2.grammar: A present-tense verb addressed to a single male 'you,' marked by the 'ta-' prefix. The root's weak final letter has dropped, leaving the short final -a; this shortened form is the jussive/apocopated form, which appears after certain particles (such as 'did not' or in questions like 'have you not seen?').
2.root: ر-أ-ي (r-ʾ-y) — to see, perceive, consider, form an opinion

3.meaning: 'To / toward / up to' — a preposition marking the endpoint, goal, or limit of an action or motion: the direction something moves toward or the boundary at which it stops.
3.grammar: An invariable preposition. It has no case ending of its own but puts the noun that follows it into the genitive ('of / to' state). It indicates direction toward, or the terminal limit of, something.

4.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
4.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

5.meaning: they claim / they allege — to assert something as true, often with the implication that the claim is doubtful or unfounded. The verb describes an ongoing, present asserting by a group.
5.grammar: A present-tense Form I verb. The ya- prefix marks a third-person subject ('they/he'), and the ending -ūna marks masculine plural together with the indicative mood (a plain ongoing statement: 'they claim'). The -na drops when a governing particle changes the mood.

6.meaning: 'That they…' — an emphatic connector 'anna' ('that, indeed') fused with the pronoun 'they,' used to introduce an affirmed clause as the content of a thought or statement.
6.grammar: Built on the particle 'anna' ('that…, indeed'), which introduces and affirms a following clause (often after verbs of knowing, thinking, or saying) and puts its noun into the accusative. The attached '-hum' is the pronoun 'they/them' for a male-inclusive group.

7.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
7.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

8.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
8.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

9.meaning: 'It was sent down / revealed': the act of being caused to descend, used especially of revelation brought down from Allah. The passive form puts the focus on the thing sent down rather than on the sender.
9.grammar: A past-tense passive verb in Form IV (anzala 'to send down' → unzila 'was sent down'). The prefix is only the u- vowel carried on the connecting hamza; the nūn that follows is the first root letter (of ن-ز-ل), not part of the prefix. The internal vowel pattern u–i marks it as passive ('was/were sent down'), with no named doer. The final -a marks the subject as 'he/it', a single masculine thing, and signals completed action.
9.root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — to descend, come down; (Form IV) to send down

10.meaning: 'To you' (addressing one person): indicating direction or motion toward a single individual — that toward which something moves or is directed.
10.grammar: The preposition ilā ('to, towards') with an attached pronoun; before a suffix ilā takes the form ilay-. The -ka ending is the pronoun 'you' for a single male addressee. Pronouns following a preposition stand in the genitive relationship, though their form does not visibly change for case.

11.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
11.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

12.meaning: 'It was sent down / revealed': the act of being caused to descend, used especially of revelation brought down from Allah. The passive form puts the focus on the thing sent down rather than on the sender.
12.grammar: A past-tense passive verb in Form IV (anzala 'to send down' → unzila 'was sent down'). The prefix is only the u- vowel carried on the connecting hamza; the nūn that follows is the first root letter (of ن-ز-ل), not part of the prefix. The internal vowel pattern u–i marks it as passive ('was/were sent down'), with no named doer. The final -a marks the subject as 'he/it', a single masculine thing, and signals completed action.
