12.root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — to descend, come down; (Form IV) to send down

13.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
13.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

14.meaning: 'Before you' (in time or place): the period or position prior to a single person — that which comes earlier or stands in front, relative to one addressee.
14.grammar: The adverb/noun qabl ('before, prior') with the attached pronoun -ka ('you', a single male). The -i ending on qabl is genitive, the case regularly taken after a preposition (such as min, 'from before') and when a noun is linked to a following possessor; here it is linked to the pronoun 'you' ('before-you').
14.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to precede, be before; priority, what comes first

15.meaning: they want / they intend — to will, desire, or purpose something. The verb conveys an active, ongoing intention or wish on the part of a group.
15.grammar: A present-tense Form IV verb (arāda, 'to will/intend'). The yu- prefix marks a third-person subject, and the ending -ūna marks masculine plural plus the indicative mood (a plain statement: 'they want'). The -na would drop under a particle that changes the mood.

16.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
16.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'
16.root: — (particle; no root)

17.meaning: they seek judgment from one another / they take a dispute to be judged — to bring a quarrel before an arbiter for a ruling. The pattern conveys a mutual action: parties referring their case to be decided.
17.grammar: A present-tense verb of the reciprocal Form VI (tafāʿala), signaling an action carried out mutually — parties seeking a ruling between themselves. The ya- prefix marks 'they', and the -ū ending marks masculine plural in the subjunctive/jussive mood (the short form taken after certain particles, where the indicative -na is dropped). The long final alif is silent (alif al-wiqāyah).
17.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — to judge, rule, govern, decide

18.meaning: 'To / toward / up to' — a preposition marking the endpoint, goal, or limit of an action or motion: the direction something moves toward or the boundary at which it stops.
18.grammar: An invariable preposition. It has no case ending of its own but puts the noun that follows it into the genitive ('of / to' state). It indicates direction toward, or the terminal limit of, something.

19.meaning: the false object of worship — anything wrongfully set up as a deity or authority beside Allah: an idol, a tyrant, a devil, or any power obeyed in rebellion against the truth. 'Ṭāghūt' is an intensive form rooted in the idea of overstepping all bounds.
19.grammar: A definite noun: the prefix al- ('the') is assimilated into the 'sun letter' ṭ (so it sounds aṭ-ṭ). The ending -i marks the genitive case, the form a word typically takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of …').
19.root: ط-غ-ي (ṭ-gh-y) — to exceed all limits, transgress, tyrannize

20.meaning: 'And indeed / while already' — the word 'wa' ('and, while') joined to 'qad', a particle that, before a past-tense verb, stresses that the action has certainly and already happened.
20.grammar: A connective 'wa' ('and', or circumstantial 'while') plus the particle 'qad'. With a past-tense verb, 'qad' emphasizes completion and certainty ('has indeed already…'); with a present-tense verb it can mean 'sometimes' or 'may'.

21.meaning: they were commanded / they were ordered — to be instructed or directed to do something. This is the passive: the doers received an order, with the commander left unnamed.
21.grammar: A past-tense passive Form I verb: the vowel pattern u–i ('umirū') shows it is passive ('were commanded'), so the subject is the one receiving the order. The suffix -ū is the masculine-plural subject ending ('they'), and the trailing alif is silent (alif al-wiqāyah).

22.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
22.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

23.meaning: they disbelieve / they reject (faith) — to deny, refuse, or cover over the truth, especially rejecting faith in Allah. At root the word means to 'cover up' or conceal.
23.grammar: A present-tense Form I verb. The ya- prefix marks a third-person subject, and the -ū ending marks masculine plural in the subjunctive/jussive mood — the shortened form (without indicative -na) taken after certain governing particles. The trailing alif is silent (alif al-wiqāyah).
23.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to disbelieve, be ungrateful

24.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
24.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

25.meaning: 'And he/it wills, wants, intends, or desires.' It conveys deliberate volition and purpose aimed at bringing something about, not mere fleeting wish.
25.grammar: A connector wa- ('and/but') joined to a present-tense (imperfect) verb in derived Form IV. The yu- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it') acting now or habitually. The final -u is the indicative ending, the default mood for a simple statement of fact.

26.meaning: Shayṭān / Satan — a rebellious, malevolent being who incites to evil; the term denotes one that is remote from goodness and given to misleading. With 'al-', it points to the well-known devil.
26.grammar: 'al-' is 'the' (its 'l' assimilates into the 'sh', doubling it). 'shayṭān' is a noun for a devil or inciter of evil. The final -u is nominative, the form a word takes as the subject or doer of an action.
26.root: ش-ط-ن (sh-ṭ-n) — to be distant/remote (from good)

27.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
27.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

28.meaning: he leads them astray / to make them stray — to cause someone to lose the right way and wander into error. The verb is causative: making others go astray. It carries an attached object 'them'.
28.grammar: A present-tense causative Form IV verb (aḍalla, 'to make stray'). The yu- prefix marks a third-person singular subject ('he/it'). The stem-final -a reflects the subjunctive/jussive mood (the short form after a governing particle). The attached -hum is an object pronoun, 'them' (masculine plural). The doubled l reflects the geminate root.
28.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to stray, get lost, err

29.meaning: straying / error — the state of being lost from the right path, wandering far from guidance and truth. A verbal noun naming the condition of going astray.
29.grammar: A verbal noun (maṣdar) on the faʿāl pattern, naming the act/state of straying. The final -an (tanwīn fatḥah) marks the accusative — often used for the object of a verb or as an absolute object reinforcing a verb ('to stray a [great] straying') — and the -n shows it is indefinite.
29.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to stray, get lost, err

30.meaning: Far, distant, remote — describing something at a great remove in space, time, or degree. As an adjective it qualifies a noun as 'far off, far-reaching'.
30.grammar: An adjective on the faʿīl pattern (often intensive: 'very far'). The -an ending (tanwīn) marks it indefinite and accusative — agreeing with an indefinite accusative noun it describes. The accusative is the case of objects and many complements; the tanwīn marks indefiniteness ('a far …').
30.root: ب-ع-د (b-ʿ-d) — distance, remoteness, being far

1.meaning: 'And when...' — a linking phrase joining 'and' to 'when', used to introduce a circumstance or a recurring situation: 'and whenever / and at the time that...'.
1.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') attached to idhā ('when'). Idhā is a particle pointing to a time or condition, generally referring to something expected or recurring in the future ('when / whenever' it happens), and it normally introduces a following clause that states what occurs at that time.

2.meaning: 'It was said' — speech was uttered or a statement was made. The passive form: the saying is reported without naming who spoke.

parts.en: was said (passive verb stem of the root q-w-l)
he/it (default short vowel of the 3rd masc. sg. past)

2.grammar: A past-tense verb in the passive voice (pattern qīla) from the hollow root ق-و-ل. The passive is formed by internal vowel change: the middle radical (wāw) is replaced by a long 'ī', which marks the verb as passive (the doer is left unnamed). The lām is the third root letter, not an ending; the final -a is simply the default short vowel of the third-person masculine singular past, here used impersonally as 'it was said'.
2.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — saying, speech, utterance

3.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
3.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

4.meaning: 'Come! / Come now!' — a call summoning people to approach or come forward, often used to invite a group toward a course of action.
4.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to a group, masculine plural ('you all'). The -aw ending carries the plural 'you' addressees; the silent alif is a spelling convention written after this plural ending. It is an invitation to approach.

5.meaning: A preposition meaning 'to,' 'toward,' or 'up to' — pointing to the end-point, goal, or limit of a motion, direction, or extent.
5.grammar: A preposition (a small linking word). It governs the noun after it, putting that noun in the genitive case, and points to a destination or limit ('to,' 'toward,' 'as far as').

6.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
6.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

7.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'he sent down, he caused to descend, he revealed' — used especially of Allah sending down revelation, rain, or blessings from above.
7.grammar: A completed (past) action by a single masculine subject ('he'); the -a ending marks third-person masculine singular. The form IV (causative) pattern means 'to make something come down,' i.e., to send it down.

8.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
8.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

9.meaning: And to / and toward; a connector "and" joined with a preposition expressing direction or destination toward which something moves or is referred.
9.grammar: A preposition meaning "to/toward," prefixed with the connector wa- ("and"). Being a preposition, it puts the noun that follows it into the genitive case (the "…toward X" relationship). It has no case ending of its own.

10.meaning: the Messenger — one sent with a message; specifically an envoy commissioned by Allah to convey His revelation. 'Rasūl' is a faʿūl-pattern noun denoting the one who is sent.
10.grammar: A definite noun: the prefix al- ('the') is assimilated into the 'sun letter' r (so it sounds ar-r). The ending -i marks the genitive case, the form a word typically takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of …').
10.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — to send; a message, an envoy

11.meaning: you saw / you have seen — to perceive with the eye, and by extension to notice or come to realize something. This form addresses a single male and refers to completed perceiving.
11.grammar: A past-tense Form I verb. The suffix -ta is the subject ending meaning 'you' (a single male) and marks the action as completed. The middle hamzah is original to the root (r-ʾ-y).

12.meaning: the hypocrites — those who outwardly profess faith while inwardly concealing disbelief; people who present one face publicly and hide another within. From a root evoking a tunnel with two openings, suggesting a hidden way out.
12.grammar: A definite noun: al- means 'the'. 'Munāfiq' is an active participle of Form III ('one who behaves hypocritically'). The ending -īna marks the masculine sound plural in the oblique case (the form used for objects of verbs and after prepositions, i.e. accusative/genitive, as opposed to nominative -ūna).
12.root: ن-ف-ق (n-f-q) — tunnel/burrow with a hidden exit; hence hypocrisy

13.meaning: they turn away / they bar (others) — to hold back, hinder, or avert; to turn oneself or others aside from something. The verb describes an ongoing, present action by a group.
13.grammar: A present-tense Form I verb. The ya- prefix marks a third-person subject, and the ending -ūna (the -ū fused into the doubled d, written ṣuddūna) marks masculine plural plus the indicative mood — a plain ongoing statement ('they turn away'). The doubled d reflects the geminate root.
13.root: ص-د-د (ṣ-d-d) — to turn away, avert, hinder, bar

14.meaning: With you / about you / from you — the preposition ʿan ('away from, about, concerning') joined to 'you' (one male); after a verb of being pleased it carries the sense 'pleased WITH you'.
14.grammar: A preposition plus an attached pronoun. ʿan basically means moving away from, or 'about/concerning' a topic; paired with a verb of contentment it yields 'pleased with'. The suffix -ka is the second-person masculine singular object ('you', one male). Together: 'with you / concerning you'.

15.meaning: turning away / aversion — the act of recoiling from something and keeping clear of it, a determined turning aside. A verbal noun naming this behavior.
15.grammar: A verbal noun (maṣdar) on the fuʿūl pattern, naming the act of turning away. The final -an (tanwīn fatḥah) marks the accusative — frequently used as an absolute object reinforcing a related verb ('they turn away a [real] turning-away') — and the -n shows it is indefinite.
15.root: ص-د-د (ṣ-d-d) — to turn away, avert, hinder, bar

1.meaning: So how? / Then in what manner or state? — kayfa is the interrogative 'how', asking after the manner, condition or circumstance of something. With the prefixed 'so/then' it introduces a question following from what precedes, often expressing wonder or warning.
1.grammar: An interrogative particle ('how') carrying the connective prefix fa- ('so / then'), which links it to a preceding statement as a consequence or follow-up. As a particle, kayfa is indeclinable: its fixed final -a is not a case ending and does not change.

2.meaning: 'When' — a particle introducing a time or circumstance, generally pointing to something expected or definite to come ('when/whenever it happens'). It sets up a condition or moment whose outcome then follows.
2.grammar: An indeclinable adverb/particle of time; it has no case ending and never changes form. It typically introduces a clause about a future or recurring event ('when …'), and is normally followed by a verb describing what takes place.
2.root: — (a time particle; no triliteral root)

3.meaning: 'it struck them / befell them / hit them' — when a misfortune, event, or thing reaches and lands upon people; the root sense is hitting the mark or reaching accurately.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb. The '-at/-t' ending marks a feminine singular subject ('she/it'), agreeing with a feminine doer. The attached '-hum' is the object 'them'. It states a completed action that reached or struck its object.
3.root: ص-و-ب (ṣ-w-b) — to hit the mark, reach, befall correctly

4.meaning: A calamity, affliction, or misfortune — something distressing that strikes a person, especially trouble that arrives suddenly and from outside one's control.
4.grammar: An active-participle-based feminine noun, here standing as a singular indefinite noun. The final -un (nunation/tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('a misfortune') and in the nominative case, the form a noun takes when it is the subject of a sentence or the thing being identified.
4.root: ص-و-ب (ṣ-w-b) — to hit a target, to strike, to befall (also linked to what is right/apt)

5.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
5.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

6.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'she/it put forward / sent ahead / advanced beforehand' — to send something on ahead, often used of deeds a person has done in advance and dispatched before themselves.
6.grammar: A completed (past-tense) verb in an intensive pattern (doubled middle letter) that conveys deliberately putting something forward. The ending -at marks a third-person feminine-singular subject, 'she' or 'it (feminine)', so it reads 'she/it sent ahead'.
6.root: ق-د-م (q-d-m) — coming before, advancing, putting forward

7.meaning: Their hands. The plural noun 'hands' carrying the masculine plural possessive 'their'; often used idiomatically for what people do, produce, or are responsible for through their own deeds.
7.grammar: A plural noun with an attached possessive pronoun '-him' meaning 'their' (a group of males, or mixed). 'aydī' is the irregular ('broken') plural of 'yad' (hand). The pronoun ending makes the whole construction definite and possessed; the 'i'-coloured stem before the suffix reflects its genitive/possessed state, the form typically following a preposition or standing as object.

8.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
8.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

9.meaning: they came to you — to arrive at or approach someone. This combines the verb 'they came' with an attached 'you', i.e. they presented themselves before a single male addressee.
9.grammar: A past-tense Form I verb. The -ū ending is the masculine-plural subject ('they'), marking completed action. The attached -ka is an object pronoun, 'you' (a single male). The plural normally carries a silent trailing alif, which drops before the attached pronoun. The hamzah is the final root letter.

10.meaning: they swear (an oath) — to make a solemn sworn declaration, calling something sacred to witness. The verb describes an ongoing, present swearing by a group.
10.grammar: A present-tense Form I verb. The ya- prefix marks a third-person subject, and the ending -ūna marks masculine plural together with the indicative mood — a plain ongoing statement ('they swear'). The -na drops when a governing particle changes the mood.
10.root: ح-ل-ف (ḥ-l-f) — to swear, take an oath

11.meaning: A phrase 'in Allah / by Allah', combining the preposition 'with/in/by' and the divine name Allah, the proper name of the One God.
11.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with, by means of') prefixed to the divine name Allah. A preposition always forces the following noun into the genitive case, which is why Allah here ends in -i. With verbs of believing, bi- conveys the object of faith — to believe IN.
11.root: — (Allah is the proper name of God and is not derived from a triliteral root in the usual sense)

12.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
12.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

13.meaning: we intended / we desired — to purpose, will, or aim at something. This is the 'we' form of the verb of intending, referring to a completed intention of the speakers.
13.grammar: A past-tense Form IV verb (arāda, 'to will/intend'). The suffix -nā is the subject ending meaning 'we' and marks the action as completed. In the past tense this Form IV verb shows the hamzah-a- prefix (ara-) rather than the present 'u-' prefix.

14.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
14.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

15.meaning: Good treatment, excellence, doing what is beautiful and right — acting toward others with kindness, generosity, and the highest moral excellence (iḥsān), going beyond mere duty to genuine goodness.
15.grammar: A verbal noun (the act of doing good). The -an ending (tanwīn fatḥ) marks the indefinite accusative; it often functions adverbially or as an object, conveying 'doing good' or '[show] good treatment' — describing the manner or content of an action.
15.root: ح-س-ن (ḥ-s-n) — to be good, beautiful, excellent

16.meaning: And reconciliation, the bringing of hearts and parties into harmony and accord; the granting of success in setting matters right between people. Built from a sense of being made to agree and fit together well.
16.grammar: A verbal noun (the action of reconciling/bringing into accord) carried by the form II pattern (taf'īl). The final -an is the indefinite accusative (nasb): it commonly marks a word as the object of a verb, or as an indefinite 'a …' that answers 'how much / what kind'. The doubled 'w' shows the connecting 'and' has been joined to the front.
16.root: و-ف-ق (w-f-q) — to be in agreement, suitable, well-matched

1.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'those' — pointing to people or things that are distant or already known. It singles out a group ('those ones', 'it is those who').
1.grammar: A plural demonstrative pronoun, 'those'. It is fixed in form (no case endings). The -ka element signals distance/remoteness, pointing to something far off or notable. It can refer to people of either gender.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: 'He/it knows' — a present-tense verb of knowing: to have knowledge of, be aware of, recognize, or understand something.
3.grammar: Present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it'). The ya- prefix marks 'he,' and the final -u marks the ordinary (indicative) present, 'he knows / does know.'
3.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — knowledge; knowing, being aware, recognizing

4.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
4.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

5.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
5.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

6.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
6.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
6.root: — (particle)

7.meaning: Their hearts. The heart as the inner seat of feeling, understanding, intention, and faith — not merely the physical organ but the core of a person's being. Marked as belonging to a group ('their').
7.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural noun, 'hearts,' with the attached possessive pronoun -him 'their' (a group of males, or a mixed group). The -i vowel is the genitive case marker, assigned by the noun's role in the sentence (for instance, governed by a preposition or as the second term of a possessive construction). The suffix -him does not itself cause the genitive; it simply attaches as the possessor, giving 'their hearts.'
7.root: ق-ل-ب (q-l-b) — to turn over, turn about; the heart (that which turns/changes)

8.meaning: So turn away, avert yourself, decline to engage — a command to one person to leave something aside or disregard it. The opening 'so/then' connects it as a consequence of what precedes.
8.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to a single male, from a form IV verb meaning 'to turn aside / pay no heed.' The bare, vowel-less ending (sukūn on the final letter) is typical of the singular masculine command: 'do it!' The prefixed fa- means 'so/then,' linking it as a result.
8.root: ع-ر-ض (ʿ-r-ḍ) — to be wide/broad, to present sideways; to turn away

9.meaning: From them; away from them; concerning them. The preposition ʿan conveys moving away from, departing from, or 'on behalf of / concerning', combined with the pronoun 'them'.
9.grammar: A preposition joined to the attached pronoun -hum, 'them' (referring to a group, grammatically masculine plural). The preposition ʿan basically signals separation or removal ('away from'), and can also mean 'about/concerning' or 'on behalf of' depending on usage.

10.meaning: And admonish them, counsel them earnestly, remind them of right conduct and its consequences in a way that softens the heart — a command to one person directed at a group.
10.grammar: A command (imperative) to a single male — 'admonish!' — with the attached object pronoun -hum 'them' (a group of males or mixed group). The verb's vowel-less stem marks the singular command; the pronoun -hum tells us who receives the admonition.

11.meaning: And say — a command to one person to utter or speak words. The plain, central act of speaking aloud.
11.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to a single male, 'say!' from a hollow verb (middle root letter 'w' drops out in the command). The vowel-less ending is the standard singular masculine imperative. Prefixed wa- 'and' joins it to a preceding clause.

12.meaning: 'For them / to them / theirs' — a preposition 'for / to / belonging to' joined to the pronoun 'them,' expressing that something pertains, belongs, or is owed to that group.
12.grammar: The preposition li- ('for / to / belonging to'), whose vowel becomes -a before an attached pronoun, joined to -hum ('them'). It commonly expresses possession or benefit — 'theirs / for them.' Particles like this carry no case or tense of their own.

13.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
13.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

14.meaning: Themselves / their own selves — the noun nafs ('self, soul, person, inner being') joined to a pronoun 'their'. Used reflexively it means 'their own selves' and conveys the inmost self, the seat of desires and the person as a whole.
14.grammar: The plural noun anfus ('selves') carries the genitive -i ending followed by the possessive pronoun -him ('their'). The genitive marks the noun as governed by a preposition or joined to a preceding word; -him makes it 'their selves'.
14.root: ن-ف-س (n-f-s) — self, soul, breath, inner being

15.meaning: 'A saying / word / statement' — an utterance or speech; that which is said.
15.grammar: A verbal noun meaning 'a saying.' The ending -an is the indefinite accusative (tanwīn fatḥ): it marks an indefinite noun in the accusative case, the form used for the object of a verb (e.g., 'to say a word') among other roles.

16.meaning: Penetrating, far-reaching, eloquent — describing speech that reaches its mark and has its full effect; words that arrive at the listener and move them. Built from the idea of reaching/arriving at a destination.
16.grammar: An adjective of the intensive faʿīl pattern, describing something that thoroughly reaches/attains its aim. The -an ending is the indefinite accusative (nasb): it typically marks an indefinite descriptive word agreeing with an accusative noun, or stands as 'an … (one).'
16.root: ب-ل-غ (b-l-gh) — to reach, attain, arrive at; eloquence (speech that reaches)

1.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

2.meaning: We sent / dispatched. From the causative verb meaning to send forth or commission, especially the sending of messengers; with 'We' as the subject.
2.grammar: Past/perfect verb in the causative (form IV) pattern meaning 'to send', 1st person plural ('we'). The suffix -nā is the subject ending 'we' on a completed action. The perfect tense presents the sending as accomplished and complete.
2.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — sending, dispatching, messengership

3.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
3.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

4.meaning: A messenger, an envoy — one who is sent bearing a message; in religious use, a prophet sent by Allah with a revealed mission. The word names the sent-one himself.
4.grammar: A noun of the faʿūl pattern meaning 'one who is sent.' The -in ending is the indefinite genitive: it usually shows the word follows a preposition, or links to a preceding noun as 'a messenger OF …,' or otherwise stands in a genitive slot. The doubled 'r' shows a preceding particle has merged onto it.
4.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — to send, dispatch; a message/messenger

5.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
5.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

6.meaning: So that he may be obeyed — expressing the purpose that someone be heeded and complied with. The action of obeying here falls upon him (he is the one obeyed), not done by him.
6.grammar: A present-tense verb in the passive voice (form IV), 'he is/be obeyed,' put into the subjunctive by the purpose-particle li- 'so that.' The yu- prefix with the passive vowelling means the subject receives the action ('be obeyed'), and the final -a is the subjunctive marking purpose or intent after li-.
6.root: ط-و-ع (ṭ-w-ʿ) — to obey, comply, submit willingly

7.meaning: 'By the leave of / with the permission of' — formed from 'with/by' plus 'permission, leave, sanction'. It conveys that something happens by someone's authorization or enabling will.
7.grammar: The prefix bi- is a preposition 'with/by'. The noun 'idhn' means 'permission, leave, sanction'. After the preposition it takes the genitive -i ending, the form used following a preposition and typically linking on to a following noun ('the permission OF …').
7.root: أ-ذ-ن (ʾ-dh-n) — to permit, give leave; also listening/ear

8.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
8.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

9.meaning: 'and if' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the particle 'if'. This particular 'if' (law) introduces a hypothetical or contrary-to-fact condition: 'if (such-and-such had been the case)…', often implying it was not.
9.grammar: A conjunction plus a conditional particle. wa- means 'and'. law is a non-changing particle (no case ending) that sets up a supposition, typically answered by a clause beginning with la- ('… then certainly …').

10.meaning: 'That they…' — an emphatic connector 'anna' ('that, indeed') fused with the pronoun 'they,' used to introduce an affirmed clause as the content of a thought or statement.
10.grammar: Built on the particle 'anna' ('that…, indeed'), which introduces and affirms a following clause (often after verbs of knowing, thinking, or saying) and puts its noun into the accusative. The attached '-hum' is the pronoun 'they/them' for a male-inclusive group.

11.meaning: When — a particle pointing to a past moment or circumstance, 'at the time that …'. It situates an event in time, typically introducing something that occurred.
11.grammar: A time particle/adverb meaning 'when' or 'at the time when,' generally pointing to the past. It is indeclinable — it never changes its ending — and serves to introduce a clause about when something happened.

12.meaning: They wronged, acted unjustly, placed something where it does not belong; oppressed or did harm against the right of another or against themselves. A completed act done by a group.
12.grammar: A past-tense (completed) verb. The ending -ū means the doers are 'they,' a group of males (or mixed). So it reads 'they wronged / they did injustice.' The doubled initial 'ẓ' shows a preceding particle has assimilated onto the verb.
12.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — injustice, wrongdoing; darkness; putting a thing out of its place

13.meaning: A noun meaning 'their own selves' or 'themselves' — the plural of 'nafs' (self, soul, person, inner self), joined to the pronoun 'their.' It commonly conveys the reflexive idea of acting upon one's own self.
13.grammar: A noun (a broken/irregular plural of 'nafs') with the attached possessive pronoun '-hum' ('their/them,' masculine plural). The -a case ending before the pronoun is accusative, typically marking the word as the direct object of a verb — i.e. the self upon which the action falls.

14.meaning: they came to you — to arrive at or approach someone. This combines the verb 'they came' with an attached 'you', i.e. they presented themselves before a single male addressee.
14.grammar: A past-tense Form I verb. The -ū ending is the masculine-plural subject ('they'), marking completed action. The attached -ka is an object pronoun, 'you' (a single male). The plural normally carries a silent trailing alif, which drops before the attached pronoun. The hamzah is the final root letter.

15.meaning: And then they sought forgiveness — a group asked Allah to pardon and cover over their faults. The 'fa-' adds the sense 'and so / then', linking it as the next step after something.
15.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in Form X, whose pattern ('istafʿala') typically means 'to seek/ask for' the root's action — here, to seek forgiveness. The prefixed 'fa-' means 'then / and so'. The '-ū' ending marks a 'they' subject (masculine plural) and a completed action.
15.root: غ-ف-ر (gh-f-r) — to cover, forgive, pardon; concealment of sins

16.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
16.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.
16.root: — (proper name)

17.meaning: And he sought forgiveness, asked to be pardoned and have his faults covered over. The verb conveys actively requesting pardon, typically from Allah.
17.grammar: A past-tense verb of form X (the ista- pattern), which carries the sense of 'seeking/asking for' the root meaning — here 'to seek forgiveness.' The bare final -a marks a single male doer: 'he sought forgiveness.' Prefixed wa- means 'and.'
17.root: غ-ف-ر (gh-f-r) — to cover, conceal, forgive; pardon

18.meaning: To them / for them — the preposition li- ('to, for') joined to the pronoun 'them'. It expresses that something is directed toward, belongs to, or is for the benefit of a group.
18.grammar: The preposition li- ('to/for') combined with the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). When li- takes a pronoun its vowel becomes 'la-'. The final -u here is a connecting vowel added to ease pronunciation before a following word; it carries no case meaning of its own.

19.meaning: 'The Messenger' — one sent with a message; in religious usage, a prophet commissioned by Allah to deliver revelation to people.
19.grammar: 'al-' is the definite article 'the' (its 'l' assimilates into the following r, doubling it). 'rasūl' is a noun meaning 'one who is sent, an envoy/messenger'. The final -u is the nominative ending, the case typically marking the subject of a sentence or a word simply being named.
19.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — sending, dispatching, a message/envoy

20.meaning: They would surely have found — a group's discovery or finding of something, presented as the certain result of a hypothetical condition. The opening 'la-' adds emphasis: 'they truly would have found.'
20.grammar: A past-tense verb with the ending -ū, 'they found' (a group of males/mixed). The prefixed la- is an emphatic particle, the typical answer to an 'if' clause: 'then they would surely have found.' Together it stresses a certain consequence.
20.root: و-ج-د (w-j-d) — to find, come upon; to perceive, to feel

21.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
21.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

22.meaning: 'Ever-relenting / constantly turning in acceptance of repentance' — an intensive descriptive form of tāba. Of Allah it means the One who again and again accepts the repentance of those who turn back; of a person, one who repents much.
22.grammar: An intensive adjective/noun on the fa''āl pattern, which signals doing something abundantly or habitually — here, repeatedly turning toward / accepting repentance. The -an ending is the accusative case with indefinite (tanwīn) 'n,' often marking it as a predicate or object describing someone as 'ever-relenting.'
22.root: ت-و-ب (t-w-b) — to turn back, repent, return

23.meaning: 'Most Merciful / deeply compassionate' — an intensive form of raḥima, denoting one full of mercy and tender compassion; a frequent description of Allah.
23.grammar: An intensive adjective on the fa'īl pattern, expressing a deep, abiding quality — abounding in mercy. The -an ending is the accusative case with indefinite (tanwīn) 'n,' often marking it as a predicate or as describing someone as 'most merciful.'

1.meaning: A two-part word: the connective particle 'fa-' meaning 'so', 'then', or 'therefore' (drawing a consequence from what precedes), joined to 'lā', the particle of negation/prohibition. Together they convey 'so do not …' or 'so there is no …'.
1.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that links a clause to what came before and often signals a result or consequence. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a present-tense verb it commonly forms a prohibition ('do not …') or a simple negation ('not'). It carries no ending of its own.

2.meaning: By your Lord — an oath sworn upon the Lord, the Master, Owner, Nurturer and Sustainer who creates, governs, and brings to maturity. 'Rabb' is one who owns and cares for, gradually nurturing what is in His charge; here addressed as 'your Lord' with an oath.
2.grammar: The noun 'Lord' with the attached possessive -ka 'your' (one male). The leading wa- here is the oath-particle 'by …,' which governs the genitive and so produces the -i ending. The possessive suffix -ka does not affect the case; it simply attaches as the possessor, giving 'your Lord.'
2.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, own, bring up

3.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
3.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

4.meaning: 'They believe / they have faith' — to affirm something as true with trusting inner conviction and to feel secure in it. The verb carries both believing and being at peace through that belief; in religious use it is to commit oneself in faith.
4.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb, masculine plural. The yu-…-una frame means 'they (men, or a mixed group) do' the action now or habitually. The retained final -na marks the indicative (a plain, unqualified statement) — 'they believe' — as opposed to forms where that -na drops. The verb is Form IV (amana), used intransitively here meaning simply 'to believe / to have faith'.

5.meaning: 'Until / up to the point that; so that' — a particle marking a limit or goal. It expresses the end-point reached ('until') or the purpose aimed at ('so that, in order that').
5.grammar: A particle indicating a goal or limit. When followed by a present-tense verb it places that verb in the subjunctive mood (clipping its ending to -a), conveying 'until / so that' something comes about. Ḥattā itself is invariable.

6.meaning: They make you (one male) the judge, appoint you to arbitrate and decide between disputing parties. Built from a sense of making firm, judging, and giving binding decisions.

parts.en: they make judge / appoint as arbiter

6.grammar: A present/ongoing verb of form II, 'to make (someone) a judge / submit a dispute to him for decision.' The -ū element means the doers are 'they' (a group of males/mixed); the attached -ka is the object 'you' (one male) — the one being made judge. Lacking a 'nūn' on the plural ending, the verb is in the subjunctive/jussive mood (typically governed by a preceding particle).
6.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — to judge, decide, govern; wisdom, firm restraint

7.meaning: A compound particle joining the preposition 'in/about' with the relative pronoun 'what', yielding 'in that which' or 'concerning what' — pointing to the matter or subject about which something is said or done.
7.grammar: A fixed combination of the preposition 'fī' and the indeclinable relative 'mā'. Being particles, neither takes a case ending; the phrase functions as 'in/about what…'.

8.meaning: It arose, sprang up, became entangled — used of a dispute or matter that grows complicated and tangled between people, like interlocking branches. The root literally evokes branching trees.
8.grammar: A past-tense (completed) verb with the bare ending -a, marking a single masculine subject: 'it arose / it became tangled.' Derived from the imagery of trees and branches interlacing, it describes a matter that has sprung up and become knotted.
8.root: ش-ج-ر (sh-j-r) — trees; to interlace, become entangled; to dispute

9.meaning: An adverb of place meaning 'between' or 'among', here joined to the attached pronoun 'them'; together it conveys 'between them / amongst them', signalling something situated in the midst of a group or shared among parties.
9.grammar: An adverb of place (ẓarf) ending in -a, the accusative marker typical of such adverbs, indicating a location or relationship. The attached suffix '-hum' is a possessive/object pronoun meaning 'them' (a group of males or a mixed group).
9.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction, what lies in the midst

10.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
10.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

11.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
11.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

12.meaning: They find, come upon, perceive — the act of finding or discovering done by a group, presented as ongoing or as a possibility (not yet completed).
12.grammar: A present-tense verb, 'they find,' with the ya-…-ū frame marking a group of males/mixed as the doers. The absence of a final 'nūn' (it is -ū, not -ūna) shows the jussive/subjunctive mood — the verb is shortened because a preceding particle governs it (e.g., a negation or condition).
12.root: و-ج-د (w-j-d) — to find, come upon; to perceive, to feel

13.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
13.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

14.meaning: Themselves / their own selves — the noun nafs ('self, soul, person, inner being') joined to a pronoun 'their'. Used reflexively it means 'their own selves' and conveys the inmost self, the seat of desires and the person as a whole.
14.grammar: The plural noun anfus ('selves') carries the genitive -i ending followed by the possessive pronoun -him ('their'). The genitive marks the noun as governed by a preposition or joined to a preceding word; -him makes it 'their selves'.
14.root: ن-ف-س (n-f-s) — self, soul, breath, inner being

15.meaning: Discomfort, constriction, distress — a tightness in the breast; resistance, reluctance, or moral unease; also a sense of sin or blame that constricts one. Built from the idea of narrowness and being hemmed in.
15.grammar: A noun meaning 'tightness, distress, hindrance.' The -an ending is the indefinite accusative (nasb): it typically marks the word as the object of a verb ('to find / feel a …') or as an indefinite 'any …'.
15.root: ح-ر-ج (ḥ-r-j) — narrowness, tightness, constriction; difficulty, sin

16.meaning: A fused word combining the preposition 'min' ('from', 'of', 'about') with the relative/indefinite 'mā' ('what', 'that which'). Together: 'from what', 'about that which', 'of what'.
16.grammar: The preposition 'min' and the word 'mā' merge in pronunciation (the 'n' assimilating into the 'm'). 'min' governs a genitive, and 'mā' here functions as a relative pronoun introducing a clause ('that which …'). These are indeclinable particles without case endings.

17.meaning: You decided, judged, decreed, brought to a conclusion — a completed act of settling a matter or passing a verdict, done by the person addressed (one male). Carries the sense of finishing and finalizing.
17.grammar: A past-tense (completed) verb. The ending -ta means the doer is 'you,' a single male: 'you decided / you decreed.' It denotes an action brought to its definitive close.
17.root: ق-ض-ي (q-ḍ-y) — to decide, decree, settle, complete; to pass judgement

18.meaning: And they submit, yield, accept fully and peacefully — surrendering to a decision or to the will of Allah without resistance, with inner acceptance. Linked to peace and wholeness.
18.grammar: A present-tense verb of form II, conveying full, active submission/surrender. The -ū element marks the doers as 'they' (a group of males/mixed). The missing final 'nūn' (it is -ū, not -ūna) shows the subjunctive/jussive mood, governed by a preceding particle. Prefixed wa- 'and' joins it to a preceding verb.
18.root: س-ل-م (s-l-m) — soundness, peace, safety; to submit, surrender wholly

19.meaning: A full submitting, a wholehearted surrender and acceptance — the verbal noun naming the very act of yielding completely and at peace. Often used to intensify the verb 'they submit,' as in 'submit with utter submission.'
19.grammar: A verbal noun of the form II pattern (taf'īl), naming the action of submitting/surrendering wholly. The -an ending is the indefinite accusative (nasb); a verbal noun in this case very often serves to reinforce its own verb, giving the sense 'to submit a thorough submitting = to submit utterly.'
19.root: س-ل-م (s-l-m) — soundness, peace, safety; to submit, surrender wholly

1.meaning: 'and if' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the particle 'if'. This particular 'if' (law) introduces a hypothetical or contrary-to-fact condition: 'if (such-and-such had been the case)…', often implying it was not.
1.grammar: A conjunction plus a conditional particle. wa- means 'and'. law is a non-changing particle (no case ending) that sets up a supposition, typically answered by a clause beginning with la- ('… then certainly …').

2.meaning: That We … — an emphatic linking particle 'that' fused with the pronoun 'We.' 'Anna' introduces and asserts a fact ('that indeed …'), and the attached 'We' names the doer (a majestic or plural 'We').
2.grammar: An emphatic particle 'anna' ('that, indeed') with the attached pronoun -nā 'we.' This family of particles takes a following noun/pronoun in the accusative as its subject, so -nā here functions as that subject: 'that We …'. It firmly introduces a stated fact.

3.meaning: We wrote / We decreed / We prescribed — a completed act of writing, and by extension of ordaining and making something binding, performed by 'We' (a majestic or plural speaker). What is 'written' is fixed and obligatory.
3.grammar: A past-tense (completed) verb. The ending -nā means the doers are 'we': 'we wrote / we decreed.' Beyond literal writing, this verb commonly means to prescribe or make obligatory — what is written down is thereby ordained.
3.root: ك-ت-ب (k-t-b) — to write, inscribe; to prescribe, ordain

4.meaning: A compound meaning 'upon them' or 'against them': the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over, against') joined to the plural pronoun 'them'. It conveys something resting on, being incumbent upon, or weighing against a group.
4.grammar: ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay- before a pronoun. The suffix -him is the attached pronominal suffix for a masculine plural group ('them'); after a preposition it carries genitive/prepositional force, and the -i- vowel reflects its position after this preposition. Together they signal a relationship of something being over, upon, or burdensome to that group.
4.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

5.meaning: That — an explanatory particle introducing the content of a preceding statement or command, roughly 'namely that …' or 'to the effect that …'. It unpacks what was said or commanded.
5.grammar: An explanatory particle 'an' meaning 'that / namely,' used to spell out the substance of a foregoing verb of saying or commanding (so the words that follow explain it). Its base form ends in a vowel-less 'n'; the -i shown here is a helping vowel added only to ease pronunciation before a following consonant, not a case ending.

6.meaning: Kill! / Fight! — a command addressed to a group to slay or put to death. The bare, forceful core meaning of taking life, directed at more than one person.
6.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to a group of males/mixed, 'kill!' The ending -ū is the plural 'you-all' command marker: it directs the order at several people rather than one. The initial vowelled 'u-' is a helping prefix that lets the otherwise vowel-less command be pronounced.
6.root: ق-ت-ل (q-t-l) — to kill, slay, put to death; to fight

7.meaning: 'Yourselves' — your own selves, persons, or souls. The base noun 'nafs' means the self, soul, or inner person.
7.grammar: A plural noun, 'selves,' with the attached pronoun '-kum' ('your,' addressed to a group). The '-a' before the pronoun is the accusative case, marking the word as the direct object — the thing being acted upon.

8.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative between two or more options, linking possibilities of which one applies.
8.grammar: A connecting particle meaning 'or'. Its base form is aw; the added -i is a 'helping' vowel given to the otherwise-silent final consonant to smooth the link to a following word that begins with a connecting (hamzat-waṣl) alif. It is not a case ending — particles do not take cases.

9.meaning: A direct command addressed to a group of men: 'go out!', 'come out!', 'depart!' It orders people to leave a place or emerge from it.
9.grammar: An imperative (command) verb. The -ū ending addresses a plural masculine 'you' (more than one person). The initial 'u-' is a helping vowel that lets the word be pronounced. Overall force: 'all of you, go out!'

10.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
10.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

11.meaning: Your homes / your dwellings — the abodes belonging to the addressed group. 'diyār' is the plural of 'dār' (home, abode, dwelling-place).
11.grammar: A plural noun ('homes') with the attached possessive pronoun '-kum' (your, for a group). The -i ending before the suffix marks the genitive case — typically because the word follows a preposition or stands in a possessive 'of' link.
11.root: د-و-ر (d-w-r) — to turn, encircle; an enclosed dwelling, abode, home

12.meaning: A short, highly versatile particle 'mā.' It can mean 'what' or 'that which,' can negate ('not'), and can serve as an intensifier attached to another word. Its precise force depends on what it accompanies, but its core is to point to a thing or to add emphasis.
12.grammar: A multifunctional particle. It does not take case endings. Depending on usage it can be a relative ('that which'), an interrogative ('what?'), a negator ('not'), or — when joined to another particle — an emphasizer. It is uninflected and indeclinable.

13.meaning: 'They did it' or 'they would have done it' — a completed action of carrying out, performing, or doing something, attributed to a group, with 'it' as the thing done.
13.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū marks a plural masculine 'they' as the doers. The attached -hu ('it/him') is the object — the thing that was done. So: 'they did it'.
13.root: ف-ع-ل (f-ʿ-l) — doing, acting, performing a deed

14.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
14.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

15.meaning: 'Few', 'little', 'a small amount/number'. Describes something scant in quantity — a small group of people or a small portion of a thing.
15.grammar: A descriptive adjective (or noun). The '-un' ending is the nominative case with nunation ('tanwīn'), marking it as indefinite ('a few', not 'the few'); the nominative typically marks the subject or a predicate.

16.meaning: 'Among them / from them / some of them' — the preposition 'min' ('from, of, among') joined to the attached pronoun 'hum' ('them').
16.grammar: The preposition 'min' ('from / of / among') with the attached pronoun 'hum' ('them'), referring to a masculine plural group. Together they often express 'part of them' or 'some among them'.

17.meaning: 'and if' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the particle 'if'. This particular 'if' (law) introduces a hypothetical or contrary-to-fact condition: 'if (such-and-such had been the case)…', often implying it was not.
17.grammar: A conjunction plus a conditional particle. wa- means 'and'. law is a non-changing particle (no case ending) that sets up a supposition, typically answered by a clause beginning with la- ('… then certainly …').

18.meaning: 'That they…' — an emphatic connector 'anna' ('that, indeed') fused with the pronoun 'they,' used to introduce an affirmed clause as the content of a thought or statement.
18.grammar: Built on the particle 'anna' ('that…, indeed'), which introduces and affirms a following clause (often after verbs of knowing, thinking, or saying) and puts its noun into the accusative. The attached '-hum' is the pronoun 'they/them' for a male-inclusive group.

19.meaning: They did, they committed, they performed — a completed action carried out by a group (masculine 'they').
19.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb. The '-ū' ending means the subject is 'they' (a masculine plural group) and that the action is already complete. This very verb (faʿala) is the standard template by which Arabic grammarians name all verb patterns.
19.root: ف-ع-ل (f-ʿ-l) — to do, make, act; an action or deed

20.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
20.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

21.meaning: 'They are admonished / exhorted / counseled' — they are given earnest moral advice and warning, urging them toward good and away from harm.
21.grammar: A present-tense passive verb ('are being … -ed'). The prefix yu- carries the passive sense (the subject receives the action) and fuses with the root's initial w (و) to give the long vowel yū-. The -ūna ending marks a plural masculine 'they' and an ongoing/repeated action.
21.root: و-ع-ظ (w-ʿ-ẓ) — admonishing, exhorting, counseling with warning

22.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
22.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

23.meaning: 'Surely it would have been / it certainly was' — the verb 'to be' (past tense) carrying an emphatic 'surely', often introducing the result of a hypothetical condition.

parts.en: it was / it would have been

23.grammar: The past-tense verb kāna ('was/were'), third-person masculine singular, with the emphatic prefix la- ('surely'). In conditional sentences this combination commonly heads the consequence clause ('then it surely would have been…'). The verb kāna typically takes a following predicate in the accusative describing the subject's state.
23.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to become

24.meaning: Good — that which is beneficial, virtuous, and excellent; goodness as a thing one can do or possess, and what is better or preferable.
24.grammar: A noun (also serving as the 'better/best' form). The final -an (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite and in the accusative case — the case used for the direct object of a verb ('to do good') and for similar governed roles.

25.meaning: 'For them / to them / theirs' — a preposition 'for / to / belonging to' joined to the pronoun 'them,' expressing that something pertains, belongs, or is owed to that group.
25.grammar: The preposition li- ('for / to / belonging to'), whose vowel becomes -a before an attached pronoun, joined to -hum ('them'). It commonly expresses possession or benefit — 'theirs / for them.' Particles like this carry no case or tense of their own.

26.meaning: 'And stronger / firmer / more intense' — a comparison expressing greater strength, severity, or intensity, joined to what precedes by 'and'.
26.grammar: A comparative adjective ('more …'), built on the 'afʿal' pattern. The wa- means 'and'. The '-a' ending is the accusative case — often marking an object, or here following the pattern of a preceding accusative word it parallels.
26.root: ش-د-د (sh-d-d) — strength, firmness, intensity, severity

27.meaning: 'A making-firm', 'a strengthening', 'a steadying' — the act of making something steadfast, firmly fixed, and resolute.
27.grammar: A verbal noun (the name of an action) on the 'tafʿīl' pattern. The '-an' ending is the indefinite accusative with nunation; such an accusative noun often specifies in what respect something holds ('in terms of strengthening') or serves as an object.
27.root: ث-ب-ت (th-b-t) — being firm, steadfast, fixed, established

1.meaning: 'And then', 'and in that case' — joins a clause with 'and' while signaling a consequence or response: 'and then (as a result) …'.
1.grammar: A particle of response/consequence ('idhan') joined by wa- ('and'). It is not inflected for case; the final 'an' is part of the word itself. It frames what follows as the outcome of a stated condition: 'and then, accordingly …'.

2.meaning: 'We surely gave them' / 'We would surely have given them' — an act of granting or bestowing performed by 'We', directed at a group ('them'), emphatically affirmed.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb with the emphatic 'la-' prefix ('surely'). The -nā ending marks 'we' as the doers; the attached -hum ('them') is the object — the recipients of the giving. So: 'We surely gave them'.
2.root: أ-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — coming; in Form IV (afʿala pattern), bringing or giving

3.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
3.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

4.meaning: 'From Us', 'from Our presence', 'from Ourselves' — denotes something proceeding directly from a giver's own self or side. 'Ladun' means 'the presence/side of', and the ending here ties it to 'Us'.
4.grammar: An invariable noun of place/source ('ladun', 'the presence of') with the attached 'us'; the doubled-n reflects 'ladun' meeting the 'nā' ('us'). It conveys 'from Our own side', stressing that what is given comes directly from the giver.

5.meaning: A reward, wage, or recompense — the return earned for work or conduct, whether worldly pay or otherworldly recompense.
5.grammar: A noun meaning 'a reward.' The final '-an' (tanwīn fatḥa) marks the indefinite accusative case, the case used for the object of a verb (e.g. of 'to give'), giving the sense 'a reward.'
5.root: ا-ج-ر (ʾ-j-r) — reward, wage, recompense for what one does

6.meaning: 'Great, immense, mighty, momentous.' It describes something vast in size, weight, or seriousness, and is often used of grave or awe-inspiring matters.
6.grammar: An adjective on the intensive faʿīl pattern. The -an ending is the indefinite accusative ('a great …'), commonly marking an adjective that agrees with an indefinite accusative noun it describes, or the object of a verb.
6.root: ع-ظ-م (ʿ-ẓ-m) — to be great, immense

1.meaning: 'And We surely guided them' / 'would surely have guided them' — an act of guiding, directing onto the right path, done by 'We' toward a group, emphatically affirmed.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb prefixed with 'and' (wa-) and the emphatic 'la-' ('surely'). The -nā marks 'we' as the doers; the attached -hum ('them') is the object — those guided. So: 'and We surely guided them'.
1.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — guidance, showing the right way

2.meaning: 'A path', 'a way', 'a road' — a clear route or way that one travels, often used for a course of conduct or a way of life.
2.grammar: A noun. The '-an' ending is the indefinite accusative with nunation ('a path', not 'the path'); the accusative typically marks the direct object of a verb.
2.root: ص-ر-ط (ṣ-r-ṭ) — a way, path, road

3.meaning: 'Straight', 'upright', 'level' — describes something direct and without crookedness or deviation; figuratively, correct and sound.
3.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer'-form describing a state) on the 'mustafʿil' pattern, literally 'that which holds itself straight'. The '-an' ending is the indefinite accusative with nunation, agreeing with the indefinite accusative noun it describes.
3.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — standing, being upright; here, being straight

1.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
1.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

2.meaning: 'Obeys' / 'complies with' — to follow and carry out the command of another, to be obedient.
2.grammar: A present-tense verb, third person masculine singular ('he obeys'), in the jussive/conditional mood (a mood used after conditional or command particles). The base jussive ends in a silent consonant; the final -i here is a helping vowel added to avoid two unvowelled consonants meeting, not a case ending. The shadda on the yā' is an assimilation (idghām) carried over in recitation from a preceding word.
2.root: ط-و-ع (ṭ-w-ʿ) — obedience, willing compliance

3.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
3.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

4.meaning: A compound: 'and the Messenger'. It joins 'and', the definite article 'the', and the noun rasūl — one who is sent, an envoy or apostle commissioned to deliver a message.
4.grammar: The wa- prefix is 'and'; al- is the definite article 'the' (its 'l' assimilates in sound to the following 'r', hence r-rasūl). The noun is on the faʿūl pattern meaning 'one sent'. The final -a ending marks the accusative case — commonly the direct object of a verb ('… the Messenger' as the one being acted upon).
4.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — sending, dispatching a message or envoy

5.meaning: So those / then those are the ones — a connector 'so/then' joined to a demonstrative pointing to a distant or already-mentioned group: 'those people, they (are the ones who)…'.
5.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector meaning 'so/then', often introducing a result or consequence. 'ulā'ika' is a plural demonstrative ('those') pointing to people, typically picking up a previously described group and setting them up as the subject. It is fixed in form and does not change for case.

6.meaning: With, together with, alongside — indicating company, accompaniment, or being in the same place or time as another.
6.grammar: A preposition of accompaniment ('with, alongside'); grammatically it is an adverbial of place/time (ẓarf) that governs the genitive. It is placed before a following noun to put one thing in the company of another, and that following noun stands in the genitive. The -a is its fixed ending.

7.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
7.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

8.meaning: 'He bestowed favor / blessed / granted bounty' — a completed act of conferring grace, blessing, and comforts upon someone.
8.grammar: A past-tense verb on the 'afʿala' pattern, with a built-in sense of conferring something upon another. Its form marks a single masculine 'he' as the doer, with no attached subject suffix. So: 'he bestowed favor'.

9.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
9.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

10.meaning: A compound meaning 'upon them' or 'against them': the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over, against') joined to the plural pronoun 'them'. It conveys something resting on, being incumbent upon, or weighing against a group.
10.grammar: ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay- before a pronoun. The suffix -him is the attached pronominal suffix for a masculine plural group ('them'); after a preposition it carries genitive/prepositional force, and the -i- vowel reflects its position after this preposition. Together they signal a relationship of something being over, upon, or burdensome to that group.
10.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

11.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
11.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

12.meaning: 'The prophets' — those whom Allah selects to receive revelation and convey His message. The plural of nabī, a prophet who brings news from Allah.
12.grammar: A definite masculine sound plural (the al- prefix means 'the'). The -īna ending marks a masculine plural in the genitive-or-accusative case — the form used when the noun is a direct object or governed by a preposition, as opposed to the -ūna form used for the subject.
12.root: ن-ب-ء (n-b-ʾ) — news, tidings; hence a prophet who brings news from Allah

13.meaning: 'And the utterly truthful ones' — those who are intensely sincere and truthful, who fully affirm and live by the truth. 'Ṣiddīq' is an emphatic form: one whose whole being is true.
13.grammar: A definite plural noun for people ('the … ones'), joined by 'and' (wa-) with 'the' (al-). The '-īna' ending is the sound masculine plural in the object/oblique case (used for direct objects and after prepositions), as opposed to '-ūna' for the subject case.
13.root: ص-د-ق (ṣ-d-q) — truthfulness, sincerity, telling the truth

14.meaning: 'And the witnesses / martyrs' — those who bear witness to the truth; in religious usage, those who give their lives for it. 'Shahīd' means both 'witness' and 'martyr'.
14.grammar: A definite broken (irregular) plural noun, joined by 'and' (wa-) with 'the' (al-). The '-i' ending is the genitive case: it typically follows a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …').

15.meaning: 'And the righteous / upright ones' — those who are morally sound, who do good and set things right in their conduct and dealings.
15.grammar: A definite plural active participle used for people ('the … ones'), joined by 'and' (wa-) with 'the' (al-). The '-īna' ending is the sound masculine plural in the object/oblique case (for direct objects and after prepositions).
15.root: ص-ل-ح (ṣ-l-ḥ) — being sound, good, upright; setting right

16.meaning: 'And how excellent / good he (or it) is' — expresses admiration and praise: 'and excellent is …'. The verb states that someone or something is fine and praiseworthy.
16.grammar: A past-tense verb of the 'faʿula' type, which describes an inherent quality (being good). Used to express praise ('how excellent is …'). Its form marks a single masculine 'he/it' as the subject, with no attached suffix.
16.root: ح-س-ن (ḥ-s-n) — beauty, goodness, excellence

17.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'those' — pointing to people or things that are distant or already known. It singles out a group ('those ones', 'it is those who').
17.grammar: A plural demonstrative pronoun, 'those'. It is fixed in form (no case endings). The -ka element signals distance/remoteness, pointing to something far off or notable. It can refer to people of either gender.

18.meaning: 'A companion', 'a comrade', 'a friend' — one who accompanies and keeps company with another, a close associate along the way.
18.grammar: A noun on the 'faʿīl' pattern. The '-an' ending is the indefinite accusative with nunation; here it functions as a 'specifier' clarifying in what respect a quality applies (e.g. 'excellent as a companion').

1.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
1.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

2.meaning: 'The bounty', 'the favor', 'the grace' — abundant, freely given goodness and generosity, especially that which is bestowed beyond what is owed.
2.grammar: A definite noun ('the …'). The '-u' ending is the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the thing being identified.
2.root: ف-ض-ل (f-ḍ-l) — abundance, bounty, surplus of goodness, favor

3.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
3.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min).
