Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

4.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
4.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

5.meaning: 'And He suffices / is enough' — to be sufficient, adequate, and fully enough so that nothing more is needed. It conveys complete adequacy, often used to affirm that Allah alone is enough.
5.grammar: The connective wa- ('and') prefixed to a 3rd-person masculine singular perfect (past-tense) verb (Form I) whose final weak root letter (the yāʾ) appears as a long -ā. It states a completed yet timeless fact — 'and He is sufficient' — the kind of perfect form used for an enduring truth.
5.root: ك-ف-ي (k-f-y) — to suffice, be enough, be adequate; to spare someone need of anything else

6.meaning: A phrase 'in Allah / by Allah', combining the preposition 'with/in/by' and the divine name Allah, the proper name of the One God.
6.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with, by means of') prefixed to the divine name Allah. A preposition always forces the following noun into the genitive case, which is why Allah here ends in -i. With verbs of believing, bi- conveys the object of faith — to believe IN.
6.root: — (Allah is the proper name of God and is not derived from a triliteral root in the usual sense)

7.meaning: 'All-Knowing', 'fully aware' — possessing complete and thorough knowledge; one who knows perfectly.
7.grammar: An intensive adjective on the 'faʿīl' pattern, conveying deep, complete knowledge. The '-an' ending is the indefinite accusative with nunation; this case is used for direct objects and for the second part of certain verbs of being ('was … all-knowing').

1.meaning: 'O…!' — a compound vocative expression used to call out and summon an audience before addressing them. It fuses the call-particle 'yā' ('O') with a noun that means 'the one(s) addressed,' yielding an emphatic 'O you…!' that introduces direct address.
1.grammar: A vocative (calling) construction. 'Yā' is the particle for calling out; 'ayyu' carries a nominative '-u' as the one being summoned; 'hā' is an attention-drawing particle. Together they function as 'O you…!,' setting up the noun of address that follows.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
3.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

4.meaning: "Take! / Hold! / Grasp!" — a command to take hold of something firmly, to grasp, seize, or hold fast; addressed to a group.
4.grammar: An imperative (command) verb addressed to a masculine plural 'you all'. The '-ū' ending is what directs the order at a group; the written 'alif' after it is silent and merely caps the plural verb form. The imperative is built on the same root as 'to take' but drops the root's initial hamza.

5.meaning: 'Your guard', 'your caution', 'your precaution' — the alertness and protective wariness one takes against danger; one's state of being on guard. With 'your', it is the caution belonging to a group.
5.grammar: A noun with the attached possessive 'your' (-kum, addressing a group). The '-a' ending before the suffix is the accusative case, which typically marks the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon — here, the caution one is told to take).

6.meaning: 'So go forth!', 'then march out!', 'then mobilize!' — a command to a group to set out and advance, especially to rush out for an undertaking such as battle. Prefixed with 'so/then'.
6.grammar: An imperative (command) verb introduced by 'fa-' ('so/then', signaling a result or sequence). The -ū ending addresses a plural masculine 'you'. The initial 'i-' is a helping vowel for pronunciation. Force: 'so, all of you, march out!'
6.root: ن-ف-ر (n-f-r) — going forth, rushing out, mobilizing

7.meaning: 'In separate parties', 'in detachments', 'in groups' — a plural meaning bands or companies of people who set out in distinct batches rather than all at once.
7.grammar: A plural noun. The '-in' ending is the indefinite genitive with nunation ('in groups'); the genitive typically follows a preposition or links to a preceding noun. It conveys advancing party by party.
7.root: ث-ب-ي (th-b-y) — a band or distinct group of people

8.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative between two or more options, linking possibilities of which one applies.
8.grammar: A connecting particle meaning 'or'. Its base form is aw; the added -i is a 'helping' vowel given to the otherwise-silent final consonant to smooth the link to a following word that begins with a connecting (hamzat-waṣl) alif. It is not a case ending — particles do not take cases.

9.meaning: 'Go forth!', 'march out!', 'mobilize!' — a command to a group to set out and advance, especially rushing out for an undertaking such as battle.
9.grammar: An imperative (command) verb. The -ū ending addresses a plural masculine 'you' (more than one person). The initial 'i-' is a helping vowel that allows the word to be pronounced. Force: 'all of you, march out!'
9.root: ن-ف-ر (n-f-r) — going forth, rushing out, mobilizing

10.meaning: A word meaning 'all together', 'all of them', or 'the whole lot' — emphasising that no one and nothing is left out of a group.
10.grammar: A noun meaning 'all/entirety' carrying the -an ending: accusative case with tanwīn (the indefinite '-n'). This accusative form is typical of a word that comes alongside another to specify it as 'all of them, every one', describing the manner or extent.

1.meaning: 'And indeed' / 'and truly' — the joining word 'wa' ('and') attached to the emphatic particle 'inna', which introduces a statement and strongly affirms it, adding certainty like 'surely' or 'indeed'.
1.grammar: A connective 'wa' ('and') plus 'inna', a particle of emphasis that opens a nominal sentence. 'Inna' puts its following noun (the subject) into the accusative case while strongly affirming the truth of the statement.

2.meaning: A combination meaning 'from among you' or 'of you' — singling out a part or some individuals out of a larger group being addressed.
2.grammar: The preposition min ('from, among, some of') with the attached pronoun -kum, which means 'you' for a group of two or more (grammatically masculine plural). Because the pronoun follows a preposition, it is in the object form; the whole expression partitions or draws out individuals from the addressed group.
2.root: — (min is a particle/preposition; -kum is a pronoun)

3.meaning: Surely whoever, indeed the one who — combines an emphasizing 'truly/surely' with 'who/whoever', introducing the person(s) about whom something is affirmed.
3.grammar: The relative/conditional pronoun 'who/whoever' prefixed with the emphatic la- ('surely, truly'). It is an indeclinable word — it has no case ending and keeps one fixed form.

4.meaning: An emphatic verbal statement meaning 'he will surely hold back / lag behind / be sluggish.' The base verb conveys deliberately being slow to act, hanging back, or dragging one's feet rather than moving forward promptly. The doubled middle consonant intensifies the action.
4.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he'). It is wrapped in a double emphasis: the prefixed 'la-' ('surely') together with the heavy suffixed '-anna' (the energetic) turns it into a strong assertion or near-oath — 'he most certainly will lag behind.' The form's normal future/present sense is reinforced into a firm prediction.

5.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'fa-' ('then', 'so', 'but') drawing a consequence, joined to the conditional particle 'in' ('if'). Together: 'then if …', 'but if …'.
5.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that signals a result or transition ('then/so'). 'in' is the conditional particle 'if', introducing a supposed condition. Both are indeclinable particles with no case ending.

6.meaning: It (feminine) befell, struck, or afflicted you — said of a calamity, blow, or misfortune reaching and hitting its target.
6.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in Form IV. The '-at' ending marks a third-person feminine singular subject ('she/it did'). The attached '-kum' is the object pronoun 'you (all)', so the whole means 'it struck you (pl.).' The verb denotes a completed action.
6.root: ص-و-ب (ṣ-w-b) — to hit the mark, befall correctly

7.meaning: A calamity, affliction, or misfortune — something distressing that strikes a person, especially trouble that arrives suddenly and from outside one's control.
7.grammar: An active-participle-based feminine noun, here standing as a singular indefinite noun. The final -un (nunation/tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('a misfortune') and in the nominative case, the form a noun takes when it is the subject of a sentence or the thing being identified.
7.root: ص-و-ب (ṣ-w-b) — to hit a target, to strike, to befall (also linked to what is right/apt)

8.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
8.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

9.meaning: A short particle placed before a verb to emphasize or affirm it. Before a past-tense verb it means 'indeed / certainly / has already (happened)'; before a present-tense verb it can mean 'sometimes / may'. It sharpens and confirms the verb that follows.
9.grammar: An indeclinable particle (its form never changes). It does not take case or tense endings; its job is to color the following verb — affirming and intensifying a past action ('has indeed done') or signaling occasional possibility with a present verb.

10.meaning: 'He bestowed favor / blessed / granted bounty' — a completed act of conferring grace, blessing, and comforts upon someone.
10.grammar: A past-tense verb on the 'afʿala' pattern, with a built-in sense of conferring something upon another. Its form marks a single masculine 'he' as the doer, with no attached subject suffix. So: 'he bestowed favor'.

11.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
11.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

12.meaning: A preposition meaning 'upon / on / over' fused with the attached pronoun 'me,' giving 'upon me / against me / on my account.' The base preposition signals being on top of, responsible for, or burdened by something, and can also carry the sense of something owed by or weighing against a person.
12.grammar: A preposition with the first-person singular pronoun 'me' attached. When the pronoun 'me' joins this preposition, its form shifts so the two merge into 'ʿalayya.' Pronouns attached to prepositions always take the object form ('me,' not 'I'), and no case ending applies to them.

13.meaning: A particle meaning 'when' or 'at the time that', used to point back to a past moment or event and introduce a recollection of something that occurred.
13.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it has no case ending and never changes form). It signals a point in past time, typically introducing a clause that recalls 'the time when' something happened.

14.meaning: A negating particle, 'not', used specifically to deny that an action happened in the past, even though it attaches to a present-tense verb form. It turns 'you do X' into 'you did not do X'.

parts.en: did not (negation of a completed act)

14.grammar: An indeclinable particle that governs the verb after it, putting that verb into the jussive (clipped) mood and giving it past-time meaning. In short: lam + a present-form verb = 'did not [verb]'.

15.meaning: A verb meaning 'I am / I happen to be,' here in a shortened (jussive) form. It is the core verb of being/existing used to link a subject to a state or description. In a shortened form like this it is typically tied to a negation or condition, yielding a sense such as 'I was (not)' or 'should I be.'
15.grammar: A present-tense verb 'to be,' first-person singular ('I'), in the shortened jussive mood marked by the bare final consonant with a silent stop (sukūn) instead of a vowel. This clipped ending is what a particle of negation or condition produces, so the verb commonly carries a past-negative ('I was not') or conditional ('were I to be') sense rather than a plain present.
15.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

16.meaning: An adverb of accompaniment, 'with / together with / in the company of,' joined to the pronoun 'them,' giving 'with them / alongside them.' It expresses being in the same place, side, or situation as others.
16.grammar: An adverb meaning 'with' carrying the third-person masculine plural pronoun 'them' (three or more males, or a mixed group). The attached pronoun is in the object form. The fixed '-a' on 'maʿa' is part of the word itself, not a case ending applied in a sentence.
16.root: — (adverb of accompaniment)

17.meaning: 'A witness' — one who sees and attests, who can give evidence; also carries the sense of one who is present and observant, and at times 'a martyr' (one who bears witness with their life).
17.grammar: An intensive describing-noun (pattern fa‘īl) meaning 'a witness, one who fully attests', indefinite. The -an ending (the accusative with 'tanwīn') marks it as indefinite and in the accusative — the case used for a direct object, or for a word that describes the state or role in which someone stands.

1.meaning: A combination meaning 'and surely if' — introducing a hypothetical condition ('if…') sworn by an implied oath, so that the outcome is strongly anticipated; roughly 'and by all means, if…'.
1.grammar: A cluster of particles, not a noun or verb, so it takes no case ending: wa- 'and', the lam al-qasam (the 'lam of swearing') that marks the following condition as sworn by an implied oath, and in 'if' which sets up the condition. This oath-lam construction correlates with a later response clause that itself carries emphasis (an emphatic lam plus the 'nūn of emphasis' on its verb), giving the sense 'and [I swear] if … they would surely …'.

2.meaning: It struck/befell you (plural). A past-tense verb meaning that something — typically a hardship, calamity, or event — reached, hit, or happened to a group of people. Built on a verb whose core idea is hitting a target or something landing squarely upon someone.
2.grammar: Third-person masculine singular past-tense verb ("it/he struck"), with the attached object pronoun -kum meaning "you all" as the ones struck. It is a Form I hollow verb (its middle root-letter is a weak letter that surfaces as the long ā). No final case-vowel applies; the -a in aṣāba is the verb's own stem vowel.
2.root: ص-و-ب (ṣ-w-b) — to hit the mark, strike a target correctly; from this, calamity striking

3.meaning: A noun meaning 'bounty, grace, favour, abundance' — an overflowing of good given freely, beyond what is strictly due. It also carries the sense of superiority, excellence, or surplus: that which is extra and granted out of generosity.
3.grammar: An indefinite masculine noun. The '-un' ending (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a bounty / some favour') and signals the nominative case, the form a word takes when it is the doer or subject of a sentence, or stands as the thing being pointed out.

4.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
4.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

5.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
5.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

6.meaning: An emphatic verbal statement meaning 'he will surely say / he is bound to say.' The base verb is the ordinary verb of speaking and saying, here charged with strong emphasis so that the saying is presented as certain to occur.
6.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he'), doubly emphasized: the prefixed 'la-' ('surely') and the heavy suffixed '-nna' (the energetic) together turn the plain 'he says' into a firm assertion of what he will certainly say.
6.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — speaking, saying, uttering

7.meaning: A compound particle meaning 'as if / as though.' It introduces a comparison or likeness, treating a situation as resembling another — presenting something as if it were a certain way, whether or not it truly is.
7.grammar: A particle of comparison formed from 'ka-' ('like / as') joined to a particle meaning 'that.' Together they function as a single linking word, 'as if,' used to liken one circumstance to another. It is a particle, so it has no case ending of its own.

8.meaning: The particle 'lam', a negating word used to push a verb into the past: it means 'did not' / 'has not'. Though it sits before a present-tense verb form, it negates the action as something that did not happen.
8.grammar: 'lam' is a negating particle that governs a following present-tense verb but gives it past meaning ('did not …'). It also puts that verb into the shortened (jussive) form. 'lam' itself carries no ending.

9.meaning: A short (jussive) form of the verb 'to be / to become', meaning 'be' or 'does not become / is not'. It expresses being, existing, or coming to be in a clipped form that typically follows a particle such as a negator or a command.
9.grammar: Present-tense verb with the ta- prefix marking a second-person masculine singular ('you') or third-person feminine singular ('it/she') subject. The clipped final consonant (sukun, no vowel) is the jussive/apocopated mood, the form used after negative particles ('did not / was not') or as a command or prohibition.
9.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

10.meaning: Between you / among you; the space or relation linking the members of a group.
10.grammar: An adverb of place ('between/among') with an attached pronoun. The fixed -a ending is characteristic of such place-words; the ending -kum means 'you' for a group, so the whole means 'among you all'.
10.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation/interval; the space between two things

11.meaning: A compound meaning 'and between it/him' — the connective 'and', plus 'between', plus an attached pronoun 'it/him'. It marks the second party of an interval: '… and between him/it'.
11.grammar: The wa- prefix is the connective 'and'. Bayna ('between') stays in its fixed -a form. The attached -hu is a third-person masculine singular pronoun ('him/it'). The -u vowel on the pronoun is its normal form after a preceding -a. The whole phrase pairs with a preceding 'between it' to mean 'between X and Y'.
11.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinctness, the space between

12.meaning: A noun meaning 'love, affection, fond attachment, cordial goodwill.' It denotes warm friendly feeling and the bond of liking between persons — closeness of heart rather than mere acquaintance.
12.grammar: An indefinite feminine verbal noun (the feminine ending tā' marbūṭa is built into the stem). The '-un' nunation marks it as indefinite ('an affection / some love') and as nominative — the case used for the subject of a sentence or a thing simply being named or pointed out. When pronounced with this ending, the tā' marbūṭa sounds as a 't,' giving 'mawaddatun.'

13.meaning: An exclamation of longing, 'Oh, would that I…! / How I wish that I…!' It combines a call of yearning with the particle of wishing for something contrary to fact or hard to attain, focused on oneself ('I / me').
13.grammar: A particle cluster: the exclamatory call 'yā' ('O!') plus 'layta' ('would that'), a particle expressing a wish — often for the impossible or the deeply desired — with the first-person singular 'me' attached. 'Layta' grammatically takes a following noun or pronoun in the object form, which is why the connecting '-nī' ('me') appears with its protective 'n.'

14.meaning: A verb meaning 'I was / I had been,' the core verb of being placed in the past for the speaker. It links 'I' to a past state or description: 'I used to be / I came to be in such a condition.'
14.grammar: The past-tense verb 'to be,' first-person singular. The suffix '-tu' is the past-tense ending that means 'I' (the one who did/was). It expresses a completed or settled past state — 'I was, I had been.'
14.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

15.meaning: With them, in their company or possession — expressing accompaniment or togetherness. Maʿa denotes being alongside or in the presence of someone or something.
15.grammar: An adverb of accompaniment ('with') fixed in the -a form, joined to the pronoun -hum ('them'). Together they express that something is in the company or possession of a group.

16.meaning: A verb meaning 'I attain / win / achieve a triumph,' linked by 'then / so' (fa-). The base verb is to succeed greatly, to gain salvation and victory, to come out triumphant and saved. Joined with 'fa-' it expresses a result: '…so that I would triumph.'
16.grammar: A present-tense verb, first-person singular ('I'), prefixed with 'fa-' ('so / then'). The final '-a' (subjunctive) ending appears because 'fa-' here introduces a hoped-for or intended outcome ('so that I might triumph'); after such a 'fa-' the verb's ending shifts from '-u' to '-a,' marking purpose or result rather than a plain statement.
16.root: ف-و-ز (f-w-z) — triumph, success, salvation, attainment

17.meaning: A noun meaning 'triumph, great success, winning, salvation' — a decisive attainment of what is sought together with deliverance from what is feared. It denotes the highest kind of winning, not merely a minor gain.
17.grammar: An indefinite masculine verbal noun. The '-an' ending (nunation with a final 'alif') marks it as indefinite ('a triumph') and as accusative — the case typically used for the object of a verb, or for a noun that specifies or reinforces an action (as in 'he triumphed a triumph,' i.e. 'a real triumph').

18.meaning: 'Great, immense, mighty, momentous.' It describes something vast in size, weight, or seriousness, and is often used of grave or awe-inspiring matters.
18.grammar: An adjective on the intensive faʿīl pattern. The -an ending is the indefinite accusative ('a great …'), commonly marking an adjective that agrees with an indefinite accusative noun it describes, or the object of a verb.

1.meaning: A command meaning 'so let him fight / let him do battle,' formed with 'then/so' (fa-) plus the 'let' particle. The base verb means to fight, to engage in combat or warfare against an opponent. The structure issues a directive to a third party: 'let him fight.'
1.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular, turned into a third-person command by the prefixed 'li-/l-' ('let him…'). This 'l-' of command puts the verb into the shortened jussive form, shown by the bare final consonant with a silent stop (sukūn) instead of a vowel. The 'mutual/effortful' verb pattern (qātala) here conveys fighting one another. 'Fa-' links it as a consequence ('so let him fight').

2.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
2.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
2.root: — (particle)

3.meaning: 'path, way, road' — a route or course; figuratively a cause or way of life one travels along. In construct ('the way OF ...').
3.grammar: A singular noun with the '-i' (genitive) ending, which typically links it to a following noun ('the way OF ...') or follows a preposition. It marks the word as connected to or possessed by what comes after.

4.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
4.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

5.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
5.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

6.meaning: A verb meaning 'they sell / barter / trade away,' or in some usages 'they buy.' The root covers both sides of a transaction — exchanging one thing for another, giving up something in return for something else.
6.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine plural ('they'). The prefix 'ya-' marks the third person and the suffix '-ūna' marks masculine plural and the indicative mood (a plain ongoing statement, 'they sell / are selling'). It describes a present or habitual action.
6.root: ش-ر-ي (sh-r-y) — selling, buying, exchanging in trade

7.meaning: "the life" — the state of being alive; living existence, vitality.
7.grammar: The al- prefix means "the." The -a ending (on the feminine -t) is accusative, which typically marks the word as the object of a verb or the noun governed by certain particles.

8.meaning: 'The nearer (life) / this world' — literally 'the nearest/lowest,' a name for the present worldly life as opposed to the Hereafter.
8.grammar: The definite article al- with dunyā, a feminine superlative/elative adjective ('the nearest, the lowest') used as a name for the present world. Its ending (alif maqṣūra) is invariable — it does not change for case — and it commonly describes 'the [worldly] life.'
8.root: د-ن-و (d-n-w) — nearness, being close or low; hence the 'near' present world

9.meaning: The noun 'the Hereafter / the next life / the world to come,' linked by 'with / for / in exchange for' (bi-). The base word means 'the last, the latter, the final' (state of affairs) and is used as the standing name for the everlasting life after this world.
9.grammar: A definite feminine noun ('the Hereafter') governed by the preposition 'bi-' ('with / for / in exchange for'). The '-i' ending is genitive: the case a noun takes after a preposition (or when linked to a preceding noun as '…of…'). Here it appears because the preposition 'bi-' requires the genitive form; the tā' marbūṭa of the stem is sounded as 't' before this ending.
9.root: ا-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — being last, coming after, the end

10.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
10.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

11.meaning: A verb meaning 'he fights / does battle / engages in combat,' in a shortened (jussive) form. The 'mutual' verb pattern conveys fighting against an opponent, reciprocal combat. In its clipped form it is typically governed by a condition ('whoever fights…').
11.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he'), in the shortened jussive mood marked by the bare final consonant with a silent stop (sukūn). This clipped ending is produced by a conditional word ('if / whoever'), so the verb commonly carries a conditional sense ('if he fights / whoever fights'). The qātala pattern signals mutual or sustained fighting.

12.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
12.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

13.meaning: 'path, way, road' — a route or course; figuratively a cause or way of life one travels along. In construct ('the way OF ...').
13.grammar: A singular noun with the '-i' (genitive) ending, which typically links it to a following noun ('the way OF ...') or follows a preposition. It marks the word as connected to or possessed by what comes after.

14.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
14.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

15.meaning: A verb meaning 'then he is killed / is slain,' formed with 'then/so' (fa-) and the passive of the verb 'to kill.' The base action is killing; in the passive the subject undergoes it — he is the one slain rather than the slayer.
15.grammar: A present-tense passive verb, third-person masculine singular ('he is killed'). The vowel pattern (yu- with 'a' before the last consonant) marks it as passive — the subject receives the action. It stands in the shortened jussive form (bare final consonant, silent stop), here carried along by a preceding conditional structure, and 'fa-' links it as a following step ('and then he is killed').

16.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
16.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

17.meaning: A verb meaning 'he overcomes / prevails / is victorious,' in a shortened (jussive) form. The base verb means to defeat, to gain the upper hand, to conquer an opponent and come out on top.
17.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he'), in the shortened jussive mood shown by the bare final consonant with a silent stop (sukūn) instead of a vowel. This clipped ending is what a conditional word produces, so the verb commonly reads conditionally ('if he prevails / whoever prevails').

18.meaning: A two-part marker meaning 'then/so' plus 'shall/will.' It announces something forthcoming as a consequence: the particle sawfa points to the future, generally a more remote or emphatic future than the shorter prefix sa-.
18.grammar: A linking particle fa- ('then/so,' signalling result or sequence) joined to the future particle sawfa, which is placed before a present-tense verb to throw its action into the future ('will/shall …').

19.meaning: A verb meaning 'We will give / grant / bestow upon him,' with the pronoun 'him' attached. The base verb is to bring, give, or hand over something to someone. The 'We' form lends it a sense of weight and majesty.
19.grammar: A present-tense verb, first-person plural ('We'), with the third-person masculine singular object 'him' attached. The prefix 'nu-' marks the doer as 'we.' The attached '-hi' ('him') is the object form of the pronoun; its vowel is '-i' after the preceding long 'ī.' The verb expresses a future or ongoing giving ('We grant / shall grant him').
19.root: ا-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — coming, bringing, giving, granting

20.meaning: A reward, wage, or recompense — the return earned for work or conduct, whether worldly pay or otherworldly recompense.
20.grammar: A noun meaning 'a reward.' The final '-an' (tanwīn fatḥa) marks the indefinite accusative case, the case used for the object of a verb (e.g. of 'to give'), giving the sense 'a reward.'
20.root: ا-ج-ر (ʾ-j-r) — reward, wage, recompense for what one does

21.meaning: 'Great, immense, mighty, momentous.' It describes something vast in size, weight, or seriousness, and is often used of grave or awe-inspiring matters.
21.grammar: An adjective on the intensive faʿīl pattern. The -an ending is the indefinite accusative ('a great …'), commonly marking an adjective that agrees with an indefinite accusative noun it describes, or the object of a verb.

1.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

2.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
2.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

3.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
3.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

4.meaning: A verb meaning 'you (all) fight / do battle.' The 'mutual' verb pattern conveys fighting against an opponent, mutual combat, addressed to a group.
4.grammar: A present-tense verb, second-person masculine plural ('you all'). The prefix 'tu-' marks the addressee ('you') and the suffix '-ūna' marks masculine plural with the indicative mood (a plain statement, 'you are fighting / you fight'). The qātala pattern signals mutual or sustained combat.

5.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
5.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

6.meaning: 'path, way, road' — a route or course; figuratively a cause or way of life one travels along. In construct ('the way OF ...').
6.grammar: A singular noun with the '-i' (genitive) ending, which typically links it to a following noun ('the way OF ...') or follows a preposition. It marks the word as connected to or possessed by what comes after.
6.root: س-ب-ل (s-b-l) — way, path, road

7.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
7.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

8.meaning: A noun/adjective in the plural, 'the oppressed / those deemed weak / the downtrodden,' joined by 'and' (wa-). It refers to people treated as weak and made helpless — held to be of no account and rendered powerless by others, rather than weak merely by nature.
8.grammar: A definite masculine sound plural, prefixed with 'wa-' ('and'). It is a passive participle of the 'seeking/deeming' (istafʿala) pattern — literally 'those who are counted weak / made weak,' i.e. the oppressed. The '-īna' ending marks masculine plural in the accusative/genitive form (used for objects, or after prepositions and links). 'Wa-' simply joins it to what precedes.
8.root: ض-ع-ف (ḍ-ʿ-f) — weakness, feebleness, being made weak

9.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
9.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

10.meaning: A noun meaning 'the men / the menfolk' — adult human males. By extension the root conveys manliness and the standing on one's feet, but the plain sense of this plural is 'men.'
10.grammar: A definite masculine plural noun ('the men'). The '-i' ending is genitive: the case a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun as '…of…' (as in 'of the men / among the men'). The 'r' is doubled in pronunciation because the 'l' of 'al-' (the) assimilates into it.
10.root: ر-ج-ل (r-j-l) — man, manliness, going on foot

11.meaning: A noun meaning 'the women / womenfolk' — adult human females, joined by 'and' (wa-). It is the plural used for women collectively.
11.grammar: A definite plural noun for women, prefixed with 'wa-' ('and'). The '-i' ending is genitive: the case used after a preposition or in an '…of…' linkage ('of the women / among the women'). The 'n' is doubled in pronunciation because the 'l' of 'al-' (the) assimilates into it. 'Nisā'' is a plural that has no singular from the same form (its singular is 'imra'a,' woman).

12.meaning: A noun meaning 'the children / the young ones / offspring,' joined by 'and' (wa-). It is the plural denoting the newly born and the young — those still in childhood.
12.grammar: A definite masculine plural noun ('the children'), prefixed with 'wa-' ('and'). The '-i' ending is genitive: the case taken after a preposition or in an '…of…' linkage ('of the children / among the children'). 'Wildān' is a plural of 'walīd / walad' (a child, one born).
12.root: و-ل-د (w-l-d) — giving birth, begetting, child, offspring

13.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
13.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

14.meaning: 'They say / they keep saying' — a present-tense verb of speaking: to say, utter, or assert in words.
14.grammar: Present-tense verb, third-person masculine plural ('they'), from a hollow (middle-vowel) root. The ya- prefix marks the 'they/he' class, the -ū marks the masculine plural subject, and the -na ending signals the ordinary (indicative) present, 'they are saying.'

15.meaning: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'our': the Master who creates, owns, sustains, and lovingly nurtures, addressed collectively as 'our Lord' — a communal calling upon the Sustainer.

parts.en: accusative ending (vocative of a possessed noun)

15.grammar: The noun rabb with the attached first-person plural pronoun -nā ('our'). It is used as a vocative, calling out 'O our Lord'. Because the noun is possessed (a muḍāf) and called out in the vocative, it takes the accusative; that -a case vowel sits on the doubled consonant before the pronoun. The pronoun -nā shows the address is made by a group.
15.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

16.meaning: A command/plea meaning 'bring us out' or 'take us out' — to cause us to exit or emerge from something. It is a request directed to a single addressee asking that 'we' be removed from a place or situation.
16.grammar: A command (imperative) verb in the causative pattern (af'ala), so it means 'cause to go out' rather than simply 'go out'. The bare imperative form addresses a single 'you'. The attached -nā is the object pronoun 'us', the ones to be brought out.
16.root: خ-ر-ج (kh-r-j) — going out, exiting, emerging

17.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
17.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

18.meaning: This (feminine) — a pointing word ('this one here') used for a single nearby thing that is grammatically feminine.
18.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun ('this') for a single feminine thing close at hand. It is fixed in form and does not change for case; it commonly precedes the noun it points to.

19.meaning: A settled place where people live — a town, village, or populated locality. It denotes a community gathered in one inhabited place.
19.grammar: A feminine singular noun marked with 'the'. The final -i is the genitive case: it typically marks the word as linked to a preceding preposition or oath particle, or as the second term of a possessive phrase ('… of …').
19.root: ق-ر-ي (q-r-y) — gathering, bringing together (people in a settlement)

20.meaning: One who does wrong or commits injustice — an oppressor or wrongdoer. The active participle describes a person characterized by ẓulm: putting things out of their rightful place, acting unjustly or tyrannically.
20.grammar: An active participle (the 'one who does X' form) on the pattern fā'il, here meaning 'the one who wrongs/oppresses'. It carries 'the'. The final -i is genitive: it typically marks linkage to a preceding preposition or oath, or possession ('… of …').

21.meaning: 'Its people' — the inhabitants, family, or folk belonging to something. Ahl denotes the people who belong to a place, household, or affiliation; with the attached pronoun it means the people of 'it' (a feminine referent).
21.grammar: A noun followed by the possessive pronoun -hā ('its/her', referring to a feminine or non-human thing). The -u ending on the noun is the nominative case, which typically marks the word as the doer/subject or the thing being identified.
21.root: أ-ه-ل ('-h-l) — belonging, family, people of a place

22.meaning: A command meaning 'make', 'set', 'appoint', or 'render' — to bring something into a state or assign it a role. Ja'ala is a versatile verb of making/placing/turning-into. With the joining 'and', it links to a preceding statement.
22.grammar: 'And' joined to a command (imperative) verb addressed to a single 'you'. The bare imperative form (with no ending vowel) issues a direct request or order to one person. The verb often takes two objects ('make X into Y').

23.meaning: 'For us / to us' — indicating that something is directed toward, or belongs to, the speaker's group.
23.grammar: The preposition li- ('for / to') with the attached pronoun -nā ('us'). When this pronoun is added, the preposition's vowel becomes 'la-'. The whole expresses benefit or direction toward 'us' — what is done for, or owed to, the speaker's group.
23.root: — (li- is a particle/preposition; -nā is a pronoun)

24.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
24.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

25.meaning: From Yourself; from Your presence. The base word ladun means 'the presence of', 'the side of', or 'directly from' — pointing to something issuing straight from a source. Here it is preceded by the preposition min ('from'), whose final n assimilates into the following l so that the l is doubled. With the attached pronoun the whole conveys 'from Your own presence', stressing that what is given comes directly from the giver.

parts.en: from (preposition; its n merges into the following l)
presence / nearness / 'from with' (doubled l from the merged n)

25.grammar: An adverb of place/source ('at, by, in the presence of') joined to the attached pronoun -ka, 'your/you' for a single masculine addressee, together conveying 'from Your presence'. The initial l is written with a shadda (doubled): this gemination results from the preceding preposition min, whose final n assimilates into the l. The word implies immediacy of source — something coming directly from the one referred to.
25.root: — (an adverbial particle of place; no triliteral verbal root)

26.meaning: A guardian, protector, ally, or close supporter — one who is near and takes charge of another's affairs. Waliyy carries the sense of nearness combined with care, authority, and friendship.
26.grammar: An indefinite noun ('a protector'). The -an ending (tanwīn fatḥa) is the accusative case: it commonly marks the word as a direct object of a verb, or as a predicate/complement after certain verbs of 'making' or 'becoming'.
26.root: و-ل-ي (w-l-y) — nearness, guardianship, alliance, friendship

27.meaning: A command meaning 'make', 'set', 'appoint', or 'render' — identical in sense to id 920. Ja'ala is a versatile verb of making/placing/turning-into; with the joining 'and' it links to a preceding statement.
27.grammar: 'And' joined to a command (imperative) verb addressed to a single 'you'. The bare imperative form (with no ending vowel) issues a direct request or order to one person. The verb often takes two objects ('make X into Y').

28.meaning: 'For us / to us' — indicating that something is directed toward, or belongs to, the speaker's group.
28.grammar: The preposition li- ('for / to') with the attached pronoun -nā ('us'). When this pronoun is added, the preposition's vowel becomes 'la-'. The whole expresses benefit or direction toward 'us' — what is done for, or owed to, the speaker's group.
28.root: — (li- is a particle/preposition; -nā is a pronoun)

29.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
29.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

30.meaning: From Yourself; from Your presence. The base word ladun means 'the presence of', 'the side of', or 'directly from' — pointing to something issuing straight from a source. Here it is preceded by the preposition min ('from'), whose final n assimilates into the following l so that the l is doubled. With the attached pronoun the whole conveys 'from Your own presence', stressing that what is given comes directly from the giver.

parts.en: from (preposition; its n merges into the following l)
presence / nearness / 'from with' (doubled l from the merged n)

30.grammar: An adverb of place/source ('at, by, in the presence of') joined to the attached pronoun -ka, 'your/you' for a single masculine addressee, together conveying 'from Your presence'. The initial l is written with a shadda (doubled): this gemination results from the preceding preposition min, whose final n assimilates into the l. The word implies immediacy of source — something coming directly from the one referred to.
30.root: — (an adverbial particle of place; no triliteral verbal root)

31.meaning: 'A helper, supporter, one who gives aid and victory' — an intensive form stressing reliable, effective help.
31.grammar: An indefinite noun on an intensive pattern (faʿīl) that conveys a strong or constant doer — 'a true helper'. The -an ending marks the accusative and indefiniteness, commonly used here as a specifier naming the capacity ('as a helper').
31.root: ن-ص-ر (n-ṣ-r) — to help, to aid, to give victory

1.meaning: Those who / the ones who — a plural relative pronoun (masculine) introducing a description: 'those (people) who …'.
1.grammar: A relative pronoun, masculine plural, meaning 'those who / the ones who'. It refers back to a group already in view and introduces a clause describing them. Its form is fixed and does not change for case.

2.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
2.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.
2.root: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — safety, security, trust, faith

3.meaning: 'They fight' or 'they do battle' — engaging in mutual combat or warfare. The pattern (qātala) conveys fighting against an opponent, a reciprocal struggle rather than mere striking.
3.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb in the mutual-action pattern (fā'ala) meaning 'to fight against'. The -ūna ending marks a masculine-plural 'they' subject and the indicative mood, which states an action as an ongoing or habitual fact.

4.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
4.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

5.meaning: 'path, way, road' — a route or course; figuratively a cause or way of life one travels along. In construct ('the way OF ...').
5.grammar: A singular noun with the '-i' (genitive) ending, which typically links it to a following noun ('the way OF ...') or follows a preposition. It marks the word as connected to or possessed by what comes after.

6.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
6.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

7.meaning: 'And those who': a connective phrase introducing a specified group of people (masculine plural) about whom something will be said. It links them to what came before.
7.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'), which is masculine plural. A relative pronoun stands for a group and is normally followed by a clause describing them. Its form does not change for case; it stays alladhīna whatever its grammatical role.

8.meaning: 'They disbelieved / rejected faith' — from a root meaning to cover over or conceal. To disbelieve in this sense is to cover up and refuse the truth, and also to be ungrateful, hiding or denying favours received.
8.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third person masculine plural: 'they disbelieved'. The completed action is built into the stem kafara ('he disbelieved'), and the -ū suffix (written وا) marks the doer as 'they' (masculine plural). The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention with no sound.
8.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to reject faith, be ungrateful

9.meaning: 'They fight' or 'they do battle' — engaging in mutual combat or warfare. The pattern (qātala) conveys fighting against an opponent, a reciprocal struggle rather than mere striking.
9.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb in the mutual-action pattern (fā'ala) meaning 'to fight against'. The -ūna ending marks a masculine-plural 'they' subject and the indicative mood, which states an action as an ongoing or habitual fact.

10.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
10.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

11.meaning: 'path, way, road' — a route or course; figuratively a cause or way of life one travels along. In construct ('the way OF ...').
11.grammar: A singular noun with the '-i' (genitive) ending, which typically links it to a following noun ('the way OF ...') or follows a preposition. It marks the word as connected to or possessed by what comes after.

12.meaning: the false object of worship — anything wrongfully set up as a deity or authority beside Allah: an idol, a tyrant, a devil, or any power obeyed in rebellion against the truth. 'Ṭāghūt' is an intensive form rooted in the idea of overstepping all bounds.
12.grammar: A definite noun: the prefix al- ('the') is assimilated into the 'sun letter' ṭ (so it sounds aṭ-ṭ). The ending -i marks the genitive case, the form a word typically takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of …').
12.root: ط-غ-ي (ṭ-gh-y) — to exceed all limits, transgress, tyrannize

13.meaning: A command 'so fight!' addressed to a group — engage in battle against an opponent. The pattern conveys mutual combat. The prefixed 'fa-' means 'so / then', drawing a consequence from what precedes.
13.grammar: 'So/then' joined to a command (imperative) verb in the mutual-action pattern (fā'ala). The -ū ending directs the command at a masculine-plural 'you (all)'. The silent alif after -ū is a spelling convention with no sound.

14.meaning: Allies, protectors, intimate friends — those taken as close supporters, patrons, or guardians, with whom one stands in mutual loyalty (plural of walī).
14.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural of 'walī.' Being a 'diptote' (a noun that resists the usual full set of endings), it takes a single final '-a' here for the accusative case, which commonly marks the direct object of a verb or signals 'as / being' something — and notably without the usual '-n' (no nunation).

15.meaning: The Shayṭān — Satan, the devil: a rebellious, evil being who tempts and misleads; the term suggests one who is far removed from goodness and burning in defiance.
15.grammar: A definite masculine noun ('the Satan / the devil'). The final -i is the genitive ending, which generally links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …') or follows a preposition.
15.root: ش-ط-ن (sh-ṭ-n) — to be remote (from good/mercy); a devil

16.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
16.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

17.meaning: A scheme, plot, stratagem, or cunning device — a carefully contrived plan, often with the connotation of secret maneuvering or trickery.
17.grammar: A singular noun. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon) or otherwise as the target of the action.

18.meaning: The Shayṭān — Satan, the devil: a rebellious, evil being who tempts and misleads; the term suggests one who is far removed from goodness and burning in defiance.
18.grammar: A definite masculine noun ('the Satan / the devil'). The final -i is the genitive ending, which generally links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …') or follows a preposition.
18.root: ش-ط-ن (sh-ṭ-n) — to be remote (from good/mercy); a devil

19.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

19.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.
19.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existence; to be

20.meaning: 'Weak', 'feeble', or 'frail' — lacking strength or firmness, whether in body, resolve, or effect.
20.grammar: An indefinite adjective ('weak'). The -an ending (tanwīn fatḥa) is the accusative case, which here commonly marks the word as a predicate/complement after a verb of 'being' or 'becoming', or describes a direct object.
20.root: ض-ع-ف (ḍ-'-f) — weakness, feebleness, being double/multiplied (a related sense)

1.meaning: 'Did not…?' — a particle combining a question with negation, used to ask 'Have I/has he not…?', often expecting agreement or serving as a gentle reminder.
1.grammar: An interrogative prefix 'a-' ('?') joined to the negation 'lam'. 'lam' negates a verb and places it firmly in the past ('did not'), and grammatically puts the following present-tense verb into the jussive (clipped) form. Together they form a rhetorical or confirming question.

2.meaning: You see, perceive, or take notice; to observe with the eye, or by extension to come to know or consider. Often used to draw attention, as in 'have you considered…?'
2.grammar: A present-tense verb addressed to a single male 'you,' marked by the 'ta-' prefix. The root's weak final letter has dropped, leaving the short final -a; this shortened form is the jussive/apocopated form, which appears after certain particles (such as 'did not' or in questions like 'have you not seen?').
2.root: ر-أ-ي (r-ʾ-y) — to see, perceive, consider, form an opinion

3.meaning: 'To / toward / up to' — a preposition marking the endpoint, goal, or limit of an action or motion: the direction something moves toward or the boundary at which it stops.
3.grammar: An invariable preposition. It has no case ending of its own but puts the noun that follows it into the genitive ('of / to' state). It indicates direction toward, or the terminal limit of, something.

4.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
4.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

5.meaning: 'It was said' — speech was uttered or a statement was made. The passive form: the saying is reported without naming who spoke.

parts.en: was said (passive verb stem of the root q-w-l)
he/it (default short vowel of the 3rd masc. sg. past)

5.grammar: A past-tense verb in the passive voice (pattern qīla) from the hollow root ق-و-ل. The passive is formed by internal vowel change: the middle radical (wāw) is replaced by a long 'ī', which marks the verb as passive (the doer is left unnamed). The lām is the third root letter, not an ending; the final -a is simply the default short vowel of the third-person masculine singular past, here used impersonally as 'it was said'.

6.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
6.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

7.meaning: A command meaning 'hold back', 'restrain', or 'withhold' — to stop or curb something from acting or moving. It is addressed to a group, telling them to keep something in check.
7.grammar: A command (imperative) verb. The -ū ending directs the order at a masculine-plural 'you (all)'. The silent alif written after -ū is a spelling convention and is not pronounced.

8.meaning: 'Your hands' (plural addressee) — the hands belonging to a group. Yad ('hand') can also stand figuratively for power, agency, or action.
8.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural noun ('hands') with the attached possessive pronoun -kum ('your', addressed to a group of males or a mixed group). This plural ends in a weak letter (yā'), and when a pronoun is attached directly to it, that yā' takes a short -a vowel as a stem/attachment rule of pronunciation — it is not a case ending. The noun's case here (accusative, as the thing acted upon) is shown instead by the form of the suffixed/construct state, not by this vowel.
8.root: ي-د-ي (y-d-y) — hand; by extension power and agency

9.meaning: And establish / set up / perform fully — a command to make something stand firm and upright, to carry it out properly and consistently (used especially of performing prayer rightly).
9.grammar: The conjunction wa- ('and') joined to a plural command verb of the causative (af'ala) pattern, meaning to make something stand/be upright. The -ū ending marks a masculine-plural addressee being told to do it.
9.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise, be upright; to establish

10.meaning: The ritual prayer (ṣalāh): the prescribed formal worship of standing, bowing, and prostrating before Allah at appointed times. As a verbal noun it also carries the underlying sense of calling upon, supplicating, and blessing.
10.grammar: A definite feminine noun. The -a ending is accusative: it generally marks the word as the direct object of a verb (the thing being acted upon, e.g. that which is established or performed), or the object of certain particles.

11.meaning: And give / hand over / bring — a command to deliver something to someone, to render it to its due recipient.
11.grammar: The conjunction wa- ('and') joined to a plural command verb of the causative (af'ala) pattern, meaning to make something come to someone, i.e. to give. The -ū ending marks a masculine-plural addressee being told to give.
11.root: أ-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (causative) to give, bring

12.meaning: The purifying alms (zakāt) — the obligatory portion given from one's wealth that purifies it and causes it to grow; an act of worship and social due.
12.grammar: A definite feminine noun (the tied tā' marks the feminine). The final -a is the accusative ending, typically marking the noun as the direct object of a verb ('the alms').
12.root: ز-ك-و (z-k-w) — to be pure; to grow, increase, be blessed

13.meaning: A connector meaning 'then, when' — it joins to what came before ('then/so') and sets up a 'when…' clause whose outcome follows. It frames a moment: 'and then, at the point when…'.
13.grammar: A compound of the connecting particle fa- ('then/so', linking to the preceding statement) and lammā, a particle meaning 'when' that introduces a past circumstance and leads the listener to expect a following result clause.

14.meaning: 'It has been prescribed / decreed / made obligatory' — also literally 'it was written'. A past-tense passive verb conveying that something has been ordained and laid down as a binding command.
14.grammar: The internal vowel pattern (u–i) makes this passive: the action was done, with no doer named. The final -a is the default third-person masculine singular ending of a past-tense verb (it is a verbal person-marker, not a noun's case ending), so the verb reads 'it was prescribed'.

15.meaning: 'Upon them / against them' — the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, against') carrying an attached plural pronoun referring to a group of males.
15.grammar: ʿalā ('upon') takes the form ʿalay- before a pronoun. The -him ending is the attached pronoun for a masculine plural 'them'; its final vowel appears as -u (himu) to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with the definite article.

16.meaning: Fighting, combat, or warfare — armed struggle between opposing parties.
16.grammar: A masculine verbal noun denoting mutual fighting. The prefix al- means 'the'. The final -u is the nominative ending, generally marking the word as the subject of a sentence or as the thing being described.
16.root: ق-ت-ل (q-t-l) — to kill, to fight; combat

17.meaning: 'When' — a particle introducing a time or circumstance, generally pointing to something expected or definite to come ('when/whenever it happens'). It sets up a condition or moment whose outcome then follows.
17.grammar: An indeclinable adverb/particle of time; it has no case ending and never changes form. It typically introduces a clause about a future or recurring event ('when …'), and is normally followed by a verb describing what takes place.

18.meaning: A group, party, or faction — a portion or section of people set apart from a larger body.
18.grammar: A masculine singular noun. The '-un' (tanwīn) marks it indefinite ('a group') and in the nominative case, typically used for the subject of a sentence.
18.root: ف-ر-ق (f-r-q) — to separate, divide; a division

19.meaning: 'Among them / from them / some of them' — the preposition 'min' ('from, of, among') joined to the attached pronoun 'hum' ('them').
19.grammar: The preposition 'min' ('from / of / among') with the attached pronoun 'hum' ('them'), referring to a masculine plural group. Together they often express 'part of them' or 'some among them'.

20.meaning: 'They fear' or 'they hold in awe' — experiencing khashya, a fear mixed with reverence and awareness of someone's greatness, especially the kind of dread that comes from knowledge of the one feared.
20.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb. The -awna ending marks a masculine-plural 'they' subject (the long final root-vowel blends into the plural ending) and the indicative mood, which states the action as an ongoing or habitual fact.
20.root: خ-ش-ي (kh-sh-y) — fear blended with awe and reverence

21.meaning: Mankind, humanity, people in general — the collective of human beings.
21.grammar: A definite noun ('the people') with the attached 'al-' ('the'). The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 'n' (a sun letter), which is why the 'n' is doubled — this is a pronunciation effect, not a separate piece. The final '-a' ending is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb (the one being acted upon) or the subject of certain particles.
21.root: ن-و-س (n-w-s) — to move/sway; by extension, people

22.meaning: 'Like the fearing of' or 'as the awe of' — a comparison expressing 'in the manner of (someone's) reverent fear'. The prefixed 'ka-' means 'like / as', and the noun denotes awe-filled fear.
22.grammar: The comparison particle 'ka-' ('like/as') attached to a feminine verbal noun meaning 'fearing/awe'. Because 'ka-' acts like a preposition, the noun takes the genitive -i ending, which links it to a following noun ('the fear OF …').
22.root: خ-ش-ي (kh-sh-y) — fear blended with awe and reverence

23.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
23.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

24.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
24.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

25.meaning: More intense, stronger, more severe or vehement; the comparative/superlative form denoting a higher degree of strength or intensity ('more / most intense').
25.grammar: A comparative/elative adjective on the pattern afʿal ('more / most …'). The final -a here is an accusative ending — note that elative adjectives are often diptotes (taking -a even in the genitive and not taking nunation). It conveys 'more intense / stronger' and is commonly followed by a noun specifying in what respect.
25.root: ش-د-د (sh-d-d) — to be strong, intense, firm, severe

26.meaning: 'Fear' or 'awe' — the verbal noun naming the act or state of khashya: a reverent dread, fear arising from awareness of greatness or consequence.
26.grammar: An indefinite feminine verbal noun ('fear'). The -an ending (tanwīn fatḥa on the tā') is the accusative case, which commonly marks the word as a direct object, or as an explanation of cause/reason ('out of fear').
26.root: خ-ش-ي (kh-sh-y) — fear blended with awe and reverence

27.meaning: And they said — to utter or declare in speech, with the action presented as completed by a group.
27.grammar: The prefix 'wa-' means 'and'. 'qāla' is the past-tense verb 'to say'; the '-ū' suffix marks a completed action done by 'they' (a masculine or mixed group). The stem shown here ('qālu') carries only the stem vowel before the suffix, with the plural '-ū' supplied by the separate ending. Past tense, so the speaking is presented as already finished.

28.meaning: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'our': the Master who creates, owns, sustains, and lovingly nurtures, addressed collectively as 'our Lord' — a communal calling upon the Sustainer.

parts.en: accusative ending (vocative of a possessed noun)

28.grammar: The noun rabb with the attached first-person plural pronoun -nā ('our'). It is used as a vocative, calling out 'O our Lord'. Because the noun is possessed (a muḍāf) and called out in the vocative, it takes the accusative; that -a case vowel sits on the doubled consonant before the pronoun. The pronoun -nā shows the address is made by a group.
28.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

29.meaning: An interrogative meaning 'why? / for what reason?' — a question asking the cause or purpose of something. It is formed from the preposition 'for/about' fused with the question-word 'what'.
29.grammar: A question particle built from li- ('for, about') joined to mā ('what'); when these combine, the long vowel of 'what' is shortened to give li-ma ('for what?, why?'). It opens a question seeking a reason or motive.

30.meaning: 'You wrote' or 'you prescribed/ordained' — addressed to a single 'you'. Kataba means to write, and by extension to decree, prescribe, or make obligatory, as a written matter is fixed and binding.
30.grammar: A past-tense verb. The suffix -ta marks the doer as a single male 'you', stating that this addressee performed or decreed the action in the past.
30.root: ك-ت-ب (k-t-b) — writing; by extension decreeing and prescribing

31.meaning: 'Upon us' / 'over us' / 'against us' — the preposition ʿalā ('on, over, upon') with an attached 'us'. It conveys something resting on, incumbent upon, or bearing against the group.
31.grammar: A preposition (ʿalā, 'upon/over') with an attached pronoun, first person plural (-nā, 'us'). When a pronoun is attached, ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay-. Such prepositional phrases put their pronoun in the object/genitive role.

32.meaning: 'Fighting', 'combat', or 'warfare' — the verbal noun naming the act of mutual fighting between opposing sides.
32.grammar: A verbal noun ('fighting') from the mutual-action pattern, carrying 'the'. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb (the thing decreed, written, or undertaken).

33.meaning: A particle of urging or exhortation meaning 'why not …?' — used to press for or demand that something be done, and sometimes to express a wish, often with a tone of reproach ('why does … not happen?').
33.grammar: An indivisible particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ). Although written as one form, it is not built up from the conditional 'if' plus a negation; in this prompting usage it is a single fixed particle meaning 'why not?' / 'if only.' Followed by a verb it presses for that action. (Note: in a different construction the same form can mean 'were it not for,' but that is a separate usage.) It is a particle and takes no case ending.

34.meaning: 'You delayed/postponed us' — addressed to a single 'you'. Akhkhara (intensive pattern) means to put back, defer, or grant a delay. With the attached 'us', it means 'you put us off' or 'granted us a respite'.
34.grammar: A past-tense verb in the intensive/causative pattern (fa''ala) meaning 'to put back, defer'. The suffix -ta marks the doer as a single male 'you'; the following -nā is the object pronoun 'us', the ones being delayed.
34.root: أ-خ-ر ('-kh-r) — being last, coming after, delaying

35.meaning: "to / towards" — a preposition marking the end-point, goal, or direction of a movement or extent ("up to," "as far as," "toward").
35.grammar: An indeclinable preposition; it has no case ending of its own and always governs a following noun in the genitive case.

36.meaning: A noun meaning 'a fixed term, an appointed time, a set deadline, a span allotted before something falls due.' It denotes the limit or end-point of a period.
36.grammar: A noun with the -in ending (with nunation): the genitive indefinite ('a term'). This form occurs after a preposition or in an 'of' linkage with a preceding noun.
36.root: ا-ج-ل (ʾ-j-l) — appointed term, fixed time, deadline

37.meaning: 'Near / soon / close' — qarīb denotes nearness in place or time, hence 'close at hand' or 'shortly,' or one who is near/related.
37.grammar: An adjective/noun on the fa'īl pattern meaning 'near.' The -in ending is the genitive case with indefinite (tanwīn) 'n,' the form taken after a preposition or in an 'of …' relationship with a preceding noun.
37.root: ق-ر-ب (q-r-b) — to be near, draw close; nearness

38.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
38.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

39.meaning: Provision, enjoyment, or the goods of life — something one is given to use and take comfort in for a time; often implies a temporary benefit or worldly furnishing rather than a lasting possession.
39.grammar: A masculine noun, indefinite. The final -u ending is nominative, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or for a word standing as the predicate ('it is …'). The absence of nunation (-un) here reflects that it is bound to a following noun in a possessive ('… of …') construction.

40.meaning: 'The nearer (life) / this world' — literally 'the nearest/lowest,' a name for the present worldly life as opposed to the Hereafter.
40.grammar: The definite article al- with dunyā, a feminine superlative/elative adjective ('the nearest, the lowest') used as a name for the present world. Its ending (alif maqṣūra) is invariable — it does not change for case — and it commonly describes 'the [worldly] life.'
40.root: د-ن-و (d-n-w) — nearness, being close or low; hence the 'near' present world

41.meaning: 'Few', 'little', 'a small amount/number'. Describes something scant in quantity — a small group of people or a small portion of a thing.
41.grammar: A descriptive adjective (or noun). The '-un' ending is the nominative case with nunation ('tanwīn'), marking it as indefinite ('a few', not 'the few'); the nominative typically marks the subject or a predicate.

42.meaning: 'And the Hereafter' — the life to come, the final and lasting abode after this world. Al-ākhira is literally 'the last/latter (life)', the world that comes after the present one.
42.grammar: 'And' joined to a feminine noun with 'the' — an adjective ('the last/latter') used as a noun for the next life. The final -u is the nominative case, which typically marks the word as the subject or the thing being talked about.
42.root: أ-خ-ر ('-kh-r) — being last, coming after, the latter

43.meaning: 'Better / best; good' — an adjective of comparison meaning more good, preferable, or superior. It also serves broadly for 'goodness' and that which is good and beneficial.
43.grammar: A noun/adjective bearing the ending -un (nunation): the doubled-u 'n' sound marks the word as both indefinite ('a/an', no 'the') and nominative — the case used for the subject of a sentence or the predicate that describes it.
43.root: خ-ي-ر (kh-y-r) — good, goodness, that which is choice and beneficial

44.meaning: 'For whoever' / 'to the one who' — a combination of 'for/to' and 'whoever'. It introduces a person (general and unspecified) as the one to whom something belongs or is directed.
44.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('for/to') joined to 'man' ('whoever / the one who'). The normally-silent end of 'man' is voiced as -i here only to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a connecting hamza; it carries no case meaning.

45.meaning: 'He was mindful/guarded himself' — from ittaqā, to practice taqwā: to shield oneself by being conscious of Allah and avoiding what brings harm or displeasure. It conveys careful, reverent self-protection through obedience.
45.grammar: A past-tense verb (pattern ifta'ala) describing a single male 'he'. It states that this person practiced taqwā — guarded and shielded himself through God-consciousness — as a completed action. The final long -ā is the original weak root-letter appearing as the verb's ending.

46.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
