8.grammar: The preposition 'from/out of' attached to the pronoun -hā ('it/her'), which refers back to a feminine or grammatically-feminine noun. After a preposition this pronoun stands in the genitive (object) position, giving the sense 'from it' — the source or point of departure of an action.

9.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
9.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

10.meaning: He intercedes — he stands as a mediator or advocate on behalf of another, pleading for a benefit to come to them or for harm to be averted from them.
10.grammar: A present-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular ('he …'). The bare, vowelless ending (sukūn on the final letter, jussive mood) is the 'cut-off' form used after conditional or jussive particles, often giving the sense of 'if he should …' or 'let him …'.
10.root: ش-ف-ع (sh-f-ʿ) — to pair, to intercede / mediate

11.meaning: An act of intercession — a single instance of pleading or mediating on someone's behalf before one who has authority.
11.grammar: A verbal noun, feminine. The final -an (tanwīn fatḥ, written over the tā' marbūṭa) marks the indefinite accusative ('an …'), the case used for an object of a verb or a specifying complement.
11.root: ش-ف-ع (sh-f-ʿ) — to pair, to intercede / mediate

12.meaning: An evil (deed) / a wrong — something bad, harmful, or sinful; a misdeed or its grievous result. The opposite of a good deed.
12.grammar: A feminine noun (built on the pattern of an intensive adjective used as a noun, 'a bad thing'). The '-an' ending (on the feminine '-at-') is indefinite accusative, the case that typically marks the direct object of a verb.
12.root: س-و-ء (s-w-ʾ) — to be bad, evil, harmful

13.meaning: He/it comes to be, becomes, or proves to be — a linking verb of being, asserting that a subject is or turns out to be in a certain state.
13.grammar: A present-tense verb of 'being', 3rd-person masculine singular ('he/it is/becomes'). It stands in the jussive mood, marked by sukūn on the final nūn (the weak middle letter of the root having dropped); this conditional form typically means 'if he should be …' or 'let it be …'.
13.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

14.meaning: A two-part phrase 'for Him' or 'to Him belongs,' expressing possession, ownership, or that something is due to one masculine being.
14.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('for/to/belonging to') with its vowel shifted to 'la-' before the pronoun. The attached -hu means 'Him', so the whole means 'for Him' or 'His'; the preposition signals possession or that something is owed or directed to that person.

15.meaning: A share, portion, or allotted part — one's due measure of something, whether of reward or of burden.
15.grammar: A noun. The final -un (tanwīn ḍamm) marks the indefinite nominative ('a …'), the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or the thing being described as existing.
15.root: ك-ف-ل (k-f-l) — to assign a share / to be responsible for, to sponsor

16.meaning: From it / from her — marking the starting point or source out of which something comes, referring to a feminine or grammatically-feminine thing.
16.grammar: The preposition 'from/out of' attached to the pronoun -hā ('it/her'), which refers back to a feminine or grammatically-feminine noun. After a preposition this pronoun stands in the genitive (object) position, giving the sense 'from it' — the source or point of departure of an action.
16.root: — (particle/preposition)

17.meaning: And he was / he became — a verb of being that places a subject in a past state or links it to a description in the past.
17.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'kāna' is a past-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular, meaning 'he was/became'; it commonly introduces a past condition and is typically followed by a noun describing the subject's state. The final -a marks completed past action by a single male.

18.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
18.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

19.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
19.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

20.meaning: 'every,' 'each,' or 'all' — a word expressing totality or completeness. It indicates the entirety of something: when joined to a singular indefinite noun it means 'every (single) one,' and when joined to a definite noun it can mean 'all of' or 'the whole of.'
20.grammar: A noun of totality. The final '-i' ending is genitive (the 'of/possession' case): it marks the word as governed by a preceding preposition or as the first term of a possessive link to a following noun, so it typically reads 'of every…' or 'every…' leading into what follows.

21.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
21.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
21.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

22.meaning: One who has full power and control over all things, sustaining and overseeing them and apportioning to each what it needs — a Watchful Sustainer and Keeper, witness over everything.
22.grammar: An active participle ('one who sustains/oversees'). The final -an (tanwīn fatḥ) marks the indefinite accusative ('a …'), the case used for objects and for predicates after certain verbs of being.
22.root: ق-و-ت (q-w-t) — sustenance, nourishment; to provide for and have charge over

1.meaning: 'And when...' — a linking phrase joining 'and' to 'when', used to introduce a circumstance or a recurring situation: 'and whenever / and at the time that...'.
1.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') attached to idhā ('when'). Idhā is a particle pointing to a time or condition, generally referring to something expected or recurring in the future ('when / whenever' it happens), and it normally introduces a following clause that states what occurs at that time.

2.meaning: You (plural) are greeted — you are met with a salutation of peace and goodwill, a wish for life and well-being extended to you.
2.grammar: A past-tense passive verb, 2nd-person masculine plural ('you all were/are greeted'). The internal vowel pattern (ḥu-…-i) marks it as passive — the subject receives the action — and the suffix -tum identifies the doers as 'you (plural)'.
2.root: ح-ي-ي (ḥ-y-y) — life; to greet / wish life and well-being

3.meaning: With a greeting — a salutation or wish of peace and well-being offered to another; literally a 'wishing of life'.
3.grammar: A verbal noun preceded by the preposition bi- ('with/by'). The final -in (tanwīn kasr, here sounded as -tin over the tā' marbūṭa) marks the indefinite genitive ('a …'), the case required after a preposition.
3.root: ح-ي-ي (ḥ-y-y) — life; to greet / wish life and well-being

4.meaning: Then greet (you plural) — extend a salutation of peace and goodwill to another. The fa- adds the sense of 'so/then', linking the command to what precedes.
4.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to a masculine plural 'you all'. The long -ū ending is the plural-command marker ('all of you, do it!'); the silent alif after it is a spelling convention. Prefixed fa- means 'so/then'.
4.root: ح-ي-ي (ḥ-y-y) — life; to greet / wish life and well-being

5.meaning: With something better, finer, or more excellent — a comparative pointing to a greater or superior instance of goodness.
5.grammar: A comparative/superlative adjective ('better, finest') after the preposition bi-. It belongs to a class of words that resist tanwīn (diptotes); for such words fatḥa (-a) is itself the genitive ending, taking the place of the usual kasra. So this -a is the genitive form proper to this word class, with the word still functioning as the object of the preposition.

6.meaning: A two-part word: the preposition 'min' ('from / out of / some of') joined to the pronoun 'it' (feminine). Together: 'from it / out of it / of it,' indicating a source or a portion taken from a feminine thing.
6.grammar: A preposition 'min' with the attached pronoun '-hā' ('it/her'), referring to a feminine noun. 'Min' indicates origin, source, or a part taken from a whole; the attached pronoun is in the object form required after a preposition.

7.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
7.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

8.meaning: Give it back / return it (you plural) — restore the thing to the one it belongs to or send back what was given. The attached 'it' refers to a feminine thing.
8.grammar: A command (imperative) to a masculine plural 'you all'. The -ū marks the plural addressee; the attached -hā is the object 'it' (referring to something grammatically feminine).
8.root: ر-د-د (r-d-d) — to return, give back, send back

9.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
9.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

10.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
10.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

11.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

11.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

12.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
12.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

13.meaning: 'every,' 'each,' or 'all' — a word expressing totality or completeness. It indicates the entirety of something: when joined to a singular indefinite noun it means 'every (single) one,' and when joined to a definite noun it can mean 'all of' or 'the whole of.'
13.grammar: A noun of totality. The final '-i' ending is genitive (the 'of/possession' case): it marks the word as governed by a preceding preposition or as the first term of a possessive link to a following noun, so it typically reads 'of every…' or 'every…' leading into what follows.

14.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
14.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
14.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

15.meaning: 'A reckoner / one who takes full account' — one who reckons, calculates, and holds to account, weighing every deed and giving each its exact due. It also carries the sense of being entirely sufficient as such an accountant.
15.grammar: A singular masculine noun/adjective on the intensive faʿīl pattern (a thorough, capable reckoner). The ending -an (tanwīn fatḥa) is the indefinite accusative, here marking the word as a specifying or circumstantial complement — telling in what capacity something is regarded ('as a reckoner'). The final nunation signals indefiniteness ('a…').
15.root: ح-س-ب (ḥ-s-b) — to count, calculate, reckon, hold to account

1.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
1.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

2.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
2.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

3.meaning: God / object of worship — a deity that is worshipped. The bare noun names the concept of a worshipped god.
3.grammar: A singular noun carrying an -a ending. This short -a typically marks the accusative (object) case; it is also the form a noun takes immediately after the absolute-negation particle 'lā' to mean 'no … (at all).'
3.root: أ-ل-ه (ʾ-l-h) — godhood, worship, being a deity

4.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
4.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

5.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
5.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

6.meaning: He will most surely gather you (plural) together — an emphatic assurance that the addressees will certainly be assembled into one place. The doubled emphasis makes it a solemn certainty.
6.grammar: A present/future verb, 3rd-person masculine singular ('he will gather'). The prefixed la- ('surely') together with the heavy ending -nna form a double emphasis ('He shall most certainly …'), and the attached -kum is the object 'you all'.
6.root: ج-م-ع (j-m-ʿ) — to gather, collect, assemble

7.meaning: A preposition meaning 'to,' 'toward,' or 'up to' — pointing to the end-point, goal, or limit of a motion, direction, or extent.
7.grammar: A preposition (a small linking word). It governs the noun after it, putting that noun in the genitive case, and points to a destination or limit ('to,' 'toward,' 'as far as').

8.meaning: 'Day' — a span of time. It denotes a day or a definite point/period of time; it links to a following word to specify which day (e.g., 'the day of …').
8.grammar: A masculine noun. Its final -i vowel is the genitive case: it typically appears after a preposition or when the word is linked to a following noun in an 'of …' relationship (as in 'the day OF …').

9.meaning: "the Resurrection" — the standing-up of all people from death to be judged; literally the act of rising or standing up.
9.grammar: The al- prefix means "the." The -i ending (on the feminine -t) is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ("the … OF this") or follows a preposition.

10.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
10.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

11.meaning: Doubt, suspicion, disquieting uncertainty — the kind of wavering that unsettles the heart, stronger than a passing question. It names the state of not being at rest about whether something is true.
11.grammar: A masculine singular noun shown with an -a ending and no tanwin. This is the accusative (mansub) noun governed by the negating particle la — its ism — taking a bare form to express absolute negation, conveying that the whole category is ruled out ('there is no doubt whatsoever').

12.meaning: 'In it / in him' — the preposition 'in, inside, within' joined to a pronoun referring to a single masculine or neuter thing. It locates something inside or as part of that referent.
12.grammar: A preposition with an attached object pronoun. The pronoun -hi refers to one masculine (or grammatically masculine) thing and stands as the object of the preposition; its vowel is -i because attached pronouns take that shape after the long -i of fi. Together they answer 'in what?' or 'in whom?'.

13.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
13.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

14.meaning: More truthful / most truthful — surpassing in truthfulness; whose statement is more in accord with reality than another's.
14.grammar: A comparative/superlative adjective ('more/most truthful'). It is of the class that does not take tanwīn (diptote); the -u ending marks the nominative, the case used for the subject or for what is being described.

15.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
15.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

16.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
16.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

17.meaning: A piece of speech, an account, a report, or a narrated statement — something said or related; the word also carries the sense of something new or newly arising.
17.grammar: A singular indefinite noun. The -an ending (tanwīn with an 'a' vowel) marks the accusative case while signalling 'a/some' (indefinite). The accusative is the case of a direct object or of a noun governed by certain particles, so it commonly reads as the receiver of an action.
17.root: ح-د-ث (ḥ-d-th) — to happen anew, to relate/narrate speech

1.meaning: A two-part expression: 'so/then' joined to a negating word 'not.' The first piece links to what precedes (drawing a result or sequence), and the second negates the statement that follows. Together roughly: 'so… not / and so it did not…'
1.grammar: A connective particle fa- ('so, then,' showing result or sequence) plus the negating particle mā. When mā precedes a past-tense verb, it denies that the action happened ('did not…').

2.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
2.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

3.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
3.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

4.meaning: the hypocrites — those who outwardly profess faith while inwardly concealing disbelief; people who present one face publicly and hide another within. From a root evoking a tunnel with two openings, suggesting a hidden way out.
4.grammar: A definite noun: al- means 'the'. 'Munāfiq' is an active participle of Form III ('one who behaves hypocritically'). The ending -īna marks the masculine sound plural in the oblique case (the form used for objects of verbs and after prepositions, i.e. accusative/genitive, as opposed to nominative -ūna).
4.root: ن-ف-ق (n-f-q) — tunnel/burrow with a hidden exit; hence hypocrisy

5.meaning: Two parties / two groups. Fiʾa means a group, party, band, or detachment of people. The form names exactly two such groups (the dual).
5.grammar: A dual noun — it denotes precisely two of the thing. The ending -ayni is the dual marker in its 'oblique' shape, used when the word is an object or follows a preposition (as opposed to -āni, used for a subject). So it means 'two groups' functioning as an object or after a preposition.
5.root: ف-ي-أ (f-y-ʾ) — to return, turn back; hence a group/faction one turns or resorts to (per classical lexica such as Lisān al-ʿArab and Lane, with yāʾ as the middle radical and hamza as the final radical)

6.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
6.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
6.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

7.meaning: He turned them back / overturned them, plunging them back into a former state — to reverse someone, casting them back down (often into error or ruin). The attached 'them' is the object.
7.grammar: A past-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular ('he turned back'), in the causative pattern ('to make something revert'). The final -a is the past-tense marker; the attached -hum is the object 'them'.
7.root: ر-ك-س (r-k-s) — to turn back, overturn, reverse / relapse

8.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
8.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

9.meaning: 'They earned / they acquired / they gained' — past-tense action of a group obtaining something through their own effort, whether good or bad. The root carries the sense of working to acquire, and is often used of the deeds people accrue.
9.grammar: A past-tense verb. The ending -ū marks a masculine plural subject ('they') who completed the action in the past.

10.meaning: Do you (plural) wish/want/intend? — an opening question asking whether the addressees seek or desire something. The prefixed hamza turns the statement into a question.
10.grammar: A yes/no question (opening hamza 'do …?') over a present-tense verb, 2nd-person masculine plural. The ending -ūna marks the plural 'you all' and the indicative mood (a plain statement of fact, here questioned).
10.root: ر-و-د (r-w-d) — to seek, desire, want, intend

11.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
11.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

12.meaning: You (plural) guide — you lead someone onto the right way, showing them the path. It can mean both showing the way and bringing one to reach it.
12.grammar: A present-tense verb, 2nd-person masculine plural ('you all guide'). It stands in the subjunctive/jussive mood: the indicative ending -ūna has lost its -na, leaving a bare -ū. This shortened form appears after particles such as those meaning 'to/that' or after conditional words — giving a sense like 'that you should guide'. (The full indicative would be tahdūna.)
12.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — guidance; to guide, show the way

13.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
13.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

14.meaning: He let go astray / led astray, or he went astray — to cause someone to lose the right way, or to stray from it oneself.
14.grammar: A past-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular ('he …'), in the causative pattern ('to cause to go astray'). The final -a (with the doubled lām) is the past-tense singular marker.
14.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to stray, go astray, lose the way

15.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
15.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

16.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
16.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.
16.root: — (pronoun/particle; no triliteral root)

17.meaning: He lets/leads astray — he causes someone to lose the right way, leaving them to wander from guidance.
17.grammar: A present-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular ('he …'), in the causative pattern ('to cause to stray'). It stands in the jussive/conditional mood (the doubled lām broken apart and given a helping -i to ease pronunciation), typically meaning 'whomever he lets stray …'.
17.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to stray, go astray, lose the way

18.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
18.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

19.meaning: So never / then never — a connector 'so/then' joined to an emphatic particle of negation that denies a future action absolutely: 'will never (at all)'.
19.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector meaning 'so/then', linking to what precedes. 'lan' negates a following present-tense verb and casts it into the future with emphatic force ('will never'); it also puts that verb into the subjunctive, which shows up as a final '-a' on the verb.
19.root: — (particle — no root)

20.meaning: A second-person present verb: 'you find / you come upon.' It denotes discovering or encountering something, whether by searching or by chance.
20.grammar: The ta- prefix marks a second-person masculine singular subject ('you'). The final -a vowel is the subjunctive, the shape used after governing particles (such as 'never' or 'that'), often projecting the action into the future.
20.root: و-ج-د (w-j-d) — to find, to come upon

21.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
21.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

22.meaning: A way, path, road, or means — a route to a destination, hence also a way or means of accomplishing something.
22.grammar: A singular noun. The '-an' ending is accusative and indefinite: the accusative case commonly marks the direct object of a verb, and the final 'n' sound marks it indefinite ('a way'). It denotes a path one travels or a means to an end.

1.meaning: 'They wished / loved / would have liked' — to desire and find pleasing, to long for something to happen.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb. The ending -ū marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they did…'); the final silent alif written after it is a spelling convention for this plural ending and is not pronounced. Past tense states a completed action.
1.root: و-د-د (w-d-d) — to love, wish, desire affectionately

2.meaning: A conditional particle introducing a hypothetical or contrary-to-fact supposition: 'if (it were the case that…)'. It typically presents a condition that is unfulfilled or merely imagined, often implying the result did not or would not happen.
2.grammar: An indeclinable particle (no case ending). It signals a hypothetical 'if': it sets up a supposed condition whose consequence is then stated, frequently with the sense 'if X were so, then Y would be so' — often where X is contrary to fact.

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'you disbelieve', 'you reject faith', or 'you are ungrateful' — to refuse to believe, to deny the truth, or to be ungrateful, addressed to a group.
3.grammar: Present/imperfect verb, second-person masculine plural ('you all'). The ta- prefix marks the second person ('you') and the -ūna ending marks a masculine-plural subject in the indicative mood (ongoing or habitual action). The root joins the ideas of denying faith and being ungrateful — covering over a truth or a blessing.
3.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to disbelieve, deny, be ungrateful, cover over

4.meaning: 'Just as / in the same way that' — a phrase of comparison joining 'like / as' to 'what', meaning 'like that which...' or 'in the manner that...'.
4.grammar: The comparison particle ka- ('like / as') joined to mā ('what / that which'). Together they introduce a likeness or manner — 'just as...', 'in the same way that...' — comparing one thing or action to another.

5.meaning: 'They disbelieved / rejected faith' — from a root meaning to cover over or conceal. To disbelieve in this sense is to cover up and refuse the truth, and also to be ungrateful, hiding or denying favours received.
5.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third person masculine plural: 'they disbelieved'. The completed action is built into the stem kafara ('he disbelieved'), and the -ū suffix (written وا) marks the doer as 'they' (masculine plural). The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention with no sound.
5.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to reject faith, be ungrateful

6.meaning: And then you (plural) would be / become — a linking verb of being stating that the addressees come to be in a certain condition. The fa- adds 'so/then', often marking a consequence.
6.grammar: A present-tense verb of 'being', 2nd-person masculine plural ('you all are/become'). The ending -ūna marks the plural 'you all' and the indicative mood (a plain statement). The prefixed fa- means 'so/then', often signalling a result.
6.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, exist, come to be

7.meaning: 'Equal / the same / alike' — a noun-adjective expressing equality or sameness; that two or more things stand on a par, with no difference between them. It can also mean a level or even thing.
7.grammar: A noun/adjective. The ending -an is accusative with nunation: the -n sound marks it as indefinite, and the accusative case commonly marks it as a predicate or the thing described/acted upon. The accusative -an is here written with a supporting alif (ـاء).
7.root: س-و-ي (s-w-y) — being level, equal, even, in balance

8.meaning: A two-part word: the connective particle 'fa-' meaning 'so', 'then', or 'therefore' (drawing a consequence from what precedes), joined to 'lā', the particle of negation/prohibition. Together they convey 'so do not …' or 'so there is no …'.
8.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that links a clause to what came before and often signals a result or consequence. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a present-tense verb it commonly forms a prohibition ('do not …') or a simple negation ('not'). It carries no ending of its own.

9.meaning: That you take, that you adopt — a present-tense verb (form VIII) meaning to take for oneself, to choose or adopt something. Addressed to a group ('you all'), and in a form used after particles meaning 'that' or 'to'.
9.grammar: A present-tense verb in the reflexive (form VIII) pattern, 'to take for oneself'. The ta- prefix with the plural ending means 'you all'. The ending is -ū (the final 'n' of -ūna has dropped), which marks the subjunctive or jussive mood — the form used after particles like 'that', 'to', or 'not'.

10.meaning: From them / among them — the preposition min ('from, out of, part of') joined to the pronoun 'them' (a group of males or a mixed group).
10.grammar: The preposition min ('from / among / part of') with the attached third-person masculine plural pronoun -hum ('them'). Pronouns after a preposition are in the genitive; the combination expresses origin, partition ('some of them'), or belonging to that group.

11.meaning: Allies, protectors, intimate friends — those taken as close supporters, patrons, or guardians, with whom one stands in mutual loyalty (plural of walī).
11.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural of 'walī.' Being a 'diptote' (a noun that resists the usual full set of endings), it takes a single final '-a' here for the accusative case, which commonly marks the direct object of a verb or signals 'as / being' something — and notably without the usual '-n' (no nunation).

12.meaning: 'Until / up to the point that; so that' — a particle marking a limit or goal. It expresses the end-point reached ('until') or the purpose aimed at ('so that, in order that').
12.grammar: A particle indicating a goal or limit. When followed by a present-tense verb it places that verb in the subjunctive mood (clipping its ending to -a), conveying 'until / so that' something comes about. Ḥattā itself is invariable.

13.meaning: They (plural) emigrate / migrate — they forsake their home and leave one place for another, especially abandoning a place for the sake of a cause. The form implies a parting of ways.
13.grammar: A present-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine plural ('they …'), in the mutual/effortful pattern ('to part from one's home'). It stands in the subjunctive/jussive mood: the indicative ending -ūna has lost its -na, leaving a bare -ū. This shortened form appears after particles such as conditional or 'until/that' words — e.g. 'until they emigrate'.
13.root: ه-ج-ر (h-j-r) — to forsake, part from, emigrate

14.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
14.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

15.meaning: 'path, way, road' — a route or course; figuratively a cause or way of life one travels along. In construct ('the way OF ...').
15.grammar: A singular noun with the '-i' (genitive) ending, which typically links it to a following noun ('the way OF ...') or follows a preposition. It marks the word as connected to or possessed by what comes after.

16.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
16.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

17.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'fa-' ('then', 'so', 'but') drawing a consequence, joined to the conditional particle 'in' ('if'). Together: 'then if …', 'but if …'.
17.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that signals a result or transition ('then/so'). 'in' is the conditional particle 'if', introducing a supposed condition. Both are indeclinable particles with no case ending.

18.meaning: 'They turned away / they turned their backs / they turned aside'. It conveys turning oneself away from something, often implying rejection or withdrawal.
18.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb, third person masculine plural: the ending '-aw' means 'they (did) …'. The Form V pattern (with the 'ta-' prefix and doubled middle letter) gives a reflexive sense — turning oneself away. It states a completed act.
18.root: و-ل-ي (w-l-y) — to be near/turn toward; in this form, to turn away

19.meaning: Then seize them / take hold of them (you plural) — lay hold of them firmly and take them. The fa- adds 'so/then'; the attached 'them' is the object.
19.grammar: A command (imperative) to a masculine plural 'you all'. The -ū marks the plural addressee; the attached -hum is the object 'them'. Prefixed fa- means 'so/then', often introducing a response to a condition.
19.root: أ-خ-ذ (ʾ-kh-dh) — to take, seize, take hold of

20.meaning: And kill them / slay them. A command to kill, with an attached object pronoun 'them.'
20.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to a second-person masculine plural ('you all'); it opens with a connecting (elidable) alif needed to begin the consonant cluster. The -ū ending marks the masculine-plural addressee, the attached -hum is the object pronoun 'them,' and wa means 'and.'

21.meaning: Wherever / in whatever place — an adverb pointing to an unspecified location, 'in the place where ...'.
21.grammar: An invariable adverb of place ('where / wherever'). Although it ends in -u, it is fixed in form and does not change for case; it is normally followed by a clause stating the situation tied to that place.

22.meaning: You (plural) found them / came upon them — you encountered or discovered them. The attached 'them' is the object found.
22.grammar: A past-tense verb, 2nd-person masculine plural ('you all found'). The suffix -tum marks 'you (plural)'; its vowel is lengthened to -tumū to link smoothly onto the following object pronoun -hum ('them').
22.root: و-ج-د (w-j-d) — to find, come upon, discover

23.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
23.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

24.meaning: That you take, that you adopt — a present-tense verb (form VIII) meaning to take for oneself, to choose or adopt something. Addressed to a group ('you all'), and in a form used after particles meaning 'that' or 'to'.
24.grammar: A present-tense verb in the reflexive (form VIII) pattern, 'to take for oneself'. The ta- prefix with the plural ending means 'you all'. The ending is -ū (the final 'n' of -ūna has dropped), which marks the subjunctive or jussive mood — the form used after particles like 'that', 'to', or 'not'.

25.meaning: From them / among them — the preposition min ('from, out of, part of') joined to the pronoun 'them' (a group of males or a mixed group).
25.grammar: The preposition min ('from / among / part of') with the attached third-person masculine plural pronoun -hum ('them'). Pronouns after a preposition are in the genitive; the combination expresses origin, partition ('some of them'), or belonging to that group.

26.meaning: A guardian, protector, ally, or close supporter — one who is near and takes charge of another's affairs. Waliyy carries the sense of nearness combined with care, authority, and friendship.
26.grammar: An indefinite noun ('a protector'). The -an ending (tanwīn fatḥa) is the accusative case: it commonly marks the word as a direct object of a verb, or as a predicate/complement after certain verbs of 'making' or 'becoming'.
26.root: و-ل-ي (w-l-y) — nearness, guardianship, alliance, friendship

27.meaning: 'And not' — a connector 'and' joined to the negative particle 'not,' negating a following statement.
27.grammar: Two particles: the joining 'and' (wa) plus the negator lā ('not'). Lā commonly negates a present-tense verb or a noun. Neither particle takes case endings.

28.meaning: 'A helper, supporter, one who gives aid and victory' — an intensive form stressing reliable, effective help.
28.grammar: An indefinite noun on an intensive pattern (faʿīl) that conveys a strong or constant doer — 'a true helper'. The -an ending marks the accusative and indefiniteness, commonly used here as a specifier naming the capacity ('as a helper').
28.root: ن-ص-ر (n-ṣ-r) — to help, to aid, to give victory

1.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
1.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: They (plural) join / connect / reach — they attach themselves to something or arrive at it; also used of maintaining ties and bonds of kinship.
3.grammar: A present-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine plural ('they …'). The ending -ūna marks the plural 'they' and the indicative mood (a plain statement of an ongoing or habitual action).
3.root: و-ص-ل (w-ṣ-l) — to join, connect, reach, maintain ties

4.meaning: A preposition meaning 'to,' 'toward,' or 'up to' — pointing to the end-point, goal, or limit of a motion, direction, or extent.
4.grammar: A preposition (a small linking word). It governs the noun after it, putting that noun in the genitive case, and points to a destination or limit ('to,' 'toward,' 'as far as').

5.meaning: A people, folk, or community — a group of persons bound together (often by kinship or shared identity); a nation or tribe.
5.grammar: A singular collective noun (grammatically masculine, referring to a group). The final -in is the genitive case with nunation (tanwīn), marking it indefinite ('a people'); the genitive typically follows a preposition or links to a preceding noun ('… of a people').
5.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise, establish; a standing group of people

6.meaning: Between you / among you; the space or relation linking the members of a group.
6.grammar: An adverb of place ('between/among') with an attached pronoun. The fixed -a ending is characteristic of such place-words; the ending -kum means 'you' for a group, so the whole means 'among you all'.
6.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation/interval; the space between two things

7.meaning: And between them — marking what lies in the space or relation separating two parties. The wa- means 'and'; the attached 'them' identifies the parties.
7.grammar: An adverb of place, 'between', joined by wa- ('and') and fixed in the -a form. It governs the attached pronoun -hum ('them'), so the whole means 'and between them'.
7.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction; what lies between

8.meaning: A binding pact, covenant, or solemn treaty — a firm agreement that obligates the parties to it. The final -un (nunation) marks it as an indefinite noun, so it conveys 'a covenant/treaty' rather than 'the covenant'.
8.grammar: A masculine singular noun on the pattern mīfʿāl, denoting an instrument or means of binding. The final -un is the nominative case with nunation: nominative typically marks the doer or subject of a sentence (or a predicate), and the nunation signals that the noun is indefinite ('a covenant').
8.root: و-ث-ق (w-th-q) — to bind firmly, to trust, to make secure

9.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
9.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

10.meaning: They came to you / they reached you — a completed act of a group arriving at or approaching addressees.
10.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'), and the attached -kum is the plural object ('you all'), so together the verb means 'they came to you'. The perfect tense presents the action as already completed.

11.meaning: It became constricted, tight, or hard-pressed — said of a chest/breast that is gripped by distress, reluctance, or unwillingness; figuratively, to feel inwardly straitened.
11.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb on the pattern faʿila, which often expresses entering a state. The -at ending marks a third-person feminine singular subject ('she/it'), commonly agreeing with a feminine noun such as 'breast/chest'. The perfect tense presents the state as already set in.
11.root: ح-ص-ر (ḥ-ṣ-r) — to confine, restrict, hem in, straiten

12.meaning: Breasts or chests — the inner being, the seat of feelings, intentions, and what a person keeps within; bosoms.
12.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural of 'breast/chest' (ṣadr). It is in the nominative (the -u before the pronoun), the case of the subject of a verb or sentence. The attached -hum is the possessive pronoun 'their' ('their breasts').
12.root: ص-د-ر (ṣ-d-r) — chest, front, the foremost part; the inner self

13.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
13.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

14.meaning: 'They fight you' — a verb of mutual combat and warfare, denoting engaging an enemy in battle, with 'you' (plural) as the opponent.
14.grammar: A present/future verb from a pattern (long 'aa' after the first letter) that carries the sense of mutual, reciprocal action (fighting one another). The yu-…-ū framing marks third-person masculine plural ('they'). The long -ū is the plural subject ending. The plain indicative would end in -na (yuqātilūna); its loss here marks the verb as non-indicative. For a plural verb the same dropped -na serves two moods — the jussive (majzūm), triggered by particles such as 'lam' ('did not'), the imperative 'li-', and conditional 'in' ('if'), and the subjunctive (manṣūb), triggered by 'an' / 'lan' / 'kay' — so the form alone does not distinguish them; the governing particle decides. The attached -kum is the object 'you (all).'

15.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
15.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

16.meaning: They fight / they would fight — mutual armed combat against an opponent.
16.grammar: A present/imperfect verb of Form III (qātala), which carries the sense of a mutual or reciprocal action — here fighting one another. The yu- prefix with the -ū plural ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'). The dropped final -na (subjunctive/jussive mood) shows the verb is governed by a preceding particle rather than standing as a plain statement.
16.root: ق-ت-ل (q-t-l) — to kill, to fight

17.meaning: Their people / their folk — the community, kinsfolk, or tribe to which 'they' belong.
17.grammar: A masculine singular noun meaning a body of people, with the attached possessive -hum ('their'). The -a ending is accusative, which typically marks the noun as the direct object of a verb ('… their people' as the thing acted upon).
17.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, to rise; a people who stand together

18.meaning: 'and if' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the particle 'if'. This particular 'if' (law) introduces a hypothetical or contrary-to-fact condition: 'if (such-and-such had been the case)…', often implying it was not.
18.grammar: A conjunction plus a conditional particle. wa- means 'and'. law is a non-changing particle (no case ending) that sets up a supposition, typically answered by a clause beginning with la- ('… then certainly …').

19.meaning: A past-tense verb 'he willed / he wished / he so desired'. It denotes an act of will or volition bringing something about.
19.grammar: Past-tense (perfect) verb, third person masculine singular ('he'). The bare stem with no suffix is the basic 'he did' form. Its subject and object are typically supplied by context.
19.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʾ) — to will, wish

20.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
20.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

21.meaning: He surely gave them power / set them in authority — to grant dominance and the ability to overcome, attached to an emphatic 'surely'.
21.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb of Form II (sallaṭa), whose doubled middle root letter gives a causative force — 'to make dominant, to give power over.' The prefixed la- is an emphatic particle ('surely'), the bare verb-stem ending marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'), and -hum is the plural object ('them'). The perfect presents the action as completed.

22.meaning: 'Upon you (all)' — the preposition 'upon/on/over' joined to the plural 'you,' indicating something resting on or directed at a group.
22.grammar: The preposition 'ʿalā' ('upon/on/over') in its joined form 'ʿalay-' plus the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you all,' masculine plural). It marks the group as the recipients or target of whatever is laid 'upon' them.

23.meaning: Then they would surely have fought you — mutual armed combat, attached to 'then' and an emphatic 'surely'.
23.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb of Form III (qātala), which conveys mutual/reciprocal action — fighting one another. The prefix fa- means 'then/so' and la- is an emphatic 'surely'; the -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'), and -kum is the plural object ('you all'). The perfect presents the action as completed.

24.meaning: A two-part connector meaning 'then if / so if.' It joins a clause to what precedes (fa-) and introduces a hypothetical condition (in, 'if').
24.grammar: A compound of two particles. Fa- means 'then/so,' connecting to a prior statement. In means 'if,' setting up a condition whose outcome follows. The final -i is a helping vowel added to the normally vowel-less in to ease pronunciation before the next word; it carries no grammatical case meaning.

25.meaning: They withdrew from you / kept apart from you — to draw aside, stay clear, and refrain from engaging.
25.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb of Form VIII (iʿtazala), which often gives a sense of doing something for oneself — here removing oneself, keeping apart. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'), and -kum is the attached object ('from you all'). The perfect presents the action as completed.
25.root: ع-ز-ل (ʿ-z-l) — to set apart, separate, isolate

26.meaning: A two-part device meaning 'did not …' — it combines 'and/then so' with a negating word that turns a present-tense verb into a flat statement that something did NOT happen in the past.
26.grammar: A connecting particle fa- ('and so / then') joined to the negative particle lam. Lam negates the past: it precedes a present-tense verb but flips its meaning to 'did not do', and it puts that following verb into the jussive (clipped) form.

27.meaning: They fight you / would fight you — mutual armed combat directed against the addressees.
27.grammar: A present/imperfect verb of Form III (qātala), carrying the sense of mutual/reciprocal action — fighting one another. The yu- prefix with the -ū plural ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'), and -kum is the attached object ('you all'). The dropped final -na shows the verb is in the subjunctive/jussive, governed by a preceding particle rather than standing as a plain statement.

28.meaning: And they cast / threw down / offered — to throw something out or extend it forward; figuratively, to put forward an offer (such as of peace or surrender), joined to 'and'.
28.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb of Form IV (alqā), which carries a causative/transitive sense — 'to make something fall, to cast it forth.' The prefix wa- means 'and'. The -aw ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they') for this weak-ending verb. The perfect presents the action as completed.
28.root: ل-ق-ي (l-q-y) — to meet, to throw down, to cast forth

29.meaning: To you / towards you — directing an action or motion at the addressees.
29.grammar: A preposition meaning 'to/towards' with the attached pronoun -kum ('you all'). The pronoun takes the helping vowel -u (kumu) when followed by a word beginning with the definite article, simply to ease pronunciation; it does not change the meaning.

30.meaning: Peace, reconciliation, or peaceful submission — the cessation of hostility and the offering of accord. The al- marks it as 'the peace' being spoken of.
30.grammar: A masculine noun with the definite article al- ('the'). Its first letter (s) is a 'sun letter,' so the l of al- assimilates into it (pronounced as-salam). The -a ending is accusative, which typically marks the noun as the direct object of a verb (the thing offered or extended).
30.root: س-ل-م (s-l-m) — soundness, safety, peace, submission

31.meaning: A two-part expression: 'so/then' joined to a negating word 'not.' The first piece links to what precedes (drawing a result or sequence), and the second negates the statement that follows. Together roughly: 'so… not / and so it did not…'
31.grammar: A connective particle fa- ('so, then,' showing result or sequence) plus the negating particle mā. When mā precedes a past-tense verb, it denies that the action happened ('did not…').

32.meaning: 'He made,' 'He appointed,' 'He set up' — to bring about, fashion, or assign something to a state or role. Beyond mere 'making,' it often means rendering one thing into another or establishing something for a purpose.
32.grammar: A past-tense verb. The stem is the three root letters; the '-a' ending on it marks 'he' as the doer and places the action in the completed past ('he made / appointed'). This verb commonly governs two objects, in the sense of 'made X into Y.'

33.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
33.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

34.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
34.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

35.meaning: A compound meaning 'upon them' or 'against them': the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over, against') joined to the plural pronoun 'them'. It conveys something resting on, being incumbent upon, or weighing against a group.
35.grammar: ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay- before a pronoun. The suffix -him is the attached pronominal suffix for a masculine plural group ('them'); after a preposition it carries genitive/prepositional force, and the -i- vowel reflects its position after this preposition. Together they signal a relationship of something being over, upon, or burdensome to that group.
35.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

36.meaning: A way, path, road, or means — a route to a destination, hence also a way or means of accomplishing something.
36.grammar: A singular noun. The '-an' ending is accusative and indefinite: the accusative case commonly marks the direct object of a verb, and the final 'n' sound marks it indefinite ('a way'). It denotes a path one travels or a means to an end.

1.meaning: You will find / you are going to find — to come upon or discover something, with a prefix marking near-future time.
1.grammar: A present/imperfect verb carrying the future particle sa- ('will/shall'). The ta- prefix together with the -ūna ending marks a second-person masculine plural subject ('you all'). The retained final -na shows the indicative mood — a plain, factual statement (here, about what will happen).
1.root: و-ج-د (w-j-d) — to find, to come upon, to perceive

2.meaning: Others / other ones — additional people distinct from those already mentioned (masculine plural of 'other').
2.grammar: A masculine plural adjective/noun meaning 'others.' The -īna ending is the accusative/genitive form of the masculine plural (its nominative counterpart would be -ūna). This ending typically marks the word as a direct object of a verb or as following a preposition.
2.root: أ-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — to come later, to be other/last

3.meaning: they want / they intend — to will, desire, or purpose something. The verb conveys an active, ongoing intention or wish on the part of a group.
3.grammar: A present-tense Form IV verb (arāda, 'to will/intend'). The yu- prefix marks a third-person subject, and the ending -ūna marks masculine plural plus the indicative mood (a plain statement: 'they want'). The -na would drop under a particle that changes the mood.

4.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
4.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

5.meaning: They feel safe from you / they would be secure from you — to trust and be free of fear regarding the addressees.

parts.en: be safe, feel secure, trust (assimilated stem)

5.grammar: A present/imperfect verb of Form I from a hamza-initial root. When the imperfect prefix ya- meets the root's initial hamza, the hamza assimilates into the prefix consonant, doubling it (yā-mushaddada); the glottal stop is no longer pronounced, so the form is read yammanū rather than yaʾmanū. The ya- prefix with the -ū plural ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'), and -kum is the attached object ('from you all'). The dropped final -na shows the subjunctive/jussive mood, governed by a preceding particle rather than standing as a plain statement.

6.meaning: And they feel safe from / would be secure from — to trust and be free of fear regarding someone, joined to 'and'.

parts.en: be safe, feel secure, trust (assimilated stem)

6.grammar: A present/imperfect verb of Form I from a hamza-initial root, prefixed with wa- ('and'). When the imperfect prefix ya- meets the root's initial hamza, the hamza assimilates into the prefix consonant, doubling it (yā-mushaddada); the glottal stop is no longer pronounced, so the form is read wa-yammanū rather than wa-yaʾmanū. The ya- prefix together with the -ū plural ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'). The dropped final -na shows the subjunctive/jussive mood, governed by a preceding particle rather than standing as a plain statement.
6.root: أ-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — safety, security, trust, faith

7.meaning: Their people / their folk — the community, kinsfolk, or tribe to which 'they' belong.
7.grammar: A masculine singular noun meaning a body of people, with the attached possessive -hum ('their'). The -a ending is accusative, which typically marks the noun as the direct object of a verb ('… their people' as the thing acted upon).
7.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, to rise; a people who stand together

8.meaning: All, every, the whole of — totality. When followed by a singular it means 'every (one)'; when followed by a definite plural or whole it means 'all of.'
8.grammar: A noun of totality, almost always joined to a following noun in the genitive ('every … / all of …'). The final -a is the accusative case, the form used when the word functions as an object of a verb.

9.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
9.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

10.meaning: They were turned back / sent back / returned — a completed act in which a group is caused to revert or be driven back; in passive voice (the subject undergoes the action).
10.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in the passive voice — its inner vowel pattern (u after the first letter) shows that the subject receives the action ('were turned back') rather than performing it. The doubled root letter (rudd-) reflects the geminate root r-d-d. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they').
10.root: ر-د-د (r-d-d) — to return, send back, turn away

11.meaning: 'To / toward / up to' — a preposition marking the endpoint, goal, or limit of an action or motion: the direction something moves toward or the boundary at which it stops.
11.grammar: An invariable preposition. It has no case ending of its own but puts the noun that follows it into the genitive ('of / to' state). It indicates direction toward, or the terminal limit of, something.

12.meaning: Trial, temptation, and discord: a testing affliction that puts faith and loyalty to the proof, and the strife or sedition that can result from it. A heavily loaded term spanning persecution, civil strife, and seductive enticement away from truth.
12.grammar: A feminine noun made definite by the article al-. The final -i (on the feminine ending) is genitive, the case typically used after a preposition, after an oath, or to link the word to a preceding noun in an 'of' relationship.
12.root: ف-ت-ن (f-t-n) — to test by fire/trial; to tempt, afflict

13.meaning: They were overturned / plunged back / made to relapse — a completed act in which a group is cast back (often into a former bad state); in passive voice.

parts.en: were turned upside down, plunged back, made to relapse

13.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb of Form IV (arkasa) in the passive voice — the u–i vowel pattern shows the subject receives the action ('were plunged back'). The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'). The perfect presents the action as completed.
13.root: ر-ك-س (r-k-s) — to turn back, overturn, set head-down

14.meaning: 'In it / therein.' A preposition with an attached pronoun: 'in' plus a feminine singular 'it,' meaning 'inside it / within it,' referring back to some feminine or grammatically feminine thing (such as a place).
14.grammar: A prepositional phrase: fī ('in, within') with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine singular). The pronoun is the object of the preposition and points back to a previously mentioned feminine noun.

15.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'fa-' ('then', 'so', 'but') drawing a consequence, joined to the conditional particle 'in' ('if'). Together: 'then if …', 'but if …'.
15.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that signals a result or transition ('then/so'). 'in' is the conditional particle 'if', introducing a supposed condition. Both are indeclinable particles with no case ending.

16.meaning: The particle 'lam', a negating word used to push a verb into the past: it means 'did not' / 'has not'. Though it sits before a present-tense verb form, it negates the action as something that did not happen.
16.grammar: 'lam' is a negating particle that governs a following present-tense verb but gives it past meaning ('did not …'). It also puts that verb into the shortened (jussive) form. 'lam' itself carries no ending.

17.meaning: They withdraw from you / keep apart from you — to draw aside, stay clear, and refrain from engaging.
17.grammar: A present/imperfect verb of Form VIII (iʿtazala), which often conveys doing something for oneself — here removing oneself, keeping apart. The ya- prefix with the -ū plural ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'), and -kum is the attached object ('from you all'). The dropped final -na shows the subjunctive/jussive mood, governed by a preceding particle.
17.root: ع-ز-ل (ʿ-z-l) — to set apart, separate, isolate

18.meaning: And they cast / throw down / offer — to throw something out or put it forward (such as an offer of peace), joined to 'and'.
18.grammar: A present/imperfect verb of Form IV (alqā), which carries a causative/transitive sense — 'to make something fall, to cast it forth.' Prefixed with wa- ('and'), the yu- prefix and -ū plural ending mark a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'). The dropped final -na shows the subjunctive/jussive mood, governed by a preceding particle.
18.root: ل-ق-ي (l-q-y) — to meet, to throw down, to cast forth

19.meaning: To you / towards you — directing an action or motion at the addressees.
19.grammar: A preposition meaning 'to/towards' with the attached pronoun -kum ('you all'). The pronoun takes the helping vowel -u (kumu) when followed by a word beginning with the definite article, simply to ease pronunciation; it does not change the meaning.
19.root: — (preposition; no triliteral root)

20.meaning: Peace, reconciliation, or peaceful submission — the cessation of hostility and the offering of accord. The al- marks it as 'the peace' being spoken of.
20.grammar: A masculine noun with the definite article al- ('the'). Its first letter (s) is a 'sun letter,' so the l of al- assimilates into it (pronounced as-salam). The -a ending is accusative, which typically marks the noun as the direct object of a verb (the thing offered or extended).

21.meaning: And they hold back / restrain / withhold — to keep something in check or stop it, joined to 'and'.
21.grammar: A present/imperfect verb of Form I with a doubled (geminate) root, prefixed with wa- ('and'). The ya- prefix with the -ū plural ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'). The dropped final -na shows the subjunctive/jussive mood, governed by a preceding particle.
21.root: ك-ف-ف (k-f-f) — to hold back, restrain, desist

22.meaning: Their hands — the physical hands; often figuratively the means by which one acts, strikes, or exerts force (plural of 'hand').
22.grammar: A plural noun (aydī, plural of yad, 'hand') with the attached possessive -hum ('their'). The -a vowel before the pronoun marks the accusative case, which typically signals that the word is the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon).

23.meaning: Then seize them / take hold of them (you plural) — lay hold of them firmly and take them. The fa- adds 'so/then'; the attached 'them' is the object.
23.grammar: A command (imperative) to a masculine plural 'you all'. The -ū marks the plural addressee; the attached -hum is the object 'them'. Prefixed fa- means 'so/then', often introducing a response to a condition.
23.root: أ-خ-ذ (ʾ-kh-dh) — to take, seize, take hold of

24.meaning: And kill them / slay them. A command to kill, with an attached object pronoun 'them.'
24.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to a second-person masculine plural ('you all'); it opens with a connecting (elidable) alif needed to begin the consonant cluster. The -ū ending marks the masculine-plural addressee, the attached -hum is the object pronoun 'them,' and wa means 'and.'

25.meaning: Wherever / in whatever place — an adverb pointing to an unspecified location, 'in the place where ...'.
25.grammar: An invariable adverb of place ('where / wherever'). Although it ends in -u, it is fixed in form and does not change for case; it is normally followed by a clause stating the situation tied to that place.

26.meaning: You found them / came upon them / overtook them — to find, encounter, or catch up with someone, often with the nuance of skillfully locating or seizing.
26.grammar: A past-tense verb for the second-person masculine plural ('you all'). The suffix -tum marks 'you all' as the subject of a completed action; it is lengthened to -tumū to carry the attached object pronoun -hum ('them').
26.root: ث-ق-ف (th-q-f) — to find, catch, overtake; skill, deftness

27.meaning: And those (people) — a far-pointing demonstrative, 'those ones,' addressed to a plural audience, joined to 'and'.
27.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'those' (used for a plural of people). The attached -kum is an address-marker directed at a plural audience ('you all'), tying the demonstrative to the ones being spoken to. Demonstratives like this are fixed in form and do not change their ending for case.

28.meaning: We made, rendered, set up, or appointed. A completed act of making or designating, done by a group or by a majestic 'We.'
28.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb with the attached subject ending -nā, meaning 'we' did the action. 'Jaʿala' carries senses from 'to make/create' to 'to render X into Y' or 'to appoint.'
28.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, render, appoint, place

29.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
29.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

30.meaning: A compound meaning 'upon them' or 'against them': the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over, against') joined to the plural pronoun 'them'. It conveys something resting on, being incumbent upon, or weighing against a group.
30.grammar: ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay- before a pronoun. The suffix -him is the attached pronominal suffix for a masculine plural group ('them'); after a preposition it carries genitive/prepositional force, and the -i- vowel reflects its position after this preposition. Together they signal a relationship of something being over, upon, or burdensome to that group.
30.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

31.meaning: Authority, sanction, or compelling proof — power or warrant given to back something up, whether kingly authority or a decisive argument. 'Sulṭān' is authorizing power or evidence.
31.grammar: A single noun ('authority') carrying the accusative indefinite ending -an (tanwīn al-naṣb). This one ending does two things at once: the -a marks the accusative case (typically the direct object of a verb), and the final -n sound (nunation) shows the noun is indefinite ('an authority / any warrant'). The nunation is a diacritic on the case vowel, not a separable suffix, so the word stays one undivided token.
31.root: س-ل-ط (s-l-ṭ) — power, dominance, authority

32.meaning: Active participle: 'clear, plain, manifest, making evident.' It describes something that is itself obvious and that also makes the truth plain to others — both 'evident' and 'evidencing'.
32.grammar: An active participle of the form-IV pattern (mufʿil), meaning 'one that makes clear.' The ending -an is the indefinite accusative (the 'tanwīn' n-sound), which commonly marks a descriptive complement or an object.

1.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

2.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

2.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.
2.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existence; to be

3.meaning: For / against a believer — one who has faith, who trusts and affirms; preceded by the preposition 'for/against.' The final -in (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a believer').
3.grammar: An active participle of Form IV (āmana, 'to believe'), meaning 'one who believes/has faith.' It is preceded by the preposition li- ('for/to'). The -in ending is the genitive case with nunation: genitive is the case taken after a preposition, and the nunation marks the noun as indefinite ('a believer').
