2.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, second person masculine plural ('you all weaken'). The ta- prefix marks 'you', and the -ū ending marks a masculine plural subject. The dropped final nūn (tahinū rather than tahinūna) shows the verb is in the subjunctive/jussive mood — the form that follows particles of negation, prohibition, or purpose.
2.root: و-ه-ن (w-h-n) — to be weak, feeble, faint

3.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
3.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

4.meaning: Seeking, pursuit, striving after — the act of actively looking for and desiring to attain something.
4.grammar: A verbal noun (the name of the action 'seeking'), from a 'form VIII' verb whose pattern adds an inner -t- and conveys earnest, deliberate pursuit. The final -i is genitive — the form used after a preposition or when linked to a following noun ('the seeking OF ...'). The long -āʾ ends the stem itself.
4.root: ب-غ-ي (b-gh-y) — to seek, desire, strive after

5.meaning: 'The people / the folk' — a collective noun for a community, nation, or group of people regarded as a body. Often it carries the nuance of one's own people or a particular group sharing a trait.
5.grammar: A collective noun with the definite article 'al-' ('the'). The final '-i' is the genitive ending, which typically appears after a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun in an 'of …' relationship.
5.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand/rise; a people, community

6.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
6.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

7.meaning: You (plural) are / you happen to be. A form of the 'hollow' verb kāna ('to be'), which links a subject to a state or description, or expresses simply being or existing.
7.grammar: Present/imperfect verb, 2nd person masculine plural ('you all'). The ta- prefix marks 2nd person; the -ū ending marks masculine plural. The dropping of the usual final -na (so takūnū rather than takūnūna) shows the verb is in the subjunctive or jussive mood — the form expected after conditional or subordinating particles.
7.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

8.meaning: You feel pain, suffer, or hurt — to be in physical or inner pain; the experience of aching or distress, addressed to a group.
8.grammar: A present-tense verb, 2nd person masculine plural ('you all suffer'). The ta- prefix marks the 'you' subject. The full ending -ūna (with the final nuun kept) shows the indicative mood — a plain statement of fact about something happening or habitually true, as opposed to a command or a clause introduced by 'that/in order to'.

9.meaning: 'for indeed they …' — a connective 'for/so' joined to an emphatic particle that strongly affirms what follows, plus the pronoun 'they'. The combination introduces a firmly stressed statement about a group.
9.grammar: The particle 'inna' gives strong emphasis ('indeed, truly') and grammatically takes a following noun or pronoun in the accusative; here that is the attached -hum ('they', masculine plural), which serves as its subject. The leading 'fa' connects the clause to what precedes ('and so / for').

10.meaning: They feel pain, suffer, or hurt — to be in physical or inner pain; said of a group of others.
10.grammar: A present-tense verb, 3rd person masculine plural ('they suffer'). The ya- prefix marks the 'they' subject. The full ending -ūna (with the final nuun kept) shows the indicative mood — a plain statement of an ongoing or habitual fact, as opposed to a command or a 'that/in order to' clause.

11.meaning: 'Just as / in the same way that' — a phrase of comparison joining 'like / as' to 'what', meaning 'like that which...' or 'in the manner that...'.
11.grammar: The comparison particle ka- ('like / as') joined to mā ('what / that which'). Together they introduce a likeness or manner — 'just as...', 'in the same way that...' — comparing one thing or action to another.

12.meaning: You feel pain, suffer, or hurt — to be in physical or inner pain; the experience of aching or distress, addressed to a group.
12.grammar: A present-tense verb, 2nd person masculine plural ('you all suffer'). The ta- prefix marks the 'you' subject. The full ending -ūna (with the final nuun kept) shows the indicative mood — a plain statement of fact about something happening or habitually true, as opposed to a command or a clause introduced by 'that/in order to'.

13.meaning: And you hope for / look forward to and expect — to anticipate something good with longing and hopeful expectation; said of a group.
13.grammar: A present-tense verb, 2nd person masculine plural ('you all hope'). The ta- prefix marks the 'you' subject. The full ending -ūna (with the final nuun kept) shows the indicative mood — a plain statement of fact. The leading wa- is a separate connecting particle ('and' or 'while').
13.root: ر-ج-و (r-j-w) — to hope, expect, look forward to

14.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
14.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

15.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
15.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

16.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
16.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

17.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
17.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

18.meaning: They hold out hope for something, expecting and longing for a good outcome (often divine reward or mercy). The verb can carry both hoping for good and, in some contexts, fearing/anticipating.
18.grammar: A present/future-tense verb. The ya- prefix together with the -ūna ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'). The -ūna ending is the indicative form, signalling a real, ongoing or habitual action ('they hope / they keep hoping').

19.meaning: And he was / he became — a verb of being that places a subject in a past state or links it to a description in the past.
19.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'kāna' is a past-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular, meaning 'he was/became'; it commonly introduces a past condition and is typically followed by a noun describing the subject's state. The final -a marks completed past action by a single male.
19.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existence

20.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
20.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

21.meaning: All-Knowing; one possessing complete, perfect knowledge. As an intensive form it conveys knowledge that is total and unfailing, encompassing all things.
21.grammar: An intensive adjective ('all-knowing') on the faʿīl pattern, which stresses the quality to its fullest degree. The -an (tanwīn) joins the -a accusative ending — typical of a predicate or object — with the -n marking it indefinite.

22.meaning: All-Wise / deeply wise — possessing perfect wisdom: putting everything in its right place and acting with flawless judgement; an intensive form denoting one whose wisdom is complete.
22.grammar: An intensive adjective on the faʿīl pattern, denoting one firmly and perfectly characterized by wisdom. The final -an (accusative, with tanwin) marks it as indefinite and as describing an accusative noun or completing the sense of a verb (e.g. as a predicate). As a divine attribute it conveys absolute, all-encompassing wisdom.
22.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — wisdom, sound judgement, to judge

1.meaning: A two-part expression: an emphatic particle that strongly affirms and confirms a statement ('truly, indeed, certainly'), fused with the attached pronoun 'we.' Together: 'truly we…' / 'indeed we…'
1.grammar: The particle inna gives strong emphasis and certainty to the clause it opens. The attached -ā is the pronoun 'we,' serving as the subject being emphasized: 'truly we…'

2.meaning: We sent down — to cause something to descend or be revealed from a higher source to a lower; classically used of revelation sent down from on high.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb of the causative (fourth) form, meaning to make something come down. The attached -nā is the subject pronoun 'we', marking the action as completed and done by a 'we' (a form of majestic/collective speech when used of Allah).
2.root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — to descend, come down, be sent down

3.meaning: 'To you' (addressing one person): indicating direction or motion toward a single individual — that toward which something moves or is directed.
3.grammar: The preposition ilā ('to, towards') with an attached pronoun; before a suffix ilā takes the form ilay-. The -ka ending is the pronoun 'you' for a single male addressee. Pronouns following a preposition stand in the genitive relationship, though their form does not visibly change for case.

4.meaning: The Book, the Scripture — a written revelation; the term for a divinely revealed text.
4.grammar: A definite noun ('the Book') with attached 'al-' ('the'). The final '-a' ending is the accusative case, typically marking the word as the direct object of a verb.
4.root: ك-ت-ب (k-t-b) — to write; a writing, book

5.meaning: 'With the truth / by means of what is true and right.' Combines the preposition 'with/by' and 'the truth' — that which is real, established, correct, and rightfully due, as opposed to falsehood.
5.grammar: A noun governed by the attached preposition bi- ('with/by'). The -i ending is the genitive case, which is required after a preposition; here it links 'the truth' to 'with', giving 'with the truth'.
5.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, right, reality, that which is established and due

6.meaning: So that you may judge, rule, or decide — to give a verdict, settle a matter, or govern between parties; expressed as a purpose ('in order to judge').
6.grammar: A present-tense verb, 2nd person masculine singular ('you judge'), governed by the particle li- ('so that, in order to'). That particle puts the verb in the subjunctive mood, shown by the final -a ending — the mood used for purpose ('in order that ...') rather than a plain statement.
6.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — to judge, decide, rule, govern

7.meaning: Between; in the midst of two things. An adverb of place marking the space separating or lying among parties or points.
7.grammar: An adverb of place ('between'). It always ends in -a and grammatically governs what follows it, putting the following noun(s) into the genitive 'of' relationship. It does not change to show 'the' or a case of its own; the fixed -a is simply how this word is formed.
7.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction, what lies between

8.meaning: Humankind, people, mankind — the collective of human beings.
8.grammar: A collective noun ('people, mankind') carrying the definite article al- ('the'); the 'l' of the article assimilates into the following 'n', doubling it (al-nās → an-nās). The genitive ending -i marks the word as governed by a preposition or as the second term of a possessive.
8.root: ء-ن-س (ʾ-n-s) — humankind, sociability, familiarity; the word for 'people' is most commonly traced to this root (related to insān, 'human being')

9.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
9.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

10.meaning: He showed you / caused you to see — to make someone perceive or behold something, whether with the eye or the understanding; addressed to a single 'you'.
10.grammar: A past-tense verb, 3rd person masculine singular ('he showed'), of the 'form IV' causative pattern ('to make someone see'). The attached -ka is the object pronoun 'you' (a single male). So the form means 'he caused you to see / he showed you', presented as completed.

12.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

13.meaning: A short (jussive) form of the verb 'to be / to become', meaning 'be' or 'does not become / is not'. It expresses being, existing, or coming to be in a clipped form that typically follows a particle such as a negator or a command.
13.grammar: Present-tense verb with the ta- prefix marking a second-person masculine singular ('you') or third-person feminine singular ('it/she') subject. The clipped final consonant (sukun, no vowel) is the jussive/apocopated mood, the form used after negative particles ('did not / was not') or as a command or prohibition.
13.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

14.meaning: For / belonging to the treacherous ones — those who betray trust and act deceitfully; a group characterized by treachery.
14.grammar: An active participle ('one who betrays') made definite by 'the' and put in the sound masculine plural ('the betrayers'). The plural ending -īna is the form used in the genitive or accusative; here it follows the preposition li- ('for, belonging to'), which calls for that genitive form.
14.root: خ-و-ن (kh-w-n) — to betray, be treacherous, breach trust

15.meaning: A disputant / pleader / contender — one who argues a case and quarrels on behalf of a side; an intensive form for a persistent advocate or opponent in dispute.
15.grammar: An intensive noun/adjective on the faʿīl pattern, denoting one strongly given to disputing or pleading. The final -an (accusative, with tanwin) marks it as indefinite and as a direct object or a predicate/state completing the sense of a verb.

6.meaning: A word meaning 'much-forgiving' or 'ever-forgiving' — an intensive form describing one whose forgiveness is abundant and constant. It is one of the qualities of Allah.
6.grammar: An intensive adjective on the pattern faʿūl, conveying that the quality is great in degree and repeated. The ending -an is the accusative case with tanwīn (the indefinite 'n' sound), written with a supporting alif; it is the form an indefinite word takes when it is, for example, a predicate of certain verbs/particles or otherwise placed in the object position.
6.root: غ-ف-ر (gh-f-r) — forgiving, covering over, pardoning

7.meaning: 'Most Merciful / deeply compassionate' — an intensive form of raḥima, denoting one full of mercy and tender compassion; a frequent description of Allah.

2.root: ج-د-ل (j-d-l) — to dispute, argue, wrangle

3.meaning: About / concerning; a particle marking the topic of inquiry or the thing one moves away from.

4.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
4.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

5.meaning: They act treacherously, betray a trust, or defraud — to be unfaithful to what has been entrusted to one. The verb conveys a recurring or ongoing breach of fidelity by a group.
5.grammar: A present/future-tense verb. The ya- prefix together with the -ūna ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they …'); the -na is the marker that the verb stays in its ordinary (indicative) form rather than being cut short. The Form VIII pattern adds a sense of doing the act for oneself.
5.root: خ-و-ن (kh-w-n) — betrayal, breach of trust, treachery

6.meaning: A noun meaning 'their own selves' or 'themselves' — the plural of 'nafs' (self, soul, person, inner self), joined to the pronoun 'their.' It commonly conveys the reflexive idea of acting upon one's own self.
6.grammar: A noun (a broken/irregular plural of 'nafs') with the attached possessive pronoun '-hum' ('their/them,' masculine plural). The -a case ending before the pronoun is accusative, typically marking the word as the direct object of a verb — i.e. the self upon which the action falls.
6.root: ن-ف-س (n-f-s) — self, soul, person; breath

11.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

13.meaning: Extremely or habitually treacherous; a chronic betrayer of trust. The doubled middle consonant gives an intensive force — not merely one who betrays, but one steeped in treachery.
13.grammar: A noun/adjective in the intensive 'fa''āl' pattern, which denotes someone who does something constantly or to an extreme degree. The final -an is the accusative case with nunation (the 'n' sound marking it as indefinite); this ending typically appears on an object of a verb or after certain particles.

21.meaning: All-encompassing; surrounding, embracing, and comprehending everything completely. Used of knowledge or power that nothing escapes.
21.grammar: An active participle (Form IV) meaning 'one who encompasses/surrounds.' The final -an is the accusative case with nunation (the indefinite 'an' sound); this ending marks the word as an indefinite object or predicate, or as following certain particles.

1.meaning: An attention-drawing phrase meaning 'here you are! / lo, you are these' — a particle of alerting ('here, behold') fused to the pronoun 'you (plural)', used to call attention to the addressees and their situation.
1.grammar: Built from the alerting particle hā ('here!, behold!') prefixed to the standalone pronoun antum ('you', masculine plural). The pronoun antum is the form used for the subject/topic — 'you all'. Together they draw attention: 'Here you are, you are the ones who…'.

2.meaning: These / those — a plural demonstrative pointing to a group of people or things. Its core sense is the near demonstrative 'these', but it is very commonly rendered 'those' in translation when the group it points to has already been described or named rather than being physically present.
2.grammar: A plural demonstrative pronoun, used for a group of either gender. Its base value is near-deixis ('these'), built from an attention-drawing prefix 'hā-' ('lo!, here') plus the base 'ulāʾi'. In practice it is often translated 'those' when the referent is already mentioned or understood rather than literally nearby. Its form is fixed and does not change for grammatical case; it points to a group rather than naming it.

3.meaning: You (a group) argued, disputed, or pleaded on behalf of someone or something — to contend back and forth in debate. The Form III pattern implies a reciprocal exchange between contending parties.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb. The suffix -tum marks the subject as second-person masculine plural ('you all …'). The Form III pattern (long vowel after the first root letter) typically signals a mutual or back-and-forth action directed at another party.

4.meaning: From them; away from them; concerning them. The preposition ʿan conveys moving away from, departing from, or 'on behalf of / concerning', combined with the pronoun 'them'.
4.grammar: A preposition joined to the attached pronoun -hum, 'them' (referring to a group, grammatically masculine plural). The preposition ʿan basically signals separation or removal ('away from'), and can also mean 'about/concerning' or 'on behalf of' depending on usage.

5.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
5.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

6.meaning: 'The life' — living existence, the state of being alive.
6.grammar: The definite article al- with the feminine noun ḥayāt ('life'); the waw belongs to the stem and the tā' marbūṭa is its feminine suffix. The final -i is the genitive case vowel, which typically marks the word as following a preposition or standing in an 'of' relationship to a following noun.
6.root: ح-ي-ي (ḥ-y-y) — life, being alive, living

7.meaning: The nearer, lower world — present worldly life as opposed to the hereafter. Literally 'the nearest/lowest,' it denotes this immediate life and its affairs.
7.grammar: A definite feminine adjective in the superlative/elative pattern ('the nearest, the lowest'), commonly used as a noun for the present world. Its ending is a fixed long -ā that does not change for case.

8.meaning: A compound meaning 'then whoever' or 'so whoever'. It combines 'then/so' with the conditional/relative 'who', introducing whatever person meets a stated condition.
8.grammar: The connector fa- ('then/so', often answering or following a condition) joined to man ('whoever / the one who'), which refers to people and introduces a condition: 'whoever does X…'. man does not change its ending; the clause after it supplies the rest of the meaning.

9.meaning: He argues, disputes, or pleads — contending back and forth in debate. The Form III pattern carries the sense of a reciprocal dispute between parties.
9.grammar: A present/future-tense verb with a third-person masculine singular subject ('he …'), shown by the yu- prefix. The final -u marks the ordinary (indicative) mood, used for a simple statement of fact. The Form III pattern signals a mutual, back-and-forth action.

10.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
10.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

11.meaning: From them; away from them; concerning them. The preposition ʿan conveys moving away from, departing from, or 'on behalf of / concerning', combined with the pronoun 'them'.
11.grammar: A preposition joined to the attached pronoun -hum, 'them' (referring to a group, grammatically masculine plural). The preposition ʿan basically signals separation or removal ('away from'), and can also mean 'about/concerning' or 'on behalf of' depending on usage.

12.meaning: The noun 'day' — a span of time, often used for a momentous Day or appointed time; in the accusative it frequently functions as 'on the day (when…)', marking the time at which something occurs.
12.grammar: A masculine noun bearing the -a (accusative) ending. As an adverb of time this ending typically gives the sense 'on the day…', fixing the moment of an event.
12.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, a period of time

13.meaning: "the Resurrection" — the standing-up of all people from death to be judged; literally the act of rising or standing up.
13.grammar: The al- prefix means "the." The -i ending (on the feminine -t) is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ("the … OF this") or follows a preposition.

14.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'or', specifically the 'or' that pairs with a preceding question to offer an alternative ('…or…?'). It links two possibilities being weighed against each other, often after an opening interrogative.

parts.en: or (in alternatives, esp. after a question)

14.grammar: An indeclinable particle (no case or tense ending). It typically introduces the second branch of a two-part question or a balanced alternative, presenting the two as equally consequential.

15.meaning: A versatile word meaning 'who / whoever / the one who.' It can ask a question ('who?') or introduce a clause ('whoever does…'), referring to persons.
15.grammar: An indeclinable particle/pronoun with a fixed form (it does not change for case). Used for rational beings ('who'), functioning either as an interrogative ('who?') or as a conditional/relative ('whoever, the one who').

16.meaning: He/it is, becomes, or comes to be. A core verb of being and existence, also used to place an action in past or continuous time when paired with other verbs.
16.grammar: A present/future-tense verb with a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it …'), shown by the ya- prefix. The final -u marks the ordinary (indicative) mood, used for a plain statement. This is a 'hollow' verb (middle weak letter), hence the long -ū in the stem.
16.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existence, coming to be

17.meaning: A compound meaning 'upon them' or 'against them': the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over, against') joined to the plural pronoun 'them'. It conveys something resting on, being incumbent upon, or weighing against a group.
17.grammar: ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay- before a pronoun. The suffix -him is the attached pronominal suffix for a masculine plural group ('them'); after a preposition it carries genitive/prepositional force, and the -i- vowel reflects its position after this preposition. Together they signal a relationship of something being over, upon, or burdensome to that group.
17.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

18.meaning: A trustee, guardian, or disposer of affairs — one to whom matters are committed and who is relied upon to manage and protect them.
18.grammar: A noun on the intensive pattern faʿīl ('one who is relied upon'). The '-an' ending (with tanwīn) marks the indefinite accusative case: it commonly signals the object of a verb, or the role/capacity in which something serves ('as a …').
18.root: و-ك-ل (w-k-l) — entrusting, reliance, appointing someone to manage one's affairs

1.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
1.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

2.meaning: He does, works, or performs a deed — to carry out an action or labor. It denotes purposeful doing and conduct.
2.grammar: A present/future-tense verb with a third-person masculine singular subject ('he …'), shown by the ya- prefix. The silent/vowelless ending (-mal with no final vowel) marks the jussive/cut-short mood, the form a verb takes after certain particles such as conditional or negating words.
2.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — doing, working, action, deed

3.meaning: Evil, harm, or wrongdoing; something bad or injurious. It denotes an ill deed or an affliction that brings hurt.
3.grammar: A noun. The final -an is the accusative case with nunation (the indefinite 'an' sound); this ending typically marks the word as the indefinite object of a verb or as following certain particles.

4.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
4.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

5.meaning: He wrongs, oppresses, or acts unjustly — to put something out of its rightful place, whether against others or oneself. The core idea is injustice and the violation of due right.
5.grammar: A present/future-tense verb with a third-person masculine singular subject ('he …'), shown by the ya- prefix. The vowelless ending (-lim with no final vowel) marks the jussive/cut-short mood, used after conditional or negating particles.

6.meaning: His own self, soul, or very being — the inner person or essence of an individual. The base noun nafs denotes the soul/self, and the attached 'his' makes it reflexive ('himself') or possessive ('his soul').
6.grammar: A noun carrying the -a (accusative) ending, which typically marks it as the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon) or the object of certain particles. The suffix -hu means 'his/him', here making the noun reflexive or possessive.
6.root: ن-ف-س (n-f-s) — self, soul, breath of life

7.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
7.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

8.meaning: He seeks forgiveness; he asks pardon (of Allah). The Form X pattern conveys actively seeking and requesting the covering-over of one's sins.
8.grammar: A present/future-tense verb with a third-person masculine singular subject ('he …'), shown by the ya- prefix. Its underlying mood is jussive (cut-short, normally vowelless), but a helping -i vowel is added to the end to ease pronunciation before a following word that begins with a cluster. The Form X pattern (sta-) means to seek or request the root action — here, forgiveness.

9.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
9.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

10.meaning: He finds, comes upon, or attains something. It denotes discovering or obtaining what was sought or encountered.
10.grammar: A present/future-tense verb with a third-person masculine singular subject ('he …'), shown by the ya- prefix. Its underlying mood is jussive (cut-short, normally vowelless), but a helping -i vowel is added at the end to ease pronunciation before a following consonant cluster.

11.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
11.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

12.meaning: A word meaning 'much-forgiving' or 'ever-forgiving' — an intensive form describing one whose forgiveness is abundant and constant. It is one of the qualities of Allah.
12.grammar: An intensive adjective on the pattern faʿūl, conveying that the quality is great in degree and repeated. The ending -an is the accusative case with tanwīn (the indefinite 'n' sound), written with a supporting alif; it is the form an indefinite word takes when it is, for example, a predicate of certain verbs/particles or otherwise placed in the object position.

13.meaning: 'Most Merciful / deeply compassionate' — an intensive form of raḥima, denoting one full of mercy and tender compassion; a frequent description of Allah.
13.grammar: An intensive adjective on the fa'īl pattern, expressing a deep, abiding quality — abounding in mercy. The -an ending is the accusative case with indefinite (tanwīn) 'n,' often marking it as a predicate or as describing someone as 'most merciful.'

1.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
1.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

2.meaning: He earns, acquires, or gains — to bring about something for oneself by one's own effort or deed, whether good or bad.
2.grammar: A present/future-tense verb with a third-person masculine singular subject ('he …'), shown by the ya- prefix. The vowelless ending (-sib with no final vowel) marks the jussive/cut-short mood, used after conditional or negating particles.
2.root: ك-س-ب (k-s-b) — earning, acquiring, gaining

3.meaning: Sin — a blameworthy, morally culpable act; deliberate wrongdoing or guilt. The '-an' nunation marks it as indefinite and accusative.
3.grammar: A noun in the indefinite accusative. The '-an' (nunation on the fatḥa, with following alif) marks it as indefinite and accusative — the case typically used for the object of a verb.

4.meaning: A compound particle 'so it is only …' or 'then indeed only.' It joins a consequence ('so/then') to an emphatic restriction ('only / nothing more than'), confining the statement to exactly what follows.
4.grammar: A cluster of particles: 'fa-' introduces a result ('so/then'), 'inna' gives emphasis ('truly'), and the attached 'mā' turns the emphasis into restriction, so the whole means 'so it is only/nothing but.' These are connective and emphatic words; they have no case ending of their own.

5.meaning: He earns or acquires it — to gain something for oneself, with an attached object 'it.' The verb's core sense is bringing about a gain through one's own action.
5.grammar: A present/future-tense verb with a third-person masculine singular subject ('he …'), shown by the ya- prefix. The -u before the suffix marks the ordinary (indicative) mood. The attached -hu is an object pronoun meaning 'it' or 'him,' receiving the action of the verb.

6.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
6.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

7.meaning: 'Himself; his own self/soul' — the inner self, soul, or person of a male individual; used reflexively to point back to the person himself.
7.grammar: The noun 'nafs' ('self/soul') with the attached pronoun '-hi' ('his'). The '-i' ending is genitive: it typically follows a preposition or links the noun possessively to what precedes ('the self OF him' = 'himself'). The pronoun appears as '-hi' (rather than '-hu') because of this preceding '-i' vowel; the long vowel mark indicates it is pronounced '-hī'.

8.meaning: And he was / he became — a verb of being that places a subject in a past state or links it to a description in the past.
8.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'kāna' is a past-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular, meaning 'he was/became'; it commonly introduces a past condition and is typically followed by a noun describing the subject's state. The final -a marks completed past action by a single male.

9.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
9.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

10.meaning: All-Knowing; one possessing complete, perfect knowledge. As an intensive form it conveys knowledge that is total and unfailing, encompassing all things.
10.grammar: An intensive adjective ('all-knowing') on the faʿīl pattern, which stresses the quality to its fullest degree. The -an (tanwīn) joins the -a accusative ending — typical of a predicate or object — with the -n marking it indefinite.

11.meaning: All-Wise; one possessing perfect wisdom, who places everything in its right place and decides with flawless judgement. As an intensive form it conveys wisdom that is complete and sound.
11.grammar: An intensive adjective ('all-wise') on the faʿīl pattern, stressing the quality to its fullest degree. The -an (tanwīn) combines the -a accusative ending — typical of a predicate or object — with the -n marking it indefinite.

1.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
1.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

2.meaning: He earns, acquires, or gains — to bring about something for oneself by one's own effort or deed, whether good or bad.
2.grammar: A present/future-tense verb with a third-person masculine singular subject ('he …'), shown by the ya- prefix. The vowelless ending (-sib with no final vowel) marks the jussive/cut-short mood, used after conditional or negating particles.
2.root: ك-س-ب (k-s-b) — earning, acquiring, gaining

3.meaning: A sin, fault, or wrongful mistake — a moral lapse or offense. It denotes a single misdeed or error that incurs guilt.
3.grammar: A feminine noun. The final -tan is the accusative case with nunation (the feminine ending 't' plus the indefinite 'an' sound); this ending typically marks the word as the indefinite object of a verb or as following certain particles.

4.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
4.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

5.meaning: Sin — a blameworthy, morally culpable act; deliberate wrongdoing or guilt. The '-an' nunation marks it as indefinite and accusative.
5.grammar: A noun in the indefinite accusative. The '-an' (nunation on the fatḥa, with following alif) marks it as indefinite and accusative — the case typically used for the object of a verb.

6.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
6.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

7.meaning: He throws, casts, or hurls — and, by extension, he accuses or imputes (a charge) to someone, as one 'casts' an accusation. The core image is launching something toward a target.
7.grammar: A present/future-tense verb with a third-person masculine singular subject ('he …'), shown by the ya- prefix. This verb's final root letter is weak; in the jussive/cut-short mood that final letter drops away, leaving a short -i, which is the form used after conditional or negating particles.

8.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
8.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

9.meaning: Innocent, free, or clear of something — quit of blame, fault, or obligation. It describes one who is exonerated and bears no guilt.
9.grammar: An adjective/noun on the 'fa'īl' pattern meaning one who is clear or free of something. The final -an is the accusative case with nunation (the indefinite 'an' sound); this ending marks the word as an indefinite object or as following certain particles.

10.meaning: 'Then/so, indeed …' — the connector 'then/so' joined to the particle 'qad', which before a past-tense verb stresses that the action has certainly and already happened.
10.grammar: A connecting particle 'fa-' ('then/so', often signalling a result) plus 'qad'. With a following perfect verb, 'qad' emphasises that the act is real and completed ('have indeed …'). The final -i on 'qad' is a helping vowel added to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a cluster; it carries no grammatical meaning of its own.

11.meaning: He bore, carried, or took upon himself a burden — to shoulder a load, often a weight of guilt or responsibility. The Form VIII pattern adds the sense of taking the burden onto oneself.

parts.en: connecting vowel + first root letter (Form VIII)
bear, carry, take on a burden (Form VIII stem)

11.grammar: A past-tense verb with a third-person masculine singular subject ('he …'). The final -a is the standard past-tense ending for 'he.' The Form VIII pattern (an infixed -t- after the first root letter) here gives the reflexive sense of loading a burden upon oneself.

12.meaning: A noun meaning 'a false accusation, slander, calumny' — a brazen lie told against someone that leaves the hearer dumbfounded.
12.grammar: A verbal noun. The final -an (tanwīn fatḥa) is the indefinite accusative; on a noun like this it commonly works adverbially to describe the manner of an action ('slanderously,' 'by way of slander') or stands as an object.
12.root: ب-ه-ت (b-h-t) — being struck dumb; slander, brazen lying

13.meaning: A noun meaning 'a sin, a moral offense, a blameworthy wrongdoing' — an act that incurs guilt.
13.grammar: A noun. The final -an (tanwīn fatḥa) is the indefinite accusative ending ('a sin'), the case used for the direct object of a verb or for a noun joined by 'and' to such an object. The opening wa- means 'and.'

14.meaning: Active participle: 'clear, plain, manifest, making evident.' It describes something that is itself obvious and that also makes the truth plain to others — both 'evident' and 'evidencing'.
14.grammar: An active participle of the form-IV pattern (mufʿil), meaning 'one that makes clear.' The ending -an is the indefinite accusative (the 'tanwīn' n-sound), which commonly marks a descriptive complement or an object.

1.meaning: "and were it not for / and if not for" — a compound particle introducing a hypothetical: it points to something whose existence prevents a stated consequence, i.e. 'had it not been for X, then Y would have happened'.

parts.en: were it not for / if not

1.grammar: A particle phrase, not a verb, so it carries no case or tense ending. It sets up a conditional that is contrary to fact, typically answered by a clause beginning with la- ('then certainly…'). The leading wa- is the connector 'and'.

2.meaning: "Bounty / grace / favour / excellence" — faḍl is overflowing generosity, favour, and grace; the surplus good that one freely bestows beyond what is owed.
2.grammar: A masculine singular noun. The final -u is the nominative case ending, typically marking the word as the subject of a sentence or the thing being asserted.
2.root: ف-ض-ل (f-ḍ-l) — to be in excess / surpass / show favour

3.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
3.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

4.meaning: "upon you / to you / against you" — the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over') with the 'you' pronoun, carrying senses of resting upon, being directed to, or bearing upon someone.
4.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The base ʿalā shifts to ʿalay- when a pronoun is added. The suffix -ka means 'you' (second-person masculine singular). Prepositions themselves take no case ending.

5.meaning: "And His mercy" — raḥma is mercy, compassion, and tender care; joined to a 'His'. Opened by the conjunction 'and'.
5.grammar: A feminine noun with the attached possessive pronoun 'hu' ('his'). The -u before the pronoun is the nominative case ending, typically marking the word as the subject or the thing being asserted. The noun's tāʾ marbūṭa is written as an open tāʾ (ت) because a pronoun is attached. Prefixed with the conjunction 'and'.

6.meaning: She/it surely resolved, intended, or was about to do something — a determined inclination toward an act. With the emphatic prefix it stresses that the resolve genuinely (or nearly) took place.
6.grammar: A past-tense verb carrying an emphatic prefix la- ('surely, indeed'), often used in the answer to an oath or hypothetical statement. The suffix -at marks the subject as third-person feminine singular ('she/it …').
6.root: ه-م-م (h-m-m) — resolve, intent, determination to act

7.meaning: A group, party, or faction — a distinct band or section of people, often a smaller portion of a larger body.
7.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-un' ending (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a group', not 'the group') and in the nominative case, the form typically used for the subject of a sentence.
7.root: ط-و-ف (ṭ-w-f) — to go around, circle; a portion that moves about

8.meaning: 'Among them / from them / some of them' — the preposition 'min' ('from, of, among') joined to the attached pronoun 'hum' ('them').
8.grammar: The preposition 'min' ('from / of / among') with the attached pronoun 'hum' ('them'), referring to a masculine plural group. Together they often express 'part of them' or 'some among them'.

9.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
9.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

10.meaning: They (a masculine plural group) would lead you astray, divert you from the right path, or cause you to err. The verb carries the sense of someone actively misdirecting another so that he loses the correct way.

parts.en: he/they (present-tense subject marker for a causative verb)

10.grammar: A present/future-tense verb. The yu- prefix plus the doubled middle marks the causative pattern 'to make someone go astray'. The -ū ending shows a masculine plural subject ('they'); because the final nūn is dropped, the verb is in the subjunctive/jussive mood, the form used after certain particles or in conditional and purpose constructions. The attached -ka is the direct object 'you'.
10.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to go astray, lose the way, err

11.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
11.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

12.meaning: They cause to go astray — they lead others away from the right path into error. The verb describes actively misguiding people.
12.grammar: A present/future-tense verb in the causative pattern (to 'make' someone stray). The '-ūna' ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they') and signals the verb is in its full (indicative) form, used for ongoing or factual statements.
12.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to stray, go astray, lose the way

13.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
13.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

14.meaning: A noun meaning 'their own selves' or 'themselves' — the plural of 'nafs' (self, soul, person, inner self), joined to the pronoun 'their.' It commonly conveys the reflexive idea of acting upon one's own self.
14.grammar: A noun (a broken/irregular plural of 'nafs') with the attached possessive pronoun '-hum' ('their/them,' masculine plural). The -a case ending before the pronoun is accusative, typically marking the word as the direct object of a verb — i.e. the self upon which the action falls.

15.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
15.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

16.meaning: They (a masculine plural group) harm you, injure you, or do you damage. The verb denotes inflicting hurt or detriment on someone.
16.grammar: A present/future-tense verb. The ya- prefix marks third person. The -ūna ending shows a masculine plural subject ('they') and, with its retained nūn, the indicative mood — the form used for a plain statement of fact ('they do/will harm'). The attached -ka is the direct object 'you'.
16.root: ض-ر-ر (ḍ-r-r) — to harm, injure, cause detriment

17.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
17.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

18.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
18.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
18.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

19.meaning: 'And He sent down / caused to descend'. It denotes bringing something down from a higher place to a lower one — characteristically the sending down of revelation. Past tense, third person masculine singular.
19.grammar: 'wa-' is the connector 'and'. 'anzala' is a past-tense verb of the causative pattern (form IV) meaning 'to make descend / send down', with the third-person masculine singular subject ('he') built in; the final '-a' is the standard past-tense ending.
19.root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — to descend, come down, send down

20.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
20.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

21.meaning: "upon you / to you / against you" — the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over') with the 'you' pronoun, carrying senses of resting upon, being directed to, or bearing upon someone.
21.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The base ʿalā shifts to ʿalay- when a pronoun is added. The suffix -ka means 'you' (second-person masculine singular). Prepositions themselves take no case ending.

22.meaning: The Book, the Scripture — a written revelation; the term for a divinely revealed text.
22.grammar: A definite noun ('the Book') with attached 'al-' ('the'). The final '-a' ending is the accusative case, typically marking the word as the direct object of a verb.
22.root: ك-ت-ب (k-t-b) — to write; a writing, book

23.meaning: "and the wisdom" — sound judgement and deep understanding that puts things in their right place; 'ḥikma' is wisdom: knowledge joined to right action, insight into the true nature and proper order of things.
23.grammar: A definite feminine noun ('the wisdom'); 'wa-' is 'and' and 'al-' is 'the.' The final '-a' is the accusative case ending, the form a noun takes as the direct object of a verb or when joined to another accusative noun.
23.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — to judge, govern wisely; wisdom, sound judgement

24.meaning: And He taught you, instructed you, imparted knowledge to you. The verb is the intensive/causative of 'to know', i.e. to cause someone to know.
24.grammar: A past-tense verb in the doubled (intensive/causative) pattern, turning 'to know' into 'to make know = to teach'. The bare -a ending with no extra subject suffix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'). The attached -ka is the direct object 'you'. The wa- prefix means 'and'.

25.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
25.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

26.meaning: A negating particle, 'not', used specifically to deny that an action happened in the past, even though it attaches to a present-tense verb form. It turns 'you do X' into 'you did not do X'.

parts.en: did not (negation of a completed act)

26.grammar: An indeclinable particle that governs the verb after it, putting that verb into the jussive (clipped) mood and giving it past-time meaning. In short: lam + a present-form verb = 'did not [verb]'.
26.root: — (particle; no triliteral root)

27.meaning: A short (jussive) form of the verb 'to be / to become', meaning 'be' or 'does not become / is not'. It expresses being, existing, or coming to be in a clipped form that typically follows a particle such as a negator or a command.
27.grammar: Present-tense verb with the ta- prefix marking a second-person masculine singular ('you') or third-person feminine singular ('it/she') subject. The clipped final consonant (sukun, no vowel) is the jussive/apocopated mood, the form used after negative particles ('did not / was not') or as a command or prohibition.
27.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

28.meaning: You (masculine singular) know, are aware of, or have knowledge of something. A simple present-tense verb of knowing.
28.grammar: A present/future-tense verb. The ta- prefix marks a second-person masculine singular subject ('you'). The final -u ending is the indicative mood, used for a straightforward statement ('you know / you do know').
28.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know, knowledge

29.meaning: And he was / he became — a verb of being that places a subject in a past state or links it to a description in the past.
29.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'kāna' is a past-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular, meaning 'he was/became'; it commonly introduces a past condition and is typically followed by a noun describing the subject's state. The final -a marks completed past action by a single male.

30.meaning: "Bounty / grace / favour / excellence" — faḍl is overflowing generosity, favour, and grace; the surplus good that one freely bestows beyond what is owed.
30.grammar: A masculine singular noun. The final -u is the nominative case ending, typically marking the word as the subject of a sentence or the thing being asserted.
30.root: ف-ض-ل (f-ḍ-l) — to be in excess / surpass / show favour

31.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
31.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

32.meaning: "upon you / to you / against you" — the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over') with the 'you' pronoun, carrying senses of resting upon, being directed to, or bearing upon someone.
32.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The base ʿalā shifts to ʿalay- when a pronoun is added. The suffix -ka means 'you' (second-person masculine singular). Prepositions themselves take no case ending.

33.meaning: 'Great, immense, mighty, momentous.' It describes something vast in size, weight, or seriousness, and is often used of grave or awe-inspiring matters.
33.grammar: An adjective on the intensive faʿīl pattern. The -an ending is the indefinite accusative ('a great …'), commonly marking an adjective that agrees with an indefinite accusative noun it describes, or the object of a verb.

1.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
1.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

2.meaning: The word for 'best / better / greatest good' — the superior or most excellent of things; also simply 'good, benefit'. The form shown is the construct (linking) form ready to attach to a following noun ('the best of …').
2.grammar: A noun used both for 'good/benefit' and, in comparisons, 'better/best'. The final -a marks the accusative case — the form used for the object of a verb or after certain particles. It often begins a construct chain meaning 'the best of …'.
2.root: خ-ي-ر (kh-y-r) — goodness, what is good; choosing the better

3.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
3.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

4.meaning: Much, many, abundant, numerous. An adjective describing a large quantity or great amount of something.
4.grammar: An indefinite adjective/noun. The -in ending (tanwīn with kasra) marks the genitive case together with indefiniteness ('much / of much'). The genitive is the case used after a preposition or when the word follows another noun in an 'of' relationship.
4.root: ك-ث-ر (k-th-r) — to be much, many, abundant

5.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
5.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

6.meaning: Their secret talk, their private conversation, their confidential or whispered discourse — speech held quietly between people apart from others.
6.grammar: A noun followed by a possessive pronoun. Najwā is a feminine verbal noun meaning confidential talk. The attached -hum means 'their' (masculine plural) and puts the noun in a possessive ('their …') construction; because of this attachment the noun stands in the genitive relationship, its final long vowel here written without a separate case mark.
6.root: ن-ج-و (n-j-w) — to confide, hold private/secret talk

7.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
7.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

8.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
8.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

9.meaning: A verb meaning 'he commanded', 'he ordered', or 'he enjoined' — to issue an authoritative instruction that something be done.
9.grammar: Past-tense (perfect) verb, third-person masculine singular ('he'). The bare three-letter stem ending in -a denotes a completed action by a single male subject: 'he gave a command'. It commonly takes a person commanded and a thing commanded.

10.meaning: With/of a charitable gift — voluntary almsgiving offered to the needy, an act of sincere giving for the sake of Allah.
10.grammar: A preposition plus an indefinite noun. The prefixed bi- means 'with / by means of'. The noun is in the genitive case (required after the preposition), marked by the -in ending (tanwīn with kasra) which also signals indefiniteness ('a charity').
10.root: ص-د-ق (ṣ-d-q) — truthfulness, sincerity; hence charitable giving

11.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
11.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

12.meaning: What is recognized as good and right — kindness, decency, fair and honourable conduct that is commonly acknowledged as proper. Literally 'that which is known/recognized' as good.
12.grammar: A passive participle ('that which is known/recognized') used as a noun meaning 'what is right and good'. The -in ending (tanwīn with kasra) marks the genitive case together with indefiniteness — the case used after a preposition or in an 'of' relationship.
12.root: ع-ر-ف (ʿ-r-f) — to know, recognize; hence the known/recognized good

13.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
13.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

14.meaning: Setting things right — making peace, reconciliation, reform, putting matters or relationships into a sound and proper state.
14.grammar: A verbal noun of the causative pattern, naming the act of 'making good / setting right'. The -in ending (tanwīn with kasra) marks the genitive case with indefiniteness — the case used after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun.
14.root: ص-ل-ح (ṣ-l-ḥ) — to be sound, good, in order; to set right

15.meaning: Between; in the midst of two things. An adverb of place marking the space separating or lying among parties or points.
15.grammar: An adverb of place ('between'). It always ends in -a and grammatically governs what follows it, putting the following noun(s) into the genitive 'of' relationship. It does not change to show 'the' or a case of its own; the fixed -a is simply how this word is formed.
15.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction, what lies between

16.meaning: Humankind, people, mankind — the collective of human beings.
16.grammar: A collective noun ('people, mankind') carrying the definite article al- ('the'); the 'l' of the article assimilates into the following 'n', doubling it (al-nās → an-nās). The genitive ending -i marks the word as governed by a preposition or as the second term of a possessive.
16.root: ء-ن-س (ʾ-n-s) — humankind, sociability, familiarity; the word for 'people' is most commonly traced to this root (related to insān, 'human being')

17.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
17.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

18.meaning: He does, makes, or carries out; the doing or performing of an act. A general verb for engaging in or committing some deed.
18.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he'). The ya- prefix marks the singular male subject. The final consonant carries no vowel (the jussive/conditional form), which is the shortened form a present verb takes after conditional or certain other particles, typically giving the sense 'if/whoever does…'.
18.root: ف-ع-ل (f-ʿ-l) — doing, making, performing an act

19.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
19.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

20.meaning: Seeking, earnestly pursuing, desiring to attain — the act of going after something diligently. As a verbal noun it means 'a seeking / out of desire for.'

parts.en: seeking / earnest pursuit (the final -a is the accusative case ending, here expressing purpose/motive)

20.grammar: A verbal noun (the 'act of seeking') in the accusative case, shown by the final -a. In this role the accusative commonly expresses purpose or motive — 'out of a desire for / in seeking.' It is built on a Form VIII pattern conveying earnest, deliberate pursuit.
20.root: ب-غ-ي (b-gh-y) — to seek, desire, strive after something

21.meaning: Good pleasure / approval / contentment of someone — the state of being well-pleased. Used especially of seeking the pleasure and approval of Allah.
21.grammar: A feminine verbal noun meaning 'good pleasure, approval.' The final -i is the genitive case ending, which typically links the word to a following noun ('the pleasure OF …') or follows a preposition. So it sets up a possessive link: 'the good pleasure of (someone).'
21.root: ر-ض-ي (r-ḍ-y) — to be pleased, satisfied, content; approval and good pleasure

22.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
22.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

23.meaning: A two-part marker meaning 'then/so' plus 'shall/will.' It announces something forthcoming as a consequence: the particle sawfa points to the future, generally a more remote or emphatic future than the shorter prefix sa-.
23.grammar: A linking particle fa- ('then/so,' signalling result or sequence) joined to the future particle sawfa, which is placed before a present-tense verb to throw its action into the future ('will/shall …').

24.meaning: A verb meaning 'We will give / grant / bestow upon him,' with the pronoun 'him' attached. The base verb is to bring, give, or hand over something to someone. The 'We' form lends it a sense of weight and majesty.
24.grammar: A present-tense verb, first-person plural ('We'), with the third-person masculine singular object 'him' attached. The prefix 'nu-' marks the doer as 'we.' The attached '-hi' ('him') is the object form of the pronoun; its vowel is '-i' after the preceding long 'ī.' The verb expresses a future or ongoing giving ('We grant / shall grant him').

25.meaning: A reward, wage, or recompense — the return earned for work or conduct, whether worldly pay or otherworldly recompense.
25.grammar: A noun meaning 'a reward.' The final '-an' (tanwīn fatḥa) marks the indefinite accusative case, the case used for the object of a verb (e.g. of 'to give'), giving the sense 'a reward.'
25.root: ا-ج-ر (ʾ-j-r) — reward, wage, recompense for what one does

26.meaning: 'Great, immense, mighty, momentous.' It describes something vast in size, weight, or seriousness, and is often used of grave or awe-inspiring matters.
26.grammar: An adjective on the intensive faʿīl pattern. The -an ending is the indefinite accusative ('a great …'), commonly marking an adjective that agrees with an indefinite accusative noun it describes, or the object of a verb.
26.root: ع-ظ-م (ʿ-ẓ-m) — to be great, immense

1.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
1.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

2.meaning: He opposes, breaks away from, sets himself in contention against, or splits from. The verb conveys hostile opposition and rupture, as if standing on the opposite side.
2.grammar: A present-tense verb of the mutual/confrontational pattern ('to set oneself against'). The yu- prefix marks third-person masculine singular ('he'). The base would end in a silent (jussive) consonant, but because of the doubled root letters a helping vowel -i is added; the jussive is the mood used in conditional clauses ('whoever opposes…').
2.root: ش-ق-ق (sh-q-q) — to split, cleave; hence to be at odds, oppose

3.meaning: The messenger, envoy, or emissary: one who is sent with a message; in the Qur'an typically a prophet sent by Allah bearing revelation to a people.
3.grammar: A noun on the form faʿūl (an intensive/agent pattern, 'one sent'), prefixed with al- ('the'). The final -a ending is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb ('… the messenger') or the subject of certain particles. The 'l' of al- assimilates into the following 'r' (a 'sun letter'), pronounced ar-rasūl.

4.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
4.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

5.meaning: A noun/adverb meaning 'after' — the time or position following something; 'afterward', 'following'.
5.grammar: An adverb of time functioning as a noun, here in the genitive case marked by the final -i. The genitive ending typically appears after a preposition or as the second term of a construct ('after THE …'), linking 'after' to a following noun to specify what it comes after.
5.root: ب-ع-د (b-ʿ-d) — to be after, to follow, distance in place or time

6.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
6.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

7.meaning: It became clear, plain, or evident — to come out into the open and be distinctly seen or understood; for something to be made manifest and unmistakable.

parts.en: it became clear / it grew evident

7.grammar: A past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular: 'it became clear'. The pattern (with the ta- prefix and doubled middle root letter) often gives the sense of a state coming about of itself. The final -a marks a single thing/male as the doer of a completed action.
7.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — to be distinct, clear, evident

8.meaning: To him / for him / he has — the preposition 'to/for' fused with a pronoun meaning 'him.' It expresses belonging, benefit, or possession (something is 'his' or done 'for him').
8.grammar: A preposition 'li-/la-' ('to, for') with the attached 3rd-person masculine singular pronoun 'him.' The pairing means 'to him' or 'for him' and often conveys possession ('he has …') or that an action is directed toward his benefit or detriment.
8.root: — (particle with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

9.meaning: The guidance; the right leading and true direction (with the definite article, 'the Guidance').
9.grammar: A definite verbal noun: the prefix al- means 'the'. It ends in a long -ā (from a weak-final root), an ending that does not change for case. It denotes the abstract reality of right guidance, made specific and definite by 'the'.
9.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — to guide, lead rightly, show the way

10.meaning: And he follows, pursues, goes after, or adheres to. The verb means to walk in another's footsteps or take something as one's path.
10.grammar: A present-tense verb of the reflexive pattern ('to follow for oneself, take to following'). The ya- prefix marks third-person masculine singular ('he'). The final silent (sukūn) ending is the jussive mood, used in conditional sentences and after certain particles ('and follows…'). The wa- prefix means 'and'.

11.meaning: 'Other than / different from / not'. A noun used to express difference or negation — 'something other than X', and so 'not-X'. It functions to exclude or contrast with what follows.
11.grammar: A noun of difference/exception. The -a ending marks the accusative case, the form it takes when it serves as a direct object or as a descriptive substitute standing in an object position; it governs a following noun in the genitive ('other than …'). That it takes case endings and tanwīn confirms it is a true noun, not a particle.
11.root: غ-ي-ر (gh-y-r) — to be other, different; otherness, change

12.meaning: 'path, way, road' — a route or course; figuratively a cause or way of life one travels along. In construct ('the way OF ...').
12.grammar: A singular noun with the '-i' (genitive) ending, which typically links it to a following noun ('the way OF ...') or follows a preposition. It marks the word as connected to or possessed by what comes after.

13.meaning: A plural noun meaning 'the believers' — those who have faith, who inwardly trust and affirm. The Form IV participle denotes one who brings about belief and security within.
13.grammar: A definite plural active participle of Form IV (āmana 'to believe'). The -īna ending marks a sound masculine plural in the accusative/genitive (object or oblique) state. The prefixed mu- marks it as a Form IV participle ('one who has/gives faith').

14.meaning: We turn him, direct him, or assign him toward something — to make someone face or be given over to a particular direction or charge.
14.grammar: A present-tense verb in the intensive/causative pattern ('to turn someone toward'). The nu- prefix marks a first-person plural subject ('we'). The verb stands in the jussive mood (as a conditional answer), its weak final letter dropped; the attached -hi means 'him'. The kasra under the pronoun reflects the preceding vowel.
14.root: و-ل-ي (w-l-y) — to be near, turn toward; to take charge of
