4.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to one male: 'say!'. Its natural form ends in a silent consonant (qul), but here a short -i vowel is added simply to smooth pronunciation before a following word that begins with a connecting sound; it carries no case meaning of its own.

5.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
5.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

6.meaning: He gives you a formal ruling — He pronounces an authoritative verdict or legal opinion to you.
6.grammar: Present-tense Form IV verb with a 'he' subject (the yu- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular doer), plus the attached object pronoun -kum ('you all'). It signals an ongoing or characteristic action of issuing a ruling.
6.root: ف-ت-ي (f-t-y) — to give a formal legal ruling/verdict (fatwā)

7.meaning: A small unit: the preposition 'in / within / during' joined to the attached pronoun 'them' referring to a group of feminine things.
7.grammar: 'fī' is the preposition 'in/within/during'. The attached -hinna is the object pronoun 'them' for a group of feminine items, so the whole means 'in/among them'. Pronouns attached to a preposition like this always take the genitive form.

8.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
8.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

9.meaning: It is recited / read aloud — a passage of revelation is being conveyed by being read out.
9.grammar: Present-tense passive verb, third-person masculine singular ('it is being recited'). The yu- prefix with the internal vowel pattern marks the passive (no doer named), and the final weak -ā shows it derives from a root ending in a weak letter; it conveys an ongoing action done to the subject.
9.root: ت-ل-و (t-l-w) — to recite, read aloud, follow

10.meaning: 'Upon you (all)' — the preposition 'upon/on/over' joined to the plural 'you,' indicating something resting on or directed at a group.
10.grammar: The preposition 'ʿalā' ('upon/on/over') in its joined form 'ʿalay-' plus the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you all,' masculine plural). It marks the group as the recipients or target of whatever is laid 'upon' them.

11.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
11.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

12.meaning: 'The Book / the Scripture' — a written record or revealed scripture; literally that which is written.
12.grammar: The definite article al- with the noun kitāb ('book, scripture'), itself a verbal noun from 'to write.' The -i ending is genitive, typically marking the word as following a preposition or standing in an 'of' relationship to a preceding noun.

13.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
13.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

14.meaning: Orphans — children who have lost their father (and by extension are without a guardian's protection). The base word denotes one bereft of a parent while still young.
14.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural noun. It ends in a fixed final -ā and does not change for case in the usual way (it is grammatically 'restricted' from full case-marking), so the same form serves where English would say 'orphans' as subject, object, or after a preposition.
14.root: ي-ت-م (y-t-m) — orphanhood, being bereft of a parent

15.meaning: 'The women' — the plural used for women/females collectively. (It serves as the plural of mar'a, 'woman.')
15.grammar: A plural noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending is genitive: it marks the word as following a preposition or standing in a possessive ('of …') relationship. The l of al- assimilates into the following n in pronunciation (a 'sun letter').

16.meaning: Those (women) who — a relative pronoun introducing a description, referring to a group of females and meaning 'the ones who…' or 'those females that…'.
16.grammar: A relative pronoun, feminine plural: 'those (women) who.' It is indeclinable — its form does not change for case — and it links a following clause back to a feminine-plural group, much like English 'who/which/that' applied to women.

17.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
17.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

18.meaning: You give them — you hand over or grant to them (a feminine group) something due, such as property or a dowry.
18.grammar: Present-tense Form IV verb ('to give/bring to') addressed to a plural 'you' (masculine), shown by the ta- prefix and the -ūna ending, with the attached object pronoun -hunna ('them', a group of females). The -ūna marks an ongoing action by a plural subject in the indicative mood.
18.root: ء-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; in Form IV, to bring/give to someone

19.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
19.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

20.meaning: 'It has been prescribed / decreed / made obligatory' — also literally 'it was written'. A past-tense passive verb conveying that something has been ordained and laid down as a binding command.
20.grammar: The internal vowel pattern (u–i) makes this passive: the action was done, with no doer named. The final -a is the default third-person masculine singular ending of a past-tense verb (it is a verbal person-marker, not a noun's case ending), so the verb reads 'it was prescribed'.

21.meaning: 'For them / to them' — the preposition 'for/to' joined to a feminine-plural 'them'.
21.grammar: The preposition li- ('for, to') with an attached object pronoun -hunna ('them', feminine plural). It expresses that something belongs to, is owed to, or is on behalf of a group of females. (The vowel appears as 'la-' before the pronoun.)

22.meaning: And you desire — you wish for, are eager toward, or set your heart upon something. With certain particles the same verb can flip to mean turning away from a thing in disinterest.
22.grammar: Present-tense Form I verb addressed to a plural 'you' (masculine): the ta- prefix plus -ūna ending mark a second-person masculine plural subject. The -ūna signals an ongoing or habitual action in the indicative mood.
22.root: ر-غ-ب (r-gh-b) — to desire, yearn for (or, with 'ʿan', to shun)

23.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
23.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

24.meaning: You marry them — you take them (a feminine group) in marriage, entering the marriage contract.
24.grammar: Present-tense Form I verb, second-person masculine plural, in the subjunctive/jussive mood — shown by the bare -ū ending (the indicative -ūna has dropped its final -na), which typically follows particles meaning 'to', 'that', or 'if'. The attached -hunna is the object 'them' (females).
24.root: ن-ك-ح (n-k-ḥ) — to marry, enter the marriage bond

25.meaning: A noun/adjective in the plural, 'the oppressed / those deemed weak / the downtrodden,' joined by 'and' (wa-). It refers to people treated as weak and made helpless — held to be of no account and rendered powerless by others, rather than weak merely by nature.
25.grammar: A definite masculine sound plural, prefixed with 'wa-' ('and'). It is a passive participle of the 'seeking/deeming' (istafʿala) pattern — literally 'those who are counted weak / made weak,' i.e. the oppressed. The '-īna' ending marks masculine plural in the accusative/genitive form (used for objects, or after prepositions and links). 'Wa-' simply joins it to what precedes.
25.root: ض-ع-ف (ḍ-ʿ-f) — weakness, feebleness, being made weak

26.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
26.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

27.meaning: The children / the little ones — the young, those in the stage of childhood.
27.grammar: A plural noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The final -i is the genitive case: it typically links the word to a preceding preposition or to a noun before it ('… of …').
27.root: و-ل-د (w-l-d) — to give birth; offspring, child

28.meaning: A two-part connector: 'and that.' The 'wa' joins what precedes, and 'an' is the subordinating particle 'that,' which introduces a following verb-clause (often steering it into the subjunctive) — used to report or quote a command, statement, or purpose.
28.grammar: The conjunction wa- ('and') plus the particle an, a subordinator meaning 'that' which heads a clause and commonly puts a following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood (often expressing purpose, intention, or reported speech). It is a particle and does not itself take a case ending.

29.meaning: You stand / uphold — you rise to maintain something, carry it out with firmness and justice. The verb carries the sense of establishing and being upright in a duty.
29.grammar: Present-tense Form I verb, second-person masculine plural, in the subjunctive/jussive mood: the bare -ū ending (indicative -ūna minus the final -na) typically appears after particles meaning 'that', 'to', or 'so that'. It denotes the act of rising up to perform or maintain.
29.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise, establish, uphold

30.meaning: For the orphans — denoting benefit or concern directed toward orphans (children who have lost a father).
30.grammar: The preposition li- ('for, to') attached to the definite article al- and the broken-plural noun 'orphans'. The noun ends in a fixed -ā and does not take a visible case vowel; the li- conveys the sense of being 'for the sake of' or 'with regard to' them.
30.root: ي-ت-م (y-t-m) — orphanhood, being bereft of a parent

31.meaning: In/with justice and equity — 'qisṭ' is fair, balanced dealing: giving each their due in full measure, without wronging anyone.
31.grammar: A masculine noun ('justice, equity') governed by the preposition 'bi-' ('in/with') and made definite by 'al-' ('the'). The final -i ending is genitive, the case a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun in an 'of' relationship.
31.root: ق-س-ط (q-s-ṭ) — justice, equity, fair measure

32.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
32.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

33.meaning: A verb meaning 'you (plural) do/make/act' — referring to an action carried out by a group being addressed. Built on the very common root for doing or performing a deed, it is the standard word for engaging in or carrying out an act.
33.grammar: Present/imperfect verb, 2nd person masculine plural. The ta- prefix signals a 'you' subject; the -ū ending marks a plural ('you all'). The bare -ū without a final nūn (rather than -ūna) shows the verb is in the subjunctive/jussive mood, the form used after particles of negation, purpose, or condition.

34.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
34.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

35.meaning: Good / goodness; also 'better' or 'best'. A word for what is good, beneficial, or excellent — and, by its pattern, often 'better than'.
35.grammar: An indefinite noun/adjective ('good' or 'better'). The final -in (nunation with -i) marks it as indefinite ('some good / any good') and in the genitive case, typically after a preposition or in a possessive link.
35.root: خ-ي-ر (kh-y-r) — good, goodness, what is better

36.meaning: A two-part connector meaning 'so/then, indeed…'. It joins fa- ('so', 'then', marking a result or consequence) to inna, an emphatic particle that strongly affirms the statement that follows ('truly', 'verily').
36.grammar: fa- is a connective prefix signaling that what follows is a consequence or next step. inna is an emphatic particle that introduces a nominal sentence, puts its following noun in the accusative, and strengthens the assertion; it does not itself take a case ending.

37.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
37.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

38.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

38.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

39.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
39.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

40.meaning: All-Knowing; one possessing complete, perfect knowledge. As an intensive form it conveys knowledge that is total and unfailing, encompassing all things.
40.grammar: An intensive adjective ('all-knowing') on the faʿīl pattern, which stresses the quality to its fullest degree. The -an (tanwīn) joins the -a accusative ending — typical of a predicate or object — with the -n marking it indefinite.

1.meaning: And if — joins a clause and introduces a condition ('if such-and-such happens, then …').
1.grammar: The connective wa ('and') plus the conditional particle in ('if'). 'In' sets up a condition whose fulfilment triggers a result clause. Its normally silent final consonant here carries a helping vowel -i to ease pronunciation before the next word; this vowel is not a case ending.

2.meaning: A woman; an adult female human being.
2.grammar: A singular feminine noun marked indefinite ('a woman'). The word ends in a tā-marbūṭa (the -a/-at of امۡرَاَة), which belongs to the stem; the inflection added on top is the tanwīn -un. This combines the -u nominative case-ending — typically marking the doer or subject of a sentence — with the -n that signals indefiniteness. The opening alif carries a helping vowel for ease of pronunciation.
2.root: م-ر-أ (m-r-ʾ) — person; (feminine) woman

3.meaning: She feared / apprehended — a female subject became afraid of, or anticipated with dread, some outcome.
3.grammar: Past-tense Form I verb with the feminine-singular ending -t, marking 'she' as the one who did the action. The verb expresses a completed act of fearing or anticipating harm.

4.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
4.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

5.meaning: Her husband — a married woman's husband; the base word baʿl denotes the master of the household and, by usage, a spouse.
5.grammar: A masculine noun ('husband') carrying the attached possessive pronoun -hā ('her'). The -i before the pronoun is the genitive case, the case regularly used when a noun is possessed by an attached pronoun or follows a preposition.
5.root: ب-ع-ل (b-ʿ-l) — husband, master, lord of a household

6.meaning: Aversion and arrogance in conduct — a turning away in haughtiness or hostility, a breakdown of right behavior between spouses marked by disdain and rebelliousness.
6.grammar: A verbal noun (the abstract 'act of being averse/rebellious'), singular and masculine. The final -an (tanwīn fatḥa) is the accusative with indefiniteness, the case typically used for a direct object of a verb.
6.root: ن-ش-ز (n-sh-z) — to rise up against, be high/discordant; marital discord

7.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
7.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

8.meaning: A turning away / shunning — deliberately averting oneself from someone or something, withdrawing attention and presence.
8.grammar: A verbal noun of Form IV (the abstract 'act of turning away'), singular and masculine. The final -an (tanwīn fatḥa) is the accusative with indefiniteness, typically marking a direct object.
8.root: ع-ر-ض (ʿ-r-ḍ) — to turn aside, present/oppose; Form IV: to turn away from

9.meaning: A two-part word: the connective particle 'fa-' meaning 'so', 'then', or 'therefore' (drawing a consequence from what precedes), joined to 'lā', the particle of negation/prohibition. Together they convey 'so do not …' or 'so there is no …'.
9.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that links a clause to what came before and often signals a result or consequence. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a present-tense verb it commonly forms a prohibition ('do not …') or a simple negation ('not'). It carries no ending of its own.

10.meaning: Blame, sin, or fault — moral liability incurred by a wrong action; the sense of wrongdoing that counts against a person, or any leaning toward error.
10.grammar: A masculine noun. The final -a is the accusative case ending; this ending appears, among other uses, on the noun governed by a negating particle (as in the common construction 'there is no blame …').
10.root: ج-ن-ح (j-n-ḥ) — to incline, lean, tilt (toward wrong); hence fault/sin

11.meaning: A compound meaning 'upon the two of them,' 'on both of them,' 'against them two.' It places a duty, blame, or claim on exactly two parties.
11.grammar: The preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, against') takes the form ʿalay- before an attached pronoun, often conveying obligation or something weighing on someone. The suffix -himā is the dual pronoun 'the two of them'; the -i- vowel is the form the pronoun takes after this preposition.

12.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
12.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

13.meaning: They two set things right / reconcile — a pair brings about peace and repair between themselves, mending what was broken.
13.grammar: Present-tense Form IV verb in the dual ('the two of them'), masculine. The yu- prefix marks a third-person subject in general (he, it, they, or dual alike); the 'two of them' reading is carried by the dual ending -ā, not by the prefix. The form is in the subjunctive/jussive mood — the dual normally ends in -āni in the indicative, and the loss of that final -ni (typically after particles meaning 'that', 'to', or 'if') leaves the bare -ā. It denotes the act of two parties bringing about reconciliation.
13.root: ص-ل-ح (ṣ-l-ḥ) — to be sound/right; Form IV: to set right, reconcile

14.meaning: Between the two of them — the space or relation lying amid a pair.
14.grammar: An adverb of place, 'between,' fixed in the accusative as adverbs of place commonly are; the -a marks its adverbial function ('in the place that is between'). The attached -humā is the dual pronoun 'the two of them' (exactly two).
14.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction; that which lies between

15.meaning: A reconciliation / settlement — an act of making peace, an amicable arrangement that repairs a dispute.
15.grammar: A verbal noun (the 'act/result of making peace'), singular and masculine. The final -an (tanwīn fatḥa) is the accusative with indefiniteness, the case typically used for a direct object or an emphasizing complement.
15.root: ص-ل-ح (ṣ-l-ḥ) — to be sound/right, to reconcile

16.meaning: And the reconciliation / the settlement — making peace regarded as a definite, known thing.
16.grammar: The connective wa ('and') plus the noun 'reconciliation' with the definite article al- (its l assimilates into the 'sun letter' ṣ, hence ṣṣ). The final -u is the nominative case, typically marking the word as the subject or topic of its clause.
16.root: ص-ل-ح (ṣ-l-ḥ) — to be sound/right, to reconcile

17.meaning: 'Better / best; good' — an adjective of comparison meaning more good, preferable, or superior. It also serves broadly for 'goodness' and that which is good and beneficial.
17.grammar: A noun/adjective bearing the ending -un (nunation): the doubled-u 'n' sound marks the word as both indefinite ('a/an', no 'the') and nominative — the case used for the subject of a sentence or the predicate that describes it.
17.root: خ-ي-ر (kh-y-r) — good, goodness, that which is choice and beneficial

18.meaning: And it/she was made present — and (something feminine) was made to be present or summoned to attend; here the passive of 'to make present / bring to attendance'.
18.grammar: Past-tense passive Form IV verb (no doer named), with the feminine-singular ending -t marking a feminine subject as the one acted upon. Its normally vowelless final -t here takes a helping vowel -i before the following word. It conveys a completed action done to the subject.
18.root: ح-ض-ر (ḥ-ḍ-r) — to be present, to attend; Form IV: to make present, summon, cause to attend

19.meaning: The souls / the selves — the inner persons, the seats of life, desire and will within human beings. Nafs can mean soul, self, or one's very being.
19.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The final -u is the nominative case, typically marking the word as the subject or doer of its clause.
19.root: ن-ف-س (n-f-s) — soul, self, breath, living being

20.meaning: Stinginess / covetous greed — a tight-fisted withholding combined with grasping desire; an ingrained miserliness of the soul.
20.grammar: A noun with the definite article al- (its l assimilates into the 'sun letter' sh, hence shsh). The final -a is the accusative case, typically marking the word as the direct object of a verb.
20.root: ش-ح-ح (sh-ḥ-ḥ) — to be stingy, covetous, grasping

21.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
21.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

22.meaning: You do good / act well — you do what is excellent and beautiful, conduct yourselves with kindness and uprightness toward others.
22.grammar: Present-tense Form IV verb, second-person masculine plural, in the subjunctive/jussive mood: the bare -ū ending (indicative -ūna minus the final -na) typically follows particles meaning 'that', 'to', or 'if'. It denotes doing good in an excellent, beautiful manner.
22.root: ح-س-ن (ḥ-s-n) — to be good/beautiful; Form IV: to do well, act with excellence (iḥsān)

23.meaning: A verb meaning 'and you (plural) guard yourselves / are mindful (of Allah)' — to exercise God-conscious caution, shielding oneself from wrongdoing and divine displeasure. This is the verbal sense of taqwā.
23.grammar: A present-tense verb of Form VIII (ittaqā 'to be wary, God-conscious'), second-person masculine plural ('you all'). The first tā' is the second-person present prefix; the second, doubled tā' results from Form VIII's infixed -t- assimilating with the root's initial wāw (wtaqā → ttaqā). The bare -ū ending (without final -na) marks the subjunctive/jussive mood, used after certain particles or to express purpose ('that you may be mindful'). The prefixed wa- means 'and.'

24.meaning: A two-part connector meaning 'so/then, indeed…'. It joins fa- ('so', 'then', marking a result or consequence) to inna, an emphatic particle that strongly affirms the statement that follows ('truly', 'verily').
24.grammar: fa- is a connective prefix signaling that what follows is a consequence or next step. inna is an emphatic particle that introduces a nominal sentence, puts its following noun in the accusative, and strengthens the assertion; it does not itself take a case ending.

25.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
25.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

26.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

26.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.
26.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existence; to be

27.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
27.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

28.meaning: You (all) do / work / act — to carry out deeds or labor.
28.grammar: A present-tense verb (Form I). The 'ta-' prefix with the '-ūna' ending marks the second-person masculine plural ('you all'). The '-ūna' (with final 'n') is the indicative form, marking a plain ongoing or habitual statement.
28.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, work, act; deeds

29.meaning: Deeply aware, well-acquainted, fully informed — one whose knowledge penetrates the inner realities and hidden details of things. As a divine attribute of Allah, the All-Aware.
29.grammar: An adjective on the pattern faʿīl meaning 'thoroughly acquainted with inner realities.' The -an ending is the indefinite accusative: here it functions as a predicate complement ('… is all-aware') in clauses that take an accusative predicate, and the doubled nasal -n (tanwīn) shows it is indefinite.
29.root: خ-ب-ر (kh-b-r) — to know thoroughly, be acquainted with the inner truth of things; inner knowledge

1.meaning: A two-part expression combining 'and' with the particle of emphatic future negation. The core particle 'lan' negates a coming action with finality: 'will never / shall not (ever).' It denies that something will happen in the future, often with a tone of absolute impossibility.
1.grammar: A conjunction 'wa' ('and') joined to the negating particle 'lan'. 'Lan' governs a following present-tense verb, putting it into the subjunctive mood and turning its meaning into an emphatic denial of the future: 'it will never happen.'

2.meaning: A verb meaning 'you (plural) are able to' or 'you have the power/capacity to do' something. From a root conveying willing obedience and being able to comply, it expresses having the strength, means, or capability to carry out an action.
2.grammar: A present/future-tense verb. The ta- prefix together with the -ū ending marks a masculine plural 'you all' subject. The final -ū (in place of the indicative -ūna) shows the verb is in a dependent (subjunctive/jussive) mood, the form taken after certain particles such as 'not', 'that', or 'lest'.
2.root: ط-و-ع (ṭ-w-ʿ) — willing obedience, being able/compliant

3.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
3.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

4.meaning: You (plural) deal justly, act with fairness, or strike a balance — giving equal and even treatment.
4.grammar: A present-tense verb, Form I, from the root for 'justice/balance'. The ta- prefix with the -ū ending means 'you (plural) …'. The bare -ū (no final nūn) marks the subjunctive/jussive mood — used after particles such as 'if' or 'that'.

5.meaning: Between; in the midst of two things. An adverb of place marking the space separating or lying among parties or points.
5.grammar: An adverb of place ('between'). It always ends in -a and grammatically governs what follows it, putting the following noun(s) into the genitive 'of' relationship. It does not change to show 'the' or a case of its own; the fixed -a is simply how this word is formed.
5.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction, what lies between

6.meaning: 'The women' — the plural used for women/females collectively. (It serves as the plural of mar'a, 'woman.')
6.grammar: A plural noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending is genitive: it marks the word as following a preposition or standing in a possessive ('of …') relationship. The l of al- assimilates into the following n in pronunciation (a 'sun letter').
6.root: ن-س-و / ن-س-ء (n-s-w / n-s-') — women / womankind

7.meaning: 'and if' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the particle 'if'. This particular 'if' (law) introduces a hypothetical or contrary-to-fact condition: 'if (such-and-such had been the case)…', often implying it was not.
7.grammar: A conjunction plus a conditional particle. wa- means 'and'. law is a non-changing particle (no case ending) that sets up a supposition, typically answered by a clause beginning with la- ('… then certainly …').

8.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'you (plural) were eager, keen, or set on' something — to crave it intensely and strive after it. The root denotes avid desire and earnest striving.
8.grammar: A completed (past-tense) verb. The suffix -tum attaches to the verb to mark the doer as 'you all' (masculine plural). The action is presented as having already happened or been the case.

9.meaning: A two-part word: the connective particle 'fa-' meaning 'so', 'then', or 'therefore' (drawing a consequence from what precedes), joined to 'lā', the particle of negation/prohibition. Together they convey 'so do not …' or 'so there is no …'.
9.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that links a clause to what came before and often signals a result or consequence. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a present-tense verb it commonly forms a prohibition ('do not …') or a simple negation ('not'). It carries no ending of its own.

10.meaning: 'You (plural) incline, lean, swerve, or deviate' — to tilt away from a straight course toward one side.
10.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) verb addressed to a masculine plural 'you.' The dropped final -n (giving -ū rather than -ūna) shows the verb is in a dependent mood (subjunctive/jussive), the form used after certain particles such as those expressing purpose ('so that…'), negation, or condition.

11.meaning: All, every, the whole of — totality. When followed by a singular it means 'every (one)'; when followed by a definite plural or whole it means 'all of.'
11.grammar: A noun of totality, almost always joined to a following noun in the genitive ('every … / all of …'). The final -a is the accusative case, the form used when the word functions as an object of a verb.

12.meaning: A noun meaning 'the leaning,' 'the inclination,' or 'the tilting' — the act of bending or swerving toward one side, whether physically or in terms of favor and partiality. With the definite article, it denotes the inclination as such.
12.grammar: A definite noun ('the inclination'). The final -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ('... OF ...') or follows a preposition or oath particle.

13.meaning: A verb meaning 'so you (plural) leave it/her,' i.e., to abandon, forsake, or let something be — to set it aside untended. It is fronted by a connective 'so/and then' that links it as a consequence to what precedes.
13.grammar: A present-tense verb with a prefixed 'so/then.' The ta-...-ū frame marks a masculine plural 'you all' subject, and the attached -hā is a feminine singular object ('her/it'). The shortened ending -ū (rather than -ūna) signals a dependent mood, as occurs after a 'so/then' of consequence.

14.meaning: A descriptive phrase meaning 'like the suspended one' (feminine) — someone or something left hanging, neither released nor settled, kept in a state of dangling uncertainty. It combines 'like' with a passive participle of 'hanging/suspending.'
14.grammar: A passive participle ('the one being suspended,' feminine) made definite and prefixed with 'like/as.' The final -i is genitive, which is the case required after the prefixed particle 'like.' The feminine ending -a(t) shows the described one is feminine.

15.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
15.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

16.meaning: A verb meaning 'you (plural) set right, mend, or reconcile' — to put things into a sound, wholesome, or peaceful state, to repair what is broken or bring parties back to harmony.
16.grammar: A present/future-tense verb in the causative pattern ('to make sound, to reconcile'). The tu- prefix with the -ū ending marks a masculine plural 'you all' subject. The shortened -ū (instead of -ūna) indicates a dependent mood, as after a particle like 'that' or 'if.'
16.root: ص-ل-ح (ṣ-l-ḥ) — soundness, setting right, reconciliation

17.meaning: A verb meaning 'and you (plural) guard yourselves / are mindful (of Allah)' — to exercise God-conscious caution, shielding oneself from wrongdoing and divine displeasure. This is the verbal sense of taqwā.
17.grammar: A present-tense verb of Form VIII (ittaqā 'to be wary, God-conscious'), second-person masculine plural ('you all'). The first tā' is the second-person present prefix; the second, doubled tā' results from Form VIII's infixed -t- assimilating with the root's initial wāw (wtaqā → ttaqā). The bare -ū ending (without final -na) marks the subjunctive/jussive mood, used after certain particles or to express purpose ('that you may be mindful'). The prefixed wa- means 'and.'

18.meaning: A two-part connector meaning 'so/then, indeed…'. It joins fa- ('so', 'then', marking a result or consequence) to inna, an emphatic particle that strongly affirms the statement that follows ('truly', 'verily').
18.grammar: fa- is a connective prefix signaling that what follows is a consequence or next step. inna is an emphatic particle that introduces a nominal sentence, puts its following noun in the accusative, and strengthens the assertion; it does not itself take a case ending.

19.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
19.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.
19.root: — (proper name)

20.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

20.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

21.meaning: A word meaning 'much-forgiving' or 'ever-forgiving' — an intensive form describing one whose forgiveness is abundant and constant. It is one of the qualities of Allah.
21.grammar: An intensive adjective on the pattern faʿūl, conveying that the quality is great in degree and repeated. The ending -an is the accusative case with tanwīn (the indefinite 'n' sound), written with a supporting alif; it is the form an indefinite word takes when it is, for example, a predicate of certain verbs/particles or otherwise placed in the object position.

22.meaning: 'Most Merciful / deeply compassionate' — an intensive form of raḥima, denoting one full of mercy and tender compassion; a frequent description of Allah.
22.grammar: An intensive adjective on the fa'īl pattern, expressing a deep, abiding quality — abounding in mercy. The -an ending is the accusative case with indefinite (tanwīn) 'n,' often marking it as a predicate or as describing someone as 'most merciful.'

1.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
1.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

2.meaning: A verb meaning 'the two of them part, separate, or go their separate ways' — to split apart and become disunited. The intensive pattern stresses a thorough or mutual parting.
2.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ya- prefix plus the dual ending -ā marks the subject as 'the two of them' (masculine dual). The verb belongs to a reflexive/intensive pattern conveying mutual or thorough separation. The bare -ā ending (without final -ni) reflects a dependent mood, as after a conditional or 'if.'
2.root: ف-ر-ق (f-r-q) — separating, dividing, parting

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'He enriches' or 'He makes (someone) free of need, self-sufficient, well-off' — to bestow sufficiency so that one no longer depends on anyone else. It can also carry the sense 'it avails / suffices.'
3.grammar: A present/future-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('He / it'), in the causative pattern ('to make rich/sufficient'). The trimmed final weak letter (yielding -ni rather than -nī) marks the jussive/conditional mood, the form taken after particles like 'if' or in the answer to a condition.
3.root: غ-ن-ي (gh-n-y) — wealth, sufficiency, freedom from need

4.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
4.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

5.meaning: A word meaning 'each one,' 'every one,' or 'all (of them)' taken individually — it singles out every member of a group. Here it stands in the indefinite, pointing to 'each' as the object or focus.
5.grammar: A noun of totality ('each / every'). The ending -an is the accusative with indefinite (tanwīn) marking; the accusative typically flags the word as the object of a verb or otherwise governed, and the doubled-n sound (tanwīn) shows it is indefinite ('a/an, some').

6.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
6.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

7.meaning: A noun meaning 'ample means,' 'abundance,' 'capacity,' or 'plenty' — the breadth of resources or room one has, with an attached pronoun 'his' indicating that the abundance belongs to him. Built from a root meaning to be wide and spacious.
7.grammar: A noun carrying a possessive pronoun 'his.' The -i ending is genitive, the case used after a preposition or in a possessive link; the pronoun -hi ('his') is itself in the -i form that regularly follows a genitive base. The feminine -at marks the noun's form.

8.meaning: And he was / he became — a verb of being that places a subject in a past state or links it to a description in the past.
8.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'kāna' is a past-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular, meaning 'he was/became'; it commonly introduces a past condition and is typically followed by a noun describing the subject's state. The final -a marks completed past action by a single male.

10.meaning: An adjective meaning 'vast,' 'all-embracing,' 'boundless in capacity' — one who or that which encompasses widely, whether in knowledge, generosity, or reach. As a divine attribute it conveys limitless amplitude.
10.grammar: An active participle used as an adjective ('encompassing / vast'). The -an ending is the accusative with indefinite (tanwīn) marking, commonly used when the word serves as the predicate of a 'was/is' type statement or as an object; the doubled-n sound signals indefiniteness.

11.meaning: All-Wise; one possessing perfect wisdom, who places everything in its right place and decides with flawless judgement. As an intensive form it conveys wisdom that is complete and sound.
11.grammar: An intensive adjective ('all-wise') on the faʿīl pattern, stressing the quality to its fullest degree. The -an (tanwīn) combines the -a accusative ending — typical of a predicate or object — with the -n marking it indefinite.

1.meaning: A phrase meaning 'and to Allah (belongs)' — expressing ownership or rightful belonging to Allah; the lām conveys possession or entitlement.
1.grammar: The conjunction 'wa-' ('and') joined to the prepositional phrase 'lillāhi'. This phrase is the preposition 'li-' ('to/for', here showing possession) prefixed to the name 'Allah'; when 'li-' attaches, the connecting hamza and the first lām of the definite article are elided in writing, leaving a single written lām for the preposition followed by the doubled (shadda-bearing) lām of the name. 'Allah' takes the -i (genitive) ending required after a preposition.

2.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
2.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

3.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
3.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

4.meaning: The heavens / the skies — the plural of 'heaven', referring to the skies above and the celestial realms; the elevated expanse over the earth.
4.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun with the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the heavens') or follows a preposition. In the sound feminine plural, this -i form also covers what would be an object role.

5.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
5.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

6.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
6.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
6.root: — (particle)

7.meaning: The earth; the land, ground, or soil. The world we walk upon, as opposed to the sky.
7.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('... of the earth') or follows a preposition (as after 'in / on the earth').

8.meaning: "And indeed / and most certainly" — combines 'and' with the emphatic 'la-' and the particle 'qad'; before a past-tense verb 'qad' affirms that the action has definitely and already happened, reinforced into 'and indeed it surely did'.
8.grammar: The conjunction 'and' plus the emphatic 'la-' ('surely') plus the particle 'qad'. With a past-tense verb, 'qad' stresses that the act is real and completed ('has indeed happened'); together they form a strong oath-like affirmation. These are function words and are not inflected.

9.meaning: A verb meaning 'We enjoined, charged, or solemnly instructed' — to give a binding directive or earnest counsel, often as a charge laid upon someone. The intensive pattern conveys emphatic, weighty instruction.
9.grammar: A completed (past-tense) verb in an intensive pattern ('to charge emphatically'). The suffix -nā marks the doer as 'we.' The action is presented as already accomplished.

10.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
10.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

11.meaning: They were given / granted — the passive past tense of the verb 'to give/bring' (form IV of ʾ-t-y), where a plural group receives something without the giver being named.
11.grammar: Passive past tense. The internal vowelling (u-...-u) marks it as passive — the subject receives the action rather than doing it. The '-ū' ending means 'they', giving 'they were given' (the giver left unmentioned).
11.root: ا-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (form IV) to bring or give

12.meaning: The Book, the Scripture — a written revelation; the term for a divinely revealed text.
12.grammar: A definite noun ('the Book') with attached 'al-' ('the'). The final '-a' ending is the accusative case, typically marking the word as the direct object of a verb.
12.root: ك-ت-ب (k-t-b) — to write; a writing, book

13.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
13.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

14.meaning: 'before you,' 'prior to you' — an expression of precedence in time or place, here relating that precedence to 'you (plural).' The core word denotes the 'before' side, what comes earlier or in front.
14.grammar: An adverb of time/place ('before') joined to the pronoun '-kum' ('you, plural'). The '-i' ending is genitive: such words of place/time regularly take this case, especially after a preposition, and the attached pronoun completes the sense as 'before you.'

15.meaning: A phrase meaning 'and you (plural)' used as a standalone object — 'and you yourselves.' The base iyyā- is a special particle that carries an object pronoun when it cannot attach directly to a verb, here with 'you all.'
15.grammar: A connective 'and' joined to a detached object pronoun. The element iyyā- exists precisely to bear an object pronoun in isolation (when it cannot be suffixed onto a verb); the attached -kum means 'you all' (masculine plural) and functions as the object.

16.meaning: That — an explanatory particle introducing the content of a preceding statement or command, roughly 'namely that …' or 'to the effect that …'. It unpacks what was said or commanded.
16.grammar: An explanatory particle 'an' meaning 'that / namely,' used to spell out the substance of a foregoing verb of saying or commanding (so the words that follow explain it). Its base form ends in a vowel-less 'n'; the -i shown here is a helping vowel added only to ease pronunciation before a following consonant, not a case ending.

17.meaning: Be mindful and wary of — guard yourselves by placing a protective barrier between yourselves and harm or wrongdoing. This is the verb of taqwā: God-conscious caution that shields one from what is forbidden.
17.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to a group ('you all'). The -ū ending directs the order to a masculine plural 'you.' Built on a reflexive pattern (Form VIII), it conveys 'protect yourselves / be on guard.'

18.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
18.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

19.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
19.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

20.meaning: A verb meaning 'you (plural) disbelieve, reject, or deny' — to refuse faith and turn away ungratefully from the truth. The root also carries the sense of covering over or being ungrateful for what one has received.
20.grammar: A present/future-tense verb. The ta- prefix with the -ū ending marks a masculine plural 'you all' subject. The shortened -ū (rather than -ūna) signals a dependent mood (subjunctive/jussive), as after particles like 'that,' 'lest,' or a negative command.

21.meaning: A two-part connector meaning 'so/then, indeed…'. It joins fa- ('so', 'then', marking a result or consequence) to inna, an emphatic particle that strongly affirms the statement that follows ('truly', 'verily').
21.grammar: fa- is a connective prefix signaling that what follows is a consequence or next step. inna is an emphatic particle that introduces a nominal sentence, puts its following noun in the accusative, and strengthens the assertion; it does not itself take a case ending.

22.meaning: A two-part word: the preposition 'li-' meaning 'to', 'for', or 'belonging to', attached to the name 'Allah'. It conveys 'to Allah' or 'for Allah'.
22.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('to/for') pulls the following noun into the genitive case, which is why 'Allah' ends in '-i' (llāhi). The '-i' ending is the regular result of a noun governed by a preposition.

31.meaning: Rich / self-sufficient / free of need — one who has ample means and is not dependent on others; needing nothing from anyone.
31.grammar: An adjective of the intensive 'fa'īl' pattern (denoting a firmly established quality). The -an ending (accusative with nunation) commonly marks it as a predicate after certain verbs ('to be …') or as a description. The doubled-n sound signals indefiniteness ('a …').
31.root: غ-ن-ي (gh-n-y) — sufficiency, freedom from need, wealth

32.meaning: An adjective meaning 'praiseworthy,' 'ever-praised,' or 'worthy of all praise' — one who deserves commendation in every respect. As a divine attribute it denotes Allah as intrinsically and perpetually praised.
32.grammar: An intensive adjective ('most praiseworthy'). The -an ending is the accusative with indefinite (tanwīn) marking, the form typically used as the predicate of a 'was/is' statement or as an object; the doubled-n sound marks indefiniteness.

8.meaning: 'And He suffices / is enough' — to be sufficient, adequate, and fully enough so that nothing more is needed. It conveys complete adequacy, often used to affirm that Allah alone is enough.
8.grammar: The connective wa- ('and') prefixed to a 3rd-person masculine singular perfect (past-tense) verb (Form I) whose final weak root letter (the yāʾ) appears as a long -ā. It states a completed yet timeless fact — 'and He is sufficient' — the kind of perfect form used for an enduring truth.
8.root: ك-ف-ي (k-f-y) — to suffice, be enough, be adequate; to spare someone need of anything else

9.meaning: A phrase 'in Allah / by Allah', combining the preposition 'with/in/by' and the divine name Allah, the proper name of the One God.
9.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with, by means of') prefixed to the divine name Allah. A preposition always forces the following noun into the genitive case, which is why Allah here ends in -i. With verbs of believing, bi- conveys the object of faith — to believe IN.
9.root: — (Allah is the proper name of God and is not derived from a triliteral root in the usual sense)

10.meaning: A trustee, guardian, or disposer of affairs — one to whom matters are committed and who is relied upon to manage and protect them.
10.grammar: A noun on the intensive pattern faʿīl ('one who is relied upon'). The '-an' ending (with tanwīn) marks the indefinite accusative case: it commonly signals the object of a verb, or the role/capacity in which something serves ('as a …').
10.root: و-ك-ل (w-k-l) — entrusting, reliance, appointing someone to manage one's affairs

1.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
1.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

2.meaning: A verb meaning 'He wills, wishes, or so chooses' — to want and intend something by sovereign decision. The root denotes willing and desiring as an act of the will.
2.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('He'). This is a hollow verb (the weak letter sits in the middle of the root, with hamza as the strong final radical). In the jussive/conditional mood the medial long vowel is shortened (giving 'yashaʾ' rather than 'yashāʾ') — the form taken after 'if' or in a conditional clause.
2.root: ش-ي-أ (sh-y-ʾ) — willing, wishing, intending

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'He takes you (plural) away,' 'He causes you to depart,' or 'He does away with you' — to remove or make something go. It carries an attached object 'you all.'
3.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('He'), in the causative pattern ('to make go / take away'), with the attached object -kum ('you all'). The unvowelled final stem consonant marks the jussive/conditional mood, as in the answer to an 'if.'

4.meaning: A vocative word used in addressing people, equivalent to 'O...!' It is part of the standard formula for calling out to someone, drawing their attention before an address.
4.grammar: A vocative particle-complex used to call out ('O...'). It introduces the one being addressed and is typically followed by the noun naming them. It is a fixed address form rather than an inflected noun expressing case.

5.meaning: 'The people / mankind' — human beings collectively, people in general, humanity.
5.grammar: A collective noun with the definite article al- ('the'); the article's 'l' assimilates into the following 'n' (al-nās → an-nās). The -u ending marks the nominative case — the case used for the subject of a sentence or the basic naming form of a noun.
5.root: ن-و-س / أ-ن-س (n-w-s / ʾ-n-s) — humankind, people, sociability

6.meaning: A verb meaning 'and He brings, comes with, or produces' — to come bearing something, hence to bring it forth. It joins to what precedes with a connective 'and.'
6.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('He'), prefixed with 'and.' The final weak letter is trimmed, marking the jussive/conditional mood — the form taken in the answer to a condition or after 'if.'
6.root: أ-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — coming, arriving, bringing

7.meaning: A phrase meaning 'with others' or 'with other ones' (masculine plural) — 'others' being people or things distinct from those already mentioned. It is governed by an attached preposition 'with/by.'
7.grammar: A noun 'others' (masculine plural) governed by the preposition 'with.' The ending -īna is the genitive/accusative form of the sound masculine plural; here it is genitive because it follows the preposition 'with' (the case required after a preposition).

So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

10.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
10.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

11.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
11.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

12.meaning: An adjective meaning 'all-powerful,' 'fully capable,' 'one who has complete power to do anything.' As a divine attribute it denotes Allah's absolute and unrestricted ability over all things.
12.grammar: An intensive adjective ('most capable, all-powerful'). The -an ending is the accusative with indefinite (tanwīn) marking, typically used as the predicate of a 'was/is' statement or as an object; the doubled-n sound shows indefiniteness.

1.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
1.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

2.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

2.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.
2.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existence; to be

3.meaning: He/it wills, wants, intends, desires — to seek or aim at something purposefully.
3.grammar: A present-tense (form IV) verb, third-person masculine singular ('he wills/wants'). The ya- prefix marks 'he', and the final -u is the indicative ending, signalling an ongoing or habitual action ('does / is doing').
3.root: ر-و-د (r-w-d) — to seek, to want; (form IV) to will/intend

4.meaning: 'The reward / recompense' — that which is given back in return for deeds, especially good return or requital.
4.grammar: A noun in the accusative case, shown by the -a ending without nunation — the accusative typically marks the object of a verb (the thing wanted, given, etc.). The bare -a (not -an) indicates that the noun is joined to a following word in a possessive ('the reward OF …') construction. The pattern denotes the recompense for action.

5.meaning: 'The nearer (life) / this world' — literally 'the nearest/lowest,' a name for the present worldly life as opposed to the Hereafter.
5.grammar: The definite article al- with dunyā, a feminine superlative/elative adjective ('the nearest, the lowest') used as a name for the present world. Its ending (alif maqṣūra) is invariable — it does not change for case — and it commonly describes 'the [worldly] life.'
5.root: د-ن-و (d-n-w) — nearness, being close or low; hence the 'near' present world

6.meaning: 'So/then with… ' or 'in the presence of' — a word denoting being beside, at, or in the keeping of someone, often used of what Allah has in store.
6.grammar: A connecting prefix 'fa' ('so/then') joined to the location-word ʿinda ('with, at, in the presence of'). ʿinda always governs a following noun in the genitive, expressing whose possession or presence the thing is in.
6.root: — (ʿinda is a particle of place/possession; no triliteral root sense)

7.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
7.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

8.meaning: A noun meaning 'reward,' 'recompense,' or 'requital' — the return or repayment given for one's deeds. The root conveys returning something or giving back in kind.
8.grammar: A noun ('reward'). The final -u ending is nominative, the case that typically marks the subject of a sentence or the thing being identified (the 'doer' or the topic), as opposed to an object.

9.meaning: 'The nearer (life) / this world' — literally 'the nearest/lowest,' a name for the present worldly life as opposed to the Hereafter.
9.grammar: The definite article al- with dunyā, a feminine superlative/elative adjective ('the nearest, the lowest') used as a name for the present world. Its ending (alif maqṣūra) is invariable — it does not change for case — and it commonly describes 'the [worldly] life.'
9.root: د-ن-و (d-n-w) — nearness, being close or low; hence the 'near' present world

10.meaning: And the Hereafter / the final, lasting life — the world to come after death, contrasted with the present worldly life.
10.grammar: The prefix wa- means 'and' and al- means 'the'. The stem is a feminine adjective used as a noun, 'the Last (abode/life)', i.e. the Hereafter. The final -i is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun or follows a preposition or oath particle.
10.root: أ-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — being last, coming after, the end

11.meaning: And he was / he became — a verb of being that places a subject in a past state or links it to a description in the past.
11.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'kāna' is a past-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular, meaning 'he was/became'; it commonly introduces a past condition and is typically followed by a noun describing the subject's state. The final -a marks completed past action by a single male.

12.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
12.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

13.meaning: All-Hearing — one who hears fully and perfectly. This is an intensive adjective (faʿīl pattern) conveying that hearing is a permanent, all-encompassing attribute, not a single act of hearing.
13.grammar: An indefinite noun/adjective on the intensive faʿīl pattern. The final -an (tanwīn fatḥah) marks the accusative case, the form a word typically takes as the object of a verb or as a predicate after certain particles; the -n also signals that it is indefinite ('a hearer / hearing').

14.meaning: An adjective meaning 'all-seeing,' 'ever-watchful,' 'one who sees and perceives clearly.' As a divine attribute it denotes Allah's perfect sight and full awareness of all that occurs.
14.grammar: An intensive adjective ('all-seeing'). The -an ending is the accusative with indefinite (tanwīn) marking, the form commonly used as the predicate of a 'was/is' statement or as an object; the doubled-n sound marks indefiniteness.

1.meaning: 'O…!' — a compound vocative expression used to call out and summon an audience before addressing them. It fuses the call-particle 'yā' ('O') with a noun that means 'the one(s) addressed,' yielding an emphatic 'O you…!' that introduces direct address.
1.grammar: A vocative (calling) construction. 'Yā' is the particle for calling out; 'ayyu' carries a nominative '-u' as the one being summoned; 'hā' is an attention-drawing particle. Together they function as 'O you…!,' setting up the noun of address that follows.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
3.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

4.meaning: Be! Become! A command to exist as, or to enter into, whatever is then described.
4.grammar: An imperative (command) verb from the verb 'to be / to become', addressed to a group. The long -ū ending (و followed by a silent alif) marks the command as directed at 'you all' (masculine plural). As a command it carries no case ending of its own.
4.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to become, to come into existence

5.meaning: A noun/adjective meaning 'those who stand firm in upholding (something),' 'maintainers,' 'guardians who see to a matter steadfastly' — people who consistently take charge of and sustain a responsibility. The intensive pattern stresses persistent, diligent upholding.
5.grammar: An intensive noun ('persistent upholders / maintainers,' masculine plural). The ending -īna is the accusative/genitive form of the sound masculine plural; this form serves as the object of a verb, the predicate of certain verbs, or the object of a preposition (as opposed to the -ūna subject form).

6.meaning: In/with justice and equity — 'qisṭ' is fair, balanced dealing: giving each their due in full measure, without wronging anyone.
6.grammar: A masculine noun ('justice, equity') governed by the preposition 'bi-' ('in/with') and made definite by 'al-' ('the'). The final -i ending is genitive, the case a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun in an 'of' relationship.
6.root: ق-س-ط (q-s-ṭ) — justice, equity, fair measure

7.meaning: Witnesses — those present who observe and can testify to what they saw; can also carry the sense of those who bear witness. Plural.
7.grammar: A broken plural on the fuʿalāʾ (فُعَلَاء) pattern, which is a diptote: it takes the -a ending for BOTH the accusative and the genitive and never takes tanwīn (the final 'n'). Because of this, the -a alone does not tell you the case — the word could be a direct object (accusative) or governed by a preposition ('of/among', genitive). Only when made definite or put into construct would it take the ordinary -i in the genitive.
7.root: ش-ه-د (sh-h-d) — to witness, observe, testify, be present

8.meaning: A two-part word: the preposition 'li-' meaning 'to', 'for', or 'belonging to', attached to the name 'Allah'. It conveys 'to Allah' or 'for Allah'.
8.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('to/for') pulls the following noun into the genitive case, which is why 'Allah' ends in '-i' (llāhi). The '-i' ending is the regular result of a noun governed by a preposition.

9.meaning: 'and if' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the particle 'if'. This particular 'if' (law) introduces a hypothetical or contrary-to-fact condition: 'if (such-and-such had been the case)…', often implying it was not.
9.grammar: A conjunction plus a conditional particle. wa- means 'and'. law is a non-changing particle (no case ending) that sets up a supposition, typically answered by a clause beginning with la- ('… then certainly …').

10.meaning: A preposition meaning 'on, upon, over,' and by extension 'against' or 'incumbent upon.' It can mark something resting on top of, an obligation laid on someone, or being set over/above something.
10.grammar: An indeclinable preposition (its form never changes). It governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case, and conveys location 'on/upon,' or figuratively duty or opposition ('against').

11.meaning: 'Yourselves' — literally 'your own selves/souls.' Anfus is the plural of nafs ('self, soul, person'); with the attached pronoun it expresses the reflexive 'your own selves.'
11.grammar: A plural noun ('selves') with an attached possessive pronoun -kum ('your,' masculine plural). The -i ending is genitive: the noun is governed by a preceding preposition or stands in a possessive ('of …') construction.

12.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative between two or more options, linking possibilities of which one applies.
12.grammar: A connecting particle meaning 'or'. Its base form is aw; the added -i is a 'helping' vowel given to the otherwise-silent final consonant to smooth the link to a following word that begins with a connecting (hamzat-waṣl) alif. It is not a case ending — particles do not take cases.

13.meaning: The two parents, i.e. the father and mother taken together as a pair. The dual form specifically means 'the two who gave rise to (a person)'.
13.grammar: A dual noun (referring to exactly two) carrying the definite article 'the'. The -ayni ending is the dual form in its accusative/genitive (oblique) state, used when the word is the object of a verb or follows a preposition; the matching subject form would be -āni.
13.root: و-ل-د (w-l-d) — to give birth, beget; offspring

14.meaning: "And the nearest ones" — the close relatives, those nearest in kinship. It joins "wa" (and) with the definite plural of "aqrab" (nearer/nearest), used as a noun for near kin.
14.grammar: The conjunction "wa-" (and) with a definite masculine sound plural. The "-īna" ending is the plural form in the genitive/accusative (oblique) case — the case used for governed nouns, after prepositions, or as objects.
14.root: ق-ر-ب (q-r-b) — to be near, draw close; nearness

15.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
15.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

16.meaning: He/it comes to be, becomes, or proves to be — a linking verb of being, asserting that a subject is or turns out to be in a certain state.
16.grammar: A present-tense verb of 'being', 3rd-person masculine singular ('he/it is/becomes'). It stands in the jussive mood, marked by sukūn on the final nūn (the weak middle letter of the root having dropped); this conditional form typically means 'if he should be …' or 'let it be …'.
16.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

17.meaning: Rich / self-sufficient / free of need — one who has ample means and is not dependent on others; needing nothing from anyone.
17.grammar: An adjective of the intensive 'fa'īl' pattern (denoting a firmly established quality). The -an ending (accusative with nunation) commonly marks it as a predicate after certain verbs ('to be …') or as a description. The doubled-n sound signals indefiniteness ('a …').
17.root: غ-ن-ي (gh-n-y) — sufficiency, freedom from need, wealth

18.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
18.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

19.meaning: 'Poor, needy, in want' — one who is destitute and lacks sufficient means, dependent on others. It denotes a person broken by poverty and need.
19.grammar: A singular masculine noun/adjective on the faʿīl pattern (often intensive: thoroughly poor). The ending -an (tanwīn fatḥa) is the indefinite accusative: it marks an indefinite noun ('a poor person') functioning as an object or predicate of a verb, or as a descriptive/circumstantial term. The final 'n' sound is nunation, signalling indefiniteness ('a…').
19.root: ف-ق-ر (f-q-r) — poverty, neediness, want; literally a notch or breaking of the spine, hence destitution

20.meaning: So Allah / then Allah; the connector 'so/then' joined to the proper name of the One True God, the sole Deity worthy of worship.
20.grammar: The connector fa- ('so, then, and so') joined to the divine name. The -u ending on the name is the nominative case, typically used when the noun is the subject of a sentence (the one doing the action) or what something is equated with.

21.meaning: More entitled, more deserving, closer in claim or priority. A comparative meaning 'worthier (of)' or 'having a stronger right (to)'.
21.grammar: An elative (comparative/superlative) adjective on the pattern afʿalu, expressing 'more X' or 'most X'. It is invariable in this spelling, ending in a long final ā, and is typically followed by 'than' or by the thing one has a claim to.

22.meaning: 'to/with the two of them' — a preposition joined to a pronoun referring to two people or things.
22.grammar: The preposition bi- ('with, by, to, in') attached to the dual pronoun -himā ('the two of them'). The form -himā (rather than -humā) appears because the preceding vowel i of bi causes the pronoun's vowel to harmonize to i.

23.meaning: A two-part word: the connective particle 'fa-' meaning 'so', 'then', or 'therefore' (drawing a consequence from what precedes), joined to 'lā', the particle of negation/prohibition. Together they convey 'so do not …' or 'so there is no …'.
23.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that links a clause to what came before and often signals a result or consequence. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a present-tense verb it commonly forms a prohibition ('do not …') or a simple negation ('not'). It carries no ending of its own.
