24.meaning: 'You (plural) follow' — a verb meaning to come after, pursue, take as a guide, or obey and imitate; addressed to a group.
24.grammar: A present-tense verb (Form VIII), second-person masculine plural ('you follow'). The ta- prefix marks the addressee 'you'; the -ū ending marks a masculine plural 'you all'. The dropped final nūn (here -ū rather than -ūna) signals that the verb is in a subjunctive/jussive mood, typical after particles of negation, prohibition, or purpose.
24.root: ت-ب-ع (t-b-ʿ) — to follow, come after, pursue

25.meaning: Whim, craving, the pull of personal desire; the inclination of the lower self toward what it wants, often contrasted with what is right or true.
25.grammar: A definite singular noun ('the desire'). It ends in a long ā written with a dagger-alif (a 'shortened' alif maqṣūra), so its case is not shown by a final vowel; the article al- marks it as definite.
25.root: ه-و-ي (h-w-y) — to incline, fall, crave; passion, whim

26.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
26.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'
26.root: — (particle; no root)

27.meaning: You (plural) deal justly, act with fairness, or strike a balance — giving equal and even treatment.
27.grammar: A present-tense verb, Form I, from the root for 'justice/balance'. The ta- prefix with the -ū ending means 'you (plural) …'. The bare -ū (no final nūn) marks the subjunctive/jussive mood — used after particles such as 'if' or 'that'.

28.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
28.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

29.meaning: You twist or distort (something) — especially to bend speech or testimony away from the truth, or to turn the tongue so as to misrepresent.
29.grammar: A present-tense verb addressed to a plural 'you' (the ta- prefix marks second person, and the long ū with the plural alif marks masculine plural). It is in a form (subjunctive/jussive) that drops the final -na, which is why it appears after particles such as 'if', 'that', or a negation.
29.root: ل-و-ي (l-w-y) — to twist, bend, turn; to distort

30.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
30.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

31.meaning: You turn away, decline, or hold back from something; to avert oneself and refuse to engage.
31.grammar: A present-tense Form IV verb addressed to a plural 'you'. The tu- prefix (with u, signalling the causative Form IV) marks second person, and the -ū ending marks masculine plural. The final -na has been dropped (subjunctive/jussive), so it characteristically follows 'if', 'that', or a negation.
31.root: ع-ر-ض (ʿ-r-ḍ) — width, presenting; turning aside, exposition

32.meaning: A two-part connector meaning 'so/then, indeed…'. It joins fa- ('so', 'then', marking a result or consequence) to inna, an emphatic particle that strongly affirms the statement that follows ('truly', 'verily').
32.grammar: fa- is a connective prefix signaling that what follows is a consequence or next step. inna is an emphatic particle that introduces a nominal sentence, puts its following noun in the accusative, and strengthens the assertion; it does not itself take a case ending.

33.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
33.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

34.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

34.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

35.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
35.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

36.meaning: You (all) do / work / act — to carry out deeds or labor.
36.grammar: A present-tense verb (Form I). The 'ta-' prefix with the '-ūna' ending marks the second-person masculine plural ('you all'). The '-ūna' (with final 'n') is the indicative form, marking a plain ongoing or habitual statement.
36.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, work, act; deeds

37.meaning: Deeply aware, well-acquainted, fully informed — one whose knowledge penetrates the inner realities and hidden details of things. As a divine attribute of Allah, the All-Aware.
37.grammar: An adjective on the pattern faʿīl meaning 'thoroughly acquainted with inner realities.' The -an ending is the indefinite accusative: here it functions as a predicate complement ('… is all-aware') in clauses that take an accusative predicate, and the doubled nasal -n (tanwīn) shows it is indefinite.
37.root: خ-ب-ر (kh-b-r) — to know thoroughly, be acquainted with the inner truth of things; inner knowledge

1.meaning: 'O…!' — a compound vocative expression used to call out and summon an audience before addressing them. It fuses the call-particle 'yā' ('O') with a noun that means 'the one(s) addressed,' yielding an emphatic 'O you…!' that introduces direct address.
1.grammar: A vocative (calling) construction. 'Yā' is the particle for calling out; 'ayyu' carries a nominative '-u' as the one being summoned; 'hā' is an attention-drawing particle. Together they function as 'O you…!,' setting up the noun of address that follows.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
3.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

4.meaning: 'Believe!' — a command to a group: have faith, trust, and affirm. Built on the verb meaning to attain security and to believe, it calls people to embrace faith.
4.grammar: A command (imperative) verb on the causative (Form IV) pattern, from the verb meaning 'to believe / to have faith'. The -ū ending directs the command to a second-person masculine plural audience, 'you all — believe!'.

5.meaning: A phrase 'in Allah / by Allah', combining the preposition 'with/in/by' and the divine name Allah, the proper name of the One God.
5.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with, by means of') prefixed to the divine name Allah. A preposition always forces the following noun into the genitive case, which is why Allah here ends in -i. With verbs of believing, bi- conveys the object of faith — to believe IN.
5.root: — (Allah is the proper name of God and is not derived from a triliteral root in the usual sense)

6.meaning: A phrase meaning 'and His Messenger' — referring to one who is sent, an envoy or apostle bearing a message, joined by 'and' and possessed by 'His.'
6.grammar: 'Messenger' joined by wa- ('and') and followed by the possessive pronoun -hi ('his'). The -i vowel before the pronoun is the genitive case, here because the word is linked in possession ('Messenger OF Him'); the pronoun takes the -hi form (with i-vowel) when it follows an i-sound.
6.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — sending, dispatching; a message or one who is sent

7.meaning: 'And the Book' — the Scripture, a written, recited revelation sent down from Allah. Joined by 'and'.
7.grammar: The connector wa ('and') plus the definite noun 'the Book', on the fiʿāl pattern often used for things acted upon (something written). The final -i is the genitive case, taken after a preposition or as the second term of a possessive construction.

8.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
8.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

9.meaning: A verb meaning 'he sent down / brought down', especially in stages or portions. The Form II shape adds intensity or gradualness to the basic 'descend', hence 'to send down piece by piece'.
9.grammar: Past-tense (perfect) verb, third-person masculine singular, Form II. The doubled middle letter marks the intensive/gradual sense; the final -a is the standard ending for a completed past-tense action done by 'he'.
9.root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — to descend, come down, send down

10.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
10.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

11.meaning: 'His Messenger' — a messenger or envoy, one sent with a message, here possessed by 'Him'.
11.grammar: A noun ('messenger') with the attached possessive pronoun -hi ('his'). The -i ending before the pronoun is genitive, typically signalling that the word follows a preposition or is the second term of a possessive phrase ('… of …'); the pronoun appears as -hi (rather than -hu) because of that preceding i vowel.
11.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — to send; a sending, message, messenger

12.meaning: 'And the Book' — the Scripture, a written, recited revelation sent down from Allah. Joined by 'and'.
12.grammar: The connector wa ('and') plus the definite noun 'the Book', on the fiʿāl pattern often used for things acted upon (something written). The final -i is the genitive case, taken after a preposition or as the second term of a possessive construction.

13.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
13.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

14.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'he sent down, he caused to descend, he revealed' — used especially of Allah sending down revelation, rain, or blessings from above.
14.grammar: A completed (past) action by a single masculine subject ('he'); the -a ending marks third-person masculine singular. The form IV (causative) pattern means 'to make something come down,' i.e., to send it down.

15.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
15.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

16.meaning: An adverb of time meaning 'before / beforehand / previously,' pointing to a moment or state that precedes something else in time. When used with the final vowel -u (qablu), it stands cut off from an explicit following noun, conveying 'before(hand)' or 'previously' in an absolute sense — the thing it is 'before' is understood rather than stated.
16.grammar: An adverb of time. The final -u ending here is the indeclinable (mabnī) form taken when the word is severed from a following genitive: rather than 'before X,' it means 'before(hand)' on its own, with the reference point left implicit.
16.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to come before, precede, be in front; to receive/accept

17.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
17.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

18.meaning: To disbelieve, to reject faith; to deny the truth and to be ungrateful, covering over and refusing what is true.
18.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it'). The final consonant carries no vowel (jussive form), an ending that typically appears after conditional or commanding particles and gives the sense 'whoever/if … disbelieves'.
18.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover over; to disbelieve, reject, be ungrateful

19.meaning: A phrase 'in Allah / by Allah', combining the preposition 'with/in/by' and the divine name Allah, the proper name of the One God.
19.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with, by means of') prefixed to the divine name Allah. A preposition always forces the following noun into the genitive case, which is why Allah here ends in -i. With verbs of believing, bi- conveys the object of faith — to believe IN.
19.root: — (Allah is the proper name of God and is not derived from a triliteral root in the usual sense)

20.meaning: "and His angels" — wa- joins it on; refers to the angels, and the attached -hi means 'His,' marking them as belonging to Allah.
20.grammar: A feminine plural noun ('angels') with an attached possessive pronoun. The -i vowel before the pronoun is the genitive (possessive/'of') case, and the suffix -hi means 'his/His'; the i-coloured form -hi (rather than -hu) is what naturally follows that -i ending.
20.root: ل-ء-ك / م-ل-ك (l-ʾ-k) — message, sending; an angel as a messenger

21.meaning: "and His books / scriptures" — wa- joins it on; the plural of 'book,' here in the sense of revealed scriptures, with -hi 'His' marking them as Allah's.
21.grammar: A plural noun ('books') with an attached possessive. The -i before the pronoun is the genitive (possessive/'of') case, and -hi means 'his/His'; the i-coloured -hi form is the one used after an -i vowel.

22.meaning: A combination 'and His messengers' — 'and' + 'messengers' + 'His'. Messengers are those sent by Allah to convey His revelation to humankind.
22.grammar: The prefix wa- is the connective 'and'. 'rusul' is the plural 'messengers'. The -i before the pronoun is genitive, used after prepositions or to show possession; with attached 'hi' ('His') it means 'His messengers'. The -hi ('His') indicates a single male/divine possessor.

23.meaning: "And the Day" — a stretch of time, a day; also used for the appointed Day of Judgement and Resurrection. The opening element is the conjunction 'and'.
23.grammar: A masculine singular noun with the definite article 'the' and the conjunction 'and'. The final -i is the genitive case ending: it typically signals that the word is linked to a preceding noun ('… of …') or governed by a preposition or oath particle.

24.meaning: An adjective meaning 'the last,' 'the latter,' or 'the final' — that which comes at the end of a sequence. It is the common counterpart to 'the first,' and is often used as a name for the world or life to come (the Hereafter, the Last Day), i.e. the ultimate end of all things.
24.grammar: An active-participle-type adjective on the pattern fāʿil. It carries the definite article 'al-' ('the'). The final -i is the genitive case, signaling that the word is governed by a preceding preposition or particle, or stands as the second term of a possessive link ('… of …'). It is masculine singular.
24.root: ء-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — to be last, to come after, to defer / postpone

25.meaning: A two-part connector: fa- means 'so', 'then', or 'and so', linking what follows as a result or consequence; qad before a past-tense verb intensifies it, conveying 'certainly', 'indeed', or 'already' — stressing that the action has truly and definitely occurred.
25.grammar: fa- is a connecting particle meaning 'so' or 'then', often marking a result. qad is a particle of emphasis; placed before a completed (past-tense) verb it affirms that the action has definitely or already happened. Neither part takes a case ending.

26.meaning: He strayed, lost the way, or went off course — to wander from the right path, whether literally or figuratively (to err, be misguided, or deviate from truth and guidance).
26.grammar: A past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he went astray'. The bare past-tense form with the -a ending signals a single male (or thing) as the doer of a completed action.
26.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to go astray, lose the way, err

27.meaning: straying / error — the state of being lost from the right path, wandering far from guidance and truth. A verbal noun naming the condition of going astray.
27.grammar: A verbal noun (maṣdar) on the faʿāl pattern, naming the act/state of straying. The final -an (tanwīn fatḥah) marks the accusative — often used for the object of a verb or as an absolute object reinforcing a verb ('to stray a [great] straying') — and the -n shows it is indefinite.
27.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to stray, get lost, err

28.meaning: Far, distant, remote — describing something at a great remove in space, time, or degree. As an adjective it qualifies a noun as 'far off, far-reaching'.
28.grammar: An adjective on the faʿīl pattern (often intensive: 'very far'). The -an ending (tanwīn) marks it indefinite and accusative — agreeing with an indefinite accusative noun it describes. The accusative is the case of objects and many complements; the tanwīn marks indefiniteness ('a far …').
28.root: ب-ع-د (b-ʿ-d) — distance, remoteness, being far

1.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
1.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
3.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

4.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
4.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

5.meaning: 'They disbelieved / rejected faith' — from a root meaning to cover over or conceal. To disbelieve in this sense is to cover up and refuse the truth, and also to be ungrateful, hiding or denying favours received.
5.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third person masculine plural: 'they disbelieved'. The completed action is built into the stem kafara ('he disbelieved'), and the -ū suffix (written وا) marks the doer as 'they' (masculine plural). The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention with no sound.
5.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to reject faith, be ungrateful

6.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
6.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

7.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
7.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

8.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
8.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

9.meaning: 'They disbelieved / rejected faith' — from a root meaning to cover over or conceal. To disbelieve in this sense is to cover up and refuse the truth, and also to be ungrateful, hiding or denying favours received.
9.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third person masculine plural: 'they disbelieved'. The completed action is built into the stem kafara ('he disbelieved'), and the -ū suffix (written وا) marks the doer as 'they' (masculine plural). The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention with no sound.
9.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to reject faith, be ungrateful

10.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
10.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

11.meaning: 'They increased / grew greater' — to become more in amount or degree. The eighth-form verb often carries the sense of adding to oneself or going further in something.
11.grammar: A past-tense verb (eighth form of 'zāda,' to increase, where the root's 'z' reshapes the form's 't' into a 'd' sound: izdāda). The stem iz'dād- carries the meaning; the separate -ū ending marks a completed action by a third-person masculine plural subject ('they').

12.meaning: Disbelief, rejection, or ingratitude — the active refusal to accept truth and faith, and the covering-over of what one knows to be true; in religious usage, denial of Allah and His message. Marked as an indefinite noun, 'a disbelief' or simply 'disbelief'.
12.grammar: A singular masculine noun in the indefinite accusative. The final '-an' (written with tanwīn fatḥa) typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as a specifying complement answering 'in what respect?', and signals that it is indefinite ('a/some disbelief').
12.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; hence to reject faith, to be ungrateful

13.meaning: The particle 'lam', a negating word used to push a verb into the past: it means 'did not' / 'has not'. Though it sits before a present-tense verb form, it negates the action as something that did not happen.
13.grammar: 'lam' is a negating particle that governs a following present-tense verb but gives it past meaning ('did not …'). It also puts that verb into the shortened (jussive) form. 'lam' itself carries no ending.

14.meaning: A core verb meaning 'to be' or 'to come to be / happen' — used to say that something exists, occurs, or is the case.
14.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it is/becomes'), in the jussive (command/conditional) mood. The base form is yakun with a silent final consonant; the -i here is a helping vowel added only to ease pronunciation before a following word that begins with a cluster.
14.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, exist, come to pass; being

15.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
15.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

16.meaning: 'so that He may forgive' — to forgive, to cover over and pardon a wrong so that it is not held against the person.
16.grammar: The purpose-particle li- ('so that, in order to') joined to a present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('He forgives'). Because of li-, the verb is subjunctive, shown by the final -a ending, which gives the sense of intended result: 'so that He may forgive'.
16.root: غ-ف-ر (gh-f-r) — to cover, shield; to forgive, pardon

17.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
17.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

18.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
18.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

19.meaning: 'so that He may guide them' — to guide, to show the way and lead someone rightly, here directed toward 'them'.
19.grammar: The purpose-particle li- ('so that') joined to a present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('He guides'), with the object pronoun -hum ('them') attached. Because of li-, the verb is subjunctive, shown by the -a ending on the stem (before the pronoun), giving the sense 'so that He may guide them'.
19.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — to guide, lead aright; guidance

20.meaning: A way, path, road, or means — a route to a destination, hence also a way or means of accomplishing something.
20.grammar: A singular noun. The '-an' ending is accusative and indefinite: the accusative case commonly marks the direct object of a verb, and the final 'n' sound marks it indefinite ('a way'). It denotes a path one travels or a means to an end.

1.meaning: Announce good news! Give glad tidings! A command to convey something joyful or hopeful to someone.
1.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to a single 'you', from an intensive Form II verb ('convey good news'). Its base imperative is bashshir with a silent final consonant; the -i shown here is a helping vowel added only to smooth pronunciation before a following word beginning with a consonant cluster.
1.root: ب-ش-ر (b-sh-r) — good news, glad tidings; skin (the face brightening)

2.meaning: the hypocrites — those who outwardly profess faith while inwardly concealing disbelief; people who present one face publicly and hide another within. From a root evoking a tunnel with two openings, suggesting a hidden way out.
2.grammar: A definite noun: al- means 'the'. 'Munāfiq' is an active participle of Form III ('one who behaves hypocritically'). The ending -īna marks the masculine sound plural in the oblique case (the form used for objects of verbs and after prepositions, i.e. accusative/genitive, as opposed to nominative -ūna).
2.root: ن-ف-ق (n-f-q) — tunnel/burrow with a hidden exit; hence hypocrisy

3.meaning: A two-part connector meaning 'because / by reason of the fact that'. It combines the preposition 'with/by' and anna ('that…'), together introducing a cause or explanation for what precedes.
3.grammar: The preposition bi- ('with/by') attached to the emphatic particle anna ('that…'). anna introduces and stresses a following statement and grammatically puts the noun after it into the accusative; the pairing as a whole signals 'because / due to the fact that'.

4.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
4.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

5.meaning: 'A punishment / torment.' A noun naming chastisement or painful suffering inflicted as a penalty.
5.grammar: A masculine noun. The -an ending marks it as indefinite ('a punishment') and in the accusative case — the form a noun takes as the object of a verb or as the thing being described/quantified.

6.meaning: An adjective meaning 'painful, agonizing, causing severe pain,' describing something that inflicts intense suffering.
6.grammar: An adjective in the intensive faʿīl pattern, which heightens the quality (deeply/intensely painful). The final -an (tanwīn fatḥa) marks it as indefinite ('a painful one') and in the accusative case — the case typically used for the object of a verb or for a describing word agreeing with such a noun.
6.root: أ-ل-م (ʾ-l-m) — pain, hurt, suffering

1.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
1.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

2.meaning: They take (for themselves), adopt, or choose something — to seize upon and make it one's own (e.g. taking allies, taking objects of worship).
2.grammar: A present-tense Form VIII verb, third-person masculine plural ('they take for themselves'). The -ūna ending marks 'they' (masculine plural) and the indicative mood — i.e. a plain statement of ongoing or habitual action, not governed by 'if' or 'that'.
2.root: أ-خ-ذ (ʾ-kh-dh) — to take, seize, grasp

3.meaning: The disbelievers / the ungrateful — those who reject faith and cover over the truth; the word also carries the sense of covering up or being ungrateful for what one has been given.
3.grammar: 'al-' is 'the'. The stem is an active participle ('one who disbelieves/is ungrateful') made plural for masculine people. The -īna ending is the accusative/genitive form of the sound masculine plural: it marks the word as an object of a verb or as governed by a preposition, as opposed to the subject form -ūna.
3.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; ingratitude, disbelief

4.meaning: Allies, protectors, intimate friends — those taken as close supporters, patrons, or guardians, with whom one stands in mutual loyalty (plural of walī).
4.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural of 'walī.' Being a 'diptote' (a noun that resists the usual full set of endings), it takes a single final '-a' here for the accusative case, which commonly marks the direct object of a verb or signals 'as / being' something — and notably without the usual '-n' (no nunation).

5.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
5.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

6.meaning: A noun used to mean 'besides', 'other than', 'apart from', or 'short of'. It points to something or someone set apart from, or lower/lesser than, a named party. Often used in the phrase 'besides Allah'.
6.grammar: 'dūn' functions as an adverb-like noun of place/relation. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, which appears because it follows a preposition (such as 'min', 'from') and because it links to a following noun ('other than …'). It commonly heads the construction 'besides/other than [someone]'.
6.root: د-و-ن (d-w-n) — to be low/beneath, to fall short; hence 'below, other than, besides'

7.meaning: A plural noun meaning 'the believers' — those who have faith, who inwardly trust and affirm. The Form IV participle denotes one who brings about belief and security within.
7.grammar: A definite plural active participle of Form IV (āmana 'to believe'). The -īna ending marks a sound masculine plural in the accusative/genitive (object or oblique) state. The prefixed mu- marks it as a Form IV participle ('one who has/gives faith').

8.meaning: 'Do they seek / are they seeking?' — to seek, pursue, or strive after something with effort and desire. The opening alif turns it into a question.
8.grammar: The question-particle a- ('do…?') prefixed to a present-tense Form VIII verb, third-person masculine plural ('they seek'). The -ūna ending marks 'they' (masculine plural) and the indicative mood (a plain statement here turned into a yes/no question by the opening a-).
8.root: ب-غ-ي (b-gh-y) — to seek, desire, strive after

9.meaning: 'in their possession / with them / on their side' — a word marking presence-at or being-with, here belonging to 'them'.

parts.en: at / with / in the presence of

9.grammar: The locational word ʿinda ('at, with, in the keeping of') with the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). Its final -a is the fixed accusative form normal for this adverb of place. The pronoun is written -humu (with an extra u) to ease linking onto a following word that begins with the definite article.
9.root: ع-ن-د (ʿ-n-d) — at, near, in the presence/keeping of

10.meaning: Might, honour, and unassailable strength; the quality of being mighty and held in high esteem, beyond reach of humiliation.
10.grammar: A definite singular noun ('the might/honour'). The -ta ending (the t of the feminine ending plus an -a) is accusative, the form a noun takes when it is the direct object of a verb or otherwise governed into that case.
10.root: ع-ز-ز (ʿ-z-z) — might, strength, dearness, being unassailable

11.meaning: A two-part connector meaning 'so/then, indeed…'. It joins fa- ('so', 'then', marking a result or consequence) to inna, an emphatic particle that strongly affirms the statement that follows ('truly', 'verily').
11.grammar: fa- is a connective prefix signaling that what follows is a consequence or next step. inna is an emphatic particle that introduces a nominal sentence, puts its following noun in the accusative, and strengthens the assertion; it does not itself take a case ending.

12.meaning: Might, honour, and unassailable strength; the quality of being mighty and held in high esteem, beyond reach of humiliation.
12.grammar: A definite singular noun ('the might/honour'). The -ta ending (the t of the feminine ending plus an -a) is accusative, the form a noun takes when it is the direct object of a verb or otherwise governed into that case.
12.root: ع-ز-ز (ʿ-z-z) — might, strength, dearness, being unassailable

13.meaning: A two-part word: the preposition 'li-' meaning 'to', 'for', or 'belonging to', attached to the name 'Allah'. It conveys 'to Allah' or 'for Allah'.
13.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('to/for') pulls the following noun into the genitive case, which is why 'Allah' ends in '-i' (llāhi). The '-i' ending is the regular result of a noun governed by a preposition.

14.meaning: A word meaning 'all together', 'all of them', or 'the whole lot' — emphasising that no one and nothing is left out of a group.
14.grammar: A noun meaning 'all/entirety' carrying the -an ending: accusative case with tanwīn (the indefinite '-n'). This accusative form is typical of a word that comes alongside another to specify it as 'all of them, every one', describing the manner or extent.

1.meaning: 'And indeed / while already' — the word 'wa' ('and, while') joined to 'qad', a particle that, before a past-tense verb, stresses that the action has certainly and already happened.
1.grammar: A connective 'wa' ('and', or circumstantial 'while') plus the particle 'qad'. With a past-tense verb, 'qad' emphasizes completion and certainty ('has indeed already…'); with a present-tense verb it can mean 'sometimes' or 'may'.

2.meaning: A verb meaning 'he sent down / brought down', especially in stages or portions. The Form II shape adds intensity or gradualness to the basic 'descend', hence 'to send down piece by piece'.
2.grammar: Past-tense (perfect) verb, third-person masculine singular, Form II. The doubled middle letter marks the intensive/gradual sense; the final -a is the standard ending for a completed past-tense action done by 'he'.
2.root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — to descend, come down, send down

3.meaning: 'Upon you (all)' — the preposition 'upon/on/over' joined to the plural 'you,' indicating something resting on or directed at a group.
3.grammar: The preposition 'ʿalā' ('upon/on/over') in its joined form 'ʿalay-' plus the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you all,' masculine plural). It marks the group as the recipients or target of whatever is laid 'upon' them.

4.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
4.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

5.meaning: 'The Book / the Scripture' — a written record or revealed scripture; literally that which is written.
5.grammar: The definite article al- with the noun kitāb ('book, scripture'), itself a verbal noun from 'to write.' The -i ending is genitive, typically marking the word as following a preposition or standing in an 'of' relationship to a preceding noun.

6.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
6.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'
6.root: — (particle; no root)

7.meaning: 'When' — a particle introducing a time or circumstance, generally pointing to something expected or definite to come ('when/whenever it happens'). It sets up a condition or moment whose outcome then follows.
7.grammar: An indeclinable adverb/particle of time; it has no case ending and never changes form. It typically introduces a clause about a future or recurring event ('when …'), and is normally followed by a verb describing what takes place.

8.meaning: You heard / you listened — to perceive by the ear; past-tense action attributed to a group 'you'.
8.grammar: A past-tense verb with the subject-ending -tum, meaning 'you (plural) did' the action — a completed act of hearing performed by a group being addressed.
8.root: س-م-ع (s-m-ʿ) — to hear, listen, perceive by ear

9.meaning: Signs, tokens, or evident proofs; also used for the discrete verses of revelation. An āya is a marker that points beyond itself to a deeper truth or to its Author.
9.grammar: A feminine plural noun ('signs/verses'). The sound-feminine plural takes -i in both the genitive and accusative; the -i ending here links it to a following noun ('… of …') or marks it as the object of a verb or preposition.

10.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
10.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

11.meaning: It is disbelieved in / rejected / denied — to be the object of rejection and ingratitude; said of something that people refuse to believe in.
11.grammar: A present-tense passive verb, third-person masculine singular ('it is being disbelieved in / rejected'). The u-vowel on the prefix marks the passive ('is being done'), and the final -u marks the indicative mood — a plain statement of an ongoing action.
11.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover up, reject, be ungrateful; disbelief

12.meaning: with it / by it — a preposition meaning 'with' or 'by means of' joined to a pronoun referring to a single feminine (or grammatically feminine) thing.
12.grammar: The bi- prefix is a preposition meaning 'with', 'by', or 'by means of'. The attached -hā is an object pronoun meaning 'it' or 'her', referring to something feminine in gender. Together they mean 'with it' or 'by means of it'.

13.meaning: 'and it is mocked at / ridiculed' — to be made the object of scorn and derision; said of something that people treat with mockery.
13.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') with a present-tense passive Form X verb, third-person masculine singular ('it is being mocked at'). The u-vowel on the prefix marks the passive, and the final -u marks the indicative mood (a plain statement of an ongoing action).

14.meaning: with it / by it — a preposition meaning 'with' or 'by means of' joined to a pronoun referring to a single feminine (or grammatically feminine) thing.
14.grammar: The bi- prefix is a preposition meaning 'with', 'by', or 'by means of'. The attached -hā is an object pronoun meaning 'it' or 'her', referring to something feminine in gender. Together they mean 'with it' or 'by means of it'.

15.meaning: A two-part word: the connective particle 'fa-' meaning 'so', 'then', or 'therefore' (drawing a consequence from what precedes), joined to 'lā', the particle of negation/prohibition. Together they convey 'so do not …' or 'so there is no …'.
15.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that links a clause to what came before and often signals a result or consequence. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a present-tense verb it commonly forms a prohibition ('do not …') or a simple negation ('not'). It carries no ending of its own.

16.meaning: You sit, stay seated, or remain (not rising or going forward) — also figuratively to hold back and keep company in a setting.
16.grammar: A present-tense verb addressed to a plural 'you' ('you sit/remain'). The ta- prefix marks second person and the -ū ending marks masculine plural. The final -na has been dropped (subjunctive/jussive), so it typically follows 'until', 'that', a negation, or 'if'.
16.root: ق-ع-د (q-ʿ-d) — to sit, stay put, remain behind

17.meaning: With them, in their company or possession — expressing accompaniment or togetherness. Maʿa denotes being alongside or in the presence of someone or something.
17.grammar: An adverb of accompaniment ('with') fixed in the -a form, joined to the pronoun -hum ('them'). Together they express that something is in the company or possession of a group.

18.meaning: 'Until / up to the point that; so that' — a particle marking a limit or goal. It expresses the end-point reached ('until') or the purpose aimed at ('so that, in order that').
18.grammar: A particle indicating a goal or limit. When followed by a present-tense verb it places that verb in the subjunctive mood (clipping its ending to -a), conveying 'until / so that' something comes about. Ḥattā itself is invariable.

19.meaning: They plunge into or engage in (idle or vain talk); to wade into a discourse, often one of mockery or falsehood.
19.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine plural ('they plunge in / engage'). The ya- prefix marks third person and the -ū ending marks masculine plural. The final -na has been dropped (subjunctive/jussive), so it characteristically follows 'until', 'that', or a negation.
19.root: خ-و-ض (kh-w-ḍ) — to wade into water; to plunge into talk or affairs

20.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
20.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

21.meaning: Speech, talk, or an account; a piece of discourse or report — that which is newly spoken or related.
21.grammar: An indefinite singular noun ('a talk / a report'). The -in ending is genitive with nunation (the -n marking 'a/an'), the form taken after a preposition or as the second term of a possessive phrase ('… of …').
21.root: ح-د-ث (ḥ-d-th) — to be new, to happen; to relate, to speak

22.meaning: 'other than it / besides it' — 'other than', 'different from', expressing distinctness from something else; here paired with 'it'.
22.grammar: The noun ghayr ('other than, something different') with the attached pronoun -hi ('it/him'). The -i ending before the pronoun is genitive, signalling that the word follows a preposition or stands as the second term of a possessive phrase; the pronoun reads -hi (not -hu) because of that preceding i vowel.

23.meaning: 'Indeed you (plural)' — the emphatic particle inna ('truly, indeed, surely'), which strongly affirms and stresses the statement that follows, fused with the attached pronoun 'you (all)'. Inna has no single English word; it functions to underline certainty.
23.grammar: Inna is an emphasising particle that introduces and strengthens a sentence; grammatically it places the following noun or pronoun in the accusative-like role of its 'subject'. The attached -kum is the masculine plural object/possessive pronoun 'you (all)'. Together: 'indeed you (all)…'.

24.meaning: In that case / then — a response particle signaling that what follows is the consequence of a just-stated condition or supposition ('if so, then…').
24.grammar: A response/consequence particle, not a noun or verb. The -an ending is a fixed part of the word (written with a final alif), not a live grammatical case. It introduces the result side of a hypothetical ('then you would…').

25.meaning: 'their like / the same as them' — a likeness, equal, or counterpart; one resembling another. Here it means 'similar to them'.
25.grammar: The noun mithl ('like, equal, counterpart') with the attached pronoun -hum ('them/their'). The -u ending before the pronoun is nominative, the form a noun takes when it serves as the subject of a sentence or as a predicate ('is …').

26.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
26.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

27.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
27.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

28.meaning: Gatherer; the one who gathers, assembles, and brings together what was scattered. An active participle — a noun describing the doer of the act of gathering.
28.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer' noun) meaning 'one who gathers'. The final -u is the nominative ending, typically marking a subject or predicate. Such a participle can also link to a following noun in a possessive-like construction ('gatherer of …'), in which case it conveys an act about to happen or characteristically done.
28.root: ج-م-ع (j-m-ʿ) — to gather, collect, bring together

29.meaning: the hypocrites — those who outwardly profess faith while inwardly concealing disbelief; people who present one face publicly and hide another within. From a root evoking a tunnel with two openings, suggesting a hidden way out.
29.grammar: A definite noun: al- means 'the'. 'Munāfiq' is an active participle of Form III ('one who behaves hypocritically'). The ending -īna marks the masculine sound plural in the oblique case (the form used for objects of verbs and after prepositions, i.e. accusative/genitive, as opposed to nominative -ūna).
29.root: ن-ف-ق (n-f-q) — tunnel/burrow with a hidden exit; hence hypocrisy

30.meaning: 'and the disbelievers' — those who cover over and reject faith; people characterized by ingratitude and refusal to believe.
30.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') with a definite sound masculine plural noun ('the disbelievers'). The -īna ending is the masculine plural in its accusative/genitive (oblique) state, used when the word is an object or follows a preposition; the matching subject form would be -ūna.
30.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover up, reject, be ungrateful; disbelief

31.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
31.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
31.root: — (particle)

32.meaning: Jahannam — a proper name for the Fire of punishment in the Hereafter, the abode of torment. It is a name rather than a descriptive common noun.
32.grammar: A proper name. Because it is a special, non-fully-inflecting noun (it does not take tanwīn), it shows the -a ending in places where most nouns would otherwise take -i; here the single -a serves for both accusative and genitive positions. As a name it carries no general dictionary 'meaning' but designates the abode of punishment.
32.root: — (a proper name; commonly treated as having no Arabic triliteral root)

33.meaning: All together; the whole of a group taken collectively, with none left out. It functions as an emphatic word stressing totality and inclusiveness — 'every one of them, as one.'
33.grammar: The -an ending is the indefinite accusative (tanwīn al-naṣb). On a word like this it typically marks it as an emphatic state-descriptor (ḥāl) — describing the manner or condition of something as 'all together / collectively / as a whole.'
33.root: ج-م-ع (j-m-ʿ) — to gather, collect, bring together

1.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
1.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

2.meaning: They wait and watch expectantly; they bide their time, lying in wait for an outcome — often with a sense of watching to see how things will turn out, especially regarding someone else's fortune or misfortune.

parts.en: to wait, lie in wait, watch for (doubled-root stem)

2.grammar: A present/imperfect verb in Form V (tafaʿʿala), which often adds a reflexive or sustained-effort nuance — here 'to keep watching and waiting.' The personal prefix ya- ('they/he, masculine') is followed by the Form V derivational ta-, then the doubled-middle-radical stem rabbaṣ (the root's middle letter b is doubled in this pattern). Note that the ta- here is the Form V marker, not part of the bare root. The -ūna ending marks the masculine plural indicative mood (an ongoing, factual action, not a command or hypothetical).
2.root: ر-ب-ص (r-b-ṣ) — to wait, lie in wait, watch for an opportunity

3.meaning: A preposition 'bi' ('with / by / in / for') joined to the attached pronoun 'you all', yielding 'with you' or 'for you (plural)'. The exact shade — attachment, instrument, or benefit — depends on the verb it accompanies.
3.grammar: A preposition plus an attached pronoun. 'bi' is a versatile preposition (with, by, in, for), and -kum is the genitive/object pronoun 'you all' (masculine plural). Pronouns following a preposition always take this attached (genitive) form.

4.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'fa-' ('then', 'so', 'but') drawing a consequence, joined to the conditional particle 'in' ('if'). Together: 'then if …', 'but if …'.
4.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that signals a result or transition ('then/so'). 'in' is the conditional particle 'if', introducing a supposed condition. Both are indeclinable particles with no case ending.

5.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

5.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

6.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
6.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

7.meaning: An opening, and by extension a victory or decisive triumph — a 'breaking open' of what was closed, hence success, conquest, or a divine verdict that opens the way.
7.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The -un ending (tanwīn al-rafʿ) marks the indefinite nominative — the case used for the subject of a sentence or the thing being identified ('a victory'). 'Indefinite' means 'a/an,' not 'the.'
7.root: ف-ت-ح (f-t-ḥ) — to open; to grant victory, to deliver a verdict

8.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
8.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

9.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
9.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

10.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
10.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.

11.meaning: 'Did not…?' — a particle combining a question with negation, used to ask 'Have I/has he not…?', often expecting agreement or serving as a gentle reminder.
11.grammar: An interrogative prefix 'a-' ('?') joined to the negation 'lam'. 'lam' negates a verb and places it firmly in the past ('did not'), and grammatically puts the following present-tense verb into the jussive (clipped) form. Together they form a rhetorical or confirming question.

12.meaning: Expresses 'we are / we be' — the first-person plural of the verb 'to be / to become,' in a shortened form used after certain particles to express a contingent or negated state ('we were not,' 'so that we may be').
12.grammar: The imperfect verb 'to be' in the jussive mood (majzūm), shown by the final consonant having no vowel (the dropped/silent ending instead of -u). The jussive is the clipped form triggered by particles of negation, command, or condition. The na- prefix means 'we.'
12.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

13.meaning: 'With you (plural)' — denotes accompaniment, togetherness, or being in the company or on the side of a group of people addressed.
13.grammar: An adverb of accompaniment (maʿa, 'with') joined to the attached pronoun -kum ('you,' addressing a group of men or a mixed group). The fixed -a on maʿa and the -kum ending together convey 'in your company / alongside you.'
13.root: — (maʿa is a particle/adverb of accompaniment; it has no triliteral root)

14.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
14.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

15.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

15.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

16.meaning: A three-part word: 'for' + 'the' + 'those who cover up the truth / reject faith.' The base noun denotes the kāfir — one who disbelieves, denies, and ungratefully conceals the truth and Allah's favor. With 'for,' it marks them as the ones for whom something is intended.
16.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('for/to') joined to a definite plural noun, masculine. The '-īna' ending is the sound masculine plural in its genitive/accusative (oblique) form, here required because it follows the preposition 'li-'. The whole denotes 'for the disbelievers.'
16.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal, disbelieve, be ungrateful

17.meaning: A portion, share, or allotted part — what falls to someone as their due lot or stake.
17.grammar: A singular noun. The final -un (tanwīn ḍamma) marks it as indefinite ('a share') and in the nominative case, the form typically used for the subject of a sentence or the thing being stated to exist ('there is a share').
17.root: ن-ص-ب (n-ṣ-b) — to allot, set up; (a share) apportioned

18.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
18.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.

19.meaning: 'Did not…?' — a particle combining a question with negation, used to ask 'Have I/has he not…?', often expecting agreement or serving as a gentle reminder.
19.grammar: An interrogative prefix 'a-' ('?') joined to the negation 'lam'. 'lam' negates a verb and places it firmly in the past ('did not'), and grammatically puts the following present-tense verb into the jussive (clipped) form. Together they form a rhetorical or confirming question.

20.meaning: We gain the upper hand; we prevail over and overpower, taking control or advantage of something or someone — to dominate and master a situation.

parts.en: to gain mastery, overpower, take control

20.grammar: A present/imperfect verb in Form X (istafʿala), which often carries the sense of seeking, taking, or claiming something for oneself — here 'to gain mastery / take control.' It is in the jussive mood (no final vowel on the last consonant), the clipped form used after particles of condition or negation. The na- prefix means 'we.'
20.root: ح-و-ذ (ḥ-w-dh) — to take possession of, dominate, drive together

21.meaning: 'Upon you (all)' — the preposition 'upon/on/over' joined to the plural 'you,' indicating something resting on or directed at a group.
21.grammar: The preposition 'ʿalā' ('upon/on/over') in its joined form 'ʿalay-' plus the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you all,' masculine plural). It marks the group as the recipients or target of whatever is laid 'upon' them.

22.meaning: 'And we hold back / protect / defend you' — to shield, fend off, and keep a group safe by warding off harm from them, or alternatively to withhold them from someone.

parts.en: to prevent, hold back, protect, defend

22.grammar: Opens with wa- ('and'). The core is a present/imperfect Form I verb in the jussive mood (final consonant unvoweled), the clipped form used after particles of condition or negation. The na- prefix means 'we (do)'; the attached -kum is the object, 'you (a group).' So: 'and we defend/withhold you.'
22.root: م-ن-ع (m-n-ʿ) — to prevent, withhold, protect, defend

23.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
23.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

24.meaning: A plural noun meaning 'the believers' — those who have faith, who inwardly trust and affirm. The Form IV participle denotes one who brings about belief and security within.
24.grammar: A definite plural active participle of Form IV (āmana 'to believe'). The -īna ending marks a sound masculine plural in the accusative/genitive (object or oblique) state. The prefixed mu- marks it as a Form IV participle ('one who has/gives faith').

25.meaning: So Allah / then Allah; the connector 'so/then' joined to the proper name of the One True God, the sole Deity worthy of worship.
25.grammar: The connector fa- ('so, then, and so') joined to the divine name. The -u ending on the name is the nominative case, typically used when the noun is the subject of a sentence (the one doing the action) or what something is equated with.

26.meaning: He judges / He will judge; He decides, rules, and decrees with authority — passing a binding verdict and governing a matter wisely.
26.grammar: A present/future-tense verb, 'he judges/will judge,' describing a single male subject (or 'He,' of Allah). The ya- prefix marks the third-person masculine singular ('he'), and the final -u marks the indicative mood — an actual, ongoing, or future action.
26.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — to judge, decide, rule; wisdom and governance

27.meaning: Between you / among you; the space or relation linking the members of a group.
27.grammar: An adverb of place ('between/among') with an attached pronoun. The fixed -a ending is characteristic of such place-words; the ending -kum means 'you' for a group, so the whole means 'among you all'.
27.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation/interval; the space between two things

28.meaning: The noun 'day' — a span of time, often used for a momentous Day or appointed time; in the accusative it frequently functions as 'on the day (when…)', marking the time at which something occurs.
28.grammar: A masculine noun bearing the -a (accusative) ending. As an adverb of time this ending typically gives the sense 'on the day…', fixing the moment of an event.
28.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, a period of time

29.meaning: "the Resurrection" — the standing-up of all people from death to be judged; literally the act of rising or standing up.
29.grammar: The al- prefix means "the." The -i ending (on the feminine -t) is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ("the … OF this") or follows a preposition.

30.meaning: A two-part expression combining 'and' with the particle of emphatic future negation. The core particle 'lan' negates a coming action with finality: 'will never / shall not (ever).' It denies that something will happen in the future, often with a tone of absolute impossibility.
30.grammar: A conjunction 'wa' ('and') joined to the negating particle 'lan'. 'Lan' governs a following present-tense verb, putting it into the subjunctive mood and turning its meaning into an emphatic denial of the future: 'it will never happen.'

31.meaning: He makes, appoints, renders, or brings about — to set something into a state or place, to establish or designate it as such.
31.grammar: A present/imperfect Form I verb. The ya- prefix means 'he / it (masculine).' The final -a marks the subjunctive mood, which is triggered by particles meaning 'so that / in order to / will not' — signaling a purpose, intention, or expected (not yet realized) action rather than a present fact.
31.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, place, render, appoint

32.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
32.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

33.meaning: A three-part word: 'for' + 'the' + 'those who cover up the truth / reject faith.' The base noun denotes the kāfir — one who disbelieves, denies, and ungratefully conceals the truth and Allah's favor. With 'for,' it marks them as the ones for whom something is intended.
33.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('for/to') joined to a definite plural noun, masculine. The '-īna' ending is the sound masculine plural in its genitive/accusative (oblique) form, here required because it follows the preposition 'li-'. The whole denotes 'for the disbelievers.'
33.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal, disbelieve, be ungrateful

34.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
34.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
34.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

35.meaning: A plural noun meaning 'the believers' — those who have faith, who inwardly trust and affirm. The Form IV participle denotes one who brings about belief and security within.
35.grammar: A definite plural active participle of Form IV (āmana 'to believe'). The -īna ending marks a sound masculine plural in the accusative/genitive (object or oblique) state. The prefixed mu- marks it as a Form IV participle ('one who has/gives faith').

36.meaning: A way, path, or road; figuratively a course of conduct, a means, or a manner of acting that one follows.
36.grammar: A singular noun (usable as masculine or feminine). The final -an (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('a way') and accusative — the case used, among other things, for a noun that specifies or clarifies a preceding statement ('… an evil path').

1.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
1.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

2.meaning: the hypocrites — those who outwardly profess faith while inwardly concealing disbelief; people who present one face publicly and hide another within. From a root evoking a tunnel with two openings, suggesting a hidden way out.
2.grammar: A definite noun: al- means 'the'. 'Munāfiq' is an active participle of Form III ('one who behaves hypocritically'). The ending -īna marks the masculine sound plural in the oblique case (the form used for objects of verbs and after prepositions, i.e. accusative/genitive, as opposed to nominative -ūna).
2.root: ن-ف-ق (n-f-q) — tunnel/burrow with a hidden exit; hence hypocrisy

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'they try to deceive / they seek to outwit.' The Form III pattern adds the nuance of a two-sided or strenuous effort — attempting to deceive someone who may deceive back, or striving hard to trick — rather than a simple, completed act of deception.
3.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, Form III, third-person masculine plural. The prefix takes the vowel 'yu-' (characteristic of Forms II–IV), and the long-ā after the first root letter (khā-) is the mark of the Form III stem. The ending -ūna is the masculine plural indicative, denoting an ongoing or habitual action. Form III typically signals an effort directed at another party or a reciprocal interaction.

4.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
4.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

5.meaning: 'And He' — the connective 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'He' (a single masculine person or thing), often introducing a new clause about the same subject.
5.grammar: A connective particle plus an independent pronoun. The wa- prefix means 'and', joining clauses or words. 'Huwa' is the detached third-person masculine singular pronoun; it carries no case ending, its final -a being fixed.

6.meaning: Those who try to deceive them / are deceiving them — people engaged in trickery and double-dealing, seeking to outwit or beguile others.

parts.en: masculine plural, doer of the action (nominative)

6.grammar: An active participle on the pattern fāʿil (khādiʿ, 'one deceiving'), the Form I active participle of the verb khadaʿa ('to deceive'), here in the masculine plural. The -ū form is the nominative plural of a doer ('those who deceive'); its original final nūn drops because the pronoun -hum ('them') is attached as the object. So the whole means 'deceivers of them / those deceiving them.'
6.root: خ-د-ع (kh-d-ʿ) — to deceive, trick, beguile, outwit

7.meaning: 'And when...' — a linking phrase joining 'and' to 'when', used to introduce a circumstance or a recurring situation: 'and whenever / and at the time that...'.
7.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') attached to idhā ('when'). Idhā is a particle pointing to a time or condition, generally referring to something expected or recurring in the future ('when / whenever' it happens), and it normally introduces a following clause that states what occurs at that time.

8.meaning: A past-tense verb 'they stood up / they stood still / they arose'. The root covers standing, rising, and standing firm.
8.grammar: Past-tense (perfect) verb, third person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (males) did'; the written alif after it is a spelling convention and is not pronounced.
8.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise, stand firm

9.meaning: 'To / toward / up to' — a preposition marking the endpoint, goal, or limit of an action or motion: the direction something moves toward or the boundary at which it stops.
9.grammar: An invariable preposition. It has no case ending of its own but puts the noun that follows it into the genitive ('of / to' state). It indicates direction toward, or the terminal limit of, something.

10.meaning: The ritual Prayer — the formal worship of standing, bowing, and prostrating before Allah at appointed times. More broadly the root conveys connection, supplication, and reaching out to the divine; it is the central act of Islamic devotion.
10.grammar: A definite feminine noun ('the prayer'). The article al- means 'the.' The -i ending (on the feminine tā') is the genitive case: it typically links the word to a preceding preposition or to another noun in an 'of' relationship (e.g. 'of the prayer / to the prayer').

11.meaning: A past-tense verb 'they stood up / they stood still / they arose'. The root covers standing, rising, and standing firm.
11.grammar: Past-tense (perfect) verb, third person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (males) did'; the written alif after it is a spelling convention and is not pronounced.
11.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise, stand firm

12.meaning: Sluggish, lazy, listless — describing people who are heavy and reluctant, dragging themselves to an action without energy or eagerness.
12.grammar: A plural adjective (the broken-plural pattern fuʿālā) meaning 'lazy / sluggish ones,' describing a group. It ends in a fixed long -ā (alif maqṣūra) and does not take the usual changing case-vowels — its form stays the same whether subject, object, or possessive. It typically functions as a state-descriptor: 'while sluggish / lazily.'

13.meaning: They show off; they act to be seen by people, making a display of deeds for others' eyes rather than for any sincere purpose — outward performance done for reputation.

parts.en: to show off, act to be seen by others

13.grammar: A present/imperfect verb in Form III (mufāʿala), a pattern that often implies mutual or directed action — here 'to display oneself to others / to be seen.' The yu-…-ūna frame means 'they (masculine plural) do'; the -ūna ending marks the indicative mood (an ongoing, factual action).
13.root: ر-أ-ي (r-ʾ-y) — to see; (Form III) to show off, make a display

14.meaning: Mankind, humanity, people in general — the collective of human beings.
14.grammar: A definite noun ('the people') with the attached 'al-' ('the'). The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 'n' (a sun letter), which is why the 'n' is doubled — this is a pronunciation effect, not a separate piece. The final '-a' ending is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb (the one being acted upon) or the subject of certain particles.
14.root: ن-و-س (n-w-s) — to move/sway; by extension, people

15.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
15.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

16.meaning: 'They remember / make mention of,' i.e., to call to mind, invoke, or mention — both inward recollection and outward utterance, often of Allah.
16.grammar: A present-tense verb. The -ūna ending marks a plural masculine subject ('they') and signals the ordinary (indicative) present tense — an ongoing or habitual remembering and mentioning.
16.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — to remember, mention, call to mind

17.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
17.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

18.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
18.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

19.meaning: Little, small, scant — small in amount, value, or number; trifling.
19.grammar: An adjective on the stable fa'īl pattern. The -an ending is the indefinite accusative, used here as it describes a noun that is itself accusative ('a little [thing]').
19.root: ق-ل-ل (q-l-l) — to be few, little, scant
