1.meaning: Wavering, vacillating ones — people who are shaken back and forth, unable to settle, swinging between two sides without firmly belonging to either.

parts.en: to waver, swing to and fro, vacillate

1.grammar: A passive participle from a reduplicated (quadriliteral) verb, meaning 'ones made to waver / vacillating ones.' The mu- prefix forms the participle ('one who is …'); the -īna ending is the masculine plural in the accusative/genitive state — the form used when the word is an object or follows a preposition.
1.root: ذ-ب-ذ-ب (dh-b-dh-b) — to waver, oscillate, swing back and forth (reduplicated root)

2.meaning: Between; the space, position, or relationship lying in the midst of two or more things. It marks an in-between location or a relation linking parties.

parts.en: between / amid / in the midst of

2.grammar: An adverb of place (ẓarf makān) meaning 'between / amid.' It is built with a fixed final -a and is followed by what it relates ('between X and Y'). It typically governs a following noun in the genitive, giving 'between [the …].'
2.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction, what lies between; clarity

3.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
3.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

4.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
4.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

5.meaning: A preposition meaning 'to,' 'toward,' or 'up to' — pointing to the end-point, goal, or limit of a motion, direction, or extent.
5.grammar: A preposition (a small linking word). It governs the noun after it, putting that noun in the genitive case, and points to a destination or limit ('to,' 'toward,' 'as far as').

6.meaning: These / those — a plural demonstrative pointing to a group of people or things. Its core sense is the near demonstrative 'these', but it is very commonly rendered 'those' in translation when the group it points to has already been described or named rather than being physically present.
6.grammar: A plural demonstrative pronoun, used for a group of either gender. Its base value is near-deixis ('these'), built from an attention-drawing prefix 'hā-' ('lo!, here') plus the base 'ulāʾi'. In practice it is often translated 'those' when the referent is already mentioned or understood rather than literally nearby. Its form is fixed and does not change for grammatical case; it points to a group rather than naming it.

7.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
7.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

8.meaning: A preposition meaning 'to,' 'toward,' or 'up to' — pointing to the end-point, goal, or limit of a motion, direction, or extent.
8.grammar: A preposition (a small linking word). It governs the noun after it, putting that noun in the genitive case, and points to a destination or limit ('to,' 'toward,' 'as far as').

9.meaning: These / those — a plural demonstrative pointing to a group of people or things. Its core sense is the near demonstrative 'these', but it is very commonly rendered 'those' in translation when the group it points to has already been described or named rather than being physically present.
9.grammar: A plural demonstrative pronoun, used for a group of either gender. Its base value is near-deixis ('these'), built from an attention-drawing prefix 'hā-' ('lo!, here') plus the base 'ulāʾi'. In practice it is often translated 'those' when the referent is already mentioned or understood rather than literally nearby. Its form is fixed and does not change for grammatical case; it points to a group rather than naming it.

10.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
10.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

11.meaning: He lets/leads astray — he causes someone to lose the right way, leaving them to wander from guidance.
11.grammar: A present-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular ('he …'), in the causative pattern ('to cause to stray'). It stands in the jussive/conditional mood (the doubled lām broken apart and given a helping -i to ease pronunciation), typically meaning 'whomever he lets stray …'.
11.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to stray, go astray, lose the way

12.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
12.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

13.meaning: So never / then never — a connector 'so/then' joined to an emphatic particle of negation that denies a future action absolutely: 'will never (at all)'.
13.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector meaning 'so/then', linking to what precedes. 'lan' negates a following present-tense verb and casts it into the future with emphatic force ('will never'); it also puts that verb into the subjunctive, which shows up as a final '-a' on the verb.

14.meaning: A second-person present verb: 'you find / you come upon.' It denotes discovering or encountering something, whether by searching or by chance.
14.grammar: The ta- prefix marks a second-person masculine singular subject ('you'). The final -a vowel is the subjunctive, the shape used after governing particles (such as 'never' or 'that'), often projecting the action into the future.
14.root: و-ج-د (w-j-d) — to find, to come upon

15.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
15.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

16.meaning: A way, path, road, or means — a route to a destination, hence also a way or means of accomplishing something.
16.grammar: A singular noun. The '-an' ending is accusative and indefinite: the accusative case commonly marks the direct object of a verb, and the final 'n' sound marks it indefinite ('a way'). It denotes a path one travels or a means to an end.
16.root: س-ب-ل (s-b-l) — a road, path, way

1.meaning: 'O…!' — a compound vocative expression used to call out and summon an audience before addressing them. It fuses the call-particle 'yā' ('O') with a noun that means 'the one(s) addressed,' yielding an emphatic 'O you…!' that introduces direct address.
1.grammar: A vocative (calling) construction. 'Yā' is the particle for calling out; 'ayyu' carries a nominative '-u' as the one being summoned; 'hā' is an attention-drawing particle. Together they function as 'O you…!,' setting up the noun of address that follows.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
3.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

4.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
4.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

5.meaning: That you take, that you adopt — a present-tense verb (form VIII) meaning to take for oneself, to choose or adopt something. Addressed to a group ('you all'), and in a form used after particles meaning 'that' or 'to'.
5.grammar: A present-tense verb in the reflexive (form VIII) pattern, 'to take for oneself'. The ta- prefix with the plural ending means 'you all'. The ending is -ū (the final 'n' of -ūna has dropped), which marks the subjunctive or jussive mood — the form used after particles like 'that', 'to', or 'not'.

6.meaning: The disbelievers / the ungrateful — those who reject faith and cover over the truth; the word also carries the sense of covering up or being ungrateful for what one has been given.
6.grammar: 'al-' is 'the'. The stem is an active participle ('one who disbelieves/is ungrateful') made plural for masculine people. The -īna ending is the accusative/genitive form of the sound masculine plural: it marks the word as an object of a verb or as governed by a preposition, as opposed to the subject form -ūna.
6.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; ingratitude, disbelief

7.meaning: Allies, protectors, intimate friends — those taken as close supporters, patrons, or guardians, with whom one stands in mutual loyalty (plural of walī).
7.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural of 'walī.' Being a 'diptote' (a noun that resists the usual full set of endings), it takes a single final '-a' here for the accusative case, which commonly marks the direct object of a verb or signals 'as / being' something — and notably without the usual '-n' (no nunation).

8.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
8.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

9.meaning: A noun used to mean 'besides', 'other than', 'apart from', or 'short of'. It points to something or someone set apart from, or lower/lesser than, a named party. Often used in the phrase 'besides Allah'.
9.grammar: 'dūn' functions as an adverb-like noun of place/relation. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, which appears because it follows a preposition (such as 'min', 'from') and because it links to a following noun ('other than …'). It commonly heads the construction 'besides/other than [someone]'.
9.root: د-و-ن (d-w-n) — to be low/beneath, to fall short; hence 'below, other than, besides'

10.meaning: A plural noun meaning 'the believers' — those who have faith, who inwardly trust and affirm. The Form IV participle denotes one who brings about belief and security within.
10.grammar: A definite plural active participle of Form IV (āmana 'to believe'). The -īna ending marks a sound masculine plural in the accusative/genitive (object or oblique) state. The prefixed mu- marks it as a Form IV participle ('one who has/gives faith').

11.meaning: Do you (plural) wish/want/intend? — an opening question asking whether the addressees seek or desire something. The prefixed hamza turns the statement into a question.
11.grammar: A yes/no question (opening hamza 'do …?') over a present-tense verb, 2nd-person masculine plural. The ending -ūna marks the plural 'you all' and the indicative mood (a plain statement of fact, here questioned).
11.root: ر-و-د (r-w-d) — to seek, desire, want, intend

12.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
12.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

13.meaning: A verb addressed to a group of males (or a mixed group): 'you (all) make', 'you set up', 'you place', or 'you render (something into something).' The verb jaʿala carries the sense of making, forming, or appointing.

parts.en: plural 'you all' (and, after a prohibition particle, the cut-off mood)

13.grammar: The 'ta-' prefix marks a present/future verb addressed to 'you'. The '-ū' ending marks a masculine plural subject ('you all'). The dropping of the final 'n' (jussive/subjunctive form) is what a preceding particle like 'lā' of prohibition triggers, turning it into 'do not do …'.
13.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, to place, to render

14.meaning: A two-part word: the preposition 'li-' meaning 'to', 'for', or 'belonging to', attached to the name 'Allah'. It conveys 'to Allah' or 'for Allah'.
14.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('to/for') pulls the following noun into the genitive case, which is why 'Allah' ends in '-i' (llāhi). The '-i' ending is the regular result of a noun governed by a preposition.

15.meaning: 'Upon you (all)' — the preposition 'upon/on/over' joined to the plural 'you,' indicating something resting on or directed at a group.
15.grammar: The preposition 'ʿalā' ('upon/on/over') in its joined form 'ʿalay-' plus the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you all,' masculine plural). It marks the group as the recipients or target of whatever is laid 'upon' them.

16.meaning: Authority, sanction, or compelling proof — power or warrant given to back something up, whether kingly authority or a decisive argument. 'Sulṭān' is authorizing power or evidence.
16.grammar: A single noun ('authority') carrying the accusative indefinite ending -an (tanwīn al-naṣb). This one ending does two things at once: the -a marks the accusative case (typically the direct object of a verb), and the final -n sound (nunation) shows the noun is indefinite ('an authority / any warrant'). The nunation is a diacritic on the case vowel, not a separable suffix, so the word stays one undivided token.
16.root: س-ل-ط (s-l-ṭ) — power, dominance, authority

17.meaning: An adjective meaning 'clear, plain, manifest' — describing something that is obvious and self-evident, or that makes things clear.
17.grammar: An active participle of form IV (mubīn), 'one that is manifest / makes clear.' The mu- prefix forms the participle. The final -an (tanwīn fatḥa) is the indefinite accusative ending ('a clear one'), used here to agree with a preceding masculine accusative noun it describes.

1.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
1.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

2.meaning: the hypocrites — those who outwardly profess faith while inwardly concealing disbelief; people who present one face publicly and hide another within. From a root evoking a tunnel with two openings, suggesting a hidden way out.
2.grammar: A definite noun: al- means 'the'. 'Munāfiq' is an active participle of Form III ('one who behaves hypocritically'). The ending -īna marks the masculine sound plural in the oblique case (the form used for objects of verbs and after prepositions, i.e. accusative/genitive, as opposed to nominative -ūna).
2.root: ن-ف-ق (n-f-q) — tunnel/burrow with a hidden exit; hence hypocrisy

3.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
3.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

4.meaning: A level, layer, or descending degree — especially a step downward. The root denotes graded stages going down, hence a depth or low tier within a series of descending ranks.
4.grammar: A definite masculine noun ('the level / depth'). The article al- means 'the.' The -i ending is the genitive case, typically marking a link to a preceding preposition or another noun in an 'of' relationship ('of the level / in the depth').
4.root: د-ر-ك (d-r-k) — to reach, attain; a graded level or stage (esp. descending)

5.meaning: The lowest, the very bottom-most — the superlative describing what is most downward or beneath all others in rank or position.
5.grammar: A definite superlative adjective ('the lowest') on the pattern afʿal. The article al- means 'the.' The -i ending is the genitive case — the form used when the word follows a preposition or describes a noun that is itself genitive ('of the lowest …').
5.root: س-ف-ل (s-f-l) — lowness, being low, the bottom

6.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
6.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

7.meaning: 'The Fire' — fire, flame; in religious usage often the Fire of Hell, the blazing punishment of the Hereafter.
7.grammar: The definite article 'al-' ('the') plus the feminine noun 'nār' ('fire'). The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 'n' (so it is pronounced 'an-nār'). The '-i' ending is genitive, the case used after a preposition or to link the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the Fire').

8.meaning: A two-part expression combining 'and' with the particle of emphatic future negation. The core particle 'lan' negates a coming action with finality: 'will never / shall not (ever).' It denies that something will happen in the future, often with a tone of absolute impossibility.
8.grammar: A conjunction 'wa' ('and') joined to the negating particle 'lan'. 'Lan' governs a following present-tense verb, putting it into the subjunctive mood and turning its meaning into an emphatic denial of the future: 'it will never happen.'

9.meaning: A second-person present verb: 'you find / you come upon.' It denotes discovering or encountering something, whether by searching or by chance.
9.grammar: The ta- prefix marks a second-person masculine singular subject ('you'). The final -a vowel is the subjunctive, the shape used after governing particles (such as 'never' or 'that'), often projecting the action into the future.
9.root: و-ج-د (w-j-d) — to find, to come upon

10.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
10.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

11.meaning: 'A helper, supporter, one who gives aid and victory' — an intensive form stressing reliable, effective help.
11.grammar: An indefinite noun on an intensive pattern (faʿīl) that conveys a strong or constant doer — 'a true helper'. The -an ending marks the accusative and indefiniteness, commonly used here as a specifier naming the capacity ('as a helper').
11.root: ن-ص-ر (n-ṣ-r) — to help, to aid, to give victory

1.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
1.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: They turned back in repentance — a third-person masculine plural past verb meaning 'they repented,' i.e. they returned to Allah, abandoning sin and re-orienting the heart toward Him.
3.grammar: Past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks the subject as 'they' (a group of males or mixed). As a perfect verb it presents the action as completed: 'they turned (back) in repentance.'

4.meaning: And they set right / reformed — they put matters into a sound, wholesome state, mending what was broken or corrupt, whether in deeds, relationships, or themselves.
4.grammar: Prefix 'wa' = 'and' (joining to what precedes). A past-tense verb of the form 'aṣlaḥa' (causative pattern), so it means to MAKE something sound/good. The -ū ending marks the subject as 'they,' and the perfect form presents the act as completed.

5.meaning: And they held fast / took firm hold — to grip tightly to a secure support, to cling for protection and refuge, seeking safety by attaching oneself firmly to something.

parts.en: to hold fast, cling, take refuge in

5.grammar: Opens with wa- ('and'). The core is a past-tense verb in Form VIII (iftaʿala), which often adds a reflexive or self-involved sense — here 'to hold oneself fast to / take refuge in.' The -ū ending marks 'they (a group of men) did' in the completed past.
5.root: ع-ص-م (ʿ-ṣ-m) — to protect, hold firmly, preserve, grant refuge

6.meaning: A phrase 'in Allah / by Allah', combining the preposition 'with/in/by' and the divine name Allah, the proper name of the One God.
6.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with, by means of') prefixed to the divine name Allah. A preposition always forces the following noun into the genitive case, which is why Allah here ends in -i. With verbs of believing, bi- conveys the object of faith — to believe IN.
6.root: — (Allah is the proper name of God and is not derived from a triliteral root in the usual sense)

7.meaning: And they made pure / sincere / exclusive — to cleanse something of any mixture so it is wholly devoted to one object, especially purifying one's intent and worship for Allah alone.

parts.en: to make pure, dedicate sincerely / exclusively

7.grammar: Opens with wa- ('and'). The core is a past-tense verb in Form IV (afʿala), which typically makes an action transitive or causative — 'to render (something) pure / exclusive.' The -ū ending marks 'they (a group of men) did' in the completed past.
7.root: خ-ل-ص (kh-l-ṣ) — purity, being unmixed, sincerity, exclusive devotion

8.meaning: Their religion / way of life — the concept of dīn: the complete system of belief, worship, obligation, and obedience by which one lives and to which one is accountable; also rendered 'faith,' 'judgment,' or 'recompense' depending on context. Here joined to 'their.'

parts.en: religion, way of life, system of obedience and accountability

8.grammar: A noun with the attached possessive pronoun -hum ('their,' a group of men). The -a vowel before the pronoun reflects the accusative case — the form typically used when the noun is the direct object of a verb ('… their religion' as the thing acted upon).
8.root: د-ي-ن (d-y-n) — religion, obedience, judgment, requital, debt/accountability

9.meaning: A two-part word: the preposition 'li-' meaning 'to', 'for', or 'belonging to', attached to the name 'Allah'. It conveys 'to Allah' or 'for Allah'.
9.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('to/for') pulls the following noun into the genitive case, which is why 'Allah' ends in '-i' (llāhi). The '-i' ending is the regular result of a noun governed by a preposition.

10.meaning: So those / then those are the ones — a connector 'so/then' joined to a demonstrative pointing to a distant or already-mentioned group: 'those people, they (are the ones who)…'.
10.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector meaning 'so/then', often introducing a result or consequence. 'ulā'ika' is a plural demonstrative ('those') pointing to people, typically picking up a previously described group and setting them up as the subject. It is fixed in form and does not change for case.

11.meaning: With, together with, alongside — indicating company, accompaniment, or being in the same place or time as another.
11.grammar: A preposition of accompaniment ('with, alongside'); grammatically it is an adverbial of place/time (ẓarf) that governs the genitive. It is placed before a following noun to put one thing in the company of another, and that following noun stands in the genitive. The -a is its fixed ending.

12.meaning: A plural noun meaning 'the believers' — those who have faith, who inwardly trust and affirm. The Form IV participle denotes one who brings about belief and security within.
12.grammar: A definite plural active participle of Form IV (āmana 'to believe'). The -īna ending marks a sound masculine plural in the accusative/genitive (object or oblique) state. The prefixed mu- marks it as a Form IV participle ('one who has/gives faith').

13.meaning: 'And soon / and shall' — the particle sawfa places a verb firmly in the future, often a more emphatic or distant future than the simpler prefix sa-, here joined with 'and.' It signals 'and indeed [it] will [happen].'
13.grammar: wa- means 'and.' sawfa is a future particle placed before a present/imperfect verb to push the action into the future ('will / shall'). It is a fixed, uninflecting word with no case ending; it carries a sense of certainty about what is to come.
13.root: — (sawfa is a future particle; it has no triliteral root)

14.meaning: He gives / grants / bestows — to hand over, confer, or bring something to someone. The root centrally means 'to come,' and in this (Form IV) sense 'to cause to come,' i.e. to give or bring forth.
14.grammar: A present/imperfect Form IV verb (afʿala, causative: 'to bring / give'). The yu- prefix means 'he / it (masculine).' The final weak letter is dropped, leaving the bare -i sound, which marks the jussive mood — the clipped form used after particles of condition, command, or negation.
14.root: أ-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (Form IV) to bring, give, grant

15.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
15.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

16.meaning: A plural noun meaning 'the believers' — those who have faith, who inwardly trust and affirm. The Form IV participle denotes one who brings about belief and security within.
16.grammar: A definite plural active participle of Form IV (āmana 'to believe'). The -īna ending marks a sound masculine plural in the accusative/genitive (object or oblique) state. The prefixed mu- marks it as a Form IV participle ('one who has/gives faith').
16.root: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — faith, safety, security

17.meaning: A reward, wage, or recompense — the return earned for work or conduct, whether worldly pay or otherworldly recompense.
17.grammar: A noun meaning 'a reward.' The final '-an' (tanwīn fatḥa) marks the indefinite accusative case, the case used for the object of a verb (e.g. of 'to give'), giving the sense 'a reward.'
17.root: ا-ج-ر (ʾ-j-r) — reward, wage, recompense for what one does

18.meaning: 'Great, immense, mighty, momentous.' It describes something vast in size, weight, or seriousness, and is often used of grave or awe-inspiring matters.
18.grammar: An adjective on the intensive faʿīl pattern. The -an ending is the indefinite accusative ('a great …'), commonly marking an adjective that agrees with an indefinite accusative noun it describes, or the object of a verb.

1.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
1.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

2.meaning: "he does / he acts / he carries out" — built on the basic verb meaning to do, make, or perform; the present tense conveys ongoing or habitual action.
2.grammar: A present/future-tense verb in the 'he' form. The ya- prefix marks third-person masculine singular ('he'). The final -u ending is the indicative mood, marking a plain statement of ongoing or habitual fact ('he does').
2.root: ف-ع-ل (f-ʿ-l) — to do, act, make

3.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
3.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

4.meaning: 'By / with your punishment' — combining the preposition 'with/by' and the noun for punishment, torment, or chastisement, joined to 'you (plural).' It expresses the means or instrument: 'by punishing you.'
4.grammar: The preposition bi- ('with / by') attaches to the noun, which therefore takes the genitive -i ending (prepositions always put their noun in the genitive). The attached -kum ('you / your,' a group) completes it: 'by your punishment / by punishing you.'

5.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
5.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

6.meaning: You gave thanks / were grateful — to acknowledge and return a kindness, to recognize a benefit and respond with gratitude, praise, and right use of what was given.

parts.en: to give thanks, be grateful, acknowledge a favor

6.grammar: A past-tense Form I verb. The attached -tum ending means 'you (a group of men or a mixed group) did' — the completed-action past, second person plural. So: 'you (all) gave thanks.'
6.root: ش-ك-ر (sh-k-r) — thankfulness, gratitude, acknowledging favor

7.meaning: 'And you believed / had faith' — to attain secure faith and trust, to affirm and commit one's heart to the truth, especially belief in Allah. Joined here with 'and.'

parts.en: to believe, have faith, place trust (Form IV)

7.grammar: Opens with wa- ('and'). The core is a past-tense verb in Form IV (āmana, 'to believe / to have faith'). The attached -tum ending means 'you (a group) did' — the completed-action past, second person plural: 'and you (all) believed.'
7.root: أ-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — security, safety, trust; (Form IV) to have faith, to believe

8.meaning: And he was / he became — a verb of being that places a subject in a past state or links it to a description in the past.
8.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'kāna' is a past-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular, meaning 'he was/became'; it commonly introduces a past condition and is typically followed by a noun describing the subject's state. The final -a marks completed past action by a single male.

9.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
9.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

10.meaning: Active participle from the verb 'to thank/be grateful': one who is thankful, grateful, or appreciative. When applied to Allah it carries an intensive sense — One who fully recognizes and richly rewards even small good deeds. The single accusative ending often marks it as a predicate or descriptive complement.
10.grammar: An active participle (the 'doer' pattern, like 'thanker'). The final '-an' is the accusative case with tanwīn (indefinite 'n' sound): it typically marks a word as the object of a verb, or as a descriptive/predicate term answering 'as what?' or 'being what?'.

11.meaning: All-Knowing; one possessing complete, perfect knowledge. As an intensive form it conveys knowledge that is total and unfailing, encompassing all things.
11.grammar: An intensive adjective ('all-knowing') on the faʿīl pattern, which stresses the quality to its fullest degree. The -an (tanwīn) joins the -a accusative ending — typical of a predicate or object — with the -n marking it indefinite.

1.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
1.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

2.meaning: He loves / likes / holds dear. To have affection for and approval of something or someone.
2.grammar: A present-tense verb in the fourth pattern, third-person masculine singular ('he…'). The yu- prefix signals a single masculine subject, and the final -u ending marks the indicative mood, presenting the action as an established fact or ongoing reality.
2.root: ح-ب-ب (ḥ-b-b) — love, affection; to hold dear

3.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
3.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

4.meaning: A definite noun meaning open, loud, public utterance — speaking out so others can hear, as opposed to what is whispered or kept private. It denotes the act of making something openly known or said aloud.
4.grammar: A definite noun ('the …'). The final '-a' is the accusative case: it typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon) or follows certain particles. Being definite, it points to a specific, known instance rather than 'a' general one.
4.root: ج-ه-ر (j-h-r) — to be open, loud, made public

5.meaning: Evil, harm, or what is bad and distressing; something that brings injury, misfortune, or moral wrong. The prefixed 'bi' adds the sense 'with/by means of' the evil, so it points to evil as the instrument or object toward which something is directed.
5.grammar: A definite noun (the al- = 'the') governed by the preposition bi- ('with/by'). The final -i is the genitive ending, which is the case automatically required after a preposition and which also links a noun to a preceding one in an 'of' relationship.

6.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
6.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

7.meaning: Speech, an utterance, a statement, or a saying — that which is said. It denotes the act or content of speaking.
7.grammar: A definite noun ('the speech'). The -i ending is the genitive case: it typically links the word to a preceding noun in an 'of …' relationship or follows a preposition.

8.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
8.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

9.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
9.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

10.meaning: A past-tense passive verb: 'he/it was wronged, treated unjustly, oppressed.' The passive form leaves the wrongdoer unnamed and focuses on the one who suffered the injustice.

parts.en: final stem vowel of the passive pattern

10.grammar: A completed-action (past) verb in the passive voice — the vowel pattern 'ẓu-li-ma' (fuʿila) signals 'was done to' rather than 'did'. The 3rd-person masculine singular ('he/it') is carried by the bare stem itself with no added suffix; the closing '-a' is simply the final short vowel of that passive pattern, not a separate person marker. The subject is whoever the wrong was done to.

11.meaning: And he was / he became — a verb of being that places a subject in a past state or links it to a description in the past.
11.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'kāna' is a past-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular, meaning 'he was/became'; it commonly introduces a past condition and is typically followed by a noun describing the subject's state. The final -a marks completed past action by a single male.

12.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
12.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

13.meaning: All-Hearing — one who hears fully and perfectly. This is an intensive adjective (faʿīl pattern) conveying that hearing is a permanent, all-encompassing attribute, not a single act of hearing.
13.grammar: An indefinite noun/adjective on the intensive faʿīl pattern. The final -an (tanwīn fatḥah) marks the accusative case, the form a word typically takes as the object of a verb or as a predicate after certain particles; the -n also signals that it is indefinite ('a hearer / hearing').

14.meaning: All-Knowing; one possessing complete, perfect knowledge. As an intensive form it conveys knowledge that is total and unfailing, encompassing all things.
14.grammar: An intensive adjective ('all-knowing') on the faʿīl pattern, which stresses the quality to its fullest degree. The -an (tanwīn) joins the -a accusative ending — typical of a predicate or object — with the -n marking it indefinite.

1.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
1.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

2.meaning: A present/future verb meaning 'you (all) disclose, make known, bring out into the open' — to reveal or show something openly.
2.grammar: Present/future verb of the causative pattern ('to make appear, bring out'). The tu- prefix together with the -ū ending marks a second-person masculine plural subject ('you all'). The bare -ū ending (without a final n) is the shortened mood used after certain particles, such as in conditional statements.
2.root: ب-د-و (b-d-w) — to appear, become visible

3.meaning: Good — that which is beneficial, virtuous, and excellent; goodness as a thing one can do or possess, and what is better or preferable.
3.grammar: A noun (also serving as the 'better/best' form). The final -an (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite and in the accusative case — the case used for the direct object of a verb ('to do good') and for similar governed roles.

4.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
4.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

5.meaning: 'You (all) conceal it' — the act of hiding, covering over, or keeping something out of sight. This verb (Form IV) carries the nuance of making a thing hidden or unseen.

parts.en: you (second-person present prefix, Form IV vocalisation)

5.grammar: A present-tense Form IV verb (afʿala, often 'to make/cause X'). The tu- prefix marks a second-person subject ('you'), the -ū makes it plural ('you all'), and -hu is the object 'it/him'. The shortened plural ending (no final nūn) shows the jussive/subjunctive mood used after conditional or negating particles.
5.root: خ-ف-ي (kh-f-y) — to be hidden; (Form IV) to hide, to conceal

6.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
6.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

7.meaning: Present/future verb, second person: 'you pardon, overlook, let off.' Its core sense is to wipe away an offence and forgo any claim to punishment, effacing the fault as if it left no trace.
7.grammar: An ongoing/future-tense verb. The 'ta-' prefix marks the doer as 'you'; the long '-ū' ending makes it plural ('you all'). This long-vowel ending is also the form used after certain particles that drop the final 'n', giving the sense 'that you (may) pardon' or in commands/prohibitions.

8.meaning: A preposition meaning 'on behalf of,' 'for,' 'about,' or 'away from.' It often conveys removing a burden from someone or acting in their place.

parts.en: on behalf of / for / away from

8.grammar: A preposition (a linking particle). It governs the noun that follows it, putting that noun into the genitive case. It does not change form.

9.meaning: Evil, harm, badness, or something offensive and grievous — that which is bad in itself or brings injury and distress. As a noun it names an evil thing or an evil deed.
9.grammar: The -in ending (nunation/tanwīn) marks an indefinite noun in the genitive case: 'an evil / of an evil'. The genitive typically appears after a preposition or as the second term of a possessive ('… of …'), and the doubled-n sound (tanwīn) signals that the noun is indefinite ('a/some').
9.root: س-و-ء (s-w-ʼ) — to be bad, evil, to grieve or distress

10.meaning: A two-part connector meaning 'so/then, indeed…'. It joins fa- ('so', 'then', marking a result or consequence) to inna, an emphatic particle that strongly affirms the statement that follows ('truly', 'verily').
10.grammar: fa- is a connective prefix signaling that what follows is a consequence or next step. inna is an emphatic particle that introduces a nominal sentence, puts its following noun in the accusative, and strengthens the assertion; it does not itself take a case ending.

11.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
11.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

12.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

12.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

13.meaning: One who pardons abundantly — who effaces and lets go of faults, blotting out wrongs as if they never were; an intensive describing a constant, generous pardoner.
13.grammar: An intensive adjective on the faʿūl pattern, which conveys that the quality is possessed to a high or constant degree ('ever-pardoning'). The -an ending (tanwīn 'a') marks the accusative case with indefiniteness, the case used for a direct object or as the predicate after certain particles.
13.root: ع-ف-و (ʿ-f-w) — to pardon, efface, forgive and overlook

14.meaning: An adjective meaning 'all-powerful,' 'fully capable,' 'one who has complete power to do anything.' As a divine attribute it denotes Allah's absolute and unrestricted ability over all things.
14.grammar: An intensive adjective ('most capable, all-powerful'). The -an ending is the accusative with indefinite (tanwīn) marking, typically used as the predicate of a 'was/is' statement or as an object; the doubled-n sound shows indefiniteness.

1.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
1.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: 'They disbelieve / reject faith', or more literally 'they cover over (the truth), they are ungrateful'. An ongoing or habitual rejection and denial.
3.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb. The ya-…-ūna frame marks a masculine plural 'they' acting now or habitually; the final -na (kept, not dropped) shows the verb is in its plain indicative form, stating an ongoing fact.
3.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — covering over; hence disbelief and ingratitude

4.meaning: A phrase 'in Allah / by Allah', combining the preposition 'with/in/by' and the divine name Allah, the proper name of the One God.
4.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with, by means of') prefixed to the divine name Allah. A preposition always forces the following noun into the genitive case, which is why Allah here ends in -i. With verbs of believing, bi- conveys the object of faith — to believe IN.
4.root: — (Allah is the proper name of God and is not derived from a triliteral root in the usual sense)

5.meaning: A combination 'and His messengers' — 'and' + 'messengers' + 'His'. Messengers are those sent by Allah to convey His revelation to humankind.
5.grammar: The prefix wa- is the connective 'and'. 'rusul' is the plural 'messengers'. The -i before the pronoun is genitive, used after prepositions or to show possession; with attached 'hi' ('His') it means 'His messengers'. The -hi ('His') indicates a single male/divine possessor.

6.meaning: And they want, intend, will, or desire — a purposeful wanting that aims at and seeks to bring something about.
6.grammar: A present-tense verb (Form IV, conveying purposeful willing) with wa- ('and'). The yu- prefix marks a third-person subject and the -ūna ending makes it masculine plural ('they'). The full -ūna ending is the indicative mood, signalling a plain ongoing or repeated action ('they want / keep wanting'), not a command or a clipped form.
6.root: ر-و-د (r-w-d) — to seek, will, intend, desire

7.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
7.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

8.meaning: Present/future verb (intensive form), third person plural: 'they make a distinction, separate, divide between things.' The doubled middle root letter gives a sense of deliberately splitting apart or treating items as separate.
8.grammar: An ongoing/future verb in the intensive (doubled) pattern, which adds force or repetition to 'separate'. The 'yu-' prefix points to a third-person subject and the long '-ū' ending makes it 'they' (masculine plural). The prefix yā' here carries a shadda (doubling), which arises when a preceding word's final 'n' assimilates into it. The bare '-ū' (without final 'n') is the form taken after certain particles meaning 'that they…' or in negative/command constructions.

9.meaning: Between; in the midst of two things. An adverb of place marking the space separating or lying among parties or points.
9.grammar: An adverb of place ('between'). It always ends in -a and grammatically governs what follows it, putting the following noun(s) into the genitive 'of' relationship. It does not change to show 'the' or a case of its own; the fixed -a is simply how this word is formed.
9.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction, what lies between

10.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
10.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

11.meaning: A combination 'and His messengers' — 'and' + 'messengers' + 'His'. Messengers are those sent by Allah to convey His revelation to humankind.
11.grammar: The prefix wa- is the connective 'and'. 'rusul' is the plural 'messengers'. The -i before the pronoun is genitive, used after prepositions or to show possession; with attached 'hi' ('His') it means 'His messengers'. The -hi ('His') indicates a single male/divine possessor.

12.meaning: A verb meaning 'and they say / and they keep saying' — to utter or assert in speech. The structure presents an ongoing or repeated act of speaking by a group.
12.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) verb joined by wa- ('and'). The ya-…-ūna frame marks the 3rd-person masculine plural ('they'); the full -ūna ending is the inseparable indicative-plural suffix, showing the verb is in its base (indicative) form and expressing an ongoing or habitual action.

13.meaning: A present-tense verb meaning 'we believe, we have faith' — to affirm trust and faith, especially in Allah and His revelation; literally 'we grant security/assent.'
13.grammar: A present/ongoing action with a first-person plural subject; the nu- prefix means 'we.' The final -u marks the indicative mood — a plain statement of fact ('we believe'). The form IV pattern of this root gives the meaning 'to have faith / to deem secure.'
13.root: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — security, safety, trust; hence faith and belief

14.meaning: 'In part / in some' — referring to a portion or some of a whole, here left indefinite. The bi- prefix gives the sense of disbelieving 'in' something.
14.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with') plus the noun baʿḍ ('a part, some'). The final -in (tanwīn kasr) is the genitive case with indefiniteness, required after bi- and marking the noun as 'some (unspecified) part.'
14.root: ب-ع-ض (b-ʿ-ḍ) — a part, portion, or some of a whole

15.meaning: '…and we disbelieve / reject faith.' Combines the joining word 'and' with a first-person plural present verb whose core sense is to cover over and reject the truth, to refuse belief.
15.grammar: An ongoing/future-tense verb joined by 'wa-' ('and'). The 'na-' prefix means 'we'. The final '-u' is the plain present-tense ending, signalling a simple statement of fact ('we disbelieve') rather than a wish or command.
15.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover over, reject, disbelieve

16.meaning: 'In part / in some' — referring to a portion or some of a whole, here left indefinite. The bi- prefix gives the sense of disbelieving 'in' something.
16.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with') plus the noun baʿḍ ('a part, some'). The final -in (tanwīn kasr) is the genitive case with indefiniteness, required after bi- and marking the noun as 'some (unspecified) part.'
16.root: ب-ع-ض (b-ʿ-ḍ) — a part, portion, or some of a whole

17.meaning: '…and they want / intend / desire.' The joining word 'and' plus a third-person plural present verb of willing — to seek after something and aim one's intention toward it.
17.grammar: An ongoing/future verb joined by 'wa-' ('and'). The 'yu-' prefix points to a third-person subject; the '-ūna' ending makes it 'they' (masculine plural) and, by keeping its final 'na', marks a plain factual statement ('they want') rather than a wish or command form.

18.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
18.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

19.meaning: Present/future verb (reflexive form), third person plural: 'they take for themselves, adopt, choose.' It denotes taking something on as one's own — selecting it and making it one's possession or position.
19.grammar: An ongoing/future verb in a reflexive pattern (taking something for oneself). The 'ya-' prefix marks a third-person subject and the long '-ū' ending makes it 'they' (masculine plural). The prefix yā' here carries a shadda (doubling), which arises when a preceding word's final 'n' assimilates into it. The bare '-ū' (no final 'n') is the form used after particles meaning 'that they…' or in negative/command constructions.
19.root: أ-خ-ذ (ʾ-kh-dh) — to take, seize, grasp

20.meaning: Between; in the midst of two things. An adverb of place marking the space separating or lying among parties or points.
20.grammar: An adverb of place ('between'). It always ends in -a and grammatically governs what follows it, putting the following noun(s) into the genitive 'of' relationship. It does not change to show 'the' or a case of its own; the fixed -a is simply how this word is formed.
20.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction, what lies between

21.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
21.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

22.meaning: A way, path, road, or means — a route to a destination, hence also a way or means of accomplishing something.
22.grammar: A singular noun. The '-an' ending is accusative and indefinite: the accusative case commonly marks the direct object of a verb, and the final 'n' sound marks it indefinite ('a way'). It denotes a path one travels or a means to an end.

1.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'those' — pointing to people or things that are distant or already known. It singles out a group ('those ones', 'it is those who').
1.grammar: A plural demonstrative pronoun, 'those'. It is fixed in form (no case endings). The -ka element signals distance/remoteness, pointing to something far off or notable. It can refer to people of either gender.

2.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (masculine plural). Standing on its own, it typically adds emphasis or marks the group out as the focus ('they, specifically', 'it is they who').
2.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It takes no case endings; the base is hum, and the final vowel appears as -u (humu) as a connecting vowel to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a definite article. Standing alone, it commonly emphasises or isolates the subject.

3.meaning: Definite plural noun/participle: 'the disbelievers, those who reject faith' — those who cover over and deny the truth. The pattern names a whole group defined by this attribute.
3.grammar: A definite active participle ('the rejecters'). The '-ūna' ending is the masculine sound plural in the nominative (subject) case — the form a word takes when it is the doer of an action or the subject of a sentence ('the disbelievers [are/do]…').
3.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover over, reject, disbelieve

4.meaning: A right, a due, or an obligation — that which is true, real, and rightfully owed; an established duty. As an adverbial accusative it conveys "as a duty/obligation, in truth, bindingly."
4.grammar: A noun in the indefinite accusative. The '-an' (nunation on the fatḥa, with a following alif) often functions adverbially here — "as a binding duty" or "in truth" — describing the manner or affirming the statement.
4.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — to be true, right, established; truth, right

5.meaning: And We have made ready — to prepare, arrange, and set something in store beforehand so it stands waiting.
5.grammar: A past-tense verb (form VIII) prefixed with 'wa' (and). The 't' in the stem is the form VIII infix, not a root letter. The suffix '-nā' is the subject ending meaning 'we (did it),' marking a completed action performed by a first-person plural — an act already accomplished.
5.root: ع-د-د (ʿ-d-d) — counting, reckoning; readying and setting in store (form VIII اعتدّ, with the doubled dāl, from this root)

6.meaning: A three-part word: 'for' + 'the' + 'those who cover up the truth / reject faith.' The base noun denotes the kāfir — one who disbelieves, denies, and ungratefully conceals the truth and Allah's favor. With 'for,' it marks them as the ones for whom something is intended.
6.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('for/to') joined to a definite plural noun, masculine. The '-īna' ending is the sound masculine plural in its genitive/accusative (oblique) form, here required because it follows the preposition 'li-'. The whole denotes 'for the disbelievers.'
6.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal, disbelieve, be ungrateful

7.meaning: 'A punishment / torment.' A noun naming chastisement or painful suffering inflicted as a penalty.
7.grammar: A masculine noun. The -an ending marks it as indefinite ('a punishment') and in the accusative case — the form a noun takes as the object of a verb or as the thing being described/quantified.

8.meaning: Disgracing and degrading — that which humiliates and brings abasement, stripping away honor and dignity.
8.grammar: An active participle (form IV) naming what causes the action: 'something that humiliates.' The final '-an' (tanwīn fatḥa) marks the indefinite accusative case, used for an object or as a describing word in that case, giving 'a humiliating (one).'
8.root: ه-و-ن (h-w-n) — lowliness, disgrace; to abase or render contemptible

1.meaning: 'And those who': a connective phrase introducing a specified group of people (masculine plural) about whom something will be said. It links them to what came before.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'), which is masculine plural. A relative pronoun stands for a group and is normally followed by a clause describing them. Its form does not change for case; it stays alladhīna whatever its grammatical role.

2.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
2.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.
2.root: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — safety, security, trust, faith

3.meaning: A phrase 'in Allah / by Allah', combining the preposition 'with/in/by' and the divine name Allah, the proper name of the One God.
3.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with, by means of') prefixed to the divine name Allah. A preposition always forces the following noun into the genitive case, which is why Allah here ends in -i. With verbs of believing, bi- conveys the object of faith — to believe IN.
3.root: — (Allah is the proper name of God and is not derived from a triliteral root in the usual sense)

4.meaning: A combination 'and His messengers' — 'and' + 'messengers' + 'His'. Messengers are those sent by Allah to convey His revelation to humankind.
4.grammar: The prefix wa- is the connective 'and'. 'rusul' is the plural 'messengers'. The -i before the pronoun is genitive, used after prepositions or to show possession; with attached 'hi' ('His') it means 'His messengers'. The -hi ('His') indicates a single male/divine possessor.

5.meaning: 'And not' — the conjunction wa- ('and') joined to lam, a particle that negates a verb and pushes its meaning into the completed past ('did not …').
5.grammar: A connector wa- ('and') plus the negative particle lam. Lam negates a following present-tense verb but turns its sense into the past: 'has not / did not …'. It also causes that verb to take the jussive (clipped) ending.

6.meaning: Present/future verb (intensive form), third person plural: 'they make a distinction, separate, divide between things.' The doubled middle root letter conveys deliberately splitting apart or treating items separately.
6.grammar: An ongoing/future verb in the intensive (doubled) pattern, adding force to 'separate'. The 'yu-' prefix points to a third-person subject and the long '-ū' ending makes it 'they' (masculine plural). The bare '-ū' (no final 'n') is the form used after particles meaning 'that they…' or in negative/command constructions.
6.root: ف-ر-ق (f-r-q) — to separate, divide, distinguish

7.meaning: Between; in the midst of two things. An adverb of place marking the space separating or lying among parties or points.
7.grammar: An adverb of place ('between'). It always ends in -a and grammatically governs what follows it, putting the following noun(s) into the genitive 'of' relationship. It does not change to show 'the' or a case of its own; the fixed -a is simply how this word is formed.
7.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction, what lies between

8.meaning: One; anyone; a single individual. Often used in negative or conditional contexts to mean 'anyone (at all)'.
8.grammar: An indefinite noun in the genitive case. The -in ending combines the genitive marker -i (the form taken after a preposition or in a possessive link, '… of …') with nunation (-n), the sign of an indefinite 'a / any'.

9.meaning: 'Among them / from them / some of them' — the preposition 'min' ('from, of, among') joined to the attached pronoun 'hum' ('them').
9.grammar: The preposition 'min' ('from / of / among') with the attached pronoun 'hum' ('them'), referring to a masculine plural group. Together they often express 'part of them' or 'some among them'.

10.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'those' — pointing to people or things that are distant or already known. It singles out a group ('those ones', 'it is those who').
10.grammar: A plural demonstrative pronoun, 'those'. It is fixed in form (no case endings). The -ka element signals distance/remoteness, pointing to something far off or notable. It can refer to people of either gender.

11.meaning: A future-marking particle meaning 'shall / will (eventually)'. Placed before a present-tense verb, it pushes the action into the future, often with a sense of a more distant or assured 'in time, it shall come to pass'.
11.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it has no case ending and never changes form). Its sole function is to mark futurity on the present-tense verb that follows it.

12.meaning: 'He gives / will give them.' A present-tense verb (causative form) meaning to bring or hand something to someone, with an attached object pronoun 'them.' The form means 'to cause to come to,' i.e. to grant or bestow.
12.grammar: An ongoing/future verb in the causative pattern ('cause to come' = give). The 'yu-' prefix marks the subject as 'he' (third-person masculine singular). The attached '-him' is an object pronoun meaning 'them,' the recipients of the giving.
12.root: أ-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (causative) to bring, give

13.meaning: 'Their rewards / their wages.' A noun naming recompense — the reward, wage, or compensation earned for deeds — with an attached 'their': 'their rewards.'
13.grammar: A plural noun meaning 'rewards/wages.' The -a ending is the accusative case, the form used when the word is the object of a verb (e.g., the thing given). The attached -hum means 'their,' referring to a group.

14.meaning: And he was / he became — a verb of being that places a subject in a past state or links it to a description in the past.
14.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'kāna' is a past-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular, meaning 'he was/became'; it commonly introduces a past condition and is typically followed by a noun describing the subject's state. The final -a marks completed past action by a single male.

15.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
15.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

16.meaning: A word meaning 'much-forgiving' or 'ever-forgiving' — an intensive form describing one whose forgiveness is abundant and constant. It is one of the qualities of Allah.
16.grammar: An intensive adjective on the pattern faʿūl, conveying that the quality is great in degree and repeated. The ending -an is the accusative case with tanwīn (the indefinite 'n' sound), written with a supporting alif; it is the form an indefinite word takes when it is, for example, a predicate of certain verbs/particles or otherwise placed in the object position.
16.root: غ-ف-ر (gh-f-r) — forgiving, covering over, pardoning

17.meaning: 'Most Merciful' / 'Ever-Merciful' — an intensive adjective describing one whose mercy is constant, deep, and abundantly poured out. As a divine attribute it points to Allah's enduring compassion toward His creation.
17.grammar: An intensive adjective on the faʿīl pattern, which signals an abundant, lasting quality ('ever-/most merciful'). The tanwīn fatḥ (-an) marks it as indefinite and accusative; here it stands as an accusative predicate complement (the quality affirmed of the one described). The shadda on the rāʾ (رَّ) reflects assimilation of a preceding definite article's lām (l + r → rr) at the word junction in recitation.

1.meaning: 'He asks you / will ask you.' A present-tense verb of asking or requesting with an attached object pronoun 'you,' meaning to put a question or demand to a single addressee.
1.grammar: An ongoing/future verb. The 'ya-' prefix marks the subject as 'he'; the '-u' is the plain present-tense ending signalling a factual statement. The attached '-ka' is an object pronoun meaning 'you' (a single male addressee), the one being asked.

2.meaning: A people or community defined by belonging — most literally a household or family, and by extension the folk or people associated with a thing, place, or way (as in 'the people of the Scripture/Book'). It denotes those who belong to or are at home with something.
2.grammar: A singular noun (used collectively). The final -u ending is nominative, the case that typically marks the subject or 'doer' of a sentence, or a thing being named or described.
2.root: ا-ه-ل (ʔ-h-l) — belonging, being settled, family/household

3.meaning: 'The Book / the Scripture' — a written record or revealed scripture; literally that which is written.
3.grammar: The definite article al- with the noun kitāb ('book, scripture'), itself a verbal noun from 'to write.' The -i ending is genitive, typically marking the word as following a preposition or standing in an 'of' relationship to a preceding noun.

4.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
4.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

5.meaning: Present/future verb (intensive form), second person: 'you send down / bring down,' especially in stages or portions. The doubled middle root letter suggests a sending-down that may be gradual or emphatic.
5.grammar: An ongoing/future verb in the intensive (doubled) pattern, hinting at a sending-down by degrees or with emphasis. The 'tu-' prefix marks the subject as 'you' (masculine singular). The final '-a' is the subjunctive ending, the form taken after particles meaning 'to / that,' giving the sense '…that you send down' or 'for you to send down.'

6.meaning: A compound meaning 'upon them' or 'against them': the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over, against') joined to the plural pronoun 'them'. It conveys something resting on, being incumbent upon, or weighing against a group.
6.grammar: ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay- before a pronoun. The suffix -him is the attached pronominal suffix for a masculine plural group ('them'); after a preposition it carries genitive/prepositional force, and the -i- vowel reflects its position after this preposition. Together they signal a relationship of something being over, upon, or burdensome to that group.
6.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

7.meaning: 'A writing / a prescribed decree' — that which is written down; by extension a fixed ordinance, an appointed term, or a binding decree.
7.grammar: An indefinite noun in the accusative case: the -an ending (the 'an' sound with nunation) marks the object of a verb or a related role, and signals an indefinite 'a writing/decree'. The pattern 'kitāb' is the verbal noun denoting a written thing.

8.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
8.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

9.meaning: The sky or heaven — the canopy overhead; the expanse above the earth, also that which is elevated or raised over something. With the definite article it means 'the sky / the heaven'.
9.grammar: A noun with the definite article al- ('the'), in the genitive marked by the -i ending. (The 'l' of al- assimilates in sound into the following 's', a 'sun letter', though it is still written.) The genitive -i ending typically appears after a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …').

10.meaning: A two-part connector: fa- means 'so', 'then', or 'and so', linking what follows as a result or consequence; qad before a past-tense verb intensifies it, conveying 'certainly', 'indeed', or 'already' — stressing that the action has truly and definitely occurred.
10.grammar: fa- is a connecting particle meaning 'so' or 'then', often marking a result. qad is a particle of emphasis; placed before a completed (past-tense) verb it affirms that the action has definitely or already happened. Neither part takes a case ending.

11.meaning: Past-tense verb, third person plural: 'they asked, requested, demanded.' A completed act of putting a question or making a demand by a group.
11.grammar: A completed-action (past) verb. The '-ū' ending (written with a silent trailing alif) marks the subject as 'they' (masculine plural) — the group who did the asking. Past tense presents the action as already finished.

12.meaning: Mūsā (Moses), the prophet — a proper name.
12.grammar: A proper name of non-Arabic origin. It is indeclinable — its ending (the long final 'ā') does not change to show case — so the same form serves whether it functions as subject, object, or after a preposition.

13.meaning: Comparative/superlative adjective: 'greater, bigger' or 'greatest, biggest.' Built on the 'more/most' pattern from the root sense of largeness, weight, or importance.
13.grammar: An elative adjective (the 'more / most' pattern, like 'greater'). The final '-a' is the accusative case ending: it typically marks the word as the object of a verb, or as a descriptive complement, and is also the case this fixed (diptote) pattern takes where others would show '-i'.
13.root: ك-ب-ر (k-b-r) — to be great, large, weighty

14.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
14.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

15.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
