15.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

16.meaning: '…so / then they said.' Combines the connector 'so/then' (showing result or sequence) with a past-tense verb of speaking, third person plural — a completed act of saying by a group.
16.grammar: A completed-action (past) verb prefixed with 'fa-' ('so/then'), which links it to what precedes as a result or next step. The '-ū' ending (with silent trailing alif) marks the subject as 'they' (masculine plural).
16.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, speak, utter

17.meaning: Command (imperative) verb with attached object: 'show us! / let us see!' A request that the speaker(s) be made to see or be shown something, addressed to a single person.
17.grammar: A command (imperative) verb in the causative pattern ('cause to see' = show), addressed to a single male. The attached '-nā' is an object pronoun meaning 'us,' the ones asking to be shown. Imperatives express a request, demand, or order.
17.root: ر-أ-ي (r-ʾ-y) — to see, perceive; (causative) to show

18.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
18.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

19.meaning: 'Openly / plainly / manifestly' — out in the open, visibly and publicly, as opposed to hidden or secret. From a root meaning to be loud, open, or out in the open, it describes something done or seen openly and unmistakably.
19.grammar: A noun used adverbially. The ending -an (nunation on the accusative) is the classic way Arabic turns a noun into an adverb of manner — 'in an open way, openly, manifestly'. The -an both marks it indefinite and signals this adverbial 'how' function.
19.root: ج-ه-ر (j-h-r) — to be open, loud, out in the open, manifest

20.meaning: '…so it seized / struck / took hold of them.' The connector 'so/then' plus a past-tense verb of seizing with a feminine-singular subject and an attached object 'them' — a completed act of being gripped or overtaken (as by a punishment or force).
20.grammar: A completed-action (past) verb prefixed with 'fa-' ('so/then'). The '-t' marks the subject as feminine singular ('she/it'). The attached '-hum(u)' is an object pronoun meaning 'them'; its vowel is lengthened to '-humu' to ease pronunciation before the next word.

21.meaning: 'The thunderbolt / the stunning blast' — a sudden overwhelming strike (a thunderclap, lightning bolt, or stunning shock) that stuns or strikes down. From a root for a crashing, stupefying blow.
21.grammar: A noun (active participle in form) with the definite article al- ('the') and the feminine ending -a(t). The final -u is the nominative ending, the case used for the subject of a sentence — so this names the thing performing or undergoing the main action as subject.
21.root: ص-ع-ق (ṣ-ʿ-q) — to strike with a thunderbolt, to stun, to fall senseless

22.meaning: '…because of / by their wrongdoing.' Combines the preposition 'bi-' (here giving a cause, 'because of') with the noun 'wrongdoing/injustice' and an attached pronoun 'their.'
22.grammar: A noun governed by the preposition 'bi-' ('by / because of'). The '-i' vowel is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a following word. The attached '-him' is a possessive pronoun meaning 'their.'

23.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
23.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

24.meaning: Past-tense verb (reflexive form), third person plural: 'they took for themselves, adopted, chose.' A completed act of taking something on as one's own.
24.grammar: A completed-action (past) verb in a reflexive pattern (taking something for oneself). The '-ū' ending (with silent trailing alif) marks the subject as 'they' (masculine plural). The opening 'i-' is a helping vowel that lets the cluster of consonants be pronounced.

25.meaning: 'The calf' — a young bovine; the offspring of a cow.
25.grammar: A definite noun ('the calf'). The '-a' ending is the accusative case, which commonly marks the direct object of a verb (the thing taken or acted upon).

26.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
26.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
26.root: — (preposition)

27.meaning: A noun/adverb meaning 'after' — the time or position following something; 'afterward', 'following'.
27.grammar: An adverb of time functioning as a noun, here in the genitive case marked by the final -i. The genitive ending typically appears after a preposition or as the second term of a construct ('after THE …'), linking 'after' to a following noun to specify what it comes after.
27.root: ب-ع-د (b-ʿ-d) — to be after, to follow, distance in place or time

28.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
28.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

29.meaning: 'It / she came to them'. A past-tense verb of coming or arriving, with a feminine singular subject ('it/she'), and an attached pronoun 'them' as the ones reached.
29.grammar: 'jāa' is a past-tense verb 'came'. The '-t' suffix marks a feminine singular subject ('she' or a feminine 'it'). The attached '-hum' means 'them' (masculine plural) as the object reached; its vowel appears as '-humu' to ease pronunciation before a following word.
29.root: ج-ي-ء (j-y-ʾ) — to come, to arrive, to bring

30.meaning: The clear proofs / evident signs — plainly manifest, self-evident pieces of evidence that make the truth unmistakable.

parts.en: clear proofs / evident signs (the final -u is the nominative case ending, marking the subject)

30.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun (with 'al-' = 'the') meaning 'clear proofs.' The plural ending 'āt' marks a feminine plural, and the final -u is the nominative case ending, which typically marks the noun as the subject/doer of a sentence ('… the clear proofs came to you'). The pattern 'bayyina' denotes something that makes things plainly evident.
30.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — clarity, distinctness; to make plain or evident

31.meaning: '…so / then we pardoned / forgave.' The connector 'so/then' plus a past-tense verb of pardoning, first person plural — a completed act of wiping away an offence and forgoing punishment.
31.grammar: A completed-action (past) verb prefixed with 'fa-' ('so/then'), linking it as a result or next step. The '-nā' ending marks the subject as 'we' (first-person plural), the ones doing the pardoning.
31.root: ع-ف-و (ʿ-f-w) — to pardon, efface, forgo

32.meaning: A preposition meaning 'on behalf of,' 'for,' 'about,' or 'away from.' It often conveys removing a burden from someone or acting in their place.

parts.en: on behalf of / for / away from

32.grammar: A preposition (a linking particle). It governs the noun that follows it, putting that noun into the genitive case. It does not change form.

33.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
33.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

34.meaning: "and We gave / brought" — to give, bring, or grant something to someone.
34.grammar: The wa- prefix is "and." This is a past-tense causative verb meaning "to give/bring (to someone)." The -nā ending marks a first-person plural subject ("we") who completed the action.
34.root: ا-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (causative) to give, bring

35.meaning: Mūsā (Moses) — the proper name of the prophet. As a name it has no Arabic root meaning; it is a non-inflecting (indeclinable) noun whose ending does not change for case.
35.grammar: A proper name ending in a fixed long -ā (written as alif maqṣūra). It is fully indeclinable (invariable): the final -ā never changes, so the word shows no case distinction at all — it looks and sounds identical whether subject, object, or possessor. (This is unlike a diptote, which still alternates between two case vowels; here there is no alternation.)

36.meaning: Authority, sanction, or compelling proof — power or warrant given to back something up, whether kingly authority or a decisive argument. 'Sulṭān' is authorizing power or evidence.
36.grammar: A single noun ('authority') carrying the accusative indefinite ending -an (tanwīn al-naṣb). This one ending does two things at once: the -a marks the accusative case (typically the direct object of a verb), and the final -n sound (nunation) shows the noun is indefinite ('an authority / any warrant'). The nunation is a diacritic on the case vowel, not a separable suffix, so the word stays one undivided token.

37.meaning: An adjective meaning 'clear, plain, manifest' — describing something that is obvious and self-evident, or that makes things clear.
37.grammar: An active participle of form IV (mubīn), 'one that is manifest / makes clear.' The mu- prefix forms the participle. The final -an (tanwīn fatḥa) is the indefinite accusative ending ('a clear one'), used here to agree with a preceding masculine accusative noun it describes.

1.meaning: "And We raised / lifted up" — to raise, lift, or elevate something physically or in rank. The form carries a 'we' subject, opened by the conjunction 'and'.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb with the attached subject suffix '-nā' ('we'), marking a completed action done by a group (or the majestic 'We'). Prefixed with the conjunction 'and'.

2.meaning: 'above them / over them.' Combines the location word 'fawq' ('above, over, on top of') with an attached pronoun 'them.' It indicates a position higher than or superior to something.
2.grammar: A noun of place used adverbially. The '-a' ending is the accusative, the case used for adverbs answering 'where?' ('above'). The attached '-hum(u)' means 'them'; its vowel is lengthened to '-humu' to ease pronunciation before the next word.
2.root: ف-و-ق (f-w-q) — to be above, over, superior

3.meaning: "The mount / mountain" — al-Ṭūr; the word denotes a mountain and is especially used as a name for Mount Sinai.
3.grammar: A masculine singular noun with the definite article 'the' (whose lām assimilates into the following ṭ, shown by the shadda). The final -a is the accusative case ending, typically marking the word as the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon).

4.meaning: '…by / because of their covenant.' Combines the preposition 'bi-' (here 'by' or 'because of') with the noun 'mīthāq' — a firm, solemn pledge or binding agreement — and an attached pronoun 'their.'
4.grammar: A noun governed by the preposition 'bi-' ('by / because of'). The '-i' vowel is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a following word. The attached '-him' is a possessive pronoun meaning 'their.'
4.root: و-ث-ق (w-th-q) — to bind firmly, trust, make a pact

5.meaning: And We said — a declaration of speech attributed to a 'We' (the divine majestic plural).
5.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. The stem is the past-tense verb 'to say', and the attached suffix -nā means 'we', marking the speakers as the doers of a completed act of saying.

6.meaning: To them / for them — the preposition li- ('to, for') joined to the pronoun 'them'. It expresses that something is directed toward, belongs to, or is for the benefit of a group.
6.grammar: The preposition li- ('to/for') combined with the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). When li- takes a pronoun its vowel becomes 'la-'. The final -u here is a connecting vowel added to ease pronunciation before a following word; it carries no case meaning of its own.

7.meaning: 'Enter!' — a command to a group to go into or enter a place.
7.grammar: An imperative (command) verb. The -ū ending directs the command at a group ('you all, enter!'). The initial alif is a helping-vowel prefix that lets the word begin (pronounced 'u-' here), needed because the stem would otherwise start with a vowelless consonant. The silent alif after the wāw spells the plural ending.

8.meaning: 'The gate' / 'the door' — an entrance, doorway, or gateway. Carries the definite article 'the'.
8.grammar: A definite noun ('the gate'). The -a ending is accusative, the case typically marking the direct object of a verb (the thing entered or acted upon). The al- prefix makes it 'the' specific gate.

9.meaning: 'Prostrating' / 'in prostration' — bowing down low with the face to the ground, the posture of deepest humility and worship. A plural describing a group in that humble, bowed state.
9.grammar: A plural active descriptor ('those prostrating'). The -an ending is the indefinite accusative, which here works adverbially — describing the manner or state in which the subject acts (i.e. doing something 'while prostrating'). The doubled middle letter marks the intensive plural pattern used for a group performing the action.
9.root: س-ج-د (s-j-d) — prostration, bowing down in worship

10.meaning: '…and we said.' The joining word 'and' plus a past-tense verb of speaking, first person plural — a completed act of saying or declaring by 'us.'
10.grammar: A completed-action (past) verb joined by 'wa-' ('and'). The '-nā' ending marks the subject as 'we' (first-person plural), the ones who spoke.

11.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
11.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

12.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
12.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

13.meaning: A second-person plural verb meaning 'you overstep, transgress, or go beyond the proper limit.' The underlying sense is to exceed a boundary or violate a rule that has been set, often in the context of breaking a divinely-fixed limit (such as the Sabbath restriction). In this jussive/subjunctive shape it expresses an action being warned against or negated.

parts.en: plural ending 'you all', shortened from the indicative -ūna

13.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) verb. The ta- prefix marks a second-person subject ('you'), and the long -ū plural ending marks more than one male/mixed addressee. The dropped final nūn (the form is -ū rather than -ūna) shows the verb is in the jussive or subjunctive mood — the shape typically used after a negative/prohibition particle or a conditional, i.e. 'that you not transgress' or 'do not transgress.'
13.root: ع-د-و (ʿ-d-w) — to overstep a limit, transgress, show enmity

14.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
14.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

15.meaning: The Sabbath — the sacred day of rest and worship, on which ordinary labour was set aside. Here in an 'of/after a preposition' relationship.

parts.en: Sabbath / day of rest (with the article's 'l' assimilated, plus the genitive vowel -i)

15.grammar: A definite noun: 'al-' is 'the', and because the next letter is a 'sun letter' (س), the article's 'l' sound merges into it, giving 'as-sabt'. The final -i is the genitive case vowel sitting on the noun's own last root letter (ت), not a separate suffix; this vowel appears when the noun follows a preposition or is linked to a preceding noun in an 'of' relationship.
15.root: س-ب-ت (s-b-t) — to rest, cease (from work); the Sabbath

16.meaning: 'And We took / received / seized.' A first-person plural past-tense verb from the root meaning 'to take.' It conveys a completed act of taking hold of something — and idiomatically, of taking a pledge or covenant FROM someone, i.e. binding them to it.
16.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb expressing a completed action. The attached -nā ending is the first-person plural subject 'we,' so the whole word means 'we took.' The prefixed wa- simply joins this statement to what precedes it ('and').
16.root: ا-خ-ذ (ʾ-kh-dh) — to take, seize, take hold of

17.meaning: From them / among them — the preposition min ('from, out of, part of') joined to the pronoun 'them' (a group of males or a mixed group).
17.grammar: The preposition min ('from / among / part of') with the attached third-person masculine plural pronoun -hum ('them'). Pronouns after a preposition are in the genitive; the combination expresses origin, partition ('some of them'), or belonging to that group.

18.meaning: A solemn binding pledge, a firm compact or covenant — a commitment that is firmly tied and confirmed between parties so that it must be honored.
18.grammar: A singular noun. The final -an (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('a covenant') and signals the accusative case — the form a noun takes when it is the direct object of a verb or otherwise grammatically governed in that position.
18.root: و-ث-ق (w-th-q) — to be firm, bind tightly, trust; make a firm pact

19.meaning: Thick, dense, heavy, and severe — describing something coarse and weighty rather than light or flimsy. Applied to a pledge it means a grave and solemn one; applied generally it suggests harshness or toughness.
19.grammar: An adjective on the intensive faʿīl pattern, conveying a strong or established quality. The final -an (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite and accusative — the case that typically matches a noun it describes when that noun stands as an object.
19.root: غ-ل-ظ (gh-l-ẓ) — thickness, coarseness, severity

1.meaning: A chain of small words meaning roughly 'so/then, by/through what...' — introducing a result and pointing to the means or cause of something.
1.grammar: A cluster of three particles. The fa- links to what precedes as a consequence ('so, then'); bi- ('by/through/with') indicates the means or cause and governs a genitive; mā here serves as 'what / that which' (and is often partly redundant, adding a nuance of emphasis or vagueness). Together: 'so, by/through that which...'

2.meaning: 'Their breaking / violating / undoing.' A verbal noun (the act of breaking) naming the rupture or annulment of something binding — typically the breaking apart of a pledge, treaty, or covenant — combined with the pronoun 'their.'
2.grammar: A verbal noun (naming an action, like English '-ing') with a possessive pronoun 'their' attached. The -i vowel before the pronoun is the genitive case, the form a noun takes when it follows a preposition or is the object of an oath/cause — broadly signalling 'because of / on account of their breaking.'
2.root: ن-ق-ض (n-q-ḍ) — to break, undo, dissolve (something firmly fastened)

3.meaning: 'Their covenant / solemn pledge.' A noun denoting a firm, binding agreement or compact entered into with full solemnity, joined to the pronoun 'their.' The word carries the weight of a formal, witnessed undertaking.
3.grammar: A noun with the possessive pronoun 'their' attached. The -a vowel before the pronoun is the accusative case, the form typically used when the noun is the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon) — i.e. the covenant as the thing being broken or taken.
3.root: و-ث-ق (w-th-q) — to bind firmly, trust, make secure; hence a binding pact

4.meaning: 'And their disbelief / rejection of faith.' The verbal noun naming the act of disbelieving — covering ingratitude toward Allah and the active rejection or denial of truth and revelation — together with the pronoun 'their.'
4.grammar: A verbal noun with 'their' attached, prefixed by 'and.' The -i vowel before the pronoun is the genitive case — the form used after prepositions or in a chain of causes ('because of … and because of their disbelief').
4.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover/conceal; hence to deny faith, reject, be ungrateful

5.meaning: 'With/in the signs of…' — the preposition bi- joined to a plural noun meaning 'signs', 'tokens', or 'verses': evidences that point to a truth beyond themselves.
5.grammar: bi- is a preposition meaning 'with/in' and always takes the genitive. āyāt is a sound feminine plural; its -i ending here is genitive, the case required after the preposition, and it typically also links to a following noun ('signs OF …').
5.root: ء-ي-ي / ء-و-ي (ʾ-y-y) — a sign, mark, or token

6.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
6.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

7.meaning: 'And their killing / slaying.' The verbal noun naming the act of killing, combined with the pronoun 'their' (i.e. the killing committed by them).
7.grammar: A verbal noun with 'their' attached, prefixed by 'and.' The -i vowel marks the genitive case (after a preposition or in a list of causes). The pronoun is voiced -himu (with a final -u) rather than -him purely to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a connecting/joining hamza.
7.root: ق-ت-ل (q-t-l) — to kill, slay, put to death

8.meaning: 'The prophets' — the plural of 'prophet,' one who brings tidings and announcements from Allah; a human being chosen to convey divine guidance.
8.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural noun made definite by al- ('the'). The final -a ending is accusative, the case that commonly marks the direct object — the thing being acted upon by a verb.
8.root: ن-ب-ا (n-b-ʾ) — news, tidings, announcement (a prophet conveys tidings)

9.meaning: 'Without' or 'other than' — the preposition bi- joined to ghayr, a noun meaning 'other than / not / lacking', together conveying the absence of something ('with no …', 'wrongfully').
9.grammar: bi- is a preposition that takes the genitive; ghayr is a noun of exception/negation ('other than'). Its -i ending is genitive (required after bi-) and it also links to a following noun in a possessive 'of' relationship, so 'bi-ghayri X' means 'without X / other than X'.
9.root: غ-ي-ر (gh-y-r) — otherness, difference, being other than

10.meaning: Truth / right / a just claim: that which is real, true, and rightfully due — what genuinely is the case, and what is owed by justice. As an indefinite noun it means 'a right' or 'rightfully', with no article.
10.grammar: An indefinite noun. The ending -in carries two signals at once: the final -n (called nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a right', not 'the right'), and the -i vowel is the genitive case, the case used after prepositions or to link one noun to another ('… of …').
10.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, reality, what is due/right

11.meaning: 'And their saying / utterance / statement.' The verbal noun naming the act of speaking or what is said, joined to the pronoun 'their.'
11.grammar: A verbal noun with 'their' attached, prefixed by 'and.' The -i vowel is the genitive case (used after prepositions or within a chain of causes). The doubled w (wwa) reflects the wa- assimilating to the preceding word in recitation.

12.meaning: Hearts — the seat of understanding, feeling, intention, and faith in a person. In Qur'anic usage the heart is the organ of comprehension and moral life, not merely the source of emotion.
12.grammar: A plural noun ('hearts') with the -u nominative ending, marking it as a subject. The attached -nā means 'our,' showing the hearts belong to the speakers.
12.root: ق-ل-ب (q-l-b) — to turn over; the heart

13.meaning: Wrapped up, covered, or sealed — as if enclosed in a covering that keeps something out. Said of hearts, it conveys being shut off and impervious, unable to receive or absorb what reaches them.
13.grammar: A plural descriptive noun ('wrapped/covered ones') with the -un ending, the nominative indefinite case, which typically marks a subject or predicate (what is being said about something). The form describes a state of being enveloped or sealed.
13.root: غ-ل-ف (gh-l-f) — to wrap, cover, sheathe; a cover/wrapping

14.meaning: A particle of retraction meaning 'rather,' 'no, but,' or 'nay' — it cancels or sets aside what was just said and shifts to a corrected or contrasting statement that follows.
14.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it never changes form). Its function is to redirect the discourse: it dismisses a prior idea and introduces what is actually the case.

15.meaning: 'He sealed / set a seal upon.' A third-person masculine singular past verb meaning to imprint or stamp shut, as a seal closes a letter so nothing can enter or leave. Applied to the heart, it conveys that it has been closed off so that guidance no longer penetrates it.
15.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb, third-person masculine singular ('he … ed'). The final -a is the standard past-tense ending for a single male subject; the subject 'he' is built into the verb and not written separately.

16.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
16.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.
16.root: — (proper divine name)

17.meaning: 'On it / upon it / over it' — the preposition 'alā ('on, upon, against') joined to the pronoun 'it/her', referring to a single feminine or grammatically feminine thing.
17.grammar: 'ʿalā' is a preposition meaning 'on/upon/over'; its ending shifts to -ay when a pronoun is attached. The suffix -hā is the object pronoun for a single feminine (or feminine-gender) thing. Together they mean 'on it'. Words after a preposition stand in the genitive, though attached pronouns like -hā do not visibly change form.

18.meaning: On account of disbelief or ingratitude — the act of covering over and rejecting truth, refusing faith. Kufr is both the denial of belief and ingratitude toward what is given.
18.grammar: A noun ('disbelief') preceded by the preposition bi- ('with/because of') and ending in -i, the genitive case that regularly follows a preposition. The attached -him means 'their,' linking the disbelief to a group.
18.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; disbelief, ingratitude

19.meaning: A two-part word: the connective particle 'fa-' meaning 'so', 'then', or 'therefore' (drawing a consequence from what precedes), joined to 'lā', the particle of negation/prohibition. Together they convey 'so do not …' or 'so there is no …'.
19.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that links a clause to what came before and often signals a result or consequence. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a present-tense verb it commonly forms a prohibition ('do not …') or a simple negation ('not'). It carries no ending of its own.

20.meaning: 'They believe / they have faith' — to affirm something as true with trusting inner conviction and to feel secure in it. The verb carries both believing and being at peace through that belief; in religious use it is to commit oneself in faith.
20.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb, masculine plural. The yu-…-una frame means 'they (men, or a mixed group) do' the action now or habitually. The retained final -na marks the indicative (a plain, unqualified statement) — 'they believe' — as opposed to forms where that -na drops. The verb is Form IV (amana), used intransitively here meaning simply 'to believe / to have faith'.

21.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
21.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

22.meaning: 'Few / little / a small amount.' An adjective describing something small in quantity, number, or degree — the opposite of much or many. It can also function adverbially in the sense of 'only a little' or 'rarely.'
22.grammar: An adjective/noun carrying the -an ending (accusative with nunation, 'tanwīn'). This ending often marks the direct object, but with words of quantity it commonly works adverbially — 'to a small degree,' 'only a little,' 'but few.'
22.root: ق-ل-ل (q-l-l) — to be few, little, scant

1.meaning: 'And for / because of their disbelief.' The verbal noun of disbelief — covering rejection of faith and ingratitude toward Allah — introduced by the preposition 'with/because of' and joined to the pronoun 'their.'
1.grammar: A verbal noun preceded by the preposition bi- ('with/because of') and followed by 'their,' all prefixed with 'and.' The preposition bi- forces the genitive case, which is why the noun shows the -i vowel before the pronoun; the sense is causal: 'and because of their disbelief.'
1.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover/conceal; hence to deny faith, be ungrateful

2.meaning: 'And their saying / utterance / statement.' The verbal noun naming the act of speaking or what is said, joined to the pronoun 'their.'
2.grammar: A verbal noun with 'their' attached, prefixed by 'and.' The -i vowel is the genitive case, the form used after prepositions or within a chain of causes ('and because of their saying').
2.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, speak, utter

3.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
3.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

4.meaning: "Maryam" — the personal name Mary, the mother of the prophet Jesus.
4.grammar: A proper name (feminine, foreign origin). It is diptote: it takes no -n (nunation), and in the genitive and accusative it ends in -a rather than -i, so the -a ending shown serves for both object and "of" positions.

5.meaning: A noun meaning 'a false accusation, slander, calumny' — a brazen lie told against someone that leaves the hearer dumbfounded.
5.grammar: A verbal noun. The final -an (tanwīn fatḥa) is the indefinite accusative; on a noun like this it commonly works adverbially to describe the manner of an action ('slanderously,' 'by way of slander') or stands as an object.
5.root: ب-ه-ت (b-h-t) — being struck dumb; slander, brazen lying

6.meaning: 'Great, immense, mighty, momentous.' It describes something vast in size, weight, or seriousness, and is often used of grave or awe-inspiring matters.
6.grammar: An adjective on the intensive faʿīl pattern. The -an ending is the indefinite accusative ('a great …'), commonly marking an adjective that agrees with an indefinite accusative noun it describes, or the object of a verb.
6.root: ع-ظ-م (ʿ-ẓ-m) — to be great, immense

1.meaning: 'And their saying / utterance / statement.' The verbal noun naming the act of speaking or what is said, joined to the pronoun 'their.'
1.grammar: A verbal noun with 'their' attached, prefixed by 'and.' The -i vowel is the genitive case (used after prepositions or within a chain of causes). The doubled w (wwa) reflects the wa- assimilating to the preceding word in recitation.

2.meaning: A two-part expression: an emphatic particle that strongly affirms and confirms a statement ('truly, indeed, certainly'), fused with the attached pronoun 'we.' Together: 'truly we…' / 'indeed we…'
2.grammar: The particle inna gives strong emphasis and certainty to the clause it opens. The attached -ā is the pronoun 'we,' serving as the subject being emphasized: 'truly we…'

3.meaning: 'We killed / slew.' A first-person plural past-tense verb from the root 'to kill,' expressing a completed act of putting someone to death as claimed by the speakers.
3.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb. The attached -nā ending is the first-person plural subject 'we,' so the word means 'we killed.' It reports a completed action claimed by the speakers.
3.root: ق-ت-ل (q-t-l) — to kill, slay, put to death

4.meaning: 'The Messiah / the Anointed One' — the title of Jesus son of Mary (ʿĪsā). Derived from a root meaning 'to wipe/anoint,' it designates the one specially anointed or set apart. The al- ('the') marks it as the well-known, definite title.
4.grammar: A definite noun (title) made definite by al- ('the'). The final -a is the accusative case, the form used when the noun is the direct object of a verb (the one being acted upon).
4.root: م-س-ح (m-s-ḥ) — to wipe, anoint, stroke; hence 'the anointed one'

5.meaning: "Isa" — the personal name of the prophet Jesus, son of Mary.
5.grammar: A proper name (a foreign/non-Arabic name). It is fully indeclinable: its ending does not change for case, so it stays the same as subject, object, or after a preposition.

6.meaning: "son" — a male child or descendant.
6.grammar: A noun beginning with a helping (elidable) vowel. The -a ending is accusative, which marks the word as the object of a verb or as an appositive describing a preceding accusative noun. When placed between two names, it functions as "son of …"
6.root: ب-ن-ي (b-n-y) — to build; son, offspring

7.meaning: "Maryam" — the personal name Mary, the mother of the prophet Jesus.
7.grammar: A proper name (feminine, foreign origin). It is diptote: it takes no -n (nunation), and in the genitive and accusative it ends in -a rather than -i, so the -a ending shown serves for both object and "of" positions.

8.meaning: 'Messenger / envoy' — one who is sent with a message. In religious usage it denotes a prophet entrusted by Allah to convey His revelation to people.
8.grammar: A noun. The final -a is the accusative case, the form a noun takes as the direct object of a verb, or — as often with this word — standing in apposition (an explanatory restatement) to another accusative noun before it.
8.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — to send; hence a messenger/envoy

9.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
9.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

10.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
10.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

11.meaning: 'They killed him.' A third-person plural past-tense verb 'they killed' with the object pronoun 'him' attached — reporting (or, in the Qur'anic context, denying) a completed act of slaying a specific male.
11.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'), and the attached -hu is the object 'him' (the one killed). So the verb itself carries both 'they' (doers) and 'him' (the one acted upon).
11.root: ق-ت-ل (q-t-l) — to kill, slay, put to death

12.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
12.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

13.meaning: 'They crucified him.' A third-person plural past-tense verb 'they crucified' with 'him' attached — to fasten or hang someone upon a cross or pole, here reported of a specific male.
13.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb. The -ū ending is the third-person masculine plural subject ('they'), and the attached -hu is the object 'him.' The word thus carries both the doers ('they') and the one acted upon ('him').
13.root: ص-ل-ب (ṣ-l-b) — to crucify, fasten upon a cross; (also: backbone, firmness)

14.meaning: 'But / however / yet' — a particle of correction and contrast that sets aside what came before and affirms something different instead.
14.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') attached to lākin ('but / however'). Lākin is a particle of rectification: it draws a contrast with, or corrects, the preceding idea and introduces an opposing or qualifying statement ('... but rather...').

15.meaning: 'It / he was made to resemble; a likeness was cast.' A passive past-tense verb from the root meaning 'to be alike.' It conveys that something was made ambiguous or counterfeit in appearance — a resemblance was presented so that one thing was mistaken for another.

parts.en: it/he was made to resemble (full passive verb)

15.grammar: A passive past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('it/he was …ed'). The vowel pattern u–i (shubbiha) is the hallmark of the passive voice — the subject is the one to whom something is done, with the doer left unnamed. The final -a is the standard past-tense ending.
15.root: ش-ب-ه (sh-b-h) — to resemble, be alike; hence to make ambiguous/counterfeit

16.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
16.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

17.meaning: 'And indeed' / 'and truly' — the joining word 'wa' ('and') attached to the emphatic particle 'inna', which introduces a statement and strongly affirms it, adding certainty like 'surely' or 'indeed'.
17.grammar: A connective 'wa' ('and') plus 'inna', a particle of emphasis that opens a nominal sentence. 'Inna' puts its following noun (the subject) into the accusative case while strongly affirming the truth of the statement.

18.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
18.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

19.meaning: A verb meaning 'they differed / disagreed / fell into dispute', also 'they varied, became diverse'. The Form VIII root expresses people taking divergent positions or one thing succeeding and differing from another.
19.grammar: Past-tense (perfect) verb (Form VIII), third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending marks a completed action done by 'they' (a masculine or mixed group); the silent alif written after it is a spelling convention, not pronounced.
19.root: خ-ل-ف (kh-l-f) — to come after, succeed, differ, be at variance

20.meaning: 'In it / in him' — the preposition 'in, inside, within' joined to a pronoun referring to a single masculine or neuter thing. It locates something inside or as part of that referent.
20.grammar: A preposition with an attached object pronoun. The pronoun -hi refers to one masculine (or grammatically masculine) thing and stands as the object of the preposition; its vowel is -i because attached pronouns take that shape after the long -i of fi. Together they answer 'in what?' or 'in whom?'.

21.meaning: A two-part expression meaning 'surely in / indeed within'. It joins an emphasis particle ('surely, indeed') with the preposition 'in', stressing that something is firmly located or contained inside.
21.grammar: The prefix la- is an emphatic particle ('surely, indeed') used to strengthen a statement. fī is a preposition ('in/within') and, like all prepositions, governs a following noun, putting it into the genitive case.

22.meaning: 'Doubt / uncertainty.' A noun for the wavering state of mind in which one is unsure and cannot settle on what is true — the opposite of firm certainty.
22.grammar: A noun with the -in ending (genitive with nunation, 'tanwīn'), marking it as indefinite ('a doubt / some doubt'). The genitive -i is the form taken after a preposition — typically conveying 'in doubt' or 'of doubt.'
22.root: ش-ك-ك (sh-k-k) — to doubt, be uncertain, waver

23.meaning: A prepositional phrase, 'from him/it' — indicating origin or source, that something proceeds out of him/it.
23.grammar: The preposition min ('from') with the attached pronoun -hu ('him/it', third-person masculine singular). As the object of a preposition the pronoun stands in the genitive; the combination indicates source or origin.

24.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
24.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

25.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
25.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

26.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
26.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

27.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
27.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

28.meaning: 'Knowledge.' A noun denoting sure, established knowing — to know a thing as it truly is. In its indefinite form it often appears in the sense 'any knowledge (at all).'
28.grammar: A noun with the -in ending (genitive with nunation, 'tanwīn'), marking it as indefinite ('any knowledge'). The genitive -i is the form used after a preposition such as 'of' or 'by' — e.g. 'of any knowledge.'
28.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know; knowledge, certainty

29.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
29.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

30.meaning: 'Following / pursuing / acting upon.' The verbal noun for the act of following something — going after it, conforming to it, or basing one's conduct on it (here, following mere conjecture rather than knowledge).
30.grammar: A verbal noun (naming an action). The final -a is the accusative case. This case commonly marks a direct object, and it is also the form used in an exception construction — 'they follow nothing except the following of conjecture.'
30.root: ت-ب-ع (t-b-ʿ) — to follow, pursue, go after

31.meaning: 'Conjecture / assumption / supposition.' A noun for an opinion or surmise that falls short of certain knowledge — a guess or probable belief. It can range from a strong impression down to baseless speculation, but in any case it is not firm, verified knowledge.
31.grammar: A definite noun made definite by al- ('the'). The final -i is the genitive case — the form used after a preposition or when one noun is possessed by another, i.e. linking it as '… of conjecture.'
31.root: ظ-ن-ن (ẓ-n-n) — to suppose, surmise, conjecture; opinion short of certainty

32.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
32.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

33.meaning: 'They killed him.' A third-person plural past-tense verb 'they killed' with the object pronoun 'him' attached — reporting (or, in the Qur'anic context, denying) a completed act of slaying a specific male.
33.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'), and the attached -hu is the object 'him' (the one killed). So the verb itself carries both 'they' (doers) and 'him' (the one acted upon).
33.root: ق-ت-ل (q-t-l) — to kill, slay, put to death

34.meaning: 'Certainly / with certainty; a matter of sure knowledge.' A noun for firm, unshakeable certainty — knowing something beyond any doubt — often used adverbially to mean 'for sure' or 'as a certainty.'
34.grammar: A noun with the -an ending (accusative with nunation, 'tanwīn'). Here the accusative works adverbially — describing the manner of an action — i.e. 'with certainty / for sure / as a certainty.'
34.root: ي-ق-ن (y-q-n) — to be certain; sure, unshakeable knowledge

1.meaning: A particle of retraction and transition meaning 'rather,' 'on the contrary,' or 'nay.' It cancels or sets aside what was just said and corrects course toward a truer statement that follows — turning the listener from one idea to another.
1.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it never changes its ending). It functions to retract or override the preceding statement and introduce a correction or contrast — 'no, rather …'

2.meaning: 'He raised / lifted him up.' A third-person masculine singular past verb 'he raised' with the object 'him' attached — to lift up or elevate, whether physically upward or in rank and honour.
2.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb, third-person masculine singular ('he …ed'). The final -a before the pronoun is the standard past-tense ending for a single male subject; the attached -hu is the object 'him' (the one raised). The subject 'he' is built into the verb.
2.root: ر-ف-ع (r-f-ʿ) — to raise, lift up, elevate (in place or rank)

3.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
3.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

4.meaning: 'To Him' or 'toward Him' — the preposition expressing direction or endpoint ('to / toward') combined with a pronoun referring to a single masculine person, indicating motion or attention directed at him.
4.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The base 'ilā shifts to 'ilay- when a pronoun is added. The suffix -hi is the third-person masculine singular object of a preposition, 'him'; its -i vowel is the form the pronoun takes after the 'ay' sound.

5.meaning: And he was / he became — a verb of being that places a subject in a past state or links it to a description in the past.
5.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'kāna' is a past-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular, meaning 'he was/became'; it commonly introduces a past condition and is typically followed by a noun describing the subject's state. The final -a marks completed past action by a single male.

6.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
6.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.
6.root: — (proper divine name)

7.meaning: Mighty, all-powerful, invincible — one who is dominant and cannot be overcome; also carrying the sense of precious and held in high honor. Of a person it means strong and unassailable.
7.grammar: An intensive adjective (of the faʿīl pattern, conveying a deep, settled quality). The final -an (tanwīn fatḥ) marks it as indefinite and in the accusative case, which typically signals a direct object or a descriptive complement governed into the accusative.
7.root: ع-ز-ز (ʿ-z-z) — might, strength, dominance; also honor and preciousness

8.meaning: All-Wise; one possessing perfect wisdom, who places everything in its right place and decides with flawless judgement. As an intensive form it conveys wisdom that is complete and sound.
8.grammar: An intensive adjective ('all-wise') on the faʿīl pattern, stressing the quality to its fullest degree. The -an (tanwīn) combines the -a accusative ending — typical of a predicate or object — with the -n marking it indefinite.

1.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
1.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

2.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
2.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

3.meaning: People of / folk of / those belonging to — the family, followers, or possessors of something (as in 'people of the Book'). It denotes those who belong to or are associated with a thing.
3.grammar: A noun meaning 'people/folk of'. The -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a following noun ('people OF …') or follows a preposition or oath particle.
3.root: ء-ه-ل (ʾ-h-l) — family, folk, people belonging to

4.meaning: 'The Book / the Scripture' — a written record or revealed scripture; literally that which is written.
4.grammar: The definite article al- with the noun kitāb ('book, scripture'), itself a verbal noun from 'to write.' The -i ending is genitive, typically marking the word as following a preposition or standing in an 'of' relationship to a preceding noun.

5.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
5.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

6.meaning: An emphatic assertion that someone will indeed believe — that is, will surely come to faith, trust, and affirm the truth. The word fuses a strong oath-like emphasis with the verb 'to believe', yielding the force of 'he most certainly will believe'.
6.grammar: A present-tense verb in the third-person masculine singular ('he'). It is wrapped in two layers of emphasis: the prefixed la- ('surely') and the heavy suffixed -nna (the emphatic nūn), which together turn a plain statement into a solemn guarantee — 'he will most assuredly do it'. The yu- prefix marks 'he'; the form carries future/imperfective force.
6.root: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — to be secure, to trust, to have faith

7.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
7.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

8.meaning: An adverb of time and place meaning 'before' — denoting what comes prior to something else, whether earlier in time or ahead of it in sequence.
8.grammar: An adverb of time/place ending in -a. It is regularly placed before a following noun to mean 'before that thing' (e.g. 'before X'), functioning much like a preposition that the next word completes.
8.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to precede, to come before; the front/fore

9.meaning: The state of dying or death, here possessed — 'his death', i.e. the death belonging to him.
9.grammar: A noun meaning 'death' with the attached pronoun -hi ('his'). The -i ending is genitive, the case typically signalling possession ('… of …') or following a preposition; combined with -hi it yields 'of him / his'. The vowel of the pronoun is -hi (with i) because it follows that genitive ending.

10.meaning: "and (on the) day" — the conjunction "and" joined to the noun for "day," a single daytime period or, more broadly, an appointed day or time of judgment/event.
10.grammar: The wa- prefix is the conjunction "and." The -a ending on the noun is accusative; on a word for "day" this frequently marks it as an adverb of time ("on the day …"), or marks it as the object of a verb.

11.meaning: "the Resurrection" — the standing-up of all people from death to be judged; literally the act of rising or standing up.
11.grammar: The al- prefix means "the." The -i ending (on the feminine -t) is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ("the … OF this") or follows a preposition.

12.meaning: 'It is / it comes to be' — the present-tense verb of being and becoming (from kāna). It expresses that something is the case, exists, or comes about.
12.grammar: A present/future-tense verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he/it is, becomes'. The ya- prefix means 'he/it', and the final -u is the indicative ending, marking a plain factual statement (as opposed to a command or a negated/subjunctive form).
12.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

13.meaning: A compound meaning 'upon them' or 'against them': the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over, against') joined to the plural pronoun 'them'. It conveys something resting on, being incumbent upon, or weighing against a group.
13.grammar: ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay- before a pronoun. The suffix -him is the attached pronominal suffix for a masculine plural group ('them'); after a preposition it carries genitive/prepositional force, and the -i- vowel reflects its position after this preposition. Together they signal a relationship of something being over, upon, or burdensome to that group.
13.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

14.meaning: 'A witness' — one who sees and attests, who can give evidence; also carries the sense of one who is present and observant, and at times 'a martyr' (one who bears witness with their life).
14.grammar: An intensive describing-noun (pattern fa‘īl) meaning 'a witness, one who fully attests', indefinite. The -an ending (the accusative with 'tanwīn') marks it as indefinite and in the accusative — the case used for a direct object, or for a word that describes the state or role in which someone stands.

1.meaning: A linking phrase meaning 'so/then, because of wrongdoing' — naming injustice or oppression (literally 'putting a thing out of its rightful place') as a cause, and introducing it as a consequence of what came before.
1.grammar: A noun 'wrongdoing' carrying two prefixes: fa- ('so, then', drawing a consequence) and bi- ('because of, by means of'). The -in ending (nunation) marks the noun as indefinite ('some wrongdoing') and genitive, the case required after the preposition bi-.
1.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — to wrong, to oppress, to put out of place; injustice, darkness

2.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
2.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

3.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
3.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

4.meaning: 'They became Jews / adopted Judaism', or in the verb's wider sense 'they turned (back) in repentance'. A completed act by a group of taking on the way of the Jewish community.

parts.en: became Jews / turned back (past, masc. plural)

4.grammar: A past-tense verb from a hollow root. The whole form hādū is already 3rd-person masculine plural ('they turned/became Jews'): the long ū plus the final silent alif are the plural marker, so no separate ending is split off. The action is presented as completed; the root carries the idea of turning toward or returning, from which the sense 'to follow Judaism' derives.
4.root: ه-و-د (h-w-d) — turning back, returning; hence following Judaism

5.meaning: 'We forbade / made unlawful' — to declare something prohibited and off-limits, treating it as sacred or forbidden so that it may not be approached or used.
5.grammar: A past-tense verb in an intensive pattern (denoting decisive, complete prohibition). The suffix -nā marks the doer as 'we', so the whole means 'we made unlawful / we forbade'. Being past tense, it reports a completed act.
5.root: ح-ر-م (ḥ-r-m) — to forbid, to make sacred/inviolable; the forbidden and the sacrosanct

6.meaning: A compound meaning 'upon them' or 'against them': the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over, against') joined to the plural pronoun 'them'. It conveys something resting on, being incumbent upon, or weighing against a group.
6.grammar: ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay- before a pronoun. The suffix -him is the attached pronominal suffix for a masculine plural group ('them'); after a preposition it carries genitive/prepositional force, and the -i- vowel reflects its position after this preposition. Together they signal a relationship of something being over, upon, or burdensome to that group.
6.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

7.meaning: 'Good things' — wholesome, pure, pleasant, and lawful things, especially good foods and agreeable provisions. The word denotes whatever is naturally pleasing and untainted.
7.grammar: A feminine plural noun/adjective ('good, wholesome things'), formed with the -āt plural ending. The final -in (nunation) marks it indefinite; on a sound feminine plural this single -in serves for both the genitive and the accusative case, the cases typically used after a preposition or as the object of a verb.
7.root: ط-ي-ب (ṭ-y-b) — to be good, pure, pleasant, wholesome

8.meaning: 'It was made lawful / permitted' — said of something that had been rendered allowable and free to use, the passive of declaring a thing permissible.
8.grammar: A past-tense passive verb ('was made lawful'). The u- vowelling at the front signals the passive — the subject receives the action rather than doing it. The suffix -at (here -t) marks a feminine singular subject, 'she/it', agreeing with a feminine noun.
8.root: ح-ل-ل (ḥ-l-l) — to be lawful/permitted; to loosen, untie, make allowable

9.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
9.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

10.meaning: A linking phrase 'and because of their barring/hindering' — naming the act of turning people away or blocking them (especially from a path or from God's way) as a cause, attributed to a group ('their').
10.grammar: A verbal noun 'a barring/hindering' with prefixes wa- ('and') and bi- ('because of'), plus the attached pronoun -him ('their'). The -i ending is genitive — the case after the preposition bi- and before a possessor — and the pronoun takes the form -him (with i) following that genitive ending: 'their hindering'.
10.root: ص-د-د (ṣ-d-d) — to turn away, to bar, to hinder, to obstruct

11.meaning: A preposition meaning 'on behalf of,' 'for,' 'about,' or 'away from.' It often conveys removing a burden from someone or acting in their place.

parts.en: on behalf of / for / away from

11.grammar: A preposition (a linking particle). It governs the noun that follows it, putting that noun into the genitive case. It does not change form.

12.meaning: 'path, way, road' — a route or course; figuratively a cause or way of life one travels along. In construct ('the way OF ...').
12.grammar: A singular noun with the '-i' (genitive) ending, which typically links it to a following noun ('the way OF ...') or follows a preposition. It marks the word as connected to or possessed by what comes after.

13.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
13.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

14.meaning: An adjective/noun meaning 'many', 'much', or 'numerous' — a large quantity or great number of something.
14.grammar: Adjective/noun in the indefinite accusative, marked by the final -an (nunation with fatḥa). The accusative typically marks a verb's object or an indefinite quantity, and the doubled-n sound shows the word is indefinite ('many').
14.root: ك-ث-ر (k-th-r) — to be much, many, abundant

1.meaning: A linking phrase 'and their taking / their acceptance' — referring to a group's act of taking, seizing, or accepting something, here attributed to them as a cause.
1.grammar: A verbal noun 'the taking/seizing' with the connector wa- ('and') and the attached pronoun -him ('their'). The -i ending is genitive, marking possession ('the taking OF them / their taking'). The pronoun is here written -himu (its final vowel raised to u to ease into a following word that begins with a connecting hamza).
1.root: ء-خ-ذ (ʾ-kh-dh) — to take, to seize, to grasp, to receive

2.meaning: Usury or interest: the prohibited practice of lending money or commodities for a guaranteed, unearned increase paid back over and above the principal. The underlying sense is of something that swells, grows, or is augmented beyond its origin.
2.grammar: A definite masculine noun (the prefix al- marks 'the'). It is written with a long final ā (the alif), and as an invariable noun of this pattern its ending does not visibly change for case. It names the concept itself.
2.root: ر-ب-و (r-b-w) — to grow, increase, swell, augment

3.meaning: 'And indeed / while already' — the word 'wa' ('and, while') joined to 'qad', a particle that, before a past-tense verb, stresses that the action has certainly and already happened.
3.grammar: A connective 'wa' ('and', or circumstantial 'while') plus the particle 'qad'. With a past-tense verb, 'qad' emphasizes completion and certainty ('has indeed already…'); with a present-tense verb it can mean 'sometimes' or 'may'.

4.meaning: 'They were forbidden / prohibited' — said of people who were told not to do something; the passive of forbidding directed at a group.
4.grammar: A past-tense passive verb (the u-vowelling signals the passive: the subjects had the prohibition imposed on them). The long -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. The written alif after it is a spelling convention on plural verbs and is not pronounced.
4.root: ن-ه-ي (n-h-y) — to forbid, to prohibit, to restrain

5.meaning: A combination meaning 'from him / from it / about him.' The preposition denotes moving away from, departing from, or concerning a thing, and the pronoun refers to a single masculine entity.
5.grammar: A preposition with a fused object pronoun. ʿan governs the genitive and conveys separation or 'concerning.' The attached -hu marks a third-person masculine singular object ('him/it').

6.meaning: A linking phrase 'and their consuming / eating' — referring to a group's act of eating or, by extension, devouring and using up (often of wealth), attributed to them.
6.grammar: A verbal noun 'eating/consuming' with the connector wa- ('and') and the attached pronoun -him ('their'). The -i ending is genitive, signalling possession ('their eating'); the pronoun takes the form -him (with i) after that genitive ending.
6.root: ء-ك-ل (ʾ-k-l) — to eat, to consume, to devour

7.meaning: Properties, possessions, wealth — the goods and assets a person owns. It is the plural of māl (money/property), denoting riches and material holdings in general.
7.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural of māl, on the afʿāl pattern. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the object of a verb. It lacks tanwīn here because it is the muḍāf — the first term of a possessive construction (iḍāfa) — and the first term of such a construction never carries tanwīn.
7.root: م-و-ل (m-w-l) — wealth, property, to have means

8.meaning: Humankind, people, mankind — the collective of human beings.
8.grammar: A collective noun ('people, mankind') carrying the definite article al- ('the'); the 'l' of the article assimilates into the following 'n', doubling it (al-nās → an-nās). The genitive ending -i marks the word as governed by a preposition or as the second term of a possessive.
8.root: ء-ن-س (ʾ-n-s) — humankind, sociability, familiarity; the word for 'people' is most commonly traced to this root (related to insān, 'human being')

9.meaning: With / by falsehood — 'the false, the vain, the baseless' joined to a preposition and 'the'.
9.grammar: The preposition bi- joined to the definite noun 'the falsehood' (an active participle meaning 'that which is null/vain'). The -i ending is the genitive, required because the noun follows the preposition.
9.root: ب-ط-ل (b-ṭ-l) — to be void, false, vain, of no effect

10.meaning: And We have made ready — to prepare, arrange, and set something in store beforehand so it stands waiting.
10.grammar: A past-tense verb (form VIII) prefixed with 'wa' (and). The 't' in the stem is the form VIII infix, not a root letter. The suffix '-nā' is the subject ending meaning 'we (did it),' marking a completed action performed by a first-person plural — an act already accomplished.
10.root: ع-د-د (ʿ-d-d) — counting, reckoning; readying and setting in store (form VIII اعتدّ, with the doubled dāl, from this root)

11.meaning: A three-part word: 'for' + 'the' + 'those who cover up the truth / reject faith.' The base noun denotes the kāfir — one who disbelieves, denies, and ungratefully conceals the truth and Allah's favor. With 'for,' it marks them as the ones for whom something is intended.
11.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('for/to') joined to a definite plural noun, masculine. The '-īna' ending is the sound masculine plural in its genitive/accusative (oblique) form, here required because it follows the preposition 'li-'. The whole denotes 'for the disbelievers.'
11.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal, disbelieve, be ungrateful

12.meaning: From them / among them — the preposition min ('from, out of, part of') joined to the pronoun 'them' (a group of males or a mixed group).
12.grammar: The preposition min ('from / among / part of') with the attached third-person masculine plural pronoun -hum ('them'). Pronouns after a preposition are in the genitive; the combination expresses origin, partition ('some of them'), or belonging to that group.

13.meaning: 'A punishment / torment.' A noun naming chastisement or painful suffering inflicted as a penalty.
13.grammar: A masculine noun. The -an ending marks it as indefinite ('a punishment') and in the accusative case — the form a noun takes as the object of a verb or as the thing being described/quantified.

14.meaning: An adjective meaning 'painful, agonizing, causing severe pain,' describing something that inflicts intense suffering.
14.grammar: An adjective in the intensive faʿīl pattern, which heightens the quality (deeply/intensely painful). The final -an (tanwīn fatḥa) marks it as indefinite ('a painful one') and in the accusative case — the case typically used for the object of a verb or for a describing word agreeing with such a noun.

1.meaning: But, however, rather — a particle that sets off a correction or contrast with what came before, redirecting the statement.

parts.en: kasra of the light (reduced) particle form

1.grammar: A contrastive particle meaning 'but/however'. This is the light/reduced form of the emphatic لٰكِنَّ (lākinna): the doubled nūn is elided and the particle no longer governs a following noun. The final kasra (-i) belongs to the identity of this reduced form rather than being mere pronunciation liaison.

2.meaning: 'The firmly-grounded ones' — those deeply rooted and well-established, especially in knowledge; people whose grasp of something is solid and unshakeable.
2.grammar: An active participle ('one who is firmly rooted') with the definite article al- ('the') and the sound masculine plural ending -ūna. The -ūna ending marks a plural of male persons in the subject role ('the firmly-grounded ones'), as opposed to the -īna form used in other cases.
2.root: ر-س-خ (r-s-kh) — to be firmly rooted, deeply established, immovable

3.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
3.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

4.meaning: The knowledge; sure and certain knowing, established information and understanding (with the definite article).
4.grammar: A definite verbal noun: al- means 'the'. The final -i is the genitive ending, which typically follows a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun in an 'of' relationship. It denotes knowledge as a settled, certain thing.

5.meaning: From them / among them — the preposition min ('from, out of, part of') joined to the pronoun 'them' (a group of males or a mixed group).
5.grammar: The preposition min ('from / among / part of') with the attached third-person masculine plural pronoun -hum ('them'). Pronouns after a preposition are in the genitive; the combination expresses origin, partition ('some of them'), or belonging to that group.

6.meaning: "and the believers" — those who have faith, who accept and trust; wa- joins it on and al- makes it definite ('the believers' as a group).
6.grammar: A masculine sound plural noun, 'believers.' The -ūna ending is the subject (nominative) form of the masculine plural, used when the word is the one doing the action; the matching object/possessive form would be -īna.
6.root: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — safety, security, faith, trust

7.meaning: 'They believe / they have faith' — to affirm something as true with trusting inner conviction and to feel secure in it. The verb carries both believing and being at peace through that belief; in religious use it is to commit oneself in faith.
7.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb, masculine plural. The yu-…-una frame means 'they (men, or a mixed group) do' the action now or habitually. The retained final -na marks the indicative (a plain, unqualified statement) — 'they believe' — as opposed to forms where that -na drops. The verb is Form IV (amana), used intransitively here meaning simply 'to believe / to have faith'.

8.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
8.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

9.meaning: 'It was sent down / revealed': the act of being caused to descend, used especially of revelation brought down from Allah. The passive form puts the focus on the thing sent down rather than on the sender.
9.grammar: A past-tense passive verb in Form IV (anzala 'to send down' → unzila 'was sent down'). The prefix is only the u- vowel carried on the connecting hamza; the nūn that follows is the first root letter (of ن-ز-ل), not part of the prefix. The internal vowel pattern u–i marks it as passive ('was/were sent down'), with no named doer. The final -a marks the subject as 'he/it', a single masculine thing, and signals completed action.
9.root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — to descend, come down; (Form IV) to send down

10.meaning: 'To you' (addressing one person): indicating direction or motion toward a single individual — that toward which something moves or is directed.
10.grammar: The preposition ilā ('to, towards') with an attached pronoun; before a suffix ilā takes the form ilay-. The -ka ending is the pronoun 'you' for a single male addressee. Pronouns following a preposition stand in the genitive relationship, though their form does not visibly change for case.

11.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
11.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

12.meaning: 'It was sent down / revealed': the act of being caused to descend, used especially of revelation brought down from Allah. The passive form puts the focus on the thing sent down rather than on the sender.
12.grammar: A past-tense passive verb in Form IV (anzala 'to send down' → unzila 'was sent down'). The prefix is only the u- vowel carried on the connecting hamza; the nūn that follows is the first root letter (of ن-ز-ل), not part of the prefix. The internal vowel pattern u–i marks it as passive ('was/were sent down'), with no named doer. The final -a marks the subject as 'he/it', a single masculine thing, and signals completed action.
12.root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — to descend, come down; (Form IV) to send down

13.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
13.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

14.meaning: 'Before you' (in time or place): the period or position prior to a single person — that which comes earlier or stands in front, relative to one addressee.
