14.grammar: The adverb/noun qabl ('before, prior') with the attached pronoun -ka ('you', a single male). The -i ending on qabl is genitive, the case regularly taken after a preposition (such as min, 'from before') and when a noun is linked to a following possessor; here it is linked to the pronoun 'you' ('before-you').
14.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to precede, be before; priority, what comes first

15.meaning: A linking phrase 'and the ones who keep up / establish' — those who maintain and uphold something steadfastly (classically used of those who keep up the prayer).
15.grammar: An active participle ('one who establishes/maintains') with the connector wa-, the article al- ('the'), and the sound masculine plural ending -īna. The -īna form is the plural of male persons used in the object or after-a-preposition (oblique) role, as distinct from the subject form -ūna.
15.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, to rise; (in this pattern) to set up, establish, keep up

16.meaning: The ritual prayer (ṣalāh): the prescribed formal worship of standing, bowing, and prostrating before Allah at appointed times. As a verbal noun it also carries the underlying sense of calling upon, supplicating, and blessing.
16.grammar: A definite feminine noun. The -a ending is accusative: it generally marks the word as the direct object of a verb (the thing being acted upon, e.g. that which is established or performed), or the object of certain particles.
16.root: ص-ل-و (ṣ-l-w) — prayer, worship, supplication

17.meaning: A linking phrase 'and the ones who give' — those who hand over or grant something to others, especially givers of charity or of what is due.
17.grammar: An active participle ('one who gives') with the connector wa-, the article al- ('the'), and the sound masculine plural ending -ūna. The -ūna form marks a plural of male persons in the subject role ('the givers'), contrasting with the -īna form used elsewhere.
17.root: ء-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (in this pattern) to bring to, to give, to hand over

18.meaning: The purifying alms (zakāt) — the obligatory portion given from one's wealth that purifies it and causes it to grow; an act of worship and social due.
18.grammar: A definite feminine noun (the tied tā' marks the feminine). The final -a is the accusative ending, typically marking the noun as the direct object of a verb ('the alms').
18.root: ز-ك-و (z-k-w) — to be pure; to grow, increase, be blessed

19.meaning: "and the believers" — those who have faith, who accept and trust; wa- joins it on and al- makes it definite ('the believers' as a group).
19.grammar: A masculine sound plural noun, 'believers.' The -ūna ending is the subject (nominative) form of the masculine plural, used when the word is the one doing the action; the matching object/possessive form would be -īna.
19.root: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — safety, security, faith, trust

20.meaning: A phrase 'in Allah / by Allah', combining the preposition 'with/in/by' and the divine name Allah, the proper name of the One God.
20.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with, by means of') prefixed to the divine name Allah. A preposition always forces the following noun into the genitive case, which is why Allah here ends in -i. With verbs of believing, bi- conveys the object of faith — to believe IN.
20.root: — (Allah is the proper name of God and is not derived from a triliteral root in the usual sense)

21.meaning: "And the Day" — a stretch of time, a day; also used for the appointed Day of Judgement and Resurrection. The opening element is the conjunction 'and'.
21.grammar: A masculine singular noun with the definite article 'the' and the conjunction 'and'. The final -i is the genitive case ending: it typically signals that the word is linked to a preceding noun ('… of …') or governed by a preposition or oath particle.

22.meaning: An adjective meaning 'the last,' 'the latter,' or 'the final' — that which comes at the end of a sequence. It is the common counterpart to 'the first,' and is often used as a name for the world or life to come (the Hereafter, the Last Day), i.e. the ultimate end of all things.
22.grammar: An active-participle-type adjective on the pattern fāʿil. It carries the definite article 'al-' ('the'). The final -i is the genitive case, signaling that the word is governed by a preceding preposition or particle, or stands as the second term of a possessive link ('… of …'). It is masculine singular.
22.root: ء-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — to be last, to come after, to defer / postpone

23.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'those' — pointing to people or things that are distant or already known. It singles out a group ('those ones', 'it is those who').
23.grammar: A plural demonstrative pronoun, 'those'. It is fixed in form (no case endings). The -ka element signals distance/remoteness, pointing to something far off or notable. It can refer to people of either gender.

24.meaning: 'We will give them' — a promise that the speaker ('we') will grant or bestow something upon a group, with the prefixed marker showing it lies in the future.
24.grammar: A present-tense verb turned into a future by the prefix sa- ('will'). The nu- prefix marks the doer as 'we'; the attached -him is the object 'them'. So the whole reads 'we shall give them'. The pronoun appears as -him (with i) in this position.
24.root: ء-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (in this pattern) to bring to, to give, to bestow

25.meaning: A reward, wage, or recompense — the return earned for work or conduct, whether worldly pay or otherworldly recompense.
25.grammar: A noun meaning 'a reward.' The final '-an' (tanwīn fatḥa) marks the indefinite accusative case, the case used for the object of a verb (e.g. of 'to give'), giving the sense 'a reward.'
25.root: ا-ج-ر (ʾ-j-r) — reward, wage, recompense for what one does

26.meaning: 'Great, immense, tremendous' — describing something vast in magnitude or weight, whether in size, importance, or seriousness.
26.grammar: An adjective ('great, immense') in an intensive pattern. The -an ending (nunation with a final alif) marks it as indefinite and in the accusative case — the case typically used for the object of a verb or for a description attached to such an object.
26.root: ع-ظ-م (ʿ-ẓ-m) — to be great, immense, mighty; greatness, a bone

1.meaning: A two-part expression: an emphatic particle that strongly affirms and confirms a statement ('truly, indeed, certainly'), fused with the attached pronoun 'we.' Together: 'truly we…' / 'indeed we…'
1.grammar: The particle inna gives strong emphasis and certainty to the clause it opens. The attached -ā is the pronoun 'we,' serving as the subject being emphasized: 'truly we…'

2.meaning: 'We revealed / inspired' — the act of God conveying revelation or inspiration; to communicate a message swiftly and privately into someone's heart or to a prophet. Here attributed to 'we'.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb in a causative pattern (to convey/send down a revelation). The suffix -nā marks the doer as 'we', giving 'we revealed'. As past tense, it reports a completed act.
2.root: و-ح-ي (w-ḥ-y) — to reveal, to inspire, to convey swiftly and secretly

3.meaning: 'To you' (addressing one person): indicating direction or motion toward a single individual — that toward which something moves or is directed.
3.grammar: The preposition ilā ('to, towards') with an attached pronoun; before a suffix ilā takes the form ilay-. The -ka ending is the pronoun 'you' for a single male addressee. Pronouns following a preposition stand in the genitive relationship, though their form does not visibly change for case.

4.meaning: 'Just as / in the same way that' — a phrase of comparison joining 'like / as' to 'what', meaning 'like that which...' or 'in the manner that...'.
4.grammar: The comparison particle ka- ('like / as') joined to mā ('what / that which'). Together they introduce a likeness or manner — 'just as...', 'in the same way that...' — comparing one thing or action to another.

5.meaning: 'We revealed / inspired' — the act of God conveying revelation or inspiration; to communicate a message swiftly and privately into someone's heart or to a prophet. Here attributed to 'we'.
5.grammar: A past-tense verb in a causative pattern (to convey/send down a revelation). The suffix -nā marks the doer as 'we', giving 'we revealed'. As past tense, it reports a completed act.
5.root: و-ح-ي (w-ḥ-y) — to reveal, to inspire, to convey swiftly and secretly

6.meaning: A preposition meaning 'to,' 'toward,' or 'up to' — pointing to the end-point, goal, or limit of a motion, direction, or extent.
6.grammar: A preposition (a small linking word). It governs the noun after it, putting that noun in the genitive case, and points to a destination or limit ('to,' 'toward,' 'as far as').

7.meaning: Noah — the proper name of the Prophet Nūḥ.
7.grammar: A proper name. The -in ending (nunation) shows it is treated as a fully declinable noun in the genitive case — the case used after a preposition or to link to a preceding word. (Most personal names are partly indeclinable, but this short name takes full case endings.)

8.meaning: A linking phrase 'and the prophets' — those raised up by God to receive revelation and convey His message to people.
8.grammar: A noun 'prophet' with the connector wa- ('and'), the article al- ('the', its l assimilating into the following n), and the sound masculine plural ending -īna. The -īna form marks a plural of male persons in the object or after-a-preposition (oblique) role, as opposed to the subject form -ūna.
8.root: ن-ب-ء (n-b-ʾ) — news, tidings; a prophet as one who brings news from God

9.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
9.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

10.meaning: 'After him / it' — 'baʿd' denotes what comes afterward in time or sequence, here joined to 'him/it'.
10.grammar: A time-noun 'baʿd' (afterness) with an attached pronoun, forming a possessive pairing. The '-i' vowel on 'baʿd' is its case ending, set by 'baʿd's' own position in the sentence (commonly governed by a preceding preposition), not by the suffix; the attached '-hi' is the possessor ('him/it'), and as the possessed-to term it sits in the genitive. The pronoun's 'i'-vowel (-hi rather than -hu) follows because it comes after a genitive '-i'.

11.meaning: A linking phrase 'and we revealed / inspired' — the act of God conveying revelation, joined by 'and' to what precedes and attributed to 'we'.
11.grammar: A past-tense verb in a causative pattern (to send down a revelation), preceded by the connector wa- ('and'). The suffix -nā marks the doer as 'we', giving 'and we revealed'. As past tense, it reports a completed act.
11.root: و-ح-ي (w-ḥ-y) — to reveal, to inspire, to convey swiftly and secretly

12.meaning: "to / towards" — a preposition marking the end-point, goal, or direction of a movement or extent ("up to," "as far as," "toward").
12.grammar: An indeclinable preposition; it has no case ending of its own and always governs a following noun in the genitive case.

13.meaning: The proper name Ibrāhīm (the Prophet Abraham).
13.grammar: A proper name of non-Arabic origin. The -a ending here serves for both accusative and genitive because the name is a diptote — a class of nouns that refuses tanwīn (no -an/-in) and uses a single -a for these two cases. So this one -a covers 'Ibrāhīm' whether as an object or as 'of Ibrāhīm'.

14.meaning: And Ismāʿīl (Ishmael), the proper name of the prophet, son of Ibrahim; preceded by the connector 'and.'
14.grammar: The connector 'wa-' ('and') joined to a proper name of non-Arabic origin. As a 'diptote' foreign name, it takes a single -a ending for both the object (accusative) and possessive/after-preposition (genitive) roles, and it does not take nunation.

15.meaning: The proper name 'Isaac' (Isḥāq), the prophet, joined to the conjunction 'and.'
15.grammar: Conjunction 'wa' (and) prefixed to a proper name. The final -a is the accusative/genitive ending; because this is a foreign (non-Arabic) name, it is grammatically 'diptote,' meaning it takes -a for both those cases and never takes nunation (the -n sound).

16.meaning: The proper name 'Jacob' (Yaʿqūb), the prophet, joined to the conjunction 'and.'
16.grammar: Conjunction 'wa' (and) prefixed to a proper name. The final -a is the accusative/genitive ending; as a foreign (non-Arabic) name it is 'diptote,' taking -a for both those cases and never taking nunation (the -n sound).
16.root: — (proper name)

17.meaning: 'The tribes / the descendants' — specifically the tribes descended from the twelve sons of Jacob (the Israelite tribes); the plural of a word for a grandson, descendant, or tribal branch.
17.grammar: Conjunction 'wa' (and) plus the definite article 'al-' (the) on a broken (irregular) plural noun. The -i ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to / possessed by a preceding word, or to match an earlier genitive noun in a list.
17.root: س-ب-ط (s-b-ṭ) — a tribe, descendant line (esp. of Jacob)

18.meaning: The proper name 'Isa' (Jesus), prefixed with 'and'. It refers to the prophet Isa, son of Maryam.
18.grammar: A proper noun joined by the connector 'wa' ('and'). The name ends in a long ā (written with the dagger alif) and is indeclinable, so it does not change its ending for case; it simply names the person.

19.meaning: A linking phrase 'and Job' — joining the proper name of the Prophet Ayyūb with 'and'.
19.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') plus a proper name. The name ends in -a and is a 'diptote' — a noun that resists full case endings, so it shows -a (not -in) and takes no nunation; this -a form covers both the object and after-a-preposition roles.

20.meaning: A linking phrase 'and Jonah' — joining the proper name of the Prophet Yūnus with 'and'.
20.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') plus a proper name. It ends in -a and is a 'diptote' — a noun that does not take full case endings, so it shows -a (not -un/-in) and no nunation; this single -a form serves for both the object and after-a-preposition roles.

21.meaning: A linking phrase 'and Aaron' — joining the proper name of the Prophet Hārūn with 'and'.
21.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') plus a proper name. It ends in -a and is a 'diptote' — a noun that does not take full case endings, so it shows -a (not -un/-in) and no nunation; this -a form covers both the object and after-a-preposition roles.

22.meaning: A linking phrase 'and Solomon' — joining the proper name of the Prophet Sulaymān with 'and'.
22.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') plus a proper name. It ends in -a and is a 'diptote' — a noun that does not take full case endings, so it shows -a (not -un/-in) and no nunation; this single -a form serves for both the object and after-a-preposition roles.

23.meaning: "and We gave / brought" — to give, bring, or grant something to someone.
23.grammar: The wa- prefix is "and." This is a past-tense causative verb meaning "to give/bring (to someone)." The -nā ending marks a first-person plural subject ("we") who completed the action.
23.root: ا-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (causative) to give, bring

24.meaning: The proper name Dāwūd (David), the prophet and king known for his psalms, his judgment, and his kingship.
24.grammar: A proper name (of foreign, non-Arabic origin). Names of this kind are diptotes: they do not take case-tanwīn, and their accusative and genitive both show a single -a ending. The -a here marks the word as an object or as the noun governed by a preposition rather than carrying full case inflection.

25.meaning: The Zabūr: the scripture (Psalms) revealed to the prophet Dāwūd; by extension, an inscribed or written book of revelation.
25.grammar: A noun in the accusative with tanwīn (-an, 'a Zabūr'). The -an ending typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb (what is being given or granted) and signals that it is indefinite ('a …').
25.root: ز-ب-ر (z-b-r) — to write, inscribe; a written piece

1.meaning: 'and messengers' — envoys, those sent by Allah with a message to a people.
1.grammar: The prefix wa- means 'and'. The base is the broken (irregular) plural of rasūl ('messenger'). The -an ending is accusative with tanwīn, typically marking the word as a direct object and indefinite ('messengers').

2.meaning: A short particle placed before a verb to emphasize or affirm it. Before a past-tense verb it means 'indeed / certainly / has already (happened)'; before a present-tense verb it can mean 'sometimes / may'. It sharpens and confirms the verb that follows.
2.grammar: An indeclinable particle (its form never changes). It does not take case or tense endings; its job is to color the following verb — affirming and intensifying a past action ('has indeed done') or signaling occasional possibility with a present verb.
2.root: — (no triliteral root; an emphasizing particle)

3.meaning: 'we recounted/narrated them' — the act of relating a story or account of someone to a listener.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb. The suffix -nā means 'we' (the doer), and the attached -hum ('them') is the direct object. So the form means 'we recounted them' — a completed action performed by 'we' upon 'them'.
3.root: ق-ص-ص (q-ṣ-ṣ) — to follow a track; to narrate, recount a story

4.meaning: "upon you / to you / against you" — the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over') with the 'you' pronoun, carrying senses of resting upon, being directed to, or bearing upon someone.
4.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The base ʿalā shifts to ʿalay- when a pronoun is added. The suffix -ka means 'you' (second-person masculine singular). Prepositions themselves take no case ending.

5.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
5.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

6.meaning: An adverb of time meaning 'before / beforehand / previously,' pointing to a moment or state that precedes something else in time. When used with the final vowel -u (qablu), it stands cut off from an explicit following noun, conveying 'before(hand)' or 'previously' in an absolute sense — the thing it is 'before' is understood rather than stated.
6.grammar: An adverb of time. The final -u ending here is the indeclinable (mabnī) form taken when the word is severed from a following genitive: rather than 'before X,' it means 'before(hand)' on its own, with the reference point left implicit.
6.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to come before, precede, be in front; to receive/accept

7.meaning: 'and messengers' — envoys, those sent by Allah with a message to a people.
7.grammar: The prefix wa- means 'and'. The base is the broken (irregular) plural of rasūl ('messenger'). The -an ending is accusative with tanwīn, typically marking the word as a direct object and indefinite ('messengers').

8.meaning: The particle 'lam', a negating word used to push a verb into the past: it means 'did not' / 'has not'. Though it sits before a present-tense verb form, it negates the action as something that did not happen.
8.grammar: 'lam' is a negating particle that governs a following present-tense verb but gives it past meaning ('did not …'). It also puts that verb into the shortened (jussive) form. 'lam' itself carries no ending.

9.meaning: 'we recount them / we relate them' — to narrate or tell the account of someone, in the present/ongoing sense.
9.grammar: A present/jussive-form verb. The na- prefix means 'we' (the doer). The attached -hum ('them') is the direct object. The bare, vowel-less ending (jussive) is the form used after negative or conditional particles, so it conveys 'we (do) not recount them' or 'should we recount them'.
9.root: ق-ص-ص (q-ṣ-ṣ) — to follow a track; to narrate, recount a story

10.meaning: "upon you / to you / against you" — the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over') with the 'you' pronoun, carrying senses of resting upon, being directed to, or bearing upon someone.
10.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The base ʿalā shifts to ʿalay- when a pronoun is added. The suffix -ka means 'you' (second-person masculine singular). Prepositions themselves take no case ending.

11.meaning: 'and he spoke' — the act of speaking, addressing, or conversing with someone using words.
11.grammar: The prefix wa- means 'and'. The base is a past-tense verb in the intensified (form II) pattern, which here carries the sense of directly addressing or conversing with someone. The final -a with no suffix marks a completed action done by 'he'.

12.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
12.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

13.meaning: Mūsā (Moses) — the proper name of the prophet. As a name it has no Arabic root meaning; it is a non-inflecting (indeclinable) noun whose ending does not change for case.
13.grammar: A proper name ending in a fixed long -ā (written as alif maqṣūra). It is fully indeclinable (invariable): the final -ā never changes, so the word shows no case distinction at all — it looks and sounds identical whether subject, object, or possessor. (This is unlike a diptote, which still alternates between two case vowels; here there is no alternation.)

14.meaning: 'in genuine speech / a real speaking' — an emphatic verbal noun stressing that the speaking was true, direct address, not figurative.
14.grammar: A verbal noun (the action of 'speaking' as a thing) in the accusative with tanwīn (-an). Placed after a verb of the same root, it functions as an emphatic 'absolute object,' reinforcing the verb — i.e. 'spoke a true speaking,' stressing that the action genuinely and fully occurred.

1.meaning: 'messengers' — envoys, those sent by Allah bearing a message to people.
1.grammar: The broken (irregular) plural of rasūl ('messenger'). The -an ending is accusative with tanwīn, typically marking the word as a direct object and indefinite ('messengers').

2.meaning: 'bearers of glad tidings' — those who announce good news and a happy outcome to people.
2.grammar: An active participle (form II, 'one who brings good news') in the masculine plural. The mu- prefix marks 'the one who does' the action. The -īna ending is the masculine sound plural in the accusative/genitive case — it names a group ('bearers of good news') functioning as object or following a preposition.
2.root: ب-ش-ر (b-sh-r) — good news, glad tidings; skin (as in the face brightening)

3.meaning: 'and warners' — those who caution people of consequences and danger, especially of divine punishment.
3.grammar: The prefix wa- means 'and'. The base is an active participle (form IV, 'one who warns') in the masculine plural. The mu- prefix marks 'the one who does' the action; the -īna ending is the masculine sound plural in the accusative/genitive case, naming a group ('warners') as object or after a preposition.
3.root: ن-ذ-ر (n-dh-r) — to warn, give notice; a warning

4.meaning: So that … not; in order that … not. A compound particle expressing negative purpose — the reason or aim behind an action stated as something to be prevented.
4.grammar: A compound of the purpose particle li- ('so that') with allā, itself a fusion of an ('that') and lā ('not'). Together they introduce a clause of negative purpose, and the following verb takes the subjunctive mood (often shown by a final -a). The whole means 'in order that … should not …'.

5.meaning: He/it is / he comes to be. A form of the verb kāna ('to be'), linking a subject to a state or asserting that something exists or occurs.
5.grammar: Present/imperfect verb, 3rd person masculine singular ('he/it'). The ya- prefix marks 3rd person masculine; the final -a marks the subjunctive mood, the form a verb takes after particles meaning 'so that', 'in order to', or 'that'. It expresses a state being brought about rather than a plain fact.
5.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

6.meaning: To the people, for mankind — addressed or directed toward human beings in general; 'an-nās' is the collective word for 'people, humankind'.
6.grammar: The preposition 'li-' (to/for) joined to 'an-nās' (the people); the article's 'a' drops in pronunciation and its 'l' assimilates into the noun's 'n' (shown by the doubling). The -i ending is the genitive case, required because the word follows the preposition 'li-'. 'nās' is a collective noun for humankind with no singular of its own root form.
6.root: ن-و-س / ا-ن-س (n-w-s / ʾ-n-s) — humankind, people

7.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
7.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
7.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

8.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
8.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

9.meaning: 'an argument / a proof' — a decisive plea, evidence, or case that one can put forward to justify oneself or establish a claim.
9.grammar: A feminine noun (its feminine -t- belongs to the tā' marbūṭa of the base ḥujja) in the nominative with tanwīn. The ending shown here, -un, typically marks the word as the subject of a sentence and signals that it is indefinite ('an argument / a proof').
9.root: ح-ج-ج (ḥ-j-j) — to argue, present a proof; a binding plea

10.meaning: After; following in time or order — the point or moment subsequent to something.
10.grammar: An adverb of time functioning much like a preposition ('after'). It is fixed in the accusative form ending in -a, and is normally followed by a noun in the 'of' relationship, giving 'after (the) …'.
10.root: ب-ع-د (b-ʿ-d) — afterness, that which comes later; distance/remoteness

11.meaning: 'the messengers' — the envoys sent by Allah, taken definitely as a known group.
11.grammar: The prefix al- ('the') makes it definite (its 'l' assimilates to the following 'r'). The base is the broken plural of rasūl. The -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the messengers') or follows a preposition.

12.meaning: And he was / he became — a verb of being that places a subject in a past state or links it to a description in the past.
12.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'kāna' is a past-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular, meaning 'he was/became'; it commonly introduces a past condition and is typically followed by a noun describing the subject's state. The final -a marks completed past action by a single male.

13.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
13.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

14.meaning: Mighty, all-powerful, invincible — one who is dominant and cannot be overcome; also carrying the sense of precious and held in high honor. Of a person it means strong and unassailable.
14.grammar: An intensive adjective (of the faʿīl pattern, conveying a deep, settled quality). The final -an (tanwīn fatḥ) marks it as indefinite and in the accusative case, which typically signals a direct object or a descriptive complement governed into the accusative.
14.root: ع-ز-ز (ʿ-z-z) — might, strength, dominance; also honor and preciousness

15.meaning: All-Wise; one possessing perfect wisdom, who places everything in its right place and decides with flawless judgement. As an intensive form it conveys wisdom that is complete and sound.
15.grammar: An intensive adjective ('all-wise') on the faʿīl pattern, stressing the quality to its fullest degree. The -an (tanwīn) combines the -a accusative ending — typical of a predicate or object — with the -n marking it indefinite.

1.meaning: But, however, rather — a particle that sets off a correction or contrast with what came before, redirecting the statement.

parts.en: kasra of the light (reduced) particle form

1.grammar: A contrastive particle meaning 'but/however'. This is the light/reduced form of the emphatic لٰكِنَّ (lākinna): the doubled nūn is elided and the particle no longer governs a following noun. The final kasra (-i) belongs to the identity of this reduced form rather than being mere pronunciation liaison.

2.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
2.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.
2.root: — (proper divine name)

3.meaning: 'he bears witness / testifies' — to give firm testimony, to attest to the truth of something with certain knowledge.
3.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ya- prefix means 'he' (the doer), and the -u ending marks the ordinary, unrestricted present tense ('he bears witness / does testify').
3.root: ش-ه-د (sh-h-d) — to witness, testify, be present

4.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
4.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

5.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'he sent down, he caused to descend, he revealed' — used especially of Allah sending down revelation, rain, or blessings from above.
5.grammar: A completed (past) action by a single masculine subject ('he'); the -a ending marks third-person masculine singular. The form IV (causative) pattern means 'to make something come down,' i.e., to send it down.

6.meaning: 'To you' (addressing one person): indicating direction or motion toward a single individual — that toward which something moves or is directed.
6.grammar: The preposition ilā ('to, towards') with an attached pronoun; before a suffix ilā takes the form ilay-. The -ka ending is the pronoun 'you' for a single male addressee. Pronouns following a preposition stand in the genitive relationship, though their form does not visibly change for case.
6.root: — (preposition + pronoun)

7.meaning: 'he sent it down' — to send down or cause to descend, used of revelation coming down from Allah.
7.grammar: A past-tense verb in the causative (form IV) pattern ('to make come down, send down'). The final -a marks a completed action by 'he,' and the attached -hu ('it') is the direct object. So: 'he sent it down.'
7.root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — to descend, come down; to send down

8.meaning: 'with His knowledge' — by means of, or accompanied by, Allah's own knowledge.
8.grammar: The prefix bi- ('with / by means of') is a preposition. The base is 'knowledge,' and the attached -hi means 'His.' The -i ending on the noun is genitive, the case required after the preposition bi-.

9.meaning: And the angels — pure, created beings of light who serve and obey Allah; 'malāʾikah' is the plural of 'malak', an angel.
9.grammar: A plural noun 'angels' made definite by 'al-' ('the') and preceded by 'wa' ('and'). The '-at-' is the feminine-form plural marker, and the final -u ending is nominative, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence.
9.root: أ-ل-ك (ʾ-l-k) — sending, conveying a message (an angel as a bearer of a message); the noun is also linked to م-ل-ك (m-l-k), dominion/ownership

10.meaning: 'they bear witness / testify' — a group giving firm testimony or attesting to the truth of something.
10.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ya- prefix together with the -ūna ending means 'they' (masculine plural). The -ūna ending marks the ordinary, unrestricted present tense for a plural subject ('they bear witness / do testify').
10.root: ش-ه-د (sh-h-d) — to witness, testify, be present

11.meaning: 'And He suffices / is enough' — to be sufficient, adequate, and fully enough so that nothing more is needed. It conveys complete adequacy, often used to affirm that Allah alone is enough.
11.grammar: The connective wa- ('and') prefixed to a 3rd-person masculine singular perfect (past-tense) verb (Form I) whose final weak root letter (the yāʾ) appears as a long -ā. It states a completed yet timeless fact — 'and He is sufficient' — the kind of perfect form used for an enduring truth.
11.root: ك-ف-ي (k-f-y) — to suffice, be enough, be adequate; to spare someone need of anything else

12.meaning: A phrase 'in Allah / by Allah', combining the preposition 'with/in/by' and the divine name Allah, the proper name of the One God.
12.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with, by means of') prefixed to the divine name Allah. A preposition always forces the following noun into the genitive case, which is why Allah here ends in -i. With verbs of believing, bi- conveys the object of faith — to believe IN.
12.root: — (Allah is the proper name of God and is not derived from a triliteral root in the usual sense)

13.meaning: 'A witness' — one who sees and attests, who can give evidence; also carries the sense of one who is present and observant, and at times 'a martyr' (one who bears witness with their life).
13.grammar: An intensive describing-noun (pattern fa‘īl) meaning 'a witness, one who fully attests', indefinite. The -an ending (the accusative with 'tanwīn') marks it as indefinite and in the accusative — the case used for a direct object, or for a word that describes the state or role in which someone stands.

1.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
1.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: 'They disbelieved / rejected faith' — from a root meaning to cover over or conceal. To disbelieve in this sense is to cover up and refuse the truth, and also to be ungrateful, hiding or denying favours received.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third person masculine plural: 'they disbelieved'. The completed action is built into the stem kafara ('he disbelieved'), and the -ū suffix (written وا) marks the doer as 'they' (masculine plural). The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention with no sound.
3.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to reject faith, be ungrateful

4.meaning: 'and they turned away / barred others' — to block, obstruct, or hinder from a path, and to turn oneself or others away from it.
4.grammar: The prefix wa- means 'and'. The base is a past-tense verb, and the -ū ending means 'they' (masculine plural). So it conveys a completed action: 'they barred / turned away.'
4.root: ص-د-د (ṣ-d-d) — to turn away, obstruct, hinder, avert

5.meaning: A preposition meaning 'on behalf of,' 'for,' 'about,' or 'away from.' It often conveys removing a burden from someone or acting in their place.

parts.en: on behalf of / for / away from

5.grammar: A preposition (a linking particle). It governs the noun that follows it, putting that noun into the genitive case. It does not change form.

6.meaning: 'path, way, road' — a route or course; figuratively a cause or way of life one travels along. In construct ('the way OF ...').
6.grammar: A singular noun with the '-i' (genitive) ending, which typically links it to a following noun ('the way OF ...') or follows a preposition. It marks the word as connected to or possessed by what comes after.
6.root: س-ب-ل (s-b-l) — way, path, road

7.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
7.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

8.meaning: A short particle placed before a verb to emphasize or affirm it. Before a past-tense verb it means 'indeed / certainly / has already (happened)'; before a present-tense verb it can mean 'sometimes / may'. It sharpens and confirms the verb that follows.
8.grammar: An indeclinable particle (its form never changes). It does not take case or tense endings; its job is to color the following verb — affirming and intensifying a past action ('has indeed done') or signaling occasional possibility with a present verb.

9.meaning: 'they went astray / erred' — to lose the right way, to wander off into error or misguidance.
9.grammar: A past-tense verb with the -ū ending meaning 'they' (masculine plural). It conveys a completed action: 'they went astray / erred.'
9.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to stray, lose the way, go astray

10.meaning: straying / error — the state of being lost from the right path, wandering far from guidance and truth. A verbal noun naming the condition of going astray.
10.grammar: A verbal noun (maṣdar) on the faʿāl pattern, naming the act/state of straying. The final -an (tanwīn fatḥah) marks the accusative — often used for the object of a verb or as an absolute object reinforcing a verb ('to stray a [great] straying') — and the -n shows it is indefinite.
10.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to stray, get lost, err

11.meaning: Far, distant, remote — describing something at a great remove in space, time, or degree. As an adjective it qualifies a noun as 'far off, far-reaching'.
11.grammar: An adjective on the faʿīl pattern (often intensive: 'very far'). The -an ending (tanwīn) marks it indefinite and accusative — agreeing with an indefinite accusative noun it describes. The accusative is the case of objects and many complements; the tanwīn marks indefiniteness ('a far …').

3.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to reject faith, be ungrateful

4.meaning: 'and they wronged / did injustice' — to commit wrong, to place something where it does not belong, especially by oppression or transgression.
4.grammar: The prefix wa- means 'and'. The base is a past-tense verb, and the -ū ending means 'they' (masculine plural). So it conveys a completed action: 'they wronged / did injustice.'

5.meaning: A negating particle, 'not', used specifically to deny that an action happened in the past, even though it attaches to a present-tense verb form. It turns 'you do X' into 'you did not do X'.

parts.en: did not (negation of a completed act)

5.grammar: An indeclinable particle that governs the verb after it, putting that verb into the jussive (clipped) mood and giving it past-time meaning. In short: lam + a present-form verb = 'did not [verb]'.

6.meaning: A core verb meaning 'to be' or 'to come to be / happen' — used to say that something exists, occurs, or is the case.
6.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it is/becomes'), in the jussive (command/conditional) mood. The base form is yakun with a silent final consonant; the -i here is a helping vowel added only to ease pronunciation before a following word that begins with a cluster.
6.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, exist, come to pass; being

7.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
7.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

8.meaning: 'so that He may forgive' — to forgive, to cover over and pardon a wrong so that it is not held against the person.
8.grammar: The purpose-particle li- ('so that, in order to') joined to a present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('He forgives'). Because of li-, the verb is subjunctive, shown by the final -a ending, which gives the sense of intended result: 'so that He may forgive'.
8.root: غ-ف-ر (gh-f-r) — to cover, shield; to forgive, pardon

9.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
9.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

10.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
10.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

11.meaning: 'so that He may guide them' — to guide, to show the way and lead someone rightly, here directed toward 'them'.
11.grammar: The purpose-particle li- ('so that') joined to a present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('He guides'), with the object pronoun -hum ('them') attached. Because of li-, the verb is subjunctive, shown by the -a ending on the stem (before the pronoun), giving the sense 'so that He may guide them'.
11.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — to guide, lead aright; guidance

12.meaning: 'a way / path / road' — a route or course one travels, literally or figuratively.
12.grammar: A noun in the accusative with tanwīn (-an). The -an ending typically marks the word as a direct object and signals that it is indefinite ('a way / path').
12.root: ط-ر-ق (ṭ-r-q) — to knock, beat a path; a road, way

1.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
1.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

2.meaning: 'the way / path of …' — a route or course one travels, here in a form that links to a following word.
2.grammar: A noun with the -a (accusative) ending and no tanwīn, which signals it is bound to a following noun in a possessive 'the … of …' construction (e.g. 'the way of so-and-so'). It functions as the object of a verb while being defined by what follows.
2.root: ط-ر-ق (ṭ-r-q) — to knock, beat a path; a road, way

3.meaning: Jahannam — a proper name for the Fire of punishment in the Hereafter, the abode of torment. It is a name rather than a descriptive common noun.
3.grammar: A proper name. Because it is a special, non-fully-inflecting noun (it does not take tanwīn), it shows the -a ending in places where most nouns would otherwise take -i; here the single -a serves for both accusative and genitive positions. As a name it carries no general dictionary 'meaning' but designates the abode of punishment.
3.root: — (a proper name; commonly treated as having no Arabic triliteral root)

4.meaning: Ones who abide / remain forever — those who dwell perpetually and permanently in a state or place, without end. The word denotes lasting, undying permanence.
4.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer' word: 'ones abiding'). The -īna ending is the sound masculine plural in its accusative/genitive form, used when the word is an object or governed by a preceding element. It describes people characterized by perpetual abiding.

5.meaning: 'In it / therein.' A preposition with an attached pronoun: 'in' plus a feminine singular 'it,' meaning 'inside it / within it,' referring back to some feminine or grammatically feminine thing (such as a place).
5.grammar: A prepositional phrase: fī ('in, within') with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine singular). The pronoun is the object of the preposition and points back to a previously mentioned feminine noun.

6.meaning: An adverb meaning 'ever / forever / at any time' — used to stress that something will never (or always) be the case throughout all time, especially with a negative to mean 'never, not ever'.
6.grammar: A noun used adverbially. The ending -an is the indefinite accusative, the form regularly used to turn a word into an adverb of time ('… ever / forever'); the -n (nunation) marks it as indefinite. Paired with a negation it strengthens it to 'never, not ever'.
6.root: ء-ب-د (ʾ-b-d) — endless duration, eternity, perpetuity

7.meaning: And he was / he became — a verb of being that places a subject in a past state or links it to a description in the past.
7.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'kāna' is a past-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular, meaning 'he was/became'; it commonly introduces a past condition and is typically followed by a noun describing the subject's state. The final -a marks completed past action by a single male.

8.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
8.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

9.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
9.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
9.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

10.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
10.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

11.meaning: 'Easy, effortless, slight, manageable.' It describes something simple to do or small in amount.
11.grammar: An adjective on the faʿīl pattern. The -an ending is the indefinite accusative ('an easy …'), commonly marking an adjective agreeing with an indefinite accusative noun it describes, or a verb's object/complement.
11.root: ي-س-ر (y-s-r) — to be easy, light, manageable

1.meaning: 'O…!' — a compound vocative expression used to call out and summon an audience before addressing them. It fuses the call-particle 'yā' ('O') with a noun that means 'the one(s) addressed,' yielding an emphatic 'O you…!' that introduces direct address.
1.grammar: A vocative (calling) construction. 'Yā' is the particle for calling out; 'ayyu' carries a nominative '-u' as the one being summoned; 'hā' is an attention-drawing particle. Together they function as 'O you…!,' setting up the noun of address that follows.

2.meaning: 'The people / mankind' — human beings collectively, people in general, humanity.
2.grammar: A collective noun with the definite article al- ('the'); the article's 'l' assimilates into the following 'n' (al-nās → an-nās). The -u ending marks the nominative case — the case used for the subject of a sentence or the basic naming form of a noun.
2.root: ن-و-س / أ-ن-س (n-w-s / ʾ-n-s) — humankind, people, sociability

3.meaning: A short particle placed before a verb to emphasize or affirm it. Before a past-tense verb it means 'indeed / certainly / has already (happened)'; before a present-tense verb it can mean 'sometimes / may'. It sharpens and confirms the verb that follows.
3.grammar: An indeclinable particle (its form never changes). It does not take case or tense endings; its job is to color the following verb — affirming and intensifying a past action ('has indeed done') or signaling occasional possibility with a present verb.

4.meaning: 'he/it came to you' — the arrival of someone or something to a group of people addressed.
4.grammar: A past-tense verb ('came'), done by 'he/it'. The verb is intransitive, so the attached -kum ('you,' plural) is not a direct object but a recipient/directional pronoun marking the people the arrival is toward ('came to you'); it is voweled -kumu before a following word. So: 'he/it came to you (all).'

5.meaning: 'The Messenger' — one sent with a message; in religious usage, a prophet commissioned by Allah to deliver revelation to people.
5.grammar: 'al-' is the definite article 'the' (its 'l' assimilates into the following r, doubling it). 'rasūl' is a noun meaning 'one who is sent, an envoy/messenger'. The final -u is the nominative ending, the case typically marking the subject of a sentence or a word simply being named.

6.meaning: 'With the truth / by means of what is true and right.' Combines the preposition 'with/by' and 'the truth' — that which is real, established, correct, and rightfully due, as opposed to falsehood.
6.grammar: A noun governed by the attached preposition bi- ('with/by'). The -i ending is the genitive case, which is required after a preposition; here it links 'the truth' to 'with', giving 'with the truth'.
6.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, right, reality, that which is established and due

7.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
7.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

8.meaning: 'Your Lord' (addressing a group). 'Rabb' is a rich term: the Master, Owner, Sustainer and Nurturer who creates, possesses, provides for, and brings a thing to its proper completion — far more than a mere ruler.
8.grammar: A noun ('Lord') with an attached possessive pronoun, forming a possessive pairing. 'Rabb' carries a doubled (geminated) 'b' — the shaddah — at its core. The '-i' vowel on 'rabb' is its case ending, determined by 'Lord's' own role in the sentence (not by the suffix); the attached '-kum' is the possessor ('your'), addressing a plural 'you', and as the possessed-to term it sits in the genitive.

9.meaning: So believe! — a command to put faith and trust in something, here joined to a preceding clause by 'so/then', directing the listeners to come to belief.
9.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to a group: 'believe!' The -ū ending marks a masculine plural addressee ('you all'). The fa- prefix is a connective meaning 'so' or 'then', linking this command to what came before as its consequence. Built on Form IV, which here carries the sense of having and giving faith/security.
9.root: أ-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — to be secure, to trust; faith, safety

10.meaning: Good — that which is beneficial, virtuous, and excellent; goodness as a thing one can do or possess, and what is better or preferable.
10.grammar: A noun (also serving as the 'better/best' form). The final -an (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite and in the accusative case — the case used for the direct object of a verb ('to do good') and for similar governed roles.

11.meaning: 'for you,' 'to you,' 'for your benefit' — the preposition 'for/to' joined to 'you (plural).' It marks the party for whose sake, benefit, or possession something exists or is given.
11.grammar: A preposition ('for/to') with the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you, plural'). It assigns a benefit, purpose, or recipient — 'for you (all).' The suffix '-kum' is the plural 'you,' showing the recipients are a group.

12.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
12.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

13.meaning: A verb meaning 'you (plural) disbelieve, reject, or deny' — to refuse faith and turn away ungratefully from the truth. The root also carries the sense of covering over or being ungrateful for what one has received.
13.grammar: A present/future-tense verb. The ta- prefix with the -ū ending marks a masculine plural 'you all' subject. The shortened -ū (rather than -ūna) signals a dependent mood (subjunctive/jussive), as after particles like 'that,' 'lest,' or a negative command.

14.meaning: A two-part connector meaning 'so/then, indeed…'. It joins fa- ('so', 'then', marking a result or consequence) to inna, an emphatic particle that strongly affirms the statement that follows ('truly', 'verily').
14.grammar: fa- is a connective prefix signaling that what follows is a consequence or next step. inna is an emphatic particle that introduces a nominal sentence, puts its following noun in the accusative, and strengthens the assertion; it does not itself take a case ending.

15.meaning: A two-part word: the preposition 'li-' meaning 'to', 'for', or 'belonging to', attached to the name 'Allah'. It conveys 'to Allah' or 'for Allah'.
15.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('to/for') pulls the following noun into the genitive case, which is why 'Allah' ends in '-i' (llāhi). The '-i' ending is the regular result of a noun governed by a preposition.

16.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
16.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

17.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
17.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

18.meaning: The heavens / the skies — the plural of 'heaven', referring to the skies above and the celestial realms; the elevated expanse over the earth.
18.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun with the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the heavens') or follows a preposition. In the sound feminine plural, this -i form also covers what would be an object role.

19.meaning: 'And the earth' — the connective 'and' joined to 'the earth', meaning the ground, land, or the world beneath the sky.
19.grammar: The connective 'wa-' ('and') with the definite feminine noun 'al-arḍ' ('the earth'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the earth') or follows a preposition, here matching the case of what it is joined to.
19.root: أ-ر-ض (ʾ-r-ḍ) — earth, land

20.meaning: And he was / he became — a verb of being that places a subject in a past state or links it to a description in the past.
20.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'kāna' is a past-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular, meaning 'he was/became'; it commonly introduces a past condition and is typically followed by a noun describing the subject's state. The final -a marks completed past action by a single male.

21.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
21.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

22.meaning: All-Knowing; one possessing complete, perfect knowledge. As an intensive form it conveys knowledge that is total and unfailing, encompassing all things.
22.grammar: An intensive adjective ('all-knowing') on the faʿīl pattern, which stresses the quality to its fullest degree. The -an (tanwīn) joins the -a accusative ending — typical of a predicate or object — with the -n marking it indefinite.

23.meaning: All-Wise; one possessing perfect wisdom, who places everything in its right place and decides with flawless judgement. As an intensive form it conveys wisdom that is complete and sound.
23.grammar: An intensive adjective ('all-wise') on the faʿīl pattern, stressing the quality to its fullest degree. The -an (tanwīn) combines the -a accusative ending — typical of a predicate or object — with the -n marking it indefinite.

1.meaning: 'O people of… / O folk of…' — a vocative call ('O!') addressed to the 'people' or 'folk' belonging to something (such as the people of a household, place, or scripture).
1.grammar: The vocative particle ya ('O') used to address or call out, plus the noun 'people/folk'. The -a ending is accusative, which is the case a called-upon noun takes when it is attached to a following word ('O people OF …'). It denotes those who belong to or are associated with something.
1.root: ا-ه-ل (ʾ-h-l) — family, folk, those belonging to

2.meaning: 'The Book / the Scripture' — a written record or revealed scripture; literally that which is written.
2.grammar: The definite article al- with the noun kitāb ('book, scripture'), itself a verbal noun from 'to write.' The -i ending is genitive, typically marking the word as following a preposition or standing in an 'of' relationship to a preceding noun.
2.root: ك-ت-ب (k-t-b) — writing, inscribing, recording

3.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
3.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

4.meaning: 'do not go to excess / overstep the bounds' — to exceed proper limits, especially exaggeration in matters of religion.
4.grammar: A present/jussive-form verb. The ta- prefix together with the -ū ending means 'you' (masculine plural). The bare, un-vowelled (jussive) form is the shape used after a prohibitive or negative particle, giving the sense 'you (should) not go to excess.'
4.root: غ-ل-و (gh-l-w) — to exceed, go beyond bounds, exaggerate

5.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
5.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

6.meaning: 'your religion / your way of life' — dīn: the complete system of belief, worship, obedience, and recompense by which one lives before Allah; here bound to 'your.'
6.grammar: The base dīn denotes the all-encompassing religion or way of obedience and accountability before Allah. The attached -kum means 'your' (plural). The -i ending is genitive — the case taken when the noun follows a preposition or is linked to a possessor, here marked by the 'your' suffix.
6.root: د-ي-ن (d-y-n) — religion, obedience, judgment; debt/recompense

7.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
7.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

8.meaning: You (all) say / utter — referring to speaking or saying words, addressed to a group. In context it is the form used after a particle so that it reads 'do not say' / 'that you may say'.
8.grammar: Present-tense verb, second-person masculine plural ('you all'). The ta- prefix marks the second person; plurality is supplied by the -ū ending. The plain ending here (without final -na) is the form a verb takes after certain particles such as 'do not' or 'so that', signalling command-prohibition or purpose.

9.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
9.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
9.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

10.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
10.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

11.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
11.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

12.meaning: The truth — that which is real, right, and established; reality, the just due, the genuine as opposed to the false.
12.grammar: A definite noun with 'the'. The -a ending is the accusative, typically marking the noun as the direct object of a verb ('the truth').
12.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, right, that which is established and real

13.meaning: 'Only / nothing but' — a restrictive particle that limits and emphasizes, asserting that the matter is exclusively so and no other ('it is only...'). It combines the emphatic 'inna' with the restricting 'mā'.
13.grammar: A compound particle formed from the emphatic inna ('indeed') and mā, which together work as a tool of restriction meaning 'only / nothing but'. It both stresses and confines the statement that follows to a single truth, excluding all alternatives.

14.meaning: Al-Masīḥ, 'the Messiah / the Anointed One' — a title of the Prophet ʿĪsā (Jesus). It signifies one who is anointed or wiped over, traditionally linked to blessing and to his role of healing by touch.
14.grammar: A definite noun used as a title. The al- prefix means 'the', making it specific. The -u ending is nominative, the case used for the subject of a sentence or for a noun identifying who or what something is. Masīḥ has the form of a passive participle ('one who is anointed/wiped').
14.root: م-س-ح (m-s-ḥ) — to wipe, anoint, stroke over

15.meaning: "Isa" — the personal name of the prophet Jesus, son of Mary.
15.grammar: A proper name (a foreign/non-Arabic name). It is fully indeclinable: its ending does not change for case, so it stays the same as subject, object, or after a preposition.

16.meaning: 'Son' — a male child or descendant. It expresses the relationship of being the son of someone.
16.grammar: A noun. The -u ending is nominative, the case used for the subject or for a noun in apposition (a word that renames or further identifies another). The initial alif is a connecting hamza, normally elided after a preceding word, so it is read as 'bnu'. It is typically followed by the name of the father or parent ('son OF …').
16.root: ب-ن-و / ب-ن-ي (b-n-w/y) — son; to build (offspring as that which is built up)

17.meaning: "Maryam" — the personal name Mary, the mother of the prophet Jesus.
17.grammar: A proper name (feminine, foreign origin). It is diptote: it takes no -n (nunation), and in the genitive and accusative it ends in -a rather than -i, so the -a ending shown serves for both object and "of" positions.

18.meaning: A messenger or envoy: one who is sent by another to deliver a message or carry out a commission. In Qur'anic usage it most often denotes a prophet sent by Allah with revelation.
18.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The final -u ending is nominative, the case that typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word identified by a linking verb ('… is …').

19.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
19.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

20.meaning: 'And His word' — a 'word' meaning an utterance, statement, or decree, joined to a possessor ('His'). A kalima is a single meaningful unit of speech; it can also carry the sense of a divine command or pronouncement.
20.grammar: Prefix wa- means 'and'. The stem is a singular feminine noun carrying the nominative -u ending (typical of a subject or predicate). The attached suffix -hu means 'his/His', marking the word as belonging to a third-person masculine possessor.

21.meaning: 'He cast/conveyed it (feminine)' — the act of throwing, casting, or delivering something onto or toward someone; figuratively, to convey or place a thing (such as a word or command) into someone or something.
21.grammar: A past-tense verb in the derived (causative) pattern, third-person masculine singular: 'he cast/conveyed'. The attached suffix -hā is the object pronoun 'it/her', referring to a grammatically feminine thing that received the action.
21.root: ل-ق-ي (l-q-y) — to meet, to cast / throw

22.meaning: A preposition meaning 'to,' 'toward,' or 'up to' — pointing to the end-point, goal, or limit of a motion, direction, or extent.
22.grammar: A preposition (a small linking word). It governs the noun after it, putting that noun in the genitive case, and points to a destination or limit ('to,' 'toward,' 'as far as').

23.meaning: "Maryam" — the personal name Mary, the mother of the prophet Jesus.
23.grammar: A proper name (feminine, foreign origin). It is diptote: it takes no -n (nunation), and in the genitive and accusative it ends in -a rather than -i, so the -a ending shown serves for both object and "of" positions.

24.meaning: 'And a spirit' — a spirit, breath of life, or animating principle. Rūḥ denotes an unseen, life-giving reality; in Qur'anic contexts it can refer to the soul, to divine inspiration, or to an exalted created being.
24.grammar: Prefix wa- means 'and'. The stem is a masculine noun with the ending -un, which is nominative (subject/predicate case) and indefinite ('a spirit'). The final -n (tanwīn) signals indefiniteness, i.e. 'a/an' rather than 'the'.

25.meaning: 'From Him' — the preposition 'from', expressing origin or source, attached to a third-person pronoun, conveying that something proceeds or originates from Him.
25.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from' (origin/source) with the attached pronoun -hu ('him/Him'). Pronouns following a preposition stand in the genitive; here the suffix marks a third-person masculine source.

26.meaning: So believe! — a command to put faith and trust in something, here joined to a preceding clause by 'so/then', directing the listeners to come to belief.
26.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to a group: 'believe!' The -ū ending marks a masculine plural addressee ('you all'). The fa- prefix is a connective meaning 'so' or 'then', linking this command to what came before as its consequence. Built on Form IV, which here carries the sense of having and giving faith/security.
26.root: أ-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — to be secure, to trust; faith, safety

27.meaning: A phrase 'in Allah / by Allah', combining the preposition 'with/in/by' and the divine name Allah, the proper name of the One God.
27.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with, by means of') prefixed to the divine name Allah. A preposition always forces the following noun into the genitive case, which is why Allah here ends in -i. With verbs of believing, bi- conveys the object of faith — to believe IN.
27.root: — (Allah is the proper name of God and is not derived from a triliteral root in the usual sense)

28.meaning: "and His messengers" — wa- joins it on; the plural of 'messenger / envoy,' those sent with a message, with -hi 'His' marking them as sent by Allah.
28.grammar: A plural noun ('messengers') with an attached possessive. The -i before the pronoun is the genitive (possessive/'of') case, and -hi means 'his/His', the i-coloured form used after an -i vowel.
28.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — to send; a messenger, an envoy

29.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
29.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

30.meaning: You (all) say / utter — referring to speaking or saying words, addressed to a group. In context it is the form used after a particle so that it reads 'do not say' / 'that you may say'.
30.grammar: Present-tense verb, second-person masculine plural ('you all'). The ta- prefix marks the second person; plurality is supplied by the -ū ending. The plain ending here (without final -na) is the form a verb takes after certain particles such as 'do not' or 'so that', signalling command-prohibition or purpose.
30.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, speak, utter

31.meaning: 'Three' — the cardinal number three. As a standalone noun it names the quantity itself.
31.grammar: A cardinal-number noun. The ending -un is nominative (the subject/predicate case) and indefinite, the final -n (tanwīn) marking it as indefinite ('three' standing on its own rather than 'the three').
31.root: ث-ل-ث (th-l-th) — three

32.meaning: 'Cease! / Desist!' — a command to stop, leave off, or refrain from doing something, addressed to a group of people.
32.grammar: A command (imperative) verb from the reflexive pattern, addressed to a plural 'you'. The long -ū ending marks a masculine plural addressee: 'all of you, stop!'
32.root: ن-ه-ي (n-h-y) — to forbid, to cease / come to an end

33.meaning: Good — that which is beneficial, virtuous, and excellent; goodness as a thing one can do or possess, and what is better or preferable.
33.grammar: A noun (also serving as the 'better/best' form). The final -an (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite and in the accusative case — the case used for the direct object of a verb ('to do good') and for similar governed roles.

34.meaning: 'for you,' 'to you,' 'for your benefit' — the preposition 'for/to' joined to 'you (plural).' It marks the party for whose sake, benefit, or possession something exists or is given.
34.grammar: A preposition ('for/to') with the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you, plural'). It assigns a benefit, purpose, or recipient — 'for you (all).' The suffix '-kum' is the plural 'you,' showing the recipients are a group.

35.meaning: 'Only / nothing but' — a restrictive particle that limits and emphasizes, asserting that the matter is exclusively so and no other ('it is only...'). It combines the emphatic 'inna' with the restricting 'mā'.
35.grammar: A compound particle formed from the emphatic inna ('indeed') and mā, which together work as a tool of restriction meaning 'only / nothing but'. It both stresses and confines the statement that follows to a single truth, excluding all alternatives.

36.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
36.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

37.meaning: A god / an object of worship — a being taken as a deity and worshipped. As an indefinite noun it means 'a god' in the general sense.
37.grammar: A singular noun. The -un ending (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a god') and in the nominative case, typically used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate.
37.root: أ-ل-ه (ʾ-l-h) — godhood, worship, being a deity

38.meaning: One / single and unique — denoting oneness: a single individual, undivided and without partner or plurality.
38.grammar: An adjective/numeral meaning 'one.' The -un ending (nunation) marks it as indefinite and in the nominative case, the case typically used for a subject, predicate, or a descriptor agreeing with such a noun.

39.meaning: An exclamation of glorification meaning 'far removed and utterly above all imperfection is He.' The verbal noun 'subḥān' declares that the One referred to is exalted beyond any deficiency, partner, or fault, and the attached 'Him' directs that declaration to a single masculine being.
39.grammar: A verbal noun used as an absolute exclamation, fixed in the accusative ending -a (an emphatic declaration, roughly 'I declare His utter transcendence'). The attached -hu is the possessive/object pronoun 'Him', referring to one masculine person.
39.root: س-ب-ح (s-b-ḥ) — to swim/glide away, hence to declare Allah free of all imperfection

40.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
40.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

41.meaning: '(That) He be / there be' — a form of the core verb 'to be/become', expressing existence or a state of being.
41.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he is/becomes' or 'there is'). The ya- prefix marks the 'he' subject. The final -a is the subjunctive ending, used after certain particles (e.g. 'that', 'so that', 'in order to') and giving the sense of a dependent or hoped-for action.
41.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to become

42.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
42.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'.
