The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

43.meaning: 'A child / a boy / offspring' — a son or child, the offspring born to a parent.
43.grammar: A noun. The -un ending is nominative with tanwīn (nunation — the doubled 'n' sound marking an indefinite noun, 'a child'). The nominative case marks it as the subject of a sentence or as a noun whose existence is being affirmed or denied. The initial wa- here is part of the root (w-l-d), not the conjunction 'and'.
43.root: و-ل-د (w-l-d) — to give birth, beget; offspring

44.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
44.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

45.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
45.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

46.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
46.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

47.meaning: The heavens / the skies — the plural of 'heaven', referring to the skies above and the celestial realms; the elevated expanse over the earth.
47.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun with the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the heavens') or follows a preposition. In the sound feminine plural, this -i form also covers what would be an object role.

48.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
48.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

49.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
49.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

50.meaning: The earth; the land, ground, or soil. The world we walk upon, as opposed to the sky.
50.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('... of the earth') or follows a preposition (as after 'in / on the earth').

51.meaning: 'And He suffices / is enough' — to be sufficient, adequate, and fully enough so that nothing more is needed. It conveys complete adequacy, often used to affirm that Allah alone is enough.
51.grammar: The connective wa- ('and') prefixed to a 3rd-person masculine singular perfect (past-tense) verb (Form I) whose final weak root letter (the yāʾ) appears as a long -ā. It states a completed yet timeless fact — 'and He is sufficient' — the kind of perfect form used for an enduring truth.
51.root: ك-ف-ي (k-f-y) — to suffice, be enough, be adequate; to spare someone need of anything else

52.meaning: A phrase 'in Allah / by Allah', combining the preposition 'with/in/by' and the divine name Allah, the proper name of the One God.
52.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with, by means of') prefixed to the divine name Allah. A preposition always forces the following noun into the genitive case, which is why Allah here ends in -i. With verbs of believing, bi- conveys the object of faith — to believe IN.
52.root: — (Allah is the proper name of God and is not derived from a triliteral root in the usual sense)

53.meaning: 'A trustee / guardian / disposer of affairs' — one entrusted with someone's affairs to manage and take charge of them; a dependable agent, protector, or guarantor on whom one relies.
53.grammar: A singular masculine noun of the faʿīl pattern. The ending -an is accusative and indefinite, a case commonly marking the object of a verb or the complement after verbs like 'to be' ('to be a trustee'). The final -n (tanwīn) marks indefiniteness.
53.root: و-ك-ل (w-k-l) — to entrust, to rely upon

1.meaning: 'Never / will not' — a particle that negates a future action emphatically. Lan denies that something will ever happen, stronger and more absolute than a simple 'not'.
1.grammar: A negating particle that applies to present-tense verbs to deny them in the future ('will never…'). Grammatically it also puts the following verb into the subjunctive mood, which clips that verb's ending to a short -a. Lan itself does not change.

2.meaning: '(That) he disdain / scorn' — to hold oneself above something out of pride, to consider a thing beneath one's dignity and so refuse it haughtily.
2.grammar: A present-tense verb in the intensive reflexive (form X) pattern, third-person masculine singular: 'he disdains/scorns'. The ya- prefix marks the 'he' subject. The final -a is the subjunctive ending, used after particles such as 'that' or 'so that' to express a dependent or potential action.
2.root: ن-ك-ف (n-k-f) — to disdain, to recoil from in pride

3.meaning: Al-Masīḥ, 'the Messiah / the Anointed One' — a title of the Prophet ʿĪsā (Jesus). It signifies one who is anointed or wiped over, traditionally linked to blessing and to his role of healing by touch.
3.grammar: A definite noun used as a title. The al- prefix means 'the', making it specific. The -u ending is nominative, the case used for the subject of a sentence or for a noun identifying who or what something is. Masīḥ has the form of a passive participle ('one who is anointed/wiped').
3.root: م-س-ح (m-s-ḥ) — to wipe, anoint, stroke over

4.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
4.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

5.meaning: '(That) He be / there be' — a form of the core verb 'to be/become', expressing existence or a state of being.
5.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he is/becomes' or 'there is'). The ya- prefix marks the 'he' subject. The final -a is the subjunctive ending, used after certain particles (e.g. 'that', 'so that', 'in order to') and giving the sense of a dependent or hoped-for action.
5.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to become

6.meaning: 'A servant / slave / bondsman' — a human being as one who serves and is wholly owned by, and submissive to, his master. In Qur'anic usage it especially conveys a worshipping servant of Allah.
6.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The ending -an is accusative and indefinite, the case that typically marks the object of a verb or a complement; the final -n (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('a servant').
6.root: ع-ب-د (ʿ-b-d) — to serve, to worship

7.meaning: 'To / for Allah' — the preposition 'to/for' (expressing belonging, purpose, or recipient) joined to the name Allah, conveying that something belongs to or is due to Allah.
7.grammar: The prefixed preposition li- ('to/for', also marking possession or purpose) attached to the proper name Allah. After this preposition the name takes the genitive (its -i ending), the case used for the object of a preposition and for showing belonging.

8.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
8.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

9.meaning: The angels; spiritual beings created by Allah who serve and obey Him and carry out His commands.
9.grammar: A collective plural noun ('the angels') made definite by the prefix al- ('the'). The -u ending is nominative, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or for the doer of an action.
9.root: م-ل-ك (m-l-k) — possess, command; an angel (some link the word to ʾ-l-k, to send a message, hence a messenger/envoy)

10.meaning: 'Those brought near / the near ones' — people who are drawn close and granted nearness (to Allah), i.e. those held in a position of intimacy and favour.
10.grammar: A passive participle of the intensive (form II) pattern with the definite article al- ('the'). The -ūna ending marks a sound masculine plural in the nominative case (the subject/predicate case): 'the ones who are brought near'. The pattern is passive in sense ('brought near' rather than 'bringing near').
10.root: ق-ر-ب (q-r-b) — to be near, to draw close

11.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
11.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

12.meaning: '(If) he disdains / scorns' — to hold oneself above something out of pride and refuse it haughtily, considering it beneath one's dignity.
12.grammar: A present-tense verb in the intensive reflexive (form X) pattern, third-person masculine singular. The ya- prefix marks the 'he' subject. The bare, vowelless ending (jussive) is the form taken after conditional or jussive particles such as 'if' or 'not', giving the sense of a conditioned or negated action.
12.root: ن-ك-ف (n-k-f) — to disdain, to recoil from in pride

13.meaning: A preposition meaning 'on behalf of,' 'for,' 'about,' or 'away from.' It often conveys removing a burden from someone or acting in their place.

parts.en: on behalf of / for / away from

13.grammar: A preposition (a linking particle). It governs the noun that follows it, putting that noun into the genitive case. It does not change form.

14.meaning: 'His worship / service' — the act of worshipping and serving, joined to a possessor ('His'). ʿibāda denotes devoted worship and humble servitude offered to Allah.
14.grammar: A verbal noun (the noun of the act of worshipping), feminine, with the attached possessive suffix meaning 'his/His'. The -i ending is genitive, the case taken when a noun is possessed by a following pronoun or governed by a preposition; the suffix form -hi (rather than -hu) follows that -i vowel.

15.meaning: 'And he acts arrogantly / is haughty' — to be proud and overbearing, to swell with self-importance and refuse to submit, regarding oneself as greater than one is.
15.grammar: Prefix wa- means 'and'. The verb is present-tense, intensive reflexive (form X), third-person masculine singular, the ya- prefix marking the 'he' subject. The bare, vowelless ending (jussive) is the form taken after conditional or jussive particles such as 'if' or 'not', expressing a conditioned or negated action.
15.root: ك-ب-ر (k-b-r) — to be great; (form X) to deem oneself great, to be arrogant

16.meaning: 'Then He will gather them' — to assemble, herd, and bring a multitude together into one place; with a future sense, that He will muster them all together.
16.grammar: Prefix fa- means 'then/so' (sequence or consequence); sa- marks the near future ('will'); ya- marks the 'he' subject. The verb is present-tense, third-person masculine singular; the -u ending is the indicative, the plain statement-of-fact form. The suffix -hum is the object pronoun 'them' (a group of males).
16.root: ح-ش-ر (ḥ-sh-r) — to gather, to assemble, to herd together

17.meaning: 'To Him' or 'toward Him' — the preposition expressing direction or endpoint ('to / toward') combined with a pronoun referring to a single masculine person, indicating motion or attention directed at him.
17.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The base 'ilā shifts to 'ilay- when a pronoun is added. The suffix -hi is the third-person masculine singular object of a preposition, 'him'; its -i vowel is the form the pronoun takes after the 'ay' sound.

18.meaning: A word meaning 'all together', 'all of them', or 'the whole lot' — emphasising that no one and nothing is left out of a group.
18.grammar: A noun meaning 'all/entirety' carrying the -an ending: accusative case with tanwīn (the indefinite '-n'). This accusative form is typical of a word that comes alongside another to specify it as 'all of them, every one', describing the manner or extent.

1.meaning: 'Then as for …' A connective opening that introduces and singles out a topic for comment, often paired later with a response. The fa- means 'then/so,' and 'ammā' sets up 'as for (such-and-such)…' to highlight one case among others.
1.grammar: A connector fa- ('then, so') joined to the detailing/conditional particle ammā ('as for…'). Ammā introduces a subject for separate treatment and normally anticipates a matching clause (often introduced by 'fa-') that gives the comment about it. Neither part takes case endings.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
3.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

4.meaning: A two-part word: 'and' + 'they did / worked / performed.' The verb denotes doing deeds, working, putting effort into action — practical doing as opposed to mere speaking or believing.
4.grammar: A conjunction 'wa' + a past-tense verb, 3rd person masculine plural. The -ū ending marks the subject as 'they' (a group of males or a mixed group): 'and they did / worked.'

5.meaning: 'The righteous deeds / good works' — the definite plural of a word meaning that which is sound, wholesome, upright, and beneficial. As a noun it refers to good, virtuous actions that set things right.
5.grammar: A definite sound feminine plural noun ('the good deeds'). The -i ending is the oblique case used by feminine plurals to mark either the genitive ('… of …' / after a preposition) or the accusative (direct object); for this plural pattern the accusative and genitive share the same -i ending.
5.root: ص-ل-ح (ṣ-l-ḥ) — to be sound, good, upright, set right

6.meaning: 'So He pays them in full / then He gives them their due completely' — preceded by 'so/then.' From an intensive verb meaning to render in full, with an attached 'them.' It conveys giving someone the whole of what is owed, without shortfall.
6.grammar: The prefix fa means 'so' or 'then.' The verb is present/future in an intensive pattern (the doubled middle root letter); the ya- prefix marks the subject as 'he.' Because the stem ends in a long vowel (-ī), the indicative is shown by that retained vowel. The attached -him means 'them' (a group).
6.root: و-ف-ي (w-f-y) — to fulfill, complete, pay/give in full

7.meaning: 'Their rewards / their wages.' A noun naming recompense — the reward, wage, or compensation earned for deeds — with an attached 'their': 'their rewards.'
7.grammar: A plural noun meaning 'rewards/wages.' The -a ending is the accusative case, the form used when the word is the object of a verb (e.g., the thing given). The attached -hum means 'their,' referring to a group.

8.meaning: 'And He will increase them / give them more' — to add to, augment, or give an increase; to provide something over and above what is already there.
8.grammar: Prefix wa- means 'and'. The verb is present-tense, third-person masculine singular ('he increases/adds'), the ya- prefix marking the 'he' subject. The -u ending is the indicative, the plain statement-of-fact form. The suffix -hum is the object pronoun 'them' (a group of males).
8.root: ز-ي-د (z-y-d) — to increase, to add, to grow

9.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
9.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

10.meaning: 'His bounty / grace / favor' — faḍl is overflowing generosity, an extra goodness given beyond what is owed; with the attached pronoun it means the bounty belonging to Him (Allah).
10.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive pronoun '-hi' ('his/His'). The -i vowel before the pronoun is the genitive case, which typically appears after a preposition or links the noun to what follows in an 'of' relationship; here it carries through to the possessor.
10.root: ف-ض-ل (f-ḍ-l) — excess, surplus; hence bounty, grace, superiority

11.meaning: 'And as for …' A connective that introduces and sets apart a new topic for separate comment, usually anticipating a matching response clause. The 'and' joins it on; 'ammā' means 'as for (such-and-such)…'
11.grammar: The conjunction wa ('and') joined to the detailing/conditional particle ammā ('as for…'). Ammā singles out a topic for separate treatment and normally anticipates a matching clause (often introduced by 'fa-') that supplies the comment. Neither part takes case endings.

12.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
12.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

13.meaning: 'They disdained / scorned' — to have held oneself above something out of pride and refused it haughtily, deeming it beneath one's dignity.
13.grammar: A past-tense verb in the intensive reflexive (form X) pattern. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject: 'they (a group) disdained' (a completed action).
13.root: ن-ك-ف (n-k-f) — to disdain, to recoil from in pride

14.meaning: 'And they acted arrogantly / were haughty' — to have been proud and overbearing, swelling with self-importance and refusing to submit.
14.grammar: Prefix wa- means 'and'. The verb is past-tense, intensive reflexive (form X). The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject: 'they (a group) were arrogant' (a completed action).
14.root: ك-ب-ر (k-b-r) — to be great; (form X) to deem oneself great, to be arrogant

15.meaning: 'Then He will punish them / torment them' — to inflict punishment or chastisement upon someone, causing pain or suffering as a penalty.
15.grammar: Prefix fa- means 'then/so' (sequence or consequence). The verb is present-tense, intensive (form II) pattern, third-person masculine singular; the yu- prefix marks the 'he' subject (this u-vowelled prefix is characteristic of the form-II/causative patterns). The -u ending is the indicative, the plain statement-of-fact form. The suffix -hum is the object pronoun 'them' (a group of males).

16.meaning: 'A punishment / torment.' A noun naming chastisement or painful suffering inflicted as a penalty.
16.grammar: A masculine noun. The -an ending marks it as indefinite ('a punishment') and in the accusative case — the form a noun takes as the object of a verb or as the thing being described/quantified.
16.root: ع-ذ-ب (ʿ-dh-b) — to torment, punish, chastise

17.meaning: 'Painful / agonizing' — causing intense pain; an adjective describing something that hurts severely, e.g. a grievous, tormenting affliction.
17.grammar: An adjective of the intensive faʿīl pattern ('intensely painful'). The ending -an is accusative and indefinite, the case typically marking a verb's object or a describing word that agrees with such a noun; the final -n (tanwīn) marks indefiniteness.
17.root: أ-ل-م (ʾ-l-m) — pain, to ache, to hurt

18.meaning: 'And not' — a connector 'and' joined to the negative particle 'not,' negating a following statement.
18.grammar: Two particles: the joining 'and' (wa) plus the negator lā ('not'). Lā commonly negates a present-tense verb or a noun. Neither particle takes case endings.

19.meaning: 'they find' — to come upon, obtain, or encounter something; to perceive a thing to be present or available.
19.grammar: A present/future verb, 3rd-person masculine plural ('they …'). The ending -ūna combines the plural 'they' (-ū) with the indicative marker -na, signalling a simple ongoing or future statement (not negated or subjunctive). The ya- prefix marks the third person.
19.root: و-ج-د (w-j-d) — to find, come upon, obtain

20.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
20.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

21.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
21.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

22.meaning: A noun used to mean 'besides', 'other than', 'apart from', or 'short of'. It points to something or someone set apart from, or lower/lesser than, a named party. Often used in the phrase 'besides Allah'.
22.grammar: 'dūn' functions as an adverb-like noun of place/relation. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, which appears because it follows a preposition (such as 'min', 'from') and because it links to a following noun ('other than …'). It commonly heads the construction 'besides/other than [someone]'.
22.root: د-و-ن (d-w-n) — to be low/beneath, to fall short; hence 'below, other than, besides'

23.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
23.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

24.meaning: A guardian, protector, ally, or close supporter — one who is near and takes charge of another's affairs. Waliyy carries the sense of nearness combined with care, authority, and friendship.
24.grammar: An indefinite noun ('a protector'). The -an ending (tanwīn fatḥa) is the accusative case: it commonly marks the word as a direct object of a verb, or as a predicate/complement after certain verbs of 'making' or 'becoming'.

25.meaning: 'And not' — a connector 'and' joined to the negative particle 'not,' negating a following statement.
25.grammar: Two particles: the joining 'and' (wa) plus the negator lā ('not'). Lā commonly negates a present-tense verb or a noun. Neither particle takes case endings.

26.meaning: 'A helper, supporter, one who gives aid and victory' — an intensive form stressing reliable, effective help.
26.grammar: An indefinite noun on an intensive pattern (faʿīl) that conveys a strong or constant doer — 'a true helper'. The -an ending marks the accusative and indefiniteness, commonly used here as a specifier naming the capacity ('as a helper').
26.root: ن-ص-ر (n-ṣ-r) — to help, to aid, to give victory

1.meaning: 'O…!' — a compound vocative expression used to call out and summon an audience before addressing them. It fuses the call-particle 'yā' ('O') with a noun that means 'the one(s) addressed,' yielding an emphatic 'O you…!' that introduces direct address.
1.grammar: A vocative (calling) construction. 'Yā' is the particle for calling out; 'ayyu' carries a nominative '-u' as the one being summoned; 'hā' is an attention-drawing particle. Together they function as 'O you…!,' setting up the noun of address that follows.

2.meaning: 'The people / mankind' — human beings collectively, people in general, humanity.
2.grammar: A collective noun with the definite article al- ('the'); the article's 'l' assimilates into the following 'n' (al-nās → an-nās). The -u ending marks the nominative case — the case used for the subject of a sentence or the basic naming form of a noun.
2.root: ن-و-س / أ-ن-س (n-w-s / ʾ-n-s) — humankind, people, sociability

3.meaning: A short particle placed before a verb to emphasize or affirm it. Before a past-tense verb it means 'indeed / certainly / has already (happened)'; before a present-tense verb it can mean 'sometimes / may'. It sharpens and confirms the verb that follows.
3.grammar: An indeclinable particle (its form never changes). It does not take case or tense endings; its job is to color the following verb — affirming and intensifying a past action ('has indeed done') or signaling occasional possibility with a present verb.

4.meaning: "he/it came to you" — a past verb "came" with the pronoun "you" as the one reached, i.e. something arrived at or reached a group of people.
4.grammar: A past-tense verb in its base third-person masculine singular form ("he/it came"), with no extra subject suffix. The verb "to come" is intransitive, so the attached -kum is not a direct object but an indirect (dative) pronoun — "to you" (masculine plural), equivalent to "came to you (all)."

5.meaning: 'A proof / decisive evidence' — a clear, conclusive demonstration that establishes the truth of something beyond doubt; a compelling argument or self-evident sign.
5.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The ending -un is nominative (the subject/predicate case) and indefinite ('a proof'); the final -n (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite rather than 'the'.

6.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
6.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

7.meaning: 'Your Lord' (addressing a group). 'Rabb' is a rich term: the Master, Owner, Sustainer and Nurturer who creates, possesses, provides for, and brings a thing to its proper completion — far more than a mere ruler.
7.grammar: A noun ('Lord') with an attached possessive pronoun, forming a possessive pairing. 'Rabb' carries a doubled (geminated) 'b' — the shaddah — at its core. The '-i' vowel on 'rabb' is its case ending, determined by 'Lord's' own role in the sentence (not by the suffix); the attached '-kum' is the possessor ('your'), addressing a plural 'you', and as the possessed-to term it sits in the genitive.

8.meaning: 'And we sent down' — to cause something to descend or come down from a higher place, often used of sending down rain, sustenance, or revelation. Prefixed with 'and' and marked for a 'we' subject in the past.
8.grammar: A past-tense verb in the causative pattern (meaning 'to make come down'). The suffix -nā marks 'we' as the doer, giving 'we sent down'. The wa- prefix is 'and'. The causative form distinguishes it from simply 'descending' — it means causing descent.

9.meaning: To you / toward you (plural) — a preposition expressing motion or direction reaching a destination, joined with 'you all' as that destination.
9.grammar: The preposition ilā ('to, toward'), whose ending shifts to -ay when a pronoun is attached, plus -kum ('you all'). Together they mark the end-point or recipient of an action — the direction 'toward' or 'unto' a group.

10.meaning: 'A light' — light, radiance, or illumination; that by which things become visible. Often used figuratively for guidance, clarity, and spiritual illumination.
10.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The ending -an is accusative and indefinite, the case that typically marks the object of a verb or a complement; the final -n (tanwīn) marks indefiniteness ('a light').

11.meaning: An adjective meaning 'clear, plain, manifest' — describing something that is obvious and self-evident, or that makes things clear.
11.grammar: An active participle of form IV (mubīn), 'one that is manifest / makes clear.' The mu- prefix forms the participle. The final -an (tanwīn fatḥa) is the indefinite accusative ending ('a clear one'), used here to agree with a preceding masculine accusative noun it describes.

1.meaning: 'Then as for …' A connective opening that introduces and singles out a topic for comment, often paired later with a response. The fa- means 'then/so,' and 'ammā' sets up 'as for (such-and-such)…' to highlight one case among others.
1.grammar: A connector fa- ('then, so') joined to the detailing/conditional particle ammā ('as for…'). Ammā introduces a subject for separate treatment and normally anticipates a matching clause (often introduced by 'fa-') that gives the comment about it. Neither part takes case endings.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
3.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

4.meaning: A phrase 'in Allah / by Allah', combining the preposition 'with/in/by' and the divine name Allah, the proper name of the One God.
4.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with, by means of') prefixed to the divine name Allah. A preposition always forces the following noun into the genitive case, which is why Allah here ends in -i. With verbs of believing, bi- conveys the object of faith — to believe IN.
4.root: — (Allah is the proper name of God and is not derived from a triliteral root in the usual sense)

5.meaning: And they held fast / took firm hold — to grip tightly to a secure support, to cling for protection and refuge, seeking safety by attaching oneself firmly to something.

parts.en: to hold fast, cling, take refuge in

5.grammar: Opens with wa- ('and'). The core is a past-tense verb in Form VIII (iftaʿala), which often adds a reflexive or self-involved sense — here 'to hold oneself fast to / take refuge in.' The -ū ending marks 'they (a group of men) did' in the completed past.
5.root: ع-ص-م (ʿ-ṣ-m) — to protect, hold firmly, preserve, grant refuge

6.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
6.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

7.meaning: An emphatic future statement meaning 'then He will most certainly cause them to enter / admit them.' It conveys the act of bringing someone in and causing them to be brought into a place, performed by a third-person masculine singular subject (Allah) upon a plural masculine group.
7.grammar: Built on the causative pattern (af'ala), so it means to 'make/cause to enter,' not merely to enter. The 'fa-' prefix is a connector ('then/so'); 'sa-' marks the near future ('will'); the 'yu-' prefix marks a third-person masculine singular doer ('he'). The bare '-u' on the verb stem is the indicative mood, used for a plain factual statement. The attached '-hum' is the object 'them' (a group of males).

8.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
8.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

9.meaning: Mercy, compassion, tender loving-kindness — the deep, womb-like care that moves one to gentleness and pardon.
9.grammar: A singular feminine noun. The -in (tanwīn) ending is the indefinite genitive, used when the word follows a preposition or links to a preceding noun ('... of mercy'). It signals the word is being governed by something before it.
9.root: ر-ح-م (r-ḥ-m) — mercy, compassion; related to the womb and its nurturing care

10.meaning: A prepositional phrase, 'from him/it' — indicating origin or source, that something proceeds out of him/it.
10.grammar: The preposition min ('from') with the attached pronoun -hu ('him/it', third-person masculine singular). As the object of a preposition the pronoun stands in the genitive; the combination indicates source or origin.

11.meaning: Means 'and of bounty / and grace / and abundant favour'. The base noun denotes extra giving beyond what is owed — surplus generosity, abundance, an outpouring of bounty.
11.grammar: A noun in the genitive, shown by the -in ending (an indefinite genitive, 'a bounty / some bounty'). The doubled-vowel ending (tanwīn) marks indefiniteness and the -i marks the genitive, here carried over by the same preposition that governs the noun it is joined to. The wa- means 'and'.

12.meaning: Means 'and He guides them / will guide them' — to lead someone along a right path, to direct and show the way. The action is done by a third-person masculine singular subject toward a plural group.
12.grammar: The 'wa-' prefix means 'and.' The 'ya-' prefix marks a third-person masculine singular doer ('he'). The verb is imperfect (present/future tense), expressing an ongoing or yet-to-come action ('guides / will guide'). The final long '-ī' belongs to the weak verb stem. The attached '-him' is the object pronoun 'them'; its vowel shifts from 'hum' to 'him' after the 'ī' sound.

13.meaning: 'To Him' or 'toward Him' — the preposition expressing direction or endpoint ('to / toward') combined with a pronoun referring to a single masculine person, indicating motion or attention directed at him.
13.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The base 'ilā shifts to 'ilay- when a pronoun is added. The suffix -hi is the third-person masculine singular object of a preposition, 'him'; its -i vowel is the form the pronoun takes after the 'ay' sound.

14.meaning: 'A path', 'a way', 'a road' — a clear route or way that one travels, often used for a course of conduct or a way of life.
14.grammar: A noun. The '-an' ending is the indefinite accusative with nunation ('a path', not 'the path'); the accusative typically marks the direct object of a verb.

15.meaning: 'Straight', 'upright', 'level' — describes something direct and without crookedness or deviation; figuratively, correct and sound.
15.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer'-form describing a state) on the 'mustafʿil' pattern, literally 'that which holds itself straight'. The '-an' ending is the indefinite accusative with nunation, agreeing with the indefinite accusative noun it describes.
15.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — standing, being upright; here, being straight

1.meaning: Means 'they ask you for a ruling / a formal legal verdict.' It refers to seeking an authoritative pronouncement (a fatwā) on a point of law, addressed by a group to a single male.
1.grammar: Built on the 'seeking/requesting' pattern (istaf'ala), so it means to 'ask for / seek to obtain' a verdict. The 'ya-' prefix together with the '-ūna' ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'). The '-na' is the nūn of the imperfect indicative (a plain factual statement); it is fully present and carries a fatḥa ('-na') before the attached pronoun. (This nūn drops only in the subjunctive or jussive moods, which is not the case here.) The attached '-ka' is the object 'you,' addressing a single male.
1.root: ف-ت-ي (f-t-y) — issuing a formal ruling / verdict

2.meaning: 'Say!' — a command to utter or declare something aloud, addressed to a single male.
2.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to one male: 'say!'. Its natural form ends in a silent consonant (qul), but here a short -i vowel is added simply to smooth pronunciation before a following word that begins with a connecting sound; it carries no case meaning of its own.
2.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, to speak

3.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
3.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

4.meaning: He gives you a formal ruling — He pronounces an authoritative verdict or legal opinion to you.
4.grammar: Present-tense Form IV verb with a 'he' subject (the yu- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular doer), plus the attached object pronoun -kum ('you all'). It signals an ongoing or characteristic action of issuing a ruling.
4.root: ف-ت-ي (f-t-y) — to give a formal legal ruling/verdict (fatwā)

5.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
5.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

6.meaning: Kalāla is a technical inheritance term for a deceased person who leaves behind neither parent (ascendant) nor child (descendant) as heir — that is, someone with no direct line above or below. It can also denote the collateral relatives who inherit in such a case.

parts.en: one with no parent or child heir

6.grammar: The 'al-' prefix is the definite article ('the'). The '-at-' (tā' marbūṭa) is a feminine noun ending. The final '-i' is the genitive case: it typically marks the word as following a preposition or oath particle, or as linked to a preceding noun in an 'of …' relationship.
6.root: ك-ل-ل (k-l-l) — being remote/peripheral; encircling

7.meaning: If — a particle introducing a condition: it sets up 'if X (happens), then Y'.
7.grammar: A conditional particle ('if') that introduces a supposed case and typically puts the following verb into the jussive (conditional) form. Its base shape is 'in', whose final nūn carries a sukūn and is fully pronounced. When the next word begins with a sukūn-bearing cluster, the otherwise-quiescent nūn is given a kasra (-i) to avoid two consecutive sukūns meeting (the 'meeting of two quiescents'); this helping vowel eases pronunciation and carries no grammatical meaning of its own.

8.meaning: Means 'a man / a person, a human individual.' It denotes a single male human being (its feminine counterpart is imra'a, 'a woman').
8.grammar: An irregular noun: the 'i-' at the front is a helping (prosthetic) vowel that eases pronunciation. The final '-un' is the nominative case with 'nunation' (the '-n' sound marking indefiniteness): the nominative typically signals that the word is the subject or doer of a sentence, and the '-n' shows it is indefinite ('a man').

9.meaning: Means 'he perished / died / passed away.' It denotes a person's death, and more broadly the perishing, ruin, or coming-to-an-end of something.
9.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in its base form, marking a completed action. The shape with the final '-a' carries a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') with no added prefix or suffix — the bare perfect verb already means 'he did.'

10.meaning: A special negating verb meaning 'is not / are not'. Unlike a simple particle, it behaves like a verb (frozen in the past-tense form) and serves to deny that something is the case, cancelling an assertion of being.
10.grammar: A defective verb fixed in the 3rd-person masculine singular ('he/it is not'). The final -a is its frozen ending; it does not conjugate for tense like other verbs. Grammatically it raises its subject to the nominative and puts its predicate in the accusative, functioning to negate a state of being.

11.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
11.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

12.meaning: 'A child / a boy / offspring' — a son or child, the offspring born to a parent.
12.grammar: A noun. The -un ending is nominative with tanwīn (nunation — the doubled 'n' sound marking an indefinite noun, 'a child'). The nominative case marks it as the subject of a sentence or as a noun whose existence is being affirmed or denied. The initial wa- here is part of the root (w-l-d), not the conjunction 'and'.
12.root: و-ل-د (w-l-d) — to give birth, beget; offspring

13.meaning: And for him / and he has; a connective 'and' joined to 'for / belonging to' and a 'him' pronoun, expressing that something accrues or belongs to a single male.
13.grammar: A cluster of connective and particle elements: wa- ('and', joining to what precedes) + la- ('for / belonging to', showing possession or entitlement) + the pronoun -hu ('him / it', a single male or thing). Together they convey 'and to him belongs …'. The pronoun's own vowel is a short -u (a plain ḍamma); any lengthening to -hū heard in recitation is a positional prolongation (madd), not part of the suffix's inherent form.

14.meaning: A sister — a female sibling; by extension a female kinswoman or female counterpart of a thing. The feminine marker plus nunation (-tun) marks a singular, indefinite noun ('a sister').
14.grammar: A feminine singular noun (the ت is the feminine marker). The -un ending (nunation) sits on the final ت and is nominative and indefinite, marking it as a subject or named thing, equivalent to English 'a sister'.

15.meaning: Then for her — links a result ('then/so') with 'belonging to / for her', referring to a single female.
15.grammar: A cluster of particles plus a pronoun: fa- ('then/so', marking a consequence), the preposition li- ('for/to', shortened to la- before a pronoun), and the attached pronoun -hā ('her', feminine singular). Altogether: 'then for her'.

16.meaning: A half; one of two equal portions of a whole.
16.grammar: A singular noun. The final -u is the nominative case-ending, which typically marks the word as the subject of a sentence or as a predicate ('… is a half'). The absence of a final -n (no tanwīn) shows it is grammatically definite, often because it is linked to a following noun ('the half of …').
16.root: ن-ص-ف (n-ṣ-f) — half, midpoint

17.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
17.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

18.meaning: He left behind / he left, abandoned, or relinquished — a completed act of leaving something or someone, including leaving property behind (as an inheritance).
18.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb. The final '-a' marks third-person masculine singular: "he" did the action, viewed as completed.

19.meaning: 'And He' — the connective 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'He' (a single masculine person or thing), often introducing a new clause about the same subject.
19.grammar: A connective particle plus an independent pronoun. The wa- prefix means 'and', joining clauses or words. 'Huwa' is the detached third-person masculine singular pronoun; it carries no case ending, its final -a being fixed.

20.meaning: Means 'he inherits it / will inherit it' — to receive property or a legacy passed down from someone who has died. The subject is a third-person masculine singular, and the object refers to a single feminine thing or person.
20.grammar: The 'ya-' prefix marks a third-person masculine singular doer ('he'). The verb is imperfect (present/future), expressing an ongoing or future action. The '-u' on the stem is the indicative mood, used for a plain statement. The attached '-hā' is the object pronoun 'her / it,' referring to a single feminine noun.

21.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
21.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

22.meaning: The particle 'lam', a negating word used to push a verb into the past: it means 'did not' / 'has not'. Though it sits before a present-tense verb form, it negates the action as something that did not happen.
22.grammar: 'lam' is a negating particle that governs a following present-tense verb but gives it past meaning ('did not …'). It also puts that verb into the shortened (jussive) form. 'lam' itself carries no ending.

23.meaning: A present-tense form of the verb 'to be / to exist / to happen', in a shortened (jussive) shape often carrying the sense 'it is' or, with a negating particle, 'it is not / was not'.
23.grammar: The ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it'). The verb is in the jussive mood, shown by the bare final consonant with sukūn (-n, no vowel) and the dropped long vowel of the root; this clipped form appears after certain particles (such as those that negate or command) and signals it is governed by one of them rather than standing as a plain statement.
23.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

24.meaning: A preposition-plus-pronoun unit meaning 'for her / to her / belonging to her.' It marks possession, benefit, or assignment directed to a single feminine party.
24.grammar: The 'la-' is the preposition 'for / to,' often expressing ownership or entitlement ('it belongs to …'). The attached '-hā' is a pronoun meaning 'her / it' (single feminine). A preposition with a pronoun like this does not take a case ending.

25.meaning: 'A child / a boy / offspring' — a son or child, the offspring born to a parent.
25.grammar: A noun. The -un ending is nominative with tanwīn (nunation — the doubled 'n' sound marking an indefinite noun, 'a child'). The nominative case marks it as the subject of a sentence or as a noun whose existence is being affirmed or denied. The initial wa- here is part of the root (w-l-d), not the conjunction 'and'.
25.root: و-ل-د (w-l-d) — to give birth, beget; offspring

26.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'fa-' ('then', 'so', 'but') drawing a consequence, joined to the conditional particle 'in' ('if'). Together: 'then if …', 'but if …'.
26.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that signals a result or transition ('then/so'). 'in' is the conditional particle 'if', introducing a supposed condition. Both are indeclinable particles with no case ending.

27.meaning: Means 'the two of them (feminine) were / used to be.' It is the verb 'to be / to exist' set in the past, describing a state belonging to a pair of feminine subjects.
27.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) form of the verb 'to be' (stem 'kāna'). The attached '-tā' is the suffix marking a third-person feminine dual subject — exactly two females ('the two of them'); the 'a' before it belongs to the verb stem, not to this suffix. This is the special dual form, distinct from both singular and plural. As a 'being' verb it sets up a state or description rather than an action.
27.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

28.meaning: Two — the cardinal number 'two' for feminine things. It is the feminine dual numeral standing on its own.
28.grammar: The feminine numeral 'two'. The -ayni ending is the dual marker in its genitive/accusative form (versus -āni for the subject case), inherently denoting exactly two. The initial alif is a connecting (helping) hamza, pronounced 'ith-' only at the start of an utterance.
28.root: ث-ن-ي (th-n-y) — two, to double, to fold

29.meaning: A connective preposition-plus-pronoun unit meaning 'then for the two of them / so to them both.' It assigns possession, benefit, or entitlement to a pair (two people).
29.grammar: The 'fa-' prefix means 'then / so,' often introducing a consequence or result. The 'la-' is the preposition 'for / to,' commonly expressing entitlement or ownership. The attached '-humā' is the dual pronoun 'the two of them' — exactly two people. A preposition with an attached pronoun takes no case ending.

30.meaning: Means 'the two-thirds' — the fraction consisting of two of three equal parts.
30.grammar: The 'al-' prefix is the definite article ('the'). The base word means 'a third'; the dual ending '-āni' makes it 'two thirds' (exactly two such parts). The '-āni' form (with final '-i') is the dual used when the word is the subject/doer of a sentence (nominative), as opposed to the '-ayni' form used elsewhere.
30.root: ث-ل-ث (th-l-th) — three; a third part

31.meaning: From what / from that which — a fusion of the preposition 'from' with the relative 'what/which', introducing the thing or situation being referred to.
31.grammar: A merger of 'min' ('from') and 'mā' ('what/that which'); the 'n' of 'min' assimilates into the 'm' of 'mā', doubling it. The combination means 'from what ...' and typically introduces a following clause describing the thing referred to. Being particles, neither part takes a case ending.

32.meaning: He left behind / he left, abandoned, or relinquished — a completed act of leaving something or someone, including leaving property behind (as an inheritance).
32.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb. The final '-a' marks third-person masculine singular: "he" did the action, viewed as completed.

33.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
33.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

34.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
34.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
34.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

35.meaning: Means 'siblings / brothers and sisters' — a plural denoting kin of the same parents or close blood relations. The word akh ('brother') broadens in the plural to cover brothers and sisters together.
35.grammar: An irregular ('broken') plural of 'brother,' reshaped internally rather than by a simple suffix. The final '-an' is the accusative case with nunation (the '-n' marking indefiniteness): the accusative typically marks the object of a verb or other complements, and the '-n' shows the word is indefinite ('siblings').

36.meaning: Means 'men' — adult male human beings. It is the plural of rajul ('a man') and can also connote people of standing or strength.
36.grammar: A 'broken' (internally reshaped) plural of 'man.' The final '-an' is the accusative case with nunation (the '-n' marking indefiniteness): the accusative commonly marks the object of a verb or a similar complement, and the '-n' indicates the word is indefinite ('men').
36.root: ر-ج-ل (r-j-l) — man, manhood; (also: foot, on foot)

37.meaning: Women — the plural used for womenfolk, the counterpart of 'men'.
37.grammar: A plural noun (a plural without a singular from the same root) in the indefinite accusative, marked by -an. This ending typically marks it as a direct object or something produced/spread. The wa- prefix is the conjunction 'and'.

38.meaning: A connective unit meaning 'then for the male / so to the male.' It assigns a share, possession, or entitlement to the male as a category.
38.grammar: The 'fa-' prefix means 'then / so,' often introducing a result or consequence. The 'li-' is the preposition 'for / to,' frequently expressing entitlement or ownership ('belongs to'). The 'al-' is the definite article ('the'); it loses its 'a' after 'li-'. The final '-i' on the noun is the genitive case, which is the case nouns take after a preposition like 'li-'.

39.meaning: 'The like (of),' 'an equivalent,' 'something matching or comparable.' It denotes a counterpart of equal measure or kind to something else.
39.grammar: A noun in the nominative case, shown by the final -u, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the thing being identified ('X is …'). It is regularly followed by a noun in the genitive to mean 'the like OF …'.

40.meaning: A share, portion, or allotted lot — the measure of something assigned to someone, especially a portion of fortune or inheritance.
40.grammar: A noun. The -i ending is genitive, which typically links it to a following noun ('the portion OF …') or follows a preposition. Here the genitive marks it as standing in a possessive relationship with what comes after it.
40.root: ح-ظ-ظ (ḥ-ẓ-ẓ) — share, allotted portion, good fortune

41.meaning: The two females — a pair of female persons. The dual of unthā ('female'), made definite with 'the'.
41.grammar: The dual form of unthā, with the definite article al-. The -ayni ending marks exactly two and is the genitive/accusative form of the dual (its other form is -āni for the subject case). So it means 'the two females', in a position governed by a preposition or as object/possessed term.

42.meaning: He makes clear / He explains; to set something forth plainly so that its meaning is evident.
42.grammar: A Form II present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he'). The yu- prefix marks 'he', and the final -u marks the indicative mood — a plain, ongoing statement of fact (he makes clear / he is making clear).

43.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
43.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

44.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
44.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

45.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
45.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

46.meaning: A verb meaning 'you go astray, you stray, you lose the right path or wander off course' — addressed to a group. It conveys deviating from correct guidance, whether literally or in belief and conduct.
46.grammar: An imperfect (present/future) verb. The ta- prefix marks a second-person subject ('you'), and the -ū ending makes it plural ('you all'). The form lacks the final nūn (taḍillūna), which signals a subjunctive or jussive mood — the verb is governed by a preceding particle such as 'so that not' or 'lest', expressing purpose or warning rather than a plain statement.
46.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to go astray, lose the way, err

47.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
47.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
47.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

48.meaning: 'Of every / with all' — the preposition 'bi' ('with / in / by') joined to the word 'every / each / all', expressing comprehensiveness applied to whatever noun follows.
48.grammar: A preposition plus a noun. The prefix bi- ('with / in / by') always places the following noun in the genitive ('of') state. The final -i on 'kull' is that genitive ending, signalling the word is governed by the preposition. 'Kull' denotes totality — 'every (single)' or 'all'.

49.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
49.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
49.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

50.meaning: 'All-Knowing / deeply knowledgeable' — an intensive adjective from the root for knowledge, describing one whose knowledge is vast and complete; when applied in the highest sense it means perfectly and comprehensively knowing all things.
50.grammar: An intensive adjective/noun of the 'faʿīl' pattern, expressing an abundant, deep-seated quality ('one who knows thoroughly'). The final -un is the nominative case with 'tanwīn' (nunation) and indefiniteness — the nominative is the basic 'subject / predicate' state, and the doubled-n sound marks it as indefinite ('(an) all-knowing one').
